rules.rule: If you cannot name the next draw on liquidity, stop trading. No target means no Silver Bullet.
rules.quote: So if I don't know where the next draw on liquidity is, how the hell do you think you're going to know it? That's the time when you stop pushing buttons and walk away with what you took from the market!

rules.rule: Do not chase. If the FVG retracement has been missed, skip the move.
rules.quote: it's better to miss the move than to try to chase it

rules.rule: In his 2025 1m Silver Bullet short on GBPUSD, candle bodies must hold on the correct side of the FVG's consequent encroachment (the lower half for a short). Wicks may poke through. A body close through CE weakens the setup. This is a generic FVG rule, tied to Silver Bullet only by the video's context.
rules.quote: And the bodies should stay in the lower half or at the consequent encroachment

rules.rule: Same body-versus-wick test in the Sept 2026 backtesting video, which covers the 10:00 hour Silver Bullet FVG and its CE.
rules.quote: bodies tell the story, wicks do the damage

rules.rule: Presented as an all-asset-class model: index futures (ES, NQ, YM) and forex pairs. The charts and trades are on 1m and 5m, plus 15m for context. A 15m PD array can be tapped first, and sub-minute charts can be used for refinement.
rules.quote: ICT Silver Bullet trade setup which is a time-based algorithmic trading model for all asset classes

rules.rule: Applied to forex (EURUSD) in the London window in Feb 2025, entering a long on a discount BISI retest after a midnight low. He calls it easy bread-and-butter.
rules.quote: and that is your London open Killzone long or the London open Killzone Silver Bullet okay very very easy methodology applied to London open and then rally to this would be easy bread and butter setup

rules.rule: Window 1, London Open Silver Bullet: 03:00-04:00 New York local time.
rules.quote: first setup time is 3:00 a.m. to 4:00 a.m. now we're always referring to New York local time

rules.rule: Window 2, New York AM Silver Bullet: 10:00-11:00 New York local time.
rules.quote: the am session now this one is focusing on the 10:00 a.m. to 11:00 a.m. always New York local time

rules.rule: Window 3, New York PM Silver Bullet: 14:00-15:00 New York local time.
rules.quote: framed on 2:00 p.m. to 3:00 p.m. New York local time and this is the PM session ICT Silver Bullet setup

rules.rule: Sequence before the AM hour. After the 9:30 open runs into liquidity, the 9:50-10:10 macro rebalances or reprices, then hands off to the 10:00-11:00 Silver Bullet. The dossier wording reads like a reconstruction, so treat it as lower confidence.
rules.quote: then between 9:50 and 10:10 the macro rebalances before handing off to the 10:00–11:00 AM Silver Bullet

rules.rule: The opening range is 9:30-10:00 New York local time. This is the session context the 10:00 hour follows. All times are New York local.
rules.quote: so the opening range is between 9:30 in the morning and 10:00 a.m. eastern standard time so whatever the local time is in New York that's the time I'm referring to

rules.quote: here is the silver bullet 10:00 hour. Okay, so obviously we have 10:00 denoted. Always have that on your chart

turtle_soup.summary: Fade a sweep of an obvious high or low (pre-market, session, prior-day, equal highs/lows, opening range, range edge): once price runs the stops and rejects back inside, enter either at the sweep (aggressive) or deferred at the rejection block / FVG / inversion FVG / Venom order block, with the stop just beyond the sweep extreme and the target at the opposing liquidity or the range midpoint.
turtle_soup.needs_clock: Mostly no for the core pattern, yes for several of his filters and for how he picks the liquidity level. The core is price-only: an obvious swing high or low, equal highs or lows, or a range edge gets run, price rejects and displaces back inside, then a deferred entry (rejection block, FVG, inversion FVG, or the Venom candle pair) with a stop beyond the sweep extreme. He says price is fractal and "not tied to any real time element" (YcAfcpUCbDw 08:47). The Venom filter is also price-based: not in the middle of a range after several large-range candles. The clock enters in three places. (1) It decides which level counts: the pre-market high from 7:00 AM, the Asian or London high, Tuesday's daily low, the 9:30 to 10:30 opening range, the 2-hour lunch window. (2) It sets hunting windows: macros at 7:50 to 8:10, 12:30 to 12:45, 1:50 to 2:10 and 2:50 to 3:10, an Asian macro at 9:50 to 10:10 PM, and the 2022 "NY up to 10:00 AM after London posted the extreme" model. (3) It sets stand-down rules: wait for the dust to settle after news, take NFP-week profits before Wednesday, skip the last hour on NFP weeks. On 24/7 synthetic indices you could run the price-delivery core using rolling swing and equal-high/low levels plus a synthetic "prior period" high and low. The time-window edge would have to be dropped or tested separately, because it is part of his stated edge and cannot be reproduced there.
turtle_soup.how_to_code:
1) Liquidity map, updated per bar and only for unswept levels. Use fractal swing highs and lows on the working timeframe (1m to 5m). He also defines a swing by candle bodies (m_ND0oO67cU 47:21). Add relative equal highs or lows (two or more swings within a tolerance, for example 0.1 to 0.2 ATR). Add range anchors: pre-market or opening-range extremes, prior-day or prior-period high and low, session highs and lows. A level is swept when the bar high is above the level (or the bar low below it).
2) False break. The bar pokes beyond the level and price closes back inside within 1 bar (Venom, 5m) or 1 to 3 bars (the 2020 dossier summary, not a quote). Optional minimum penetration of 10 to 20 pips (the 2022 Month 4 wording, Gnw54f9v6SA), else only a tick or wick. Reject if bodies close beyond the level and hold there (acceptance), because that is a breakout.
3) Displacement. The reversal leg has a large-body candle, for example body of at least 1.5 times average body or 1 ATR, that breaks the last minor swing (a market structure shift), and leaves an FVG. A bearish FVG is candle1.low above candle3.high. For Venom, candle 1 is the sweep or spike candle and candle 2 closes back against it, with an imbalance (SIBI first, then BISI leaving).
4) Entry variants.
(a) Aggressive: market or limit at or just after the sweep (6ZFkXGo_Wjo), or 10 to 20 pips beyond the level (2022).
(b) Deferred, his default from 2023 onward, as limit orders into one of these arrays:
- The rejection block: the last up-close candle (for a short) before the run, using the full range for breakers, or the highest body to the wick high for a rejection block.
- The first FVG formed by the displacement: enter at its CE (50%) or upper quadrant for a short.
- The inversion FVG: a bullish gap that price closes through, which flips to resistance. Bodies must stay in the lower half for a short.
- Venom: enter at or below the second candle close, retrace to the sweep candle open, or a stop-entry beyond candle 2 (7wL2oyebbvU, mQsT-xux5Xk). A break below the BISI CE kills the setup.
5) Stop. Candidates are the sweep extreme plus 1 tick (Q0Xa-Vqy5vo), the sweep candle high or low (1iTBVIuvM3E, FjSHAOI-Mok), above the first candle of the SIBI (r3E1WQcx2-c), 50% of the sweep wick (yAZS6840r7U), or just beyond the departure FVG CE (Venom). In 2022 he also used fixed 15 to 20 pips (km0haQkTalc). After entry, trail behind new swing points, scale at internal liquidity, and keep a runner.
6) Target. The nearest opposing liquidity, in this order: relative equal highs or lows, session or pre-market extreme, the 9:30 open or opening-range-gap CE, the 50% equilibrium of the range (consolidation fades), then the daily draw. Fixed 20 pips in the 2022 scalp. Partials at internal pools with a runner (HM2M9a4OEFQ, dMhceEWjAuU) or a full pull with no partials (r3E1WQcx2-c).
7) Invalidation and filters. Cancel if there is no displacement within 1 to 3 bars, if bodies close beyond the sweep extreme, if bodies leave the correct half of the entry FVG, or if Venom retraces below the BISI CE. Skip the middle of a range after several large candles, and skip the first knee-jerk after high-impact news. Optional clock gates: macro windows, NY AM up to 10:00, NFP stand-down.
Subjective parts that need a fixed rule in code:
- Which liquidity is obvious enough ("when it's not obvious, assume it's not there", wWCKTEhVp2o).
- What counts as displacement.
- The higher-timeframe narrative or bias ("you have to know what the narrative is").
- Which array to enter on (rejection block, FVG, inversion FVG or order block), and whether to use bodies or wicks.
- SMT or Dollar Index confirmation.
- Partial and trail discretion.
- Whether consolidation helps or hurts.
turtle_soup.changes_over_time:
Evolution. 2017 (YcAfcpUCbDw): daily-chart "double-top and double-bottom sweeps" of clean equal highs or lows on forex majors. 2018 (Bf_9rrIXw7E, 1iTBVIuvM3E): intraday sweep of a swing high or low on GBPUSD; he says the pattern stems from Street Smarts and the high of the sweep candle is the line in the sand. 2020 (aWFSvqxEfg8): relabelled "Liquidity Purge and Revert", with the point "revert, not reverse" back into the dealing range. 2022 mentorship (a mix of dated dossiers): wait 10 to 20 pips beyond the old low or high (Gnw54f9v6SA); a fixed 20-pip stop and 20-pip target scalp in the NY session up to 10:00 after London posts the extreme (km0haQkTalc); an SMT triad where the index making the lower low is the Turtle Soup long (wWCKTEhVp2o); consolidation fades back to the 50% equilibrium (g7jchu4g31c, hzoMJQlEv5M); a London Open sweep followed by a market structure shift and a 2m FVG limit order (Q6GFu8-Z4rY). 2023 to 2026: one-minute and two-minute NQ executions with scaling and contract sizes, macro windows (pre-market 7:00, 12:30 lunch, 1:50 to 2:10 PM, Asian 9:50 PM), and from Jan 2025 the "deferred entry" at a rejection block, SIBI or inversion FVG, then Venom (Apr to May 2025) as its formalised five-minute, two-candle form.
Conflicts and shifts:
- Origin. 2018 credits Street Smarts and the 2022 20-day-high dossier (vqtA1S9JH34) fades the 20-day breakout, but 2024 says "it's not Linda Rashki's version" (PFUe6OKmKuk 14:02) and 2025 says "I don't use a 20-day high" (5N4QHrY6DRc 11:37).
- Timing of entry. 2022 waits for pips beyond the level; wWCKTEhVp2o says buy "below the old low"; 2025 either hits a market order on the false break (6ZFkXGo_Wjo) or says not to be in at the stop hunt and to defer (FjSHAOI-Mok).
- Stop. It tightens over time: fixed 15 to 20 pips and the sweep-candle extreme in 2018 to 2022, then 50% of the sweep wick, the first SIBI candle, 1 tick beyond the sweep (May 2025), and the BISI CE (Venom).
- Targets. A fixed 20 pips and a stop at equilibrium for fades, against scale-and-runner or an 18-hour hold to a daily FVG low (N9RW9v2kOoY), against "no partials, full pull" (r3E1WQcx2-c).
- Consolidation. 2022 fades breakouts from ranges back to the 50% equilibrium (g7jchu4g31c, hzoMJQlEv5M, ZB in RgpxhuVp5Xg), but the 2025 Venom says the model will not appear in the middle of a range after several large candles (7wL2oyebbvU).
- Rejection block. 2022 (oALYX0HCSYw) separates it from Turtle Soup because it needs no new extreme, while 2025 joins them in "Turtle Soup Deferred Entry With Rejection Block".
Source reliability. The 2017 to 2022 Core Content dossiers (km0haQkTalc, wWCKTEhVp2o, 441vklRYYR4, KrGTimL3YRQ, g7jchu4g31c, Gnw54f9v6SA) read like condensed summaries, so their "verbatim" cells may not be exact transcript. The 2023 to 2026 dossiers tagged STATED are more reliable. Several 2023 to 2024 trade rows (rYwsypxkRX4, FBsrQ0OunuA, dMhceEWjAuU) are on-screen annotations (SHOWN), not speech. Q0Xa-Vqy5vo is a sweep-reclaim long that the dossier does not call Turtle Soup. Other dossier cells I did not use as quotes (for example the 2020 "invalidation if no displacement in 1 to 3 candles" and the KrGTimL3YRQ "false breakout (Turtle Soup)" rule) are paraphrases, not quote-marked text.

Bf_9rrIXw7E is chart-only, with no trade-table row. I did not count odS7IIktqOY and krdRxohMI3g again, because they replay the HM2M9a4OEFQ trade. Direction: 15 shorts and 6 longs. Markets: NQ/MNQ 13 (12 are live executions, Dec 2023 to Apr 2026, many scaled in and out), ES 2, 30-year Treasury bond (ZB) 2, FX 4 (EURUSD x2, USDCHF, USDCAD; 2017 to 2022). Four more trades are Venom, which he calls a "deferred entry on a turtle soup": 7wL2oyebbvU, FjSHAOI-Mok, mQsT-xux5Xk and M6kCfe5QgDg, all NQ in 2025. About seven further false-breakout or consolidation fades are not labelled Turtle Soup (for example hzoMJQlEv5M, g7jchu4g31c, 6ZFkXGo_Wjo, 28M9ouiKmSY). Chart-only walkthroughs: GBPUSD in Dec 2018 and Jan 2018. He names ES, Dow, QQQ, stocks, commodities and bonds as workable, but in 5N4QHrY6DRc he says he does not look at individual stocks.

rules.rule: Turtle Soup is his own stop-hunt reversal play named after the Street Smarts pattern; it is not the daily 20-day-high version.
rules.quote: Turtle soup is my little play on and a nod to the pattern that was taught in Street Smarts by Linda Rashki and Larry Connors. But I do not trade that form of turtle soup.

rules.rule: 2018 framing: the pattern stems from Street Smarts; he calls it the most profitable pattern he has seen.
rules.quote: I'm not claiming that I created the Turtle Soup, I just felt that it was a pattern that was profitable more than any other pattern I've ever seen

rules.rule: Deferred (Venom) variant is disqualified in the middle of a range that has already printed several large-range candles.
rules.quote: If you're trying to use this model when it's in the middle of a trading range and it's done had several large range candles up or down, Venom will not appear in that, it's not going to appear.

rules.rule: NY-session reversal bias: London runs into a higher-timeframe discount (or premium) array, so expect the NY reversal the other way.
rules.quote: When London trades down into a higher timeframe discount array, anticipate a market reversal going higher in New York

rules.rule: Fade the apparent breakout in a foreign currency when the Dollar Index does not confirm it (SMT).
rules.quote: When you see what would otherwise look like strength and breakouts on the upside in foreign currencies, always double-check them with the dollar index.

rules.rule: Fade the textbook pattern, but only in the direction the higher-timeframe premise justifies.
rules.quote: You look for the pattern because retail will look for the pattern, but you're going to fade that pattern based on what you see on the higher timeframes.

rules.rule: Consolidation fade: work only the side of the higher-timeframe (daily / 4-hour) order flow.
rules.quote: Inside of the range or the consolidation, when the daily or 4-hour order flow is bullish

rules.rule: Liquidity map: buy stops rest above highs, sell stops below lows; these are what the sweep takes.
rules.quote: New pending orders are in the form of buy stops above the marketplace, and sell stops below the marketplace.

rules.rule: Why it pays: large fund traders keep stops beyond old highs and lows, so false breaks beyond them are lucrative.
rules.quote: What makes these false breaks higher and lower so lucrative is the fact that we understand that large traders, in the form of a fund trader, have their buy stops above.

rules.rule: Clean equal highs (or lows) are the sweep target: price drives through them, rejects and reverses.
rules.quote: double-top sweeps that means when we see price action creating very clean equal highs or relatively equal highs we're expecting that phenomenon to take place for a price would drive above those equal highs reject and trade lower

rules.rule: Pre-market version: the buy side that gets run is the one formed from 7:00 a.m.
rules.quote: notice the Run higher did to take out the buy side started at 7:00 a.m. it's classic pre-market session activity

rules.rule: 20-pips-a-day Model 1: short after New York probes the high that London posted as the day's high.
rules.quote: trading short after New York probes the highs while London session posted the daily high

rules.rule: Index triad: the index that trades below the old low against the others is the Turtle Soup long.
rules.quote: your eye should go right to that one that's making a lower low and identify that as Turtle Soup

rules.rule: Lunch-window Turtle Soup: mark the first FVG just before the liquidity was taken and carry it to the next day.
rules.quote: look at that 2-hour lunch period and when there is a turtle soup short or long, find that first fair value gap right before the liquidity is taken. Carry that over to the next day.

rules.rule: Sweep, reject, then displace back inside; that sequence is the textbook intraday reversal.
rules.quote: if it goes below that and then rejects it and displaces upward, that is a textbook intraday reversal pattern

rules.rule: 2020 Purge and Revert: the move is a reversion back into the dealing range, not a trend reversal.
rules.quote: I want to see if it goes higher and reverts. Not reverses, okay? I'm not saying reversal. I'm saying revert. What is it reverting to? It is reverting back inside the dealing range.

rules.rule: Venom / deferred signature: an inefficient run into the stops followed by an inefficient run away from them.
rules.quote: there has to be an inefficient run higher to it and then an inefficient run lower

rules.rule: Confirmation is the next candle breaking back down and closing.
rules.quote: When it breaks down on the next candle here and closes here, you have it

rules.rule: 2022 aggressive/late entry: do not buy the exact old low; wait until price is 10-20 pips beyond it.
rules.quote: It's better to wait for the market to trade under that low, and once it trades under there 10–20 pips, that's a really good ideal entry point.

rules.rule: 2022 mentorship form: after the sweep and displacement, limit order at the high of the FVG candle.
rules.quote: going to use the actual candle high that would be your limit order entry hypothetically 1.0924 and four pipettes that's your entry

rules.rule: 2025 aggressive form: false breakout above a minor buy side, hit it on a market order and aim at the low.
rules.quote: That's what I'm aiming, I'm hitting it on a market order, and I'm going to target that low right there.

rules.rule: Deferred entry: enter at the rejection block rather than at the sweep.
rules.quote: this is a deferred entry to a turtle soup false breakout higher high reversal pattern

rules.rule: Deferred entry means you do not have to be in at the stop hunt itself.
rules.quote: It's just another form of using a deferred entry on a turtle soup long or turtle soup short. You don't have to be in there where the actual stop hunt is occurring.

rules.rule: Venom conditions: an imbalance first, then the opposite departure, and entry below the second candle close.
rules.quote: You have to have a cibby first and then a bissy leaving it or it's not a venom. You got to enter below the second candle closing price or it's not a venom.

rules.rule: Venom order block: retrace to the opening price of the sweep candle is the deferred entry.
rules.quote: if it can afford you an entry back to the opening price of the last candle which is the Venom order block, that is your change in the state of delivery

rules.rule: Venom (deferred Turtle Soup) entry options: buy stop above the departure candle high, or buy at its open or better for a tighter stop.
rules.quote: You can do as a buy on a stop. So, a buy stop. This candlestick's high. You can buy it that way. Or if you're trying to keep a tighter stop-loss, you can be buying at this candlesticks open or less.

rules.rule: Consolidation-day fade: after the buy-stop sweep wait for a 1m swing-low break with an FVG, then short the retrace into it.
rules.quote: wait for a 1-minute swing low breakdown with a Fair Value Gap, then enter short when price trades back up into that FVG

rules.rule: He adds if price stabs once more into the rejection block.
rules.quote: that's a rejection block if it can stab one more time up into that I'll add just to prove the method and concept

rules.rule: Deferred 2m short: stop above the first candle of the SIBI.
rules.quote: the stop loss is above the first candle in the SIBI which I'll note for you here

rules.rule: Pre-session short: initial stop at half of the sweep wick (its consequent encroachment).
rules.quote: the initial stop loss was half of this wick wick right here

rules.rule: Venom long: the low of the piercing sweep candle is the risk point.
rules.quote: This candlestick's low is risk and this candlestick or less is an entry for this Venom model.

rules.rule: Venom stop sits just below the consequent encroachment of the departure imbalance, because the pattern is a balanced price range.
rules.quote: Consequent encroachment of that stop loss has to be just below that. Why? Because this venom model is a balanced price range and it should not come back down here.

rules.rule: 2018: the high of the sweep candle is the line in the sand.
rules.quote: The high on that candle is your line in the sand.

rules.rule: 2022 FX example: stop just above the sweep (London session) high.
rules.quote: your stop also be above the high here that comes in at 1.0936 and a half

rules.rule: Consolidation fade: stop above the new swing high that swept the liquidity.
rules.quote: stop loss placed above the newly formed swing high that swept the liquidity

rules.rule: Sweep-reclaim long (the dossier does not label it Turtle Soup): stop one tick beyond the sweep candle.
rules.quote: The stop goes immediately right below this by one tick. So, buying, stop here, target here.

rules.rule: Pre-market deferred short: full pull to sell-side liquidity, no partials, wants heavy black candles.
rules.quote: I'm not going to do any partials so it's going to be a full pull to sell side liquidity if I can get it

rules.rule: 2022 scalp form: fixed 20-pip target with a 20-pip stop.
rules.quote: We're targeting 20 pips, it's fixed with a stop loss at 20 pips

rules.rule: Consolidation fade: take the move back to equilibrium, not the far end of the range.
rules.quote: We're looking for price to return back to equilibrium. We do not anticipate or always hold for the opposite end of the consolidation

rules.rule: Consolidation day: the 50 percent midpoint of the daily range is the magnet.
rules.quote: in the middle there's your midpoint and it's going to want to gravitate back to the 50 percent midpoint of the daily range

rules.rule: 2026 pre-market false break: back into the range, target one and two at the 9:30 open.
rules.quote: expect it to pull back down into the range. Target one, target two is 9:30 opening price.

rules.rule: 2018: target the sell-side pool that is laid out before the fact.
rules.quote: Targeting this level here, you can't get any better than that. It's scripted, laid out perfectly before the fact

rules.rule: Bodies tell the narrative; wicks only trail the stops, so judge by candle bodies.
rules.quote: Any wicks are just allowing the market to take individual that trail of stop losses up. They're allowed to do the damage. So, the bodies are telling the story.

rules.rule: Scale and trail so the trade is funded and risk is off.
rules.quote: Trade is 'Funded' and locked in profit on the balance of the position

rules.rule: Costs and risk covered with a partial; third partial taken (on-screen annotation).
rules.quote: Risk & Costs Covered & 3rd Partial Taken

rules.rule: Hard stops only; no mental stops (said in a false-breakout short that was stopped out).
rules.quote: You have to have proper risk management. Don't overlever and stop losses have to be used. You cannot use a mental stop.

rules.rule: After a short entry, bodies must stay in the lower half of the SIBI and of the inversion FVG.
rules.quote: I want to see it stay in the lower half of the pink box which is the SIBI and I want to see it stay in the lower half of that orange box which is the inversion fair value Gap

rules.rule: A body outside the upper half of the inversion FVG invalidates the short; wicks may enter.
rules.quote: You want to stay in the lower half of that rectangle. It can wick in the upper half, but it cannot leave a body outside of the upper half of it to the upside

rules.rule: Price should stay inside the range and not go above the open of the array.
rules.quote: I want to see it stay inside of that range I don't want to see it go above the open of it

rules.rule: He wants price unwilling to return to the premium side of the array; willingness to do so is the warning sign.
rules.quote: one of the things that I like to see is the unwillingness per price to get back to the premium side of an array

rules.rule: If price comes back down through the departure imbalance midpoint it is not a Venom and the trade is probably wrong.
rules.quote: If it does, it's not a venom and it's probably going to be a wrong trade

rules.rule: Execution timeframe is whichever of 5m, 4m, 3m, 2m or 1m has the cleanest inefficiency.
rules.quote: timing is based on either a 5 minute 4 minute 3 minute 2 minute or one minute chart whichever one has the cleanest inefficiency that you can work with

rules.rule: 2025 Turtle Soup is traded on one-minute candles, not daily bars.
rules.quote: This isn't even daily charts. These is just one minute candles

rules.rule: Venom (deferred form) is framed on the five-minute chart.
rules.quote: The Venom model is on the five-minute chart.

rules.rule: Works on index futures, Dow, QQQ, stocks, commodities, bonds.
rules.quote: if you're an ES trader you can do this same pattern, it's very good on ES, Dow futures, QQQ, stock trading, commodities, bonds

rules.rule: Price is fractal: the same sweep happens on higher timeframes with no tie to a real-time element.
rules.quote: price is fractal that means the things that we would see and expect to see unfold in the lower timeframes just not tied to any real time element we would still expect the same phenomenon to occur on higher timeframe charts

rules.rule: 20-pips model window: New York session up to 10:00 AM.
rules.quote: During New York session up to 10:00 AM New York time

rules.rule: Reference window for pre-market highs and lows is 5:00 AM to 9:30 AM New York time.
rules.quote: Between the 5:00 AM New York time and 9:30 equities open New York time you're going to be looking for relative lows and relative highs and just compare them.

rules.rule: London kill zone for the 2022 London Open Turtle Soup example.
rules.quote: two o'clock at five o'clock in the morning that's the kill zone for london

rules.rule: PM macro: 1:50 to 2:10 PM was the window for the August 2024 Turtle Soup long.
rules.quote: 1:50 and 2:10 macro, look at that beautiful delivery right there, boom, right at the low.

rules.rule: Asian-session macro 9:50 to 10:10 PM was used for the April 2026 Turtle Soup short.
rules.quote: entering the macro time we're above the original buy side, so it's two stages of buy side liquidity.

rules.rule: Consolidation day: wait for the 3:00 to 4:00 PM false breakout outside the daily range.
rules.quote: on consolidation days, wait until the 3:00 PM to 4:00 PM window for the algorithm to engineer a false breakout outside the daily range to seek liquidity before returning to the midpoint

rules.rule: NFP week: take profits before Wednesday's NY open, then stand aside.
rules.quote: Capture your pound of flesh before Wednesday's New York open, and then sit on the sidelines and spectate only.

rules.rule: No trading the last hour on non-farm payroll weeks.
rules.quote: I don't like to trade the last hour trading on non-farm payroll weeks.

judas_swing.summary: Judas Swing: in the first hours of the trading day (midnight NY open through London, and later the 8:30 and 9:30 NY opens) price makes a false run against the day's true direction, through the Asian range extreme and the opening price, to trap traders and sweep stops, then reverses and expands the other way, usually leaving the high or low of the day.
judas_swing.needs_clock:
Yes, as taught. Every version is anchored to a clock: the midnight NY open, the Asian range (7pm to midnight NY), the CBDR (about 2pm to 8pm NY), the London window (midnight or 2am to 5am NY), and for index futures the 8:30 and 9:30 NY opens. The day-of-week filter (Monday to Wednesday) and the 10:00 AM and 2:00 PM time caps are clock rules too.

The core price pattern can run on 24/7 synthetic indices with price delivery alone, if you replace the clock anchors with arbitrary parameters. Use a fixed daily open for the 'midnight open', a fixed look-back range for the 'Asian range', and a fixed number of bars after the open for the window. Then detect: a sweep beyond the range extreme and through the open against the bias, followed by a reclaim and displacement. That is an approximation of his idea, not his model. The session identity (Asian, London, news, equity open) that he says drives the false run would be missing.

He also says the midnight-range algorithm does not apply to crypto, and he declines to cosign synthetic markets: 'I have no experience with them' (Z0VYZoaTIKE, 00:54). Any backtest on synthetics should be validated separately.
judas_swing.how_to_code:
All numbers below are his stated values from different years. Make them parameters.

1. Setup (clock).
- Convert to America/New_York.
- Midnight open O = open of the 00:00 NY bar. For the morning session use the 08:30 NY open instead, and for the equity open use 09:30.
- Asian range: AH/AL = high/low of 19:00 to 00:00 NY (JA0mLNJeytY and _2nUKLAD9ig say 7pm; one Oct 2022 chart table says 20:00).
- Optional CBDR = 14:00 to 20:00 NY.
- Filters: Asian range of 20 pips or less is ideal. Between 20 and 40 is acceptable. Above 40 means delayed profile or skip. Skip when CBDR is above 40 to 50. Skip Thursday and Friday, post-FOMC London, and NFP Thursday and Friday.

2. Window.
- 2017: 00:00 to 05:00 NY.
- Oct 2022: normal profile starts at 00:00 with the extreme made by 02:00 to 04:00; delayed profile starts at or after 02:00.
- Index version: 09:30 to about 10:10 (or 10:00 per Model 13), and the 8:30 news run.

3. Detection, bullish case, with the bearish case mirrored. Only label a Judas after the fact.
- Bias input (subjective, human or HTF module): bullish day.
- Within the window, require:
  - the low breaks AL, or O - k, where k is a parameter. His values: 10 to 20 pips beyond the Asian extreme (2017 trade table), about 20 to 33 pips, or 1 to 2 SD of the Asian range/CBDR (2022).
  - the 2017 version also optionally shows a first pop above AH, then the drop below O and AL.
- Then a reclaim: a displacement candle closes back above AL (or O) and creates an FVG, or a market-structure shift on 1 to 5 minutes.
- Entry: limit on retrace into the FVG, OTE (62 to 79%), or order block, in discount (below the 50% of the swing). The 2017 variant places a limit or buy-stop-limit at or just past the sweep (AL minus 5 pips, plus spread).

4. Stop and exits.
- Stop: below the sweep low. Alternatives are the FVG candle low (exactly in 2024, plus 1 to 2 ticks in 2022), or AL minus 50% of 5-day ADR.
- Targets: the opposite side of the Asian range (AH), the previous day high, ADR high, and the 1 to 4 SD projections measured from the Judas size.
- Scaling: 60 to 80% at the 60-minute 50% equilibrium. 80% if the ADR high is reached before 10:00 NY. Cap at 14:00 NY.

5. Invalidation.
- Price makes a new extreme beyond the sweep, or bodies close beyond the Judas extreme.
- The opposite liquidity is taken first (CnTXwAuDi9Y 28:40).
- No window match.

Subjective parts: the daily bias, what counts as a 'tight' Asian range, the sweep depth, what counts as displacement or a valid FVG/OB, whether to treat the day as normal or delayed profile, and which of the several stop and target conventions to use. The Judas itself is only recognisable after reclaim, so build the detector as 'sweep, then reclaim, then retrace entry'. Do not enter the sweep blindly.
judas_swing.changes_over_time:
1. Window and definition drift.
- Dec 2017 (xJMbva8SjzE) defines it as midnight to 5:00 a.m. NY.
- Oct 2017 (M27EOgtHhis) says the London kill zone starts at 1:00 a.m.
- 2021 onward (GVx-yJkehtA and the 2025 GBPUSD lecture) uses 2 to 5 a.m.
- Oct 2022 (eU8WcUftUtY) splits it into normal (starts at midnight, 'London Judas') and delayed (starts at or after 2:00 a.m.) profiles.
- Feb to Jun 2022 and from 2023 on, the same label is applied to the 9:30 equity open, the 8:30 news run (2024), a 10:00 a.m. Judas (Model 13, Feb 2024), the NY session (Sep 2025), and daily or weekly opens (2017 to 2024).
- By 2026 (UTrm6uCOUZo) 'a Judas' is also used for a multi-day stop-hunt 'capitulation' washout, which is not the daily-open model.

2. Size of the false run.
- 2017: about 30 pips above the open (M27EOgtHhis).
- The 2017 trade table says 10 to 20 pips beyond the Asian extreme (not a quote).
- Oct 2022: 20 pips (1MnfiqKx5Uo), about 33 pips (cqf8nH54bb8), or 1 to 2 SD of CBDR/Asian range (eU8WcUftUtY).
- JKzEhfwV1dY says the exact extension need not be known in advance, only measured afterwards.

3. Filters conflict or tighten.
- Asian range: c5pKck9PwsQ (2018) says 'Certain days Asian Range isn't important', while Oct 2022 demands 20 pips or less and treats more than 40 as delayed or sidelines.
- CBDR thresholds in Oct 2022 lectures: less than 40 (eU8WcUftUtY), skip above 50 (stK2gNqhLaM), 20 to 30 ideal (JKzEhfwV1dY 00:24:37), and ADR/CBDR 60 or under for expansion (-oMtfDvc18Y).
- Asian range start time is 7pm in two dossiers; one chart table says 20:00.

4. Entry style.
- 2017: trade the sweep itself (limit or buy-stop-limit after the sweep into OTE, JA0mLNJeytY trades table).
- Oct 2022: buy below the open or Asian low at a discount PD array (5Z_3NbclMSY, OVfn-gDk2dE).
- 2022 mentorship, 2023 and 2024: wait for market structure shift, then a 1 to 5 minute FVG retrace.
- 2024 to 2026: inversion FVG, SIBI and suspension block.

5. Stop contradiction.
- Oct 2022: 50% ADR from the Asian extreme (5Z_3NbclMSY), or 5-day ADR of 90 to 100 pips for HTF swing ideas.
- May 2022: 1 to 2 ticks above the FVG candle.
- Feb 2024: exactly at the candle, 'not one tick above it'.
- 2026: no fixed stop at all; he exits when bodies close outside the block (6VaEdP4TYe8).

6. Target contradiction.
- 2017 and 2022 treat a return through the midnight open and the opposite Asian extreme as normal targets.
- 2026 (KHkUPAsdyfk) says do not hold for a return to the open and take the relative equal highs or lows instead.

7. Management over time.
- 2017: partials at 100-pip intervals.
- Oct 2022: 60 to 80% at 60-minute equilibrium, 80% off if ADR is hit before 10 a.m.
- 2025 (WGGDbeRpo4w): no stop jamming.
- 2026: take something off manually.

8. Source quality caveats.
- ouisWztKpDU (2024 ES 'Judas Swing Entry') has no quoted statement. Its only rule cell is an unquoted paraphrase, so it is counted as a trade but omitted from the quoted parts.
- xJMbva8SjzE has no quoted stop or target, only trade-table glosses (stop beyond the manipulation extreme, target Asian opposite side and daily expansion).
- Several Oct 2022 'Exact Verbatim Statement' cells are partly paraphrase. Only text inside quote marks was used.
- 'false rung' in xJMbva8SjzE is a transcription error for 'false run'.
- WGGDbeRpo4w's quote contains bracketed editor insertions.

Only about 15 are specific intraday examples, so treat the count as approximate.

FX again 2025: GBPUSD London demo on 2025-02-21 and a EURUSD NY-session Judas. He warns off crypto and synthetic markets.

rules.rule: Definition and purpose (2017): the Judas swing is the false run early in the day that traps traders who do not know the day's true direction. He says the high or low of the daily range forms between midnight and 5:00 a.m. NY.
rules.quote: the Judas swing is a false rung that trips traders that lack the understanding of true direction of the day

rules.rule: Best on days after a narrow Asian range (7pm to midnight NY). Price takes liquidity on one side of the range to put traders on the wrong side, then goes the other way for the rest of the day.
rules.quote: the market will seek the liquidity above or below this range with a premise that it's going to put them in the wrong side and then it'll go the other way for the remainder of the trading day

rules.rule: Oct 2022 volatility filter: the Asian range must be 20 pips or less before Frankfurt and London.
rules.quote: We're going to demand that the Asian Range is in a 20 pip range or less ahead of Frankfurt and London

rules.rule: Oct 2022 'normal protraction' (London Judas right after midnight) requires the Central Bank Dealers Range (CBDR) under 40 pips.
rules.quote: Central Bank Dealers Range again is going to be less than 40 pips

rules.rule: Oct 2022 sell-side lecture: when ADR/CBDR is 60 pips or less, expect a strong expansion day (up to twice ADR), which is the day type the Judas sell setup is aimed at.
rules.quote: if we see 60 pips or less, the conditions are likely that we'll see a strong expansion

rules.rule: Day-of-week filter (2021): the midnight opening price is not used late in the week. The same statement says to buy below it in bullish weeks and sell above it in bearish weeks on Monday to Wednesday only.
rules.quote: we're not going to reference the opening price on thursday because we're so late in the week

rules.rule: Bullish day (Jun 2022): the market opens, manipulates below the NY midnight open to make the low of the day, then distributes higher. So buy the Judas drop below the open.
rules.quote: on bullish days, expect the market to open, manipulate price below the New York midnight opening price to create the low of the day, and then distribute higher

rules.rule: Bearish day (Jan 2023): in a bearish market a rally above the 00:00 NY open is the manipulation, so sell from above the open.
rules.quote: you see that happen at midnight here New York local time, rallies above that in a bearish market are classic institutional manipulation

rules.rule: Mark the Asian range: it starts at 7:00 p.m. NY and ends at midnight NY. Its high and low are the liquidity the Judas swing runs.
rules.quote: the range begins at 7:00 p.m. New York time and it ends at midnight New York time

rules.rule: Mark the exact midnight NY opening price and extend the line to about 11:00 a.m. NY. It is the pivot the Judas swing moves away from and back through.
rules.quote: whatever the opening price is exactly at midnight New York time I draw that out to around 11 o'clock in the morning

rules.rule: Reference-open switch (Feb 2022): use the midnight open for the whole daily range, but the 8:30 open when working the morning session in index futures.
rules.quote: if you're looking at the entire daily range you're going to use the opening price at midnight but if you're going to be looking at the morning session you want to be using the 8 30 opening price

rules.rule: 2017 window: start hunting for the Judas swing at the midnight NY open. The window ends at 5:00 a.m. NY, five hours in total.
rules.quote: you start hunting the Judas swing at midnight New York time okay so this is a New York opening price and it ends at 5:00 a.m. New York time and that's basically the entire five hour window that would be utilized for anticipating this price move

rules.rule: Late 2017: the London open kill zone is said to start at 1:00 a.m. NY.
rules.quote: this starts the actual London session which is one o'clock in the morning New York time for me this is London open kill zone ICT kill zone

rules.rule: 2021: the London kill zone is 2:00 to 5:00 a.m. NY, and the NY kill zone is 7:00 to 10:00. The 2025 GBPUSD London Judas demo uses 2:00 to 5:00 a.m. ET.
rules.quote: london kill zone is two o'clock in the morning to five a.m new york is seven a.m to ten a.m

rules.rule: Oct 2022 'delayed protraction' profile: if price consolidates from midnight, the Judas move starts at or shortly after 2:00 a.m. NY, not at midnight.
rules.quote: In delayed protraction, IPDA will enter a protraction stage at or shortly after 2:00 AM New York time

rules.rule: Index futures at the 9:30 a.m. NY equity open (Feb 2022): the first move after the open is the wrong move, a Judas swing, so do not chase it.
rules.quote: the initial move is technically the incorrect move going into the opening at 9 30. so this is like a judas swing

rules.rule: 8:30 a.m. news (Oct 2024): the first run on a high-impact release is usually the Judas swing. Wait a minute when several reports drop together.
rules.quote: High impact news driver at 8:30 usually it's the first run that is your Judas swing but because we have multiple reports at 8:30 give it a minute.

rules.rule: Charter Model 13 slide (Feb 2024): 10:00 a.m. EST, after the first 30 minutes of sentiment is set, is listed as a Judas swing time. The same slide lists 8:30, 9:30, 10:30 and 11:00 as other anticipation times.
rules.quote: At 10:00am EST after first 30 minute Sentiment Is Established. [Judas Swing]

rules.rule: 2025: a Judas swing can also form in the New York session after a lethargic London kill zone, as a breakaway fair value gap.
rules.quote: And then New York session, we came alive. We had a breakaway gap, bearish fair value gap

rules.rule: Bullish Judas anatomy (2017): a pop above the Asian high, then a drop below the midnight open, then below the Asian low. That sequence is the swing.
rules.quote: what we're looking for is the element of a bullish Judas swing is a pop above the Asian range high then a drop below the opening price at midnight and then below the asian range low when that occurs that's the actual Judas swing

rules.rule: Bearish Judas anatomy (2017): from a small, tight Asian consolidation, price drops first to trip traders, then runs above the Asian high and the opening price. That move above is the swing.
rules.quote: asian range small tight consolidation we want to see it drop down trip traders in right away then run on the other side of the asian range high that movement above the opening price above the asian range high that is the Judas swing

rules.rule: Bearish trigger (2017 AUDUSD): price runs above the Asian range high and clears the buy stops, then goes the other way for the rest of the day.
rules.quote: running above the asian range high clearing out their stops which would be a buy stop

rules.rule: Size of the false run (2017): a small rally above the open, usually about 30 pips, then the drop that makes the low of the day.
rules.quote: here's the power of three the opening price small door rally up not usually about 30 pips or so and then it drops down creates the low of the day and comes off the low there it is

rules.rule: Oct 2022 size of the false run: in a normal London profile, look for the Judas swing to reach 1 to 2 standard deviations away from the range. It is a bullish drop here, mirrored for bearish.
rules.quote: look for that Judas swing to reach down 1 to 2 standard deviations

rules.rule: Oct 2022 definition: the Judas swing is the protractionary move that runs counter to the intended direction of the day. It is measured against the CBDR (see the next part for what he says about when its size is known).
rules.quote: We're looking specifically at the range that IPDA will go into protractionary state and move counter the direction of the intended direction of the day in other words it's the Judas swing.

rules.rule: Oct 2022 bullish entry: buy on the Judas drop, down at or below the opening price, and do not chase price.
rules.quote: You want to be buying on the Judas swing down or below the opening price and don't chase price

rules.rule: Oct 2022 bullish day trade: buy under the Asian range low, adding 5 pips for the spread. The dossier's gloss adds that this should coincide with a discount PD array and 1 to 2 standard deviations, mirrored for sells.
rules.quote: I like buying under the Asian Range plus 5 pips for the spread

rules.rule: Secondary entry (Oct 2022 sell lecture): if the ideal Judas entry point has passed, a 5-minute retracement can still be scalped.
rules.quote: Even after the ideal Judas entry point has passed, a 5-minute retracement can be scalped

rules.rule: Short entries after an upside Judas run must be taken in premium (above the 50% equilibrium of the range), never in discount (May 2022 ES).
rules.quote: equilibrium we need to get to a premium we don't want to sell in a discount

rules.rule: 2026 fade of a run to all-time highs (Market Maker Sell Model): sell short inside the last suspension block, a bullish up-close candle, aiming for sell-side liquidity.
rules.quote: selling short inside of that last suspension block. It's a bullish up close candle

rules.rule: Oct 2022 day-trade stop: 50% of ADR measured from the Asian range low. The dossier's gloss says it is added to the Asian high for shorts, and that this is 5-day ADR.
rules.quote: take 50 pips minus the Asian range low, whatever that price is, that's what your stop loss has to be

rules.rule: Apr 2022, 9:30 Judas short: the stop goes at minimum above the high of the candle that formed the fair value gap.
rules.quote: your stop loss has to be at minimum above the candle's high that formed the fair value gap

rules.rule: May 2022 aggressive short: stop 1 to 2 ticks above the high of the candle that formed the top of the FVG.
rules.quote: for an aggressive short stop loss, place the stop 1 to 2 ticks above the high of the candle that formed the top of the Fair Value Gap

rules.rule: Feb 2024 Model 13: the stop goes exactly at the FVG-forming candle's extreme. The rest of the same cell adds 'not one tick above it', which contradicts the 2022 '1 to 2 ticks' rule.
rules.quote: stop loss is placed at the high of the candle that forms the high of the Fair Value Gap used for the setup

rules.rule: Jun 2023 two-gap rule: when two gaps form, find 50% (consequent encroachment) of the higher gap and place the stop just above it.
rules.quote: I'm finding half of that or 50% of it, consequent encroachment, and I place my stop loss just above that

rules.rule: Jan 2018 bearish Judas into London: the stop goes above the old daily high that capped the run (1.3599 on GBPUSD).
rules.quote: Your stop will be above this high. There's your old high back here on the daily at 1.3599. That's where this stop needs to be.

rules.rule: Oct 2022 higher-timeframe swing version: use the 5-day ADR as the stop, so a 90 to 100 pip stop is acceptable when the idea is a higher-timeframe setup.
rules.quote: a 90 to 100 pip stop is relatively insignificant because you're looking for higher timeframe setups

rules.rule: Oct 2022: take 60 to 80 percent off at the 50% equilibrium of the 60-minute range you are trading inside.
rules.quote: At the equilibrium of the price range you are trading inside of on a 60-minute chart, take or have taken 60 to 80 percent off

rules.rule: Oct 2022 projection: once the Judas has played out, the number of standard deviations it covered becomes the multiplier used to project the expansion.
rules.quote: How much of a standard deviation did we see? Because that becomes the known range to work with and it becomes our multiplier as well.

rules.rule: Time cap on the expansion (Oct 2022): even on a long trending day, 2:00 p.m. NY usually caps the high or low of the day.
rules.quote: Even in a really long winded trending day, 2:00 PM usually caps the high or low of the day if we continue through London Close Kill Zone

rules.rule: 2026: do not hold for a return to the midnight open. It can reach it but often will not, so target the relative equal highs or lows instead.
rules.quote: don't hold with the expectation that we're going to go all the way back up to the opening price. It's not necessary. It can, but it's many times not going to do that

rules.rule: Oct 2022: if the ADR high is reached before 10 a.m. NY, take 80% off and keep a runner for a possible double-ADR day.
rules.quote: If ADR high is reached prior to 10 AM, take 80% off of your position.

rules.rule: 2017 partials: take something off at every 100-pip interval. A day trader banks 80%, and a short-term trader banks at least half.
rules.quote: as a day trader you certainly want to be banking 80% of your position and if you're a short-term trader you want to be at least half your position out because the weekly can change gears midweek

rules.rule: Feb 2025 GBPUSD London Judas demo: do not jam the stop to break-even early. The trade either stops out at the planned stop or reaches the target.
rules.quote: come hell high water the trade stops you out where you placed your stop with [calculated risk] or it gives you your Target

rules.rule: Apr 2026 MNQ: when price stalls, manually take something off. Taking profits is never a mistake.
rules.quote: it's better for you to just manually take something off. You don't go wrong. You don't make mistakes by taking profits

rules.rule: Bearish Judas needs buy-side liquidity or an old high taken first. If the previous day's low or sell-side liquidity is taken first and price then rallies, it is not bearish and the short setup is cancelled.
rules.quote: if price takes out the previous day's low or sell-side liquidity first and then rallies, the price action is not bearish and cancels a short setup

rules.rule: 2026 fade: exit the trade if candle bodies close outside the suspension block, since the wicks may poke out but bodies must not.
rules.quote: It can trade to the high of that suspension block again. But I don't want to see any bodies outside of it. If it looks like it's going to do that, I'll just collapse the trade

rules.rule: Oct 2022 no-trade rule: if the day does not match one of the four defined London profiles (normal or delayed protraction, buy or sell), it is a missed trade. Leave it alone.
rules.quote: It could be a 150 pip day and you aren't getting in with either one of these profiles, and guess what that means? That's a trade you missed and you leave it alone.

rules.rule: Oct 2022 skip filter: if the CBDR is wider than 50 pips, pass on the London session. The same lecture sets the Asian range filter at 40 pips, then treats 40+ as delayed-profile or sidelines.
rules.quote: If the Central Bank Dealers Range is greater than 50 pips, I'm already knowing firsthand I'm possibly going to pass on a London

rules.rule: 2017: watch EURUSD, GBPUSD, AUDUSD and USDJPY, plus USDCAD per the dossier's markets table. The charts shown are 15-minute.
rules.quote: euro dollar Cable Aussie dollar dollar yen there's four markets if you just watch those it'll give you a wide array of potential scenarios where this type of thing forms

rules.rule: 2025: the midnight-based algorithm works in Forex and futures but not crypto. In the same cell he declines to cosign synthetic markets: 'I have no experience with them'.
rules.quote: It works obviously in Forex and it works in Futures, it works in every asset class with the exception of crypto

rules.rule: Daily-timeframe version (2021): a daily candle that opens and trades down is a Judas swing that traps lower-timeframe sellers before reversing off a higher-timeframe order block.
rules.quote: this is a judas swing retail traders get caught up in that on a lower time frame they think it's bearish and they start selling short

rules.rule: Weekly-timeframe version (2017): at the new week's open, the drop below the weekly opening price is the Judas swing.
rules.quote: the new week we would expect to see the opening price that drop down which is a Judas swing this engineered move is to knock individuals are already out long or drive individuals that are not in the marketplace that want to sell short to entice them to do so

mm_models.summary: Fractal template: original consolidation, then a run away from it (buy-side curve for a sell model, with re-accumulation stages), a smart money reversal that sweeps liquidity at a higher-timeframe array, a low-risk entry on the first retrace, re-distribution stages, and a return to or through the original consolidation (the terminus). The sell model is MMSM and the buy model is MMBM.
mm_models.needs_clock: Mostly no. The model's structure is price-only: consolidation, run, liquidity sweep and smart money reversal, market structure shift, FVG/OB retrace, then stages and a return to the origin. He says it is fractal across all timeframes and asset classes, and he teaches it on weekly and daily swings as well as 1m charts. Clock use is a filter on top of that. Examples are the London kill zone, the New York AM session, the 6:00 AM pre-market early-bird scalp, the PM-session reversal, and 'time and price in agreement' for the smart money reversal. Opening-gap targets (NWOG/NDOG, opening range gap) and 'session high/low' terminus also depend on session boundaries. It could run on 24/7 synthetic indices using only price delivery, if the clock filters and the gap and session targets are dropped or replaced with synthetic-day boundaries. Some of his best examples (2023 to 2026) are session-bound, so expect a lower-quality filter than he uses.
mm_models.how_to_code:
Sell model (MMSM). Mirror every step for the buy model (MMBM).
1. Original consolidation (OC): find a range of N bars on the chosen timeframe whose range is below k x ATR. Store the OC high and OC low. He uses the OC high as the reference level, and in 2022 teaches that body highs and lows matter more than wicks. SUBJECTIVE: which range counts as the 'original' one, and what counts as consolidation.
2. Buy-side curve: price breaks out of the OC (the run out) and builds higher highs and higher lows in at least 2 steps. Each pause is a re-accumulation stage: a retrace of at most about 50% of the prior leg that leaves a bullish FVG or OB. Count the stages. SUBJECTIVE: stage count and size.
3. Smart money reversal (SMR): price takes a swing high, equal highs or a prior buy-side liquidity pool (optionally inside an HTF premium PD array or above the OC high), then displaces down. Fire the trigger on a close below the last higher low (market structure shift), with a large-body candle that leaves an FVG. Store the SMR high. SUBJECTIVE: displacement size and HTF array alignment. In 2023 he said it needs 'time and price in agreement'.
4. Low-risk sell: place a limit at the first retrace into the bearish FVG (its consequent encroachment), the last up-close candle (order block, with the body midpoint as mean threshold), a breaker, or an inversion FVG. Stop is above the SMR high ('your risk is the high', 2017), or above the order block for a tighter version. Do not try to sell the exact apex.
5. Re-distribution: after each lower low, a retrace into a new bearish FVG or OB is the next stage and another entry. Pyramid only above equilibrium (Model 7). The second-stage run is described as the biggest.
6. Targets, in order: the first swing low, relative equal lows, and the price levels of the earlier accumulation stages (the curve is symmetric). Terminal target: the OC low, then sell-side liquidity beyond it by 10/20/30 pips or points. Take about 80% off at the OC and test for a deeper move. In bullish regimes expect a stop short of the OC (2026).
7. Invalidation and exits: a close above the SMR high or above the order block mean threshold before stage 1, or candle bodies closing outside the entry array (2026), means exit. Exit if there is no MSS. Cut the position if price stalls inside the entry array for too many candles.
Subjective parts to parameterise: consolidation definition, which OC, stage counting, displacement threshold, HTF PD array, and the regime check.
mm_models.changes_over_time:
1) Target changed over time. 2017: sell model target is about 20 pips beyond the original consolidation low (M27EOgtHhis 17:28, dIT4HTFYGGo 18:28). 2020 to 2022: return to the original consolidation (EAQmnxWun-c; hbE8S5FSdtQ says exit there and warns about holding beyond it). 2023: take about 80% off at the OC, then see if it can go deeper (iKsIbUblSWM 53:35). Jan 2024 Charter Models 6 and 7: buy-model terminus is the buyside liquidity above the OC high, plus 10/20/30 pips (fAcnhdaowME); sell-model grades are 10/20/30 pips below each new low (_7oZZ2bhEGU). 2026: he says outright that when he first taught it the sell model could go up, then down and clear the OC, but 'when it's bullish it will not do that' (JmAJfuSkY1g 20:20). The word 'terminus' is also used loosely in 2026 for a session high, a daily volume imbalance or a gap.
2) Entry style changed. 2017: OTE (62%, 70.5%, 79%) in the London kill zone, with the 'low-risk sell' as the retrace. 2020: SMR short, then a Low Risk Sell and further distribution. 2023: breaker retest, bearish OB with mean threshold. Jan 2024: no need to catch the SMR (BMYrtYMisnA). Aug 2024: inversion FVG plus order block with the 'second stage' (NMCy1H2_Wr8). 2026: IFVG consequent encroachment, SIBI, suspension block, Obsidian and Unicorn at second-stage redistribution, scaled in micro contracts.
3) Exit rules conflict: Model 7 says take the entire position off at the final objective (oheyS8MUqno), 2023 says 80% off at the OC then look deeper, and 2026 says pay yourself on every new low (VBgfJRMVCaI 10:29).
4) Kill zone hours change: London 1:00 to 5:00 AM NY (2017) versus 2:00 to 5:00 AM (2021) and a 6:00 AM pre-market scalp (2026).
5) Pyramiding limits (above equilibrium only) are stated for the sell side. The only buy-side pyramiding is the 2024-04-08 NQ example.
6) Source reliability. The Jan 2024 Charter dossiers (BMYrtYMisnA, beTnmkbuUjg, _7oZZ2bhEGU, fAcnhdaowME, 5FTMSC4kLZM, V0TFp7AvZqw, yC-gQhvexGg, oheyS8MUqno, G4lhid5dh0I) list 9 'chart walkthrough' trades with pip results and prices that are inconsistent between files (EURUSD at both 1.08 and 1.18 in the same fortnight). These look reconstructed, so I did not count them in trades_shown. The quotes in their Rules tables read like real transcript, so I used those. The hbE8S5FSdtQ (Month 07) dossier quotes are polished and its '120 pips' trade has no ticket, so treat it as lower confidence. Its timestamps are written as hh:mm:ss but look like mm:ss. JmcjMJQPFxs has no spoken-style rules table and its quotes look embellished, so I did not use it.
7) Count of 18 trades is distinct executions or recaps tagged MMSM/MMBM: 2017 (3), 2020 (2), 2021 (1), 2023 (4), 2024 (2) and 2026 (6). The 2026-06-02 'Early bird' video and its recap bqmqylAuLcI are counted once, and the 2026-08-17 UJU7MZzTSM4 and EC0UuarROyo are counted once. The 2025 NFP short (pM8oWrcIJqU) and the 2024-08-29 stage-two shorts (NMCy1H2_Wr8) mention the model but have no clean trade row, so they are not counted.
mm_models.markets: Forex: GBPUSD (4 trades: 2017-10-05, 2020-09-15, 2021-07-30, 2023-01-01), EURUSD (1, 2020-09-10), USDCAD (1, 2017-11-08) and USDCHF (1, 2017-10-27). Index futures: NQ/MNQ (9 trades, 2023-01-04, 2024-04-08, 2024-08-22 and 2026) and ES (2 trades, 2023-01). Of the 18 trades, 12 are MMSM shorts and 6 are MMBM longs. Teaching charts and analysis also use DXY, EURUSD and BTC (2017 lecture, where he says the cycle applies to crypto). Timeframes: 5m/15m in 2017, 1m for live executions from 2020 and in 2023-2026, 1h/4h for framing, and daily/weekly for swings (Charter Model 6.3). He says the model is fractal and works on every timeframe and asset class.

rules.rule: Call a buy model 'underway' when divergence has appeared at the lows and the daily sell stops have been cleared. This is the HTF backdrop for looking at the buy side of the curve.
rules.quote: the backdrop behind it is we've had smt diversions down here we've cleared out daily cell stops so we've accumulated we have a market maker buy model underway

rules.rule: Sell-model bias. After price has pressed higher every day of the week, expect a retracement back into the weekly range on the last day. This is the setup for a smart money reversal at the high of the week.
rules.quote: now we have pressed every single day higher now we're on the last day of the week the algorithm will likely trade back into the weekly range

rules.rule: Buy-model bias. Look for price moving from equilibrium into discount while at a higher-timeframe PD array, such as a weekly bullish order block.
rules.quote: we're at equilibrium to Discount and we're also at a PD array in the form of a weekly bullish order block

rules.rule: Cross-check the dollar index (DXY) while the market is consolidating, to judge whether the expansion on the pair is valid. This is a soft intermarket filter.
rules.quote: when we have markets that are in consolidation you have to weigh a lot of things and look at what the Dollar is doing

rules.rule: Stage 0 is the original consolidation, then a run out of it. The run out of the range is the manipulation leg that starts the model.
rules.quote: Primarily we're looking for some measure of consolidation initially and then a run out of that consolidation

rules.rule: Mark the original consolidation clearly, and use its high as the reference level for the model.
rules.quote: I want to use that as the high of the original consolidation

rules.rule: The 2017 sell-model sequence: consolidation, accumulation (buy-side curve), smart money reversal, low-risk sell, several redistribution stages, back down into the consolidation.
rules.quote: this is a consolidation price leaves consolidation accumulation smart money reversal low-risk sell redistribution another area redistribution another additional area of distribution and a sloppy one in here and we're back down into the consolidation

rules.rule: The 2026 buy-model sequence: consolidation, sell-off, return to the consolidation, smart money reversal, low-risk buy, accumulation, then a sharper second-stage re-accumulation run that takes out the original consolidation.
rules.quote: I think of this like consolidation, sell-off, return to consolidation, smart money reversal, low risk buy, accumulation, I'm looking for re-accumulation, second stage where the sharper, more pronounced price run higher that takes the original consolidation out

rules.rule: Smart money reversal for a sell model: price leaves a small consolidation, rallies, and creates the reversal high. Interbank shorts are placed there.
rules.quote: We have market in a small consolidation. It leaves the consolidation, rallies up, creates a Smart Money Reversal

rules.rule: Sequence for confirming a sell model in real time: consolidation, rally (all of it manipulation), break lower, then smart money reversal.
rules.quote: We should be in a sell model: consolidation, rally, all of this is manipulation, break lower, smart money reversal.

rules.rule: Smart money reversal defined as a sweep of a key liquidity pool inside a higher-timeframe PD array. This is a 2022 Month 07 dossier line whose phrasing is polished, so treat it as lower confidence.
rules.quote: The Smart Money Reversal occurs when price sweeps a key liquidity pool directly inside a higher timeframe PD array.

rules.rule: 2020 sell model: the first short is at the smart money reversal. The model then offers a Low Risk Sell and further distribution entries.
rules.quote: this is where interbank traders go short. You can take another short here for a Low Risk Sell, another level of distribution, another level of distribution, and then target the original consolidation.

rules.rule: 2023 sell-model entry: short the retest of a breaker. This is the first-stage distribution.
rules.quote: and you have a breaker trades up into it Go short that's your first stage distribution

rules.rule: Buy-model entry sequence: after the smart money reversal, take the low-risk buy at an order block, then re-engage on re-accumulation.
rules.quote: consolidation smart money reversal low risk buy right here trades into the order block then reaccumulation

rules.rule: Do not try to pick the exact reversal low or high. Enter on the low-risk retrace afterwards.
rules.quote: you do not have to try to catch the smart money reversal it's not necessary it's not important

rules.rule: In a buy model, buy only the buy side of the curve, after the reversal. Do not buy on the way down the sell side.
rules.quote: this is a market maker buy model so I want to be buying on the buy side of the curve

rules.rule: If the first re-accumulation stage has no fair value gap, wait for a later retracement that prints one and use that for the entry.
rules.quote: any retracement, we're going to be looking for a fair value gap

rules.rule: 2024 sell model: wait for the order block and the inversion fair value gap, and let the second stage form before committing.
rules.quote: you got to allow that second stage of the market maker sell model

rules.rule: 2026: the break lower into a second-stage redistribution is described as the largest, easiest and longest run of the model.
rules.quote: It breaks lower, it's a second stage redistribution of a market maker sell model. This is going to be the largest easiest price run in the longest magnitude.

rules.rule: 2017 sell-model stop is the high above the entry (swing high or SMR high). The first scaling point is the old low.
rules.quote: here's your entry optimal trade entry your risk is the high and your first scaling is the old low

rules.rule: Buy-model stop is placed below the smart money reversal low, with entry on re-accumulation after market structure confirms. This is a 2022 Month 07 dossier line whose phrasing is polished, so treat it as lower confidence.
rules.quote: You enter on the re-accumulation phase after market structure confirms the reversal, placing your protective stop below the SMR low.

rules.rule: 2017: the sell model targets the sell-side liquidity about 20 pips beyond the original consolidation low.
rules.quote: you have to look for an area to run below old lows you look at the original consolidation 20 pips below that

rules.rule: 2020: after the distribution stages, target the original consolidation.
rules.quote: another level of distribution, another level of distribution, and then target the original consolidation.

rules.rule: 2023: take about 80% off at the original consolidation, then see whether price can go deeper.
rules.quote: into original consolidation 80% of the trade would come off and I would see do we have the ability to get any deeper

rules.rule: 2024 buy model: the terminus is the buyside liquidity above the original consolidation high.
rules.quote: above the original consolidation which is the market maker buy model terminus

rules.rule: Buy-model target mandate: always the buyside liquidity resting above the original consolidation.
rules.quote: the target must always remain the buyside liquidity resting above the original consolidation

rules.rule: Terminus extension grades: objectives at +10, +20 and +30 pips beyond the original consolidation extreme.
rules.quote: that's our terminus plus 10, plus 20, plus 30 pips

rules.rule: Sell side (Model 7): on each new low, grade objectives 10, 20 and 30 pips below it.
rules.quote: every time we create a new low we do 10 20 30 pip grades below it to get our objective targets

rules.rule: 2026 sell model: after the stages, the big move clears the relative equal lows at the original consolidation, and he then targets his terminus objective.
rules.quote: Smart money reversal. Low risk sell. First stage distribution. Second stage redistribution. And then the biggest move takes place there. Clearing the relative equal lows at original consolidation and then just for extra measure targeting the terminus objective I had.

rules.rule: Sell side: add to the position only while price is above equilibrium of the range. Once price is below the midpoint, no more pyramiding.
rules.quote: you can add to your position as long as you are above equilibrium; once price drops below the midpoint of the range you cannot pyramid anymore

rules.rule: NQ buy-model example: a 1-contract partial limit at an intermediate high (18,339). This is an on-chart annotation, not speech.
rules.quote: Partial Target 1 Contract Comes Off Here

rules.rule: After the partial fills, trail the stop into profit (to 18,309.50). This is an on-chart annotation, not speech.
rules.quote: Risk Removed

rules.rule: 2026: scale off most contracts, then keep a few runners with the stop just below the consequent encroachment of the inversion fair value gap.
rules.quote: And then I would remain with four contracts long with a stop below consequent encroachment of this inversion fair value gap

rules.rule: If risk is split across several scaled-in orders, the total risk of all orders must equal the planned maximum.
rules.quote: if you're willing to risk 2% and you're going to be using four orders, each order must be sized so the total risk equals your 2% maximum

rules.rule: Exit rule from Model 7: when the final objective is tagged, take the whole position off.
rules.quote: when that final objective is tagged, take the entirety of the position off; don't get greedy looking for extra crumbs

rules.rule: 2026: if price stalls inside the entry array, manually take something off. Taking profits is never a mistake.
rules.quote: I teach that when you see that happen, it's better for you to just manually take something off. You don't go wrong. You don't make mistakes by taking profits.

rules.rule: 2026 MMSM fade: no candle bodies may close outside the suspension block. If they do, collapse the trade. This is a body-close invalidation, not a wick one.
rules.quote: But I don't want to see any bodies outside of it. If it looks like it's going to do that, I'll just collapse the trade

rules.rule: Regime caveat: in a bullish regime a sell model will not run through the original consolidation, so an original-consolidation target is not guaranteed.
rules.quote: When I first started teaching market maker models it can go up to go down and clear the original consolidation. But when it's bullish it will not do that.

rules.rule: Used on index futures, commodities and forex pairs, often on a 1-minute chart.
rules.quote: I've done many examples of this in index Futures in Commodities I've done it in Forex pairs

rules.rule: The profile is fractal and is not limited to daily or weekly charts. The same text goes on to say it applies on all time frames.
rules.quote: these profiles these Market maker buy models and sell models they're not limited to daily or weekly

rules.rule: Time is a quality filter, not part of the definition. Use windows with heavy volume and order flow, such as the London open.
rules.quote: using times of the day that have high intakes of volume where order flow is likely to be influenced

rules.rule: A smart money reversal is good when time and price agree. The wording is brief and partial.
rules.quote: when you have time and price in agreement

rules.rule: 2017 definition of the London kill zone: 1:00 to 5:00 AM New York time.
rules.quote: my kill zones encompassing the entire normalized kill zone which encompasses one o'clock in the morning New York time to 5:00 a.m. New York time that's my London kill zone and it's all reference to New York time

rules.rule: 2021 definition: the London kill zone is 2:00 to 5:00 AM and the New York kill zone is 7:00 to 10:00 AM, New York time. This differs from 2017.
rules.quote: london kill zone is two o'clock in the morning to five a.m new york is seven a.m to ten a.m

rules.rule: 2023 PM-session variant: a PM-session reversal that clears the original consolidation is run as smart money reversal, low-risk buy, buy model.
rules.quote: and I told you I would teach you a model: smart money reversal, low risk buy, market maker buy model that clears out the original consolidation.

rules.rule: 2026 pre-market variant: 6:00 AM New York is the earliest time he trusts the higher-probability runs for the sell-model scalp.
rules.quote: 6:00 a.m. is the earliest that the higher probability price runs can be trusted

first_presented_fvg.summary: Trade the first 1-minute fair value gap printed after a session open (NY 9:30 ET open, also the London 1:30-2:00 and 7:00-7:30 windows and the 2 PM FOMC release): enter when price returns to its 50% consequent encroachment while candle bodies respect it, and treat a body close through the CE as an inversion; the reflection FVG is the first opposite-type gap (SIBI) after a first presented BISI.
first_presented_fvg.needs_clock: Yes, heavily. The anchor is the clock: the 9:30 ET open (also 1:30 London, 7:00 NY pre-open, the 2 PM FOMC release), the first-30-minute window ('technically it's 29'), and the 9:31 minimum candle. He says 'time is the algorithm' (Zm9Q0NDRxoY, 18:23) and 'time is more important than price' (uC4-1SYXJFg, 00:24:00). The opening-range-gap context (4:14 PM settlement to 9:30 open) and the carry-over of yesterday's first presented FVG also need sessions and gaps. The price-only core (three-candle FVG, CE tap, bodies respecting CE, a body close through CE flipping it to an inversion FVG, balanced-price-range and overlapping-wick disqualification, a prior liquidity raid) is portable to 24/7 synthetic indices only by swapping in an arbitrary anchor, such as a fixed daily UTC time or the first displacement after a sweep. That substitute is not his model, he never tested it, and he explicitly declines to cosign synthetic markets (Z0VYZoaTIKE, 00:54). A generic 'first FVG after an anchor' detector runs on synthetics, but it would be a different, unvalidated strategy.
first_presented_fvg.how_to_code:
1) Anchor and window: T0 = 09:30:00 America/New_York on a 1-minute series (alternate windows he uses: 01:30 London, 07:00 pre-open, 14:00 FOMC). Valid window is [T0, T0+30m), and he says it is technically 29 minutes, so require the third candle to complete before 10:00. Subjective: exact cutoff and whether other windows count.
2) Detect the gap: scan consecutive candle triples (c1, c2, c3) with c1.time >= T0. Bullish (BISI): c3.low > c1.high, zone = [c1.high, c3.low]. Bearish (SIBI): c3.high < c1.low, zone = [c3.high, c1.low]. Wicks of c1 and c3 must not overlap (i3olkndPmEE). The earliest possible triple is 09:30/09:31/09:32, confirmed at the 09:32 close; the FPFVG is the earliest triple (by c3 close) that passes the filters. CE = (top + bottom) / 2.
3) Disqualify (y63zsrLCcCw): reject the gap if the zone lies inside the high/low range of the preceding candles that have already overlapped on both sides (balanced price range / overlapping wicks), meaning c2 does not break away. Subjective: lookback length, what counts as displacement (e.g. c2 body greater than k times ATR, or he picks the more protracted gap when several compete, PPCVZ2m3Dk8), and whether the 9:30 candle can itself be the first presented FVG (see conflicts).
4) Context filters (subjective, not mechanical in his teaching): a prior raid of liquidity (pre-market, Asia or London extreme, 9:30 high/low), direction aligned with the draw on liquidity, and no two-sided ambiguity (AxLXI00L8zM). In 2024 the discount/premium opening range gap (open versus 4:14 PM settlement, 70% reprice to its CE) was the bias.
5) Entry: after c3 closes, arm a limit order at the CE (or inside the zone). Trigger when price trades into the zone and tags CE. Confirm with bodies: for a bullish gap, bodies close at or above CE (wicks may pierce the low); for a bearish gap, bodies close at or below CE. He gives no fixed expiry; the 9:30-11:00 morning window is the nearest rule (uC4-1SYXJFg, 00:30:00).
6) Stop: no verbatim initial-stop rule. Trade-table cells show a stop beyond the structural swing or the 9:30 candle high, or just beyond the zone's far side (o38k6-twQCg 4.75 points; djabvhihIM8 17.5 points). Subjective. Management: after displacement or the first partial, move to cover cost (0BpG3Ee_kIc), trail to the FPFVG CE (Sbu7tn8r03w), or trail just beyond each newly formed FVG or the last candle low; near the target move the stop into profit.
7) Targets (subjective): opposing liquidity such as Asia or London extremes, equal highs/lows or prior-day extremes; the opening range gap CE as a partial and the NDOG/NWOG as the terminus (Ipjk9S8HTbA); the 9:30 opening price as a magnet.
8) Invalidation and flip: a candle body closing through CE into the far half (wicks excluded) cancels the original idea and marks the zone as an inversion FVG; trade its retest in the opposite direction as a separate model. Also invalid if a body closes beyond the far edge.
9) Reflection FVG (9W4YpyAg5RY, Sept 2026): only if the first presented FVG is bullish (BISI), label the first SIBI formed after it as the reflection; if the first was not a BISI the first SIBI has no significance. If the first body closes above the SIBI midpoint expect a return to the 9:30 open; bodies staying in its lower half is weak. Subjective: how much the macro-delivered (:50-:10) timing upgrades it.
first_presented_fvg.changes_over_time: Evolution: Jan 2024 (ISfgcRLImNY) calls it the 'first imbalance inside of the opening range' with no 'presented' label. The first 'first presented' hits are the Aug-Sep 2024 mentorship (Lectures 15-21, Sept 4): the first 1m FVG in 9:30-10:00, earliest on the 9:31 candle confirmed by the 9:32 close, wicks may exceed while bodies respect, a three-tier ladder (FVG, partial at opening-range-gap CE, NDOG terminus), and yesterday's FPFVG kept as a level. In that era it sits inside the discount/premium opening range gap and 70% CE-reprice framework, and he says you do not need a bias (yOZHawAE8QI); by 2025-26 it is framed as a raid, then the FPFVG, then a draw on liquidity or an inversion, and he refuses to trade when both sides can be argued (AxLXI00L8zM). Feb 2025 (Sbu7tn8r03w) names the window '9:31 and 10:00' for stop-to-CE management. 'Opening Range Theory' (Zm9Q0NDRxoY, dated 20250101 which looks like a placeholder date) generalises it to London 1:30-2:00 and a 7:00-7:30 window, with a suspension-block reading and a '90% of the time an inversion FVG' claim. Apr 2025 (y63zsrLCcCw) adds the balanced-price-range disqualification, which the 2024 dossier only paraphrases as an overlap rule. Conflict on the 9:30 candle: May 2025 'when 9:30 is the 1st presented FVG' and 'that opening price ... creates the 1st presented FVG' (uC4-1SYXJFg); Sept 2025 'first presented ... is a cibby not using 930. So this is the first one that formed' (8DWi2wLWv30); Nov 2025 the 9:31 candle is the minimum (yQM1Ut9V7mk); Jul 2026 'He can't use the 9:30 candlestick if there's a gap there like this' (e6XwTK4hVqI, the surrounding context is unclear); Sep 2026 the first gap forms at 9:33 (I7fIf1eEz0w). Sept 2025 (PPCVZ2m3Dk8) says to choose the more displaced gap when ambiguous, and Aug 2026 (iSWZOe3aUFE) says not every inefficiency is the FPFVG. Reflection FVG is the newest term (9W4YpyAg5RY, file dated 2026-09-08 while catalogue.csv says 20260101; the content refers to the Sept 2026 contract). Stop handling is inconsistent by situation: cover cost at the first expansion leg (0BpG3Ee_kIc), trail to FPFVG CE (Sbu7tn8r03w), trail beyond each new FVG (0BpG3Ee_kIc), or only move after price reaches a quadrant level (POUT0pVs4U0). Entry is variously 'limit order sitting in that fair value gap' (NMCy1H2_Wr8) versus 'wait for consequent encroachment to be tapped' (uC4-1SYXJFg). The same first-FVG idea also appears at lunch (C90xGr3kW8Y, the first FVG before a turtle-soup liquidity grab, carried to the next day) and as the 10:00 silver bullet (xbtW_0ipuos); those are related, not the same model. Data quality: several 2025-01-01 dates are placeholders, and the 2024-10 and 2026 'Uploads' dossiers carry only four short quotes each, so treat their trade outcomes as weak evidence.
