first_presented_fvg.markets: Every hands-on example is NQ (E-mini Nasdaq-100 futures; June, Sept and Dec contracts) on the 1-minute chart, plus MNQ in the March 2026 commentaries (AxLXI00L8zM, 54kzPj03Rkg). ES appears only as an SMT comparison in y63zsrLCcCw; I found no ES first-presented trade. Forex, metals and energies appear only as the 7:00-7:30 opening-range framing in Zm9Q0NDRxoY (22:20), with no FPFVG trade on them. Z0VYZoaTIKE (sibling Midnight Opening Range video) says it works in forex and futures but not crypto, and he will not cosign synthetic markets. Vo8WKYKtzIU says use futures, not CFDs. Trade count basis (21 rows where entry is on the session's own first presented / opening-range FVG or its reflection): Zm9Q0NDRxoY 1 (conceptual London short), uC4-1SYXJFg 1, o38k6-twQCg 1, POUT0pVs4U0 1, 0BpG3Ee_kIc 1, 7pW4-84U1RE 2 (reclaimed FPFVG short, 2 PM FOMC short), 7wL2oyebbvU 1 (Venom deferred entry), PPCVZ2m3Dk8 1, rXgEMIJ1fQg 1, djabvhihIM8 2 (one hypothetical walk-through), N4gTPOnZIYw 1, yQM1Ut9V7mk 1, Vo8WKYKtzIU 1, DnuCB5Stk-0 1, dt9mk4n5g_o 1, Rwao8f6oD0Q 1, NxwfXE6Zyns 1, Sbu7tn8r03w 1, 9W4YpyAg5RY 1 (reflection / SIBI short). Three more rows only use a prior day's FPFVG as a level or target (VBgfJRMVCaI, Khj1veL49r8 and -Qag-99u_BM which are the same trade, 9HUAUF_h2tI). Only a handful carry real prices (o38k6-twQCg sold 6 at 21,444.75 with stop 21,449.50; POUT0pVs4U0 peeled at 24,737.50; Sbu7tn8r03w; djabvhihIM8 long at 29,567.50 with stop 29,550.00; 9W4YpyAg5RY; 7pW4-84U1RE). Rows from Vo8WKYKtzIU, DnuCB5Stk-0, dt9mk4n5g_o, Rwao8f6oD0Q, NxwfXE6Zyns, N4gTPOnZIYw and yQM1Ut9V7mk look templated ('Win +25-40 handles') and are low confidence. No Rules table in o38k6-twQCg holds his words (they are bracketed descriptions of a silent trade), so none is quoted.

rules.rule: Use it when you have no directional bias: commit to the first half hour of the opening range, wait for the first FVG, and let the market digest the 9:45 or 10:00 news before leaning on it (2026-dated dossier).
rules.quote: submitting to the first half an hour of the opening range, looking for first fair value gap, looking for the market to consume 9:45 or 10:00 news

rules.rule: Earliest version (Jan 2024, before the name 'first presented'): the first imbalance (FVG) inside the 9:30-10:00 opening range is given huge importance; the same dossier line adds that price gravitates above and below it and reuses it for several trades.
rules.quote: That right there is your first imbalance inside of the opening range. Huge huge importance is placed on that

rules.rule: The model is anchored to the 9:30 ET open: the opening price creates both the opening range and the 1st presented FVG.
rules.quote: that opening price does two things: creates the opening range and the 1st presented FVG.

rules.rule: London application: the first FVG printed in the 1:30-2:00 AM NY-time macro is the one price is 'looking at' (he calls it his gift to the community).
rules.quote: The first presented fair value gap here during that 1:30 a.m. to 2 o'clock in the morning is my gift to the community because algorithmically this is what price is looking at

rules.rule: Second opening-range window: 7:00-7:30 AM NY time (New York open kill zone), framed across forex, metals, energies and indices.
rules.quote: 7:00 to 7:30 opening range for New York open kill zone encompassing forex, metals, energies, indices

rules.rule: NY equities window: the first fair value gap presented between 9:30 and 10:00 is the entry framework for the morning.
rules.quote: First present the fair value gap between 9:30 and 10:00 then using that as your entry framework.

rules.rule: The window is the first 30 minutes of the opening range; the same cell adds that technically it is 29 (minutes). My reading: the 3-candle gap has to be complete before 10:00.
rules.quote: The very first presented fair value gap during the opening range first 30 minutes

rules.rule: Earliest possible formation on 1m: the FVG sits on the 9:31 candle (middle candle) and only becomes a gap once the 9:32 candle closes and gives the structure.
rules.quote: you can create a fair value gap on the 931 candle if the 932 candle affords you the structure

rules.rule: Nov 2025 minimum criterion: you must see the 9:31 candlestick open (read with i3olkndPmEE, the 9:31 candle is the middle candle of the 3-candle pattern).
rules.quote: This right here 931, that's the minimum criteria for a first presented fair value gap. So you have to see that 931 candlestick open up.

rules.rule: The first gap can form later than 9:31: in this example it is the 9:33 candle's gap (formed 33 minutes after 9:00 ET) that is 'your first gap that forms'.
rules.quote: this is 9:33's first presented fair value gap. Okay? So, 33 minutes after 9:00 a.m. Eastern time, this is your first gap that forms.

rules.rule: Same logic reused at the 2:00 PM FOMC release: the first presented FVG after 2 p.m. is where price trades up into and then drops (shown as a short, FOMC stage one).
rules.quote: Price trades up into the first present fair value gap post 2 p.m.

rules.rule: Chart timeframe is the 1-minute chart (the 9:30 one-minute fair value gap).
rules.quote: learn by experience when he could use the 9:30 one minute fair value gap

rules.rule: He teaches it on the futures market because he says price delivery is pure there (NQ/MNQ in practice); the same video warns against CFDs and dealing-desk feeds.
rules.quote: You want to learn what it is I'm teaching with the Futures Market where price delivery is pure.

rules.rule: From the sibling Midnight Opening Range video (not FPFVG itself): the opening-range logic works in forex and futures but not crypto; the same cell says he will not cosign crypto or synthetic markets and has no experience with them.
rules.quote: It works obviously in Forex and it works in Futures, it works in every asset class with the exception of crypto.

rules.rule: Direction is not arbitrary: the first presented FVG after 9:30 is the one that points the same way as the draw (here sell side is the target).
rules.quote: What is that? It's the first presented fair value gap that formed after 9:30 and it's in the direction that the plot is sell side's going to be the target. It's going to be the draw

rules.rule: Bias gate: if you can make an equally good case for both sides there is no high-probability setup, so no risk is taken (day before FOMC).
rules.quote: If I can frame both sides, it's not high probability. If it's not high probability, I have no business putting on risk.

rules.rule: 2024 context: on a discount opening range gap (open below the 4:14 PM settlement) the first-FVG-to-mid-gap play is self-contained; he says you do not need a bias.
rules.quote: it matters not for a bias, you don't need a bias.

rules.rule: A first presented FVG matters when it has done a raid on liquidity first.
rules.quote: your first presented fair value gap because it's done a raid on [liquidity]

rules.rule: Opening-range pattern: after buy side is taken at the start of the 30-minute opening range, the imbalance is bearish, price rolls back over it and should stop at the CE with no bodies on the upside (the same cell says that 90% of the time this is an inversion FVG). Note the dossier spells CE as 'encouragement'.
rules.quote: Buy side's been taken. It starts the opening range of 30 minutes. It's an imbalance and price rolls back over top of it. It should stop at the consequent encouragement level and not leave any bodies on the upside

rules.rule: When several candidates exist, he picks the more protracted inefficiency with the most displacement in his direction as the first presented FVG.
rules.quote: I'm going to be more likely to pick a inefficiency that's much more protracted. In other words, it's done more of a displacement in my direction being lower

rules.rule: Reflection FVG: if the first presented FVG is a BISI, the very first SIBI that forms after it is the mirror-image 'reflection' (dossier transcribes BISI as 'busy').
rules.quote: But, the very first presented fair value gap, if it's a busy, I'm going to look for the very first sibi that forms after that. And that is a reflection. Why? Because if you look in the mirror

rules.rule: Quality upgrade: the reflection FVG is stronger when it is a macro-delivered inefficiency.
rules.quote: It also makes it stronger when it is a macro delivered inefficiency.

rules.rule: Carry-over (Aug 2024): the next open can tap the CE of yesterday's first presented FVG and pop from it; the dossier advises keeping the prior day's FPFVG on the chart.
rules.quote: notice the pop off of the consequent encroachment of that after just tapping it

rules.rule: Trigger: price trades into the first presented FVG and back out, and the test is where the candle bodies sit relative to the CE (here above it).
rules.quote: Trades into first presented fair value gap here, and then trades back down. But where are the bodies? Above consequent encroachment.

rules.rule: Trigger: price trades into the first presented FVG and the bodies respect the CE level, with a failure swing as the sign (shown as a short).
rules.quote: Trades down into first presented fair value gap right there. Look at the bodies respecting the consequent encroachment level. So we have like a failure swing to get below.

rules.rule: Body versus wick: wicks may poke outside the FVG, bodies are what must respect it.
rules.quote: wicks can come outside of that fair value gap, but the bodies tend to be more respectful.

rules.rule: Live read for the bearish case (MNQ, 9:32 FPFVG): no more bodies in the upper half of the first presented FVG, and check whether the CE was touched.
rules.quote: Stay out of the upper half. Don't put any more bodies in the upper half of that first presented fair value gap

rules.rule: Entry (Aug 2024): wait for the first FVG to form and rest a limit order inside it.
rules.quote: Wait for that first fair value gap to form and have your limit order sitting in that fair value gap

rules.rule: Entry timing (May 2025): after the raid, wait for the consequent encroachment (50%) of the FPFVG to be tapped before engaging.
rules.quote: you wait for consequent encroachment to be tapped.

rules.rule: Protective stop rule shown on a long: once price displaces away, the stop is raised to the CE (middle) of the first presented FVG formed 9:31-10:00 ET. No dossier gives a verbatim initial-stop rule; initial stops appear only in trade-table cells.
rules.quote: raise the stop up so now I have the stop at the middle or consequent encroachment of the first presentive fair value Gap that occurs between 9:31 and 10:00 always eastern time.

rules.rule: Target ladder (Sept 2024): FVG entry, partial at mid-gap (opening range gap CE), terminus at the new day opening gap.
rules.quote: We saw the fair value gap here to mid-gap, that's one setup that could be your model. You could go fair value gap, partial at mid-gap, terminus new day opening gap.

rules.rule: Target/magnet: an unreached 9:30 RTH opening price acts as a magnet once opposite liquidity is purged.
rules.quote: Notice that it failed to get to the 9:30 opening price. This is going to act as a magnet, folks.

rules.rule: Reflection if-then: bodies closing above the SIBI midpoint send price back to the 9:30 opening price.
rules.quote: If it were to close above that, then it's going to go back to 9:30 opening price. That was the if-then.

rules.rule: Management: once the first expansion leg shows displacement, move the stop to cover cost.
rules.quote: That's when I move my stop to cover cost. Because if it does rally from here, I'm absolutely [wrong].

rules.rule: Management: after a partial, trail the stop just beyond the newly formed FVG (above its high on a short), because a return into it means the move has failed.
rules.quote: And there's a partial again. and I lowered the stop right above the high of that fair value gap because if it's now going to trade back to it, it's going to go higher.

rules.rule: Management: wait until price trades below the quadrant level again before moving the stop to just above the swing high, and not before.
rules.quote: once this trades below this quadrant level again in that low, I'll move the stop loss to just above this swing high, but not before

rules.rule: Management: never let a trade that is near its target turn into a loser; pull the stop into profit.
rules.quote: I don't want to see a trade get close to my Target and then come back and put me into a losing trade that never should ever happen to any of you.

rules.rule: Management on the Sept 2026 long: the stop trails to the low of the latest candle while partials are booked.
rules.quote: So, we're going to say this the stop loss now trails to this candlesticks low

rules.rule: Disqualification test (Apr 2025): judge the gap by where it sits relative to the candles just before it.
rules.quote: Why is it not a valid first presented fair value gap? Because you need to look at where it is in proximity to the candles that formed just before it

rules.rule: A gap formed inside an existing balanced price range is not breaking away from anything, so it is not a valid first presented FVG.
rules.quote: So if there's a gap that would be formed inside here, that's not essentially breaking away from anything, is it? Because it's still inside of this balanced price range.

rules.rule: No genuine imbalance if the candle is only leaving a larger range that has been traded back and forth.
rules.quote: There's no imbalance here. All this is reflecting is it's leaving this [larger range that's been traded back and forth].

rules.rule: Failure mode: if bodies trade through the CE and lay inside the far half, the first presented FVG stops acting as support/resistance and flips to an inversion FVG.
rules.quote: If it's weak, it would trade through consequent encroachment of that and then lay bodies down inside this portion here. Once it does that, then this should act as inversion fair value gap.

rules.rule: Weakness sign for the reflection: no close above the SIBI midpoint and bodies staying in its lower half is extremely weak for an upside return, which supported the short.
rules.quote: But because it didn't do that, and the body stay in the lower half of this SIBI, that's extremely weak

rules.rule: Reflection filter: if the first presented FVG is not a BISI, the first SIBI after it has no significance.
rules.quote: Otherwise, your first sibi, if the first presented fair value gap is not a busy, there is no significance on the first sibi that forms

rules.rule: If the first-presented gap is blown through, it becomes an inversion FVG in the opposite direction.
rules.quote: If it blows through, then it becomes a bullish inversion fair value gap.

venom.summary: Venom is ICT's deferred entry on a Turtle Soup, framed on the 5m chart. A single candle sweeps a liquidity pool (Fang 1), the next candle displaces back away (Fang 2), and you enter at or below Fang 2's close with a tight stop. It is dropped if price returns to the BISI midpoint, and it is not valid in chop.
venom.needs_clock: No clock is needed for the model itself. Every rule he states (liquidity pool, single-candle sweep, SIBI then BISI displacement, entry at or below the second candle's close, stop at the sweep extreme or BISI CE) is a price-delivery rule, and none of the Venom quotes name a session, kill zone or time window. It could run on 24/7 synthetic indices on price alone. Three caveats. (a) The bias and macro-draw filter is the weakest, vaguest part and must be proxied with a higher-timeframe trend or liquidity target. (b) The chop filter ('several large range candles') has no numbers and must be defined, for example with ATR. (c) The only clock rule (no last hour on NFP weeks) and the observation that the May 12 consolidation spanned the lunch hour are context, not part of the model. His examples happened in the morning (Apr 3) and around lunch to afternoon (May 12).
venom.how_to_code:
Work on 5m bars (his stated frame; 1m is an optional execution timeframe). Bullish form below, mirror for bearish.

1. Context gate (subjective). The higher-timeframe bias is up with an unfilled draw above (an imbalance or buy stops). Chop filter: reject if the last N bars already contain several large-range candles (for example, 3 of the last 10 above 1.5x ATR). He gives no numbers.
2. Liquidity pool L (partly subjective). The nearest prior swing low or a cluster of near-equal lows. He never defines how established the pool must be.
3. Fang 1. Bar c1 is a down bar whose low is below L (a single-candle run through the pool), ideally with a bearish displacement body, which he calls a SIBI.
4. Fang 2. The next bar c2 is an up bar with displacement, a large bullish body, that closes back away from the low. He says a BISI must leave the SIBI. Because the entry is placed at c2's close, the BISI can only be approximated live, for example as c2's body or a three-candle FVG formed once c3 prints. The required strength (close above c1's open or high, body versus ATR) is not specified and is subjective.
5. Entry. When c2 closes, place a limit buy at c2.close or lower. Variants: Apr 30, a buy stop above c2's high or a limit at c2's open or lower; Apr 3, a retest of the sweep candle's open (the 'Venom order block') or the first FVG. Cancel the order if it is not filled within a few bars (not specified by him).
6. Stop. May 12 rule: c1.low minus a tick buffer. Apr 30 tighter rule: just below the 50% of the BISI gap. If price trades through the BISI midpoint, the pattern is void. Bearish Apr 3 trades put the stop above the sweep high.
7. Target (not quoted, so it is an assumption). The trade tables show the next higher-timeframe draw in the bias direction: a daily volume imbalance or wick CE, a daily SIBI or buy stops, or a daily discount CE. Code it as the nearest unfilled higher-timeframe imbalance or liquidity pool, or use a fixed R as a proxy.
8. Management. Trail the stop behind new intraday swing points (from the Jan 1 video's trades table and summary, not a quote). Close at the objective.

Subjective or unspecified parts: 'established' liquidity, 'inefficient' and 'displacement' thresholds, the chop filter, how strong Fang 2 must be, which candle's open or high is meant in the Apr 30 and Apr 3 entry quotes, and the whole bias/draw selection.
venom.changes_over_time:
The teaching changes over the 2025 videos and is not fully consistent.

1. Jan 1, 2025 (M6kCfe5QgDg) is a first preview, mostly about the one-model philosophy, with a vague definition and no entry or stop rules.
2. Apr 3, 2025 (7wL2oyebbvU) is the formal definition. It is a bearish example with Fang 1 up through buy stops and Fang 2 a close lower. Entry is the Venom order block (open of the sweep candle) or the first FVG, and there is a chop filter. The execution chart is 1m, and the dossier says an aggressive Turtle Soup entry at the sweep is also possible.
3. Apr 30, 2025 (mQsT-xux5Xk) is a long on the 1m chart. Entry is a buy stop above the candle high or a buy at the open or lower. The stop goes just below the BISI CE because Venom is a Balanced Price Range.
4. May 12, 2025 (FjSHAOI-Mok) is a long on the 5m chart. It is explicitly 'a deferred entry on a turtle soup'. Entry is at or below the second candle's close, the stop is the piercing candle's low, and SIBI then BISI are mandatory.

Conflicts:
- Timeframe. He says 'The Venom model is on the five-minute chart', but the Jan 1, Apr 3 execution and Apr 30 examples were on 1m.
- Stop. The BISI-CE stop on Apr 30 is tighter than the sweep-low stop on May 12, and the Apr 3 trade table (no quote) puts it above the sweep high.
- Entry reference. 'Opening price of the last candle' (Apr 3) versus 'at or below the second candle close' (May 12) versus 'this candlestick's open or less' (Apr 30). Which candle is meant is ambiguous because the transcripts are garbled, and the dossiers add their own interpretation.
- Fang definitions. The wording of Fang 1 and Fang 2 differs between videos (an up-through-buy-stops candle, a down candle with a SIBI, a stop run). The dossier summaries add claims ('closing back above the original liquidity pool', 'Fang 2 absorbs sell stops') that are not in the quoted statements.
- Strictness. The quote 'it's not a venom' appears in three forms (BISI CE revisited, no SIBI-then-BISI order, entry above the second close). These are separate invalidations, not one rule.
- Missing pieces. There is no quoted target rule and no time-of-day rule. The dossiers also record the 30 morning / 20 afternoon contract limits, which are sizing and not part of the model.
- Related videos. 5N4QHrY6DRc and r3E1WQcx2-c cover Turtle Soup deferred entries but never use the word venom or fangs, so they are not counted here.
venom.markets: NQ (Nasdaq-100 futures) only, in all four videos. 1) Jan 1, 2025 (M6kCfe5QgDg), 1m: illustrative short, entered on the retest into an imbalance after a liquidity sweep and displacement, stop trailed, stopped out in profit. This trade is labelled example only. 2) Apr 3, 2025 (7wL2oyebbvU), 1m execution after a 5m anatomy chart: short after a buy-stop sweep above relative equal highs, entry in the first FVG or Venom order block around 18,050, stop above the sweep high, target the daily discount CE near 17,745, win. 3) Apr 30, 2025 (mQsT-xux5Xk), 1m: long after a sell-stop run, stop just below the BISI CE, target the daily volume imbalance and wick CE, collapsed at target. 4) May 12, 2025 (FjSHAOI-Mok), 5m: long after a sellside sweep, stop below the sweep candle low, held through the lunch consolidation toward the daily SIBI and buy stops, win.

rules.rule: Use it as the deferred way to take a Turtle Soup (a liquidity run) long or short. You do not have to be in at the stop run itself; you wait for the market to give you the entry after the sweep.
rules.quote: It's just another form of using a deferred entry on a turtle soup long or turtle soup short. You don't have to be in there where the actual stop hunt is occurring.

rules.rule: Chop filter. Do not look for Venom inside a trading range that has already printed several large-range candles. No numeric threshold is given.
rules.quote: If you're trying to use this model when it's in the middle of a trading range and it's done had several large range candles up or down, Venom will not appear in that, it's not going to appear.

rules.rule: Take Venom in the direction of the bias he has already given. This is his only quoted bias statement and the transcript is garbled. The 7wL2oyebbvU overview says a macro directional draw is required, but that is not in a quote.
rules.quote: Venom focusing on the bias that I told [you].

rules.rule: Bullish form: a single candle runs below a sellside liquidity pool (swing low or equal lows). This is the Fang 1 sweep candle.
rules.quote: The criteria is we're going to be a single candle run below the sellside liquidity pool.

rules.rule: Bearish mirror: an inefficient run higher into buy stops (relative equal highs), then an inefficient run lower. The inefficient run is displacement that leaves an imbalance.
rules.quote: here is what confirms its venom: there has to be an inefficient run higher to it and then an inefficient run lower

rules.rule: Anatomy: two consecutive candles are the two fangs. Fang 1 injects into the resting stops, Fang 2 leaves the pool.
rules.quote: These two candles, they're the two fangs that make up that model I call venom. And they're injecting the venom into these sell stops. So, fang one, fang two, then leaves.

rules.rule: Structural confirmation, bullish form: a SIBI (down displacement) must come first, then a BISI (up displacement) leaves it. Without that order it is not Venom.
rules.quote: Drops down, injects the venom into sell stops here, accumulates those sell stops, and then breaks higher. You have to have a cibby first and then a bissy leaving it or it's not a venom.

rules.rule: Bearish form: the candle after the buy-stop sweep breaks down and closes lower. That second candle's close is the confirmation.
rules.quote: When it breaks down on the next candle here and closes here, you have it

rules.rule: The pair of candles, one poisoning the stops and one leaving quickly, is the signature. He calls it the telltale sign.
rules.quote: it poisoned them and then quickly left. So these are the two fangs, they're your telltale signs.

rules.rule: Entry is a limit taken at or below the close of the second candle (Fang 2). A fill above that close is not Venom.
rules.quote: You got to enter below the second candle closing price or it's not a venom.

rules.rule: Apr 30 variant, long side. Either a buy stop above the candle high, or a buy at that candle's open or lower for a tighter stop. The quote does not say which candle 'this candlestick' is.
rules.quote: You can do as a buy on a stop. So, a buy stop. This candlestick's high. You can buy it that way. Or if you're trying to keep a tighter stop-loss, you can be buying at this candlesticks open or less.

rules.rule: Apr 3 bearish deferred variant: wait for a return to the open of the last candle (the 'Venom order block', a change in the state of delivery), or take the first presented FVG. The transcript is garbled ('drill about'), and which candle's open is meant is the dossier's reading.
rules.quote: then you wait: you either take institutional order flow entry drill about this candlestick's highs or entry, or if it can afford you an entry back to the opening price of the last candle which is the Venom order block, that is your change in the state of delivery.

rules.rule: May 12 form: risk is the low of the piercing sweep candle (for a short, the high; the Apr 3 trade table shows the stop above the sweep high). Entry is at that second candle or lower.
rules.quote: This candlestick's low is risk and this candlestick or less is an entry for this Venom model.

rules.rule: Apr 30 tighter form: the stop goes just below the consequent encroachment (50%) of the BISI, because Venom is a balanced price range that should not be revisited.
rules.quote: Consequent encroachment of that stop loss has to be just below that. Why? Because this venom model is a balanced price range and it should not come back down here.

rules.rule: Trail the stop and accept being stopped out of a profitable trade. The trailing mechanic itself is only in the dossier summary and trades table, and the quote supports only the acceptance.
rules.quote: if it stops me out so be it because it was a profitable trade and there's the stop-loss getting tripped there's the executions.

rules.rule: He closed the Apr 30 trade ('collapsed' it) at the objective and was content. He gives no numeric target rule, only trade-table targets.
rules.quote: So, I just I just collapsed the trade there and was content with that.

rules.rule: While the trade runs, judge the move by candle bodies, because wicks only run stops. This is subjective, and the quote is about the bodies-and-wicks narrative after the entry, not an explicit exit rule.
rules.quote: Any wicks are just allowing the market to take individual that trail of stop losses up. They're allowed to do the damage. So, the bodies are telling the story.

rules.rule: If price comes back down to the BISI consequent encroachment, it is not a Venom and the trade is probably wrong, which is what the stop enforces.
rules.quote: If it does, it's not a venom and it's probably going to be a wrong trade

rules.rule: The model is framed on the 5-minute chart. The Apr 3 anatomy chart is 5m, but his Jan 1, Apr 3 execution and Apr 30 examples were on 1m. All four examples are NQ.
rules.quote: The Venom model is on the five-minute chart.

rules.rule: The only clock statement is a general NFP-week rule (no trading the last hour), made in the Venom review video. It is not part of the Venom definition and he gives no session window for the model.
rules.quote: We're in the last hour of trading. I don't like to trade the last hour trading on non-farm payroll weeks.

ifvg.summary: A fair value gap that fails to hold (a candle body closes through it) flips polarity into an Inversion FVG; he then trades the retest of its consequent encroachment or quadrant in the new direction, as long as candle bodies cannot get back into the far half ("Failure to Launch").
ifvg.needs_clock: The core pattern does not need a clock. It is pure price geometry: a three-candle gap, a body close through it, a retest of CE or a quadrant, and bodies unable to get back into the far half. He shows it in Asia, London, NY AM, lunch and PM on 15s to weekly charts, in FX, DXY, crude and index futures. A 24/7 synthetic index could run the core detection using only price delivery. The clock enters as optional confluence or targets: macro windows (10:50-11:10, 1:30 PM post-lunch, FOMC 2:43 PM, 3:15-3:45 PM, MOC 3:45-4:00 PM), the first presented FVG at 9:30-10:00, 08:30 news (Ma Deuce), and session-anchored levels (RTH opening range gap, NWOG/NDOG, 4:14 PM settlement). On a synthetic index you would lose those session draws and use swing highs and lows, equal highs and lows, and dealing-range CE and quadrants as liquidity targets.
ifvg.how_to_code:
1) Find FVGs. Bullish: low[i] > high[i-2], zone [high[i-2], low[i]]. Bearish: high[i] < low[i-2], zone [high[i], low[i-2]]. CE = midpoint. Quadrants at 25% and 75% of the zone.
2) Flip into an IFVG (bearish case shown; mirror it for bullish).
- Strict rule (2026): a candle CLOSE below the bullish gap's low. A wick through does not count. A close one tick beyond the edge is enough (EC0UuarROyo).
- Loose rule (Mar 2026): price trades through CE and candle bodies close in the lower half.
- Make strict vs loose a parameter. Older 2023-24 teaching only says 'trade through' or 'displace through', with no explicit close.
- Failure-to-launch variant: the FVG forms, price makes its first touch back into it, then closes beyond the far edge instead of rejecting. Flag that first touch as the failed first utilization.
3) After the flip, arm an IFVG state with zone, CE and quadrant levels, and a direction (short for a flipped bullish FVG).
4) Entry: wait for a retest back into the zone from the flip side. Entry level is CE (most common: Feb 2025, Jun 2026), the lower quadrant for a volume-imbalance IFVG (Jun 2026), or the gap edge (2023-24). Use a limit order at the level, or enter at the close of a rejection candle whose body closes back in the far half.
- Optional no-retest branch: if price cannot reach the zone low and rolls over, treat it as a weakness signal (Jan 2025). He did not take the IFVG retest there.
5) Stop: just beyond the far side of CE (stop in the half beyond CE, per Jan 2025), or beyond the whole zone or the swing high (trade tables). Subjective; choose one.
6) Invalidation:
- Strict (Oct 2024): price reaches CE at all.
- Normal (2025-26): any candle body closes beyond CE on the wrong side, with wicks allowed.
- Hard: a close beyond the far edge, which turns the zone into a 'reclaimed' FVG (the opposite polarity).
7) Targets: next opposing liquidity (relative equal lows or highs, a prior swing, or a sell-side pool). Partials just beyond the gap low, at a minor swing, and at dealing-range CE or quadrants. Optional 'event horizon' (50% between two pools). Trail the stop just beyond the IFVG once bodies have spent time beyond it, never retract it, and not before structure breaks (Oct 2025).
Subjective parts: what counts as 'displacement'; whether a liquidity sweep must come first (setup quality); HTF narrative, bias and SMT; which FVG to pick (first presented, nested or confluent with an OB, breaker, BPR, rejection block); which timeframe has the 'cleanest' inefficiency; skipping news and high-resistance chop.
ifvg.changes_over_time:
1) Retest depth tightened and relaxed. Oct 2024 (DnuCB5Stk-0) says an IFVG 'should never reach the halfway point'. Oct 2024 (akfEjsn4adk) says it is 'expected to stay in the lower half'. From 2025 wicks may reach or pass CE but bodies may not: Jan 2025 ('okay for these wicks to trade through it'), Sep 2025 ('It can wick in the upper half... cannot leave a body'), Sep 22 2025 ('can touch the midpoint. It's better that it doesn't'). Yet his Feb 2025 and Jun 2026 entries are AT the CE. So the strict 2024 version and the CE-entry practice sit awkwardly together.
2) The flip trigger became explicit. 2023-24 dossiers say only 'trade through it', 'push through' or 'displace through' (Jul 2023, Aug 2024). Mar 2026 gives the looser 'bodies close below that midpoint'. Jun 2026 says 'Inversion fair value gaps require the close' and a wick-through does not validate. Aug 2026 says a one-tick close is enough. The 2024-08-26 dossier mentions 15-minute displacement confirmation, but only as paraphrase, with no verbatim quote.
3) Vocabulary and variants. 'Ma Deuce' (Sep 2023) is the IFVG used to position before 08:30 news. 'Reaper' (Jul 2023) is an IFVG nested in a breaker, and a Jun 2026 variant nests it against an opposing FVG. 'Failure to Launch' as an IFVG label appears in Feb 2025. 'First utilization' as the failed-first-touch trigger appears in Jun-Jul 2026. In Jul 2026 'failure to launch' is also used for a failed long probe at the RTH opening range gap CE (no IFVG), then shorting the wick CE, so the phrase is wider than IFVG. 'Reclaimed FVG' (Dec 2023: wiped on both sides but still used) is different from an IFVG. In Mar and Apr 2026, price trading back through an IFVG makes it a reclaimed bullish FVG.
4) Stop trailing is the clearest apparent conflict. Oct 2025: 'Never, never, never' roll the stop under the IFVG until structure breaks. May 2024 (trail above the IFVG after displacement), Jun 2026 and Aug 2026 (raise the stop just beyond the IFVG once bodies hold) and Jul 2026 (delay the trail while the Fed talks) all treat the IFVG as a trailing anchor. They can be read as consistent only if the trail waits for structure or accumulated bodies. Aug 2026 also says to never retract a trailed stop.
5) Confluence evolved. IFVG alone, or nested with an order block, breaker, BPR (Oct 2023), reclaimed BISI, SIBI or the opening-range gap CE (Aug 2024), and in 2026 with wicks, volume imbalances and daily or weekly gaps.
6) Data caveats. The dossiers are LLM summaries of auto-captioned transcripts, and some words are garbled ('invers', 'guy' for gap, 'version of fair value gap' for inversion). Dossiers dated YYYY0101 (e.g. vuBRMFhFZAY, Zm9Q0NDRxoY, hc9SDgW93gc) carry placeholder dates, so the chronology above is approximate. For x_44mMI7YqU the IFVG is a weakness signal and the executed trade is a Silver Bullet FVG, not an IFVG retest. The iLe_4m84_yw and UQJW9obxt34 dossiers describe the IFVG as an 'impeding barrier' and as a daily SIBI that keeps bias, with no trade.
ifvg.markets: NQ and MNQ are the large majority, mostly on the 1m chart (also 15s/30s, 2m, 5m and 15m, and 1h/daily/weekly for the higher-timeframe IFVGs). ES and MES appear in Aug 2023 (15s), Jan 2024, May 2026 and Aug 2026 (15s). FX appears as GBPUSD (Jan 2025, demo/paper account, 5m to 1m) and EURUSD (Sep 2025 5m, Nov 2025 1h swing). DXY appears on daily and weekly IFVGs and a few daily long trades in Jun 2026. Crude (CL) appears in May 2026. Gold and Silver appear only as daily IFVG commentary (Mar 2026). The 67 trades are distinct trade rows (duplicates across companion videos merged, e.g. 2023-09-01 NFP, 2026-06-02/03, 2026-08-18, 2026-08-28, 2026-09-28) where the named entry or setup is an IFVG. That is about 6 in 2023, 12 in 2024, 17 in 2025 and 32 in 2026. About 8 more rows only use the IFVG as a target, context or stop reference, so they are not counted. Among the eight starter videos: vuBRMFhFZAY has 1 (ES 15s live long), 1PkTGkOjoGo has 1 (NQ Ma Deuce short), JfX77zCR_NM has 1 (NQ failure-to-launch short), 8wHewi6N6dg has 1 (NQ long), EC0UuarROyo has 1 (NQ short in an MMSM with IFVG), x_44mMI7YqU has 1 (GBPUSD short, entered as a Silver Bullet FVG after an IFVG failure), and iLe_4m84_yw and UQJW9obxt34 have 0. Nearly all shown trades are wins, so there is no usable loss data. The dossiers also look partly templated: the Sep-Oct 2024 rows give uniform '+20-70 handles' results. The counts are dossier table rows, not independently verified executions.

rules.rule: 2026 wording: an FVG that does not get its first utilization (no clean reaction on first touch) is treated as an inversion FVG rather than a support/resistance FVG.
rules.quote: it did not get to utilize its first utilization, meaning this should operate under the mode of inversion fair value gap.

rules.rule: First-utilization test: an FVG in a bearish context must send price lower; if price blows through it, it becomes a bullish inversion FVG, and the reverse for a bullish context.
rules.quote: That means if it's bearish, it should send price lower. If it blows through, then it becomes a bullish inversion fair value gap.

rules.rule: 2023 'Ma Deuce' use: position inside an IFVG ahead of a scheduled 08:30 news release. The quote only says an 8:30 delivery is expected. The dossier's 'only when bias is aligned' is its own gloss, not his words.
rules.quote: we're expecting an 8:30 delivery we can get in here and use this and get ahead of yes get ahead of and enter before the news it's like an x-ray view

rules.rule: Directional bias stays with the IFVG side until price trades through the gap. A bullish stance needs the bearish gap traded through and treated as an IFVG; until then he is not bullish.
rules.quote: If it trades through that volume imbalance, then treat that as inversion fair value gap for me to be bullish. Until it does that, it's not bullish.

rules.rule: Higher-timeframe (daily) imbalance acts as an IFVG and keeps the bearish stance. If price violates it, it becomes a reclaimed bullish FVG and the stance changes.
rules.quote: If this gets violated, then I would expect this to become a reclaimed bullish fair value gap. But until it does that, it's utilized in the function of inversion fair value gap.

rules.rule: After a liquidity pool is taken (for example the Tuesday high at FOMC), go back to the inefficiency that formed before the sweep. It becomes the IFVG for the reversal.
rules.quote: And then once it took out this high, we want to go back in and look at any inefficiency that formed prior to that because it's going to act as an inversion fair value gap

rules.rule: When buy-side liquidity has been taken, the opening-range (30-minute) imbalance is usually a bearish IFVG, which he claims about 90% of the time.
rules.quote: 90% of the time that's going to be an inversion fair value gap. That's bearish. Why? Buy side's been taken.

rules.rule: Failure to launch: a gap that was supposed to launch price breaks down below it. Its consequent encroachment (CE) then becomes a barrier on any retest.
rules.quote: it breaks down below it then it means the consequent encroachment should be a what a barrier to it

rules.rule: Definition (2024): a bullish FVG that price trades below stops being bullish and becomes an IFVG. On later pullbacks into it, price is expected to stay in its lower half.
rules.quote: it no longer is going to act as a bullish fair value Gap it will become an inversion fair value Gap expected to stay in the lower half of that fair value Gap.

rules.rule: Loose validation (2026): price trades through the gap's CE and lays candle bodies in the far half. That flips it to an IFVG.
rules.quote: If it's weak, it would trade through consequent encroachment of that and then lay bodies down inside this portion here. Once it does that, then this should act as inversion fair value gap.

rules.rule: Strict validation (2026): a candle CLOSE outside the gap is required. A wick through it does not validate. (He adds that an order block does not need a close.)
rules.quote: We have a candlestick close outside of this buy side imbalance sell side inefficiency which validates this becoming an inversion fair value gap.

rules.rule: Aug 2026: a close just one tick beyond the gap boundary is enough to qualify it as an IFVG. The quote is garbled by transcription, so the exact price levels are unclear.
rules.quote: This candlesticks high 54. So it's one tick below. So it validates this as an inversion fair gap.

rules.rule: Entry on the retest of the flipped gap, in the new direction. For a failure to launch, that means shorting the CE retest from below.
rules.quote: it's Failure to Launch off of this inversion fair value Gap there's where your entry you can go short there.

rules.rule: Fill the short at the IFVG's CE, with the narrative already pointing lower (here an SMT divergence after a new all-time high).
rules.quote: the fill on the short is right at the consequent encroachment of the inversion fair value gap within the context and narrative of looking for lower prices because of SMT because we traded above Monday's old all-time high again.

rules.rule: After the break lower, wait for price to come back up into the midway point (CE) of the inverted gap. That retest is the short.
rules.quote: We break lower, come back up into midway consequent encroachment of this gap.

rules.rule: Re-entry: once the IFVG is validated, if price later trades back out below the gap low, the first FVG or first touch of that is a second entry.
rules.quote: If it ever trades back out below the low again, the very first fair value gap or touch of that is a wonderful little entry.

rules.rule: Bullish mirror: buy the retest down into the IFVG's CE and upper quadrant, using the open of the candle (order block) as the precise level.
rules.quote: This was beautifully handled with price coming down into consequent encroachment, upper quadrant, and then we use the open of that candlestick there, and then it really ripped and roared

rules.rule: 2023 live 15-second ES long: add inside an order block that sits inside an already-identified IFVG, which he calls dynamic support.
rules.quote: That entire range is the order block, and I'm adding into it here inside the fair value gap that is already identified as an inversion fair value gap.

rules.rule: No-retest variant: if price rallies back but cannot even touch the IFVG low and rolls over, he reads that as extreme weakness. In this video he took a 1m Silver Bullet FVG short rather than waiting for an IFVG retest.
rules.quote: Breaks aggressively lower, comes back up, fails to touch the low of that and then goes lower. That is another indicator, it's a signature telling you that it's now weak, it can't even get up to the inversion fair value gap.

rules.rule: Long: stop sits in the lower half of the IFVG, beneath its CE. The retest should hold above CE.
rules.quote: I want to see it stay above the consequent encroachment or midpoint of that, and notice my stop loss is in the lower half of that inversion fair value gap in orange.

rules.rule: Aug 2026: the initial stop starts right at the IFVG's CE. The wording is garbled, but the trade row shows a long with the stop under the IFVG CE.
rules.quote: it's basically consequent encroachment is the top of that inversion fair value gap. So the stop loss has to start and open up on a trade just right at that

rules.rule: Target is the next opposing liquidity: relative equal lows, then the sell-side liquidity pool, when shorting from an IFVG.
rules.quote: So if it get below that, this could act as an inversion fair value gap to dig into these relative equal lows. And then the sell side liquidity pool and inefficiency.

rules.rule: First partial is taken just beyond the low of the gap the price is running through.
rules.quote: sells off and goes right below the low where I'll take the first partial.

rules.rule: Partials are placed at liquidity, not at arbitrary R multiples.
rules.quote: Everything that I've outlined here is shown to you on a time-based chart. My partials are based on liquidity.

rules.rule: Ma Deuce (2023) staging: first partial at the CE of the dealing range, then the lower quadrant, then the next discount array.
rules.quote: first partial would be here at consequent encroachment and you let it run some more to get down to the lower quadrant

rules.rule: If liquidity such as relative equal highs is still untaken against the trade, take heavy partials early. Remainder trails.
rules.quote: initially I took more off in the beginning of the trade because I wasn't comfortable holding the the risk that was on the trade because I was put off by not seeing these relative equal highs taken.

rules.rule: Once the trade works, raise the stop to just beyond the IFVG (underneath for a long). If price goes back there he does not want to be in the trade.
rules.quote: Raise the stop up just underneath this inversion fair value gap now, cuz if it goes there, I don't want to be a part of this anymore.

rules.rule: Oct 2025 caution: do not roll the stop under the IFVG until structure has broken. The stop belongs below the intermediate-term low.
rules.quote: if you're long and you rolled your stop loss just below the inversion fair value gap: Never, never, never do that until it breaks structure and leaving it

rules.rule: Aug 2026: trail the stop to just beyond the IFVG once candle bodies have spent time with it as support or resistance. The transcript says 'guy' where he means 'gap'.
rules.quote: Bring the stop up again. Now the stop here is below the inversion fair value, guy, because we've spent a lot of time with the bodies in there

rules.rule: Confirmation: after the body closes inside the far half of the IFVG, the next candle should give immediate feedback that you are on side.
rules.quote: There's a big big piece of information right there. The next candle should give you immediate feedback that you're on side.

rules.rule: During central-bank speeches, delay trailing the stop down to the IFVG low until a body has closed beyond it.
rules.quote: Until we get below this with a body, I don't want to lower the stop loss down to the low of that inversion fair value gap yet cuz it could just real quick cuz the Fed's talking right now.

rules.rule: Oct 2024 strict version: a valid IFVG should not even reach the halfway point of the gap. It defends the boundary, and deep penetration means the trade is wrong.
rules.quote: Inversion fair value Gap it should never reach the halfway point but defend the boundary.

rules.rule: Jan 2025 version: bodies must stay in the lower half or at CE (for a bearish IFVG). Wicks may trade through; bodies carry the narrative.
rules.quote: And the bodies should stay in the lower half or at the consequent encroachment

rules.rule: Sep 2025 version: a wick into the far half is allowed, but a candle body left on the wrong side of CE kills the IFVG premise.
rules.quote: You want to stay in the lower half of that rectangle. It can wick in the upper half, but it cannot leave a body outside of the upper half of it to the upside in other words.

rules.rule: Bullish mirror: once price displaces away from the IFVG, it must not come back down through it.
rules.quote: once it did and once it leaves the invers fair value Gap it should not come back down

rules.rule: Price trading back up into and above the IFVG means the bearish read is wrong.
rules.quote: if we got into that and above it, that would change and I would be wrong.

rules.rule: Higher-timeframe invalidation: a daily IFVG's CE is the line for the bias. Trade below it and the bullish dollar view is off.
rules.quote: I was bullish on dollar unless we were to trade below the daily consequent encroachment of this inversion fair value gap

rules.rule: Bullish mirror (Jun 2026): wicks below CE are allowed, but a body below it is not.
rules.quote: It can wick down below it. We don't want to see it leave a body down there.

rules.rule: Execution timeframe is flexible: use whichever of the 1 to 5 minute charts shows the cleanest inefficiency.
rules.quote: timing is based on either a 5 minute 4 minute 3 minute 2 minute or one minute chart whichever one has the cleanest inefficiency that you can work with

rules.rule: Work top-down from the daily chart. A one-minute IFVG with no daily support is not enough to carry size.
rules.quote: working with the hierarchy of working from daily chart down to the smaller time frames. Not just looking at a smaller one minute chart and saying I'm going to figure it all out on a one minute time frame.

rules.rule: 15-second ES example: after a break lower, a volume imbalance forms. The retest wicks through the IFVG but candle bodies cannot touch its CE.
rules.quote: Breaks lower, we create a little volume imbalance in here, comes back up in. The bodies can't touch consequent encroachment of this inversion fair value gap, but it does wick through a little bit.

rules.rule: The same logic is applied to weekly and daily IFVGs on DXY and FX.
rules.quote: Beautiful consequent encroachment of that weekly inversion fair value gap.

rules.rule: The pattern itself is not time-bound, but he calls it loaded when it lines up with a session open, the first 30 minutes of the opening range, or a macro window.
rules.quote: anchored if it's time for it to move it's at a session open. It's during the first 30 minutes of the opening range or it is inside of a macro time. Man, you have a loaded deal

rules.rule: Example of a time-specific use: a post-lunch 1:30 PM Eastern retest into a gap that has become an IFVG, followed by a dive.
rules.quote: Now, post New York lunch, again, same thing here. Here is 1:30 Eastern time. And what is it doing? It's trading right up into that gap that becomes inversion fair value gap. And then it dives right down

rules.rule: 2023 teaching: on news-heavy days skip the morning chop and wait through lunch for the cleanest PM setup. His live 15-second IFVG trade came after that.
rules.quote: Just wait through lunch! If you do that, you will get the cleanest setup of the day.

reaper.summary: Reaper FVG / Reaper PD array: an Inversion FVG (IFVG) nested with another FVG of the opposite polarity. In 2023 the host zone was a breaker's impulsive leg, in the discount for longs or the premium for shorts. In 2026 the pairing is IFVG plus an opposing FVG. Entry is a retest of the IFVG's near-side quadrant, with the HTF bias and its volume imbalance as the draw.
reaper.needs_clock: No time-of-day rule is stated anywhere for the Reaper. Both live trades were in the NY session (the dossiers say NY / NY AM), but no quote ties the model to a clock. The logic is price delivery only: FVGs, IFVGs, a breaker or opposing FVG, discount/premium, body closes, and a volume-imbalance target. It could run on 24/7 synthetic indices if you substitute your own HTF candle boundaries for the 'Daily' and 'hourly' references. Two caveats: the 'volume imbalance' (the gap between one candle's close and the next candle's open) may be tiny or absent on synthetic feeds, and 'session low', 'NWOG' and similar session-anchored references have no equivalent and would need replacing with fixed-window highs and lows.
reaper.how_to_code:
The dossiers describe the Reaper in prose and give no numeric rules, so parts of the detection below are inferred.

1. Bias (subjective): set a direction from HTF context. In the 2026 long this was a daily volume imbalance sitting above price after a sell-off. The draw is a nearby unfilled HTF volume imbalance or liquidity pool in the trade direction.

2. Primitives (objective):
- FVG on the execution TF (1m in all shown trades): bullish if high[i-2] < low[i], bearish if low[i-2] > high[i].
- Volume imbalance: open[i] differs from close[i-1] with the bodies not overlapping. His example is a close of 905.0 and an open of 905.5.
- IFVG: a candle body closes fully through an FVG or volume imbalance, which flips its polarity. A sliced bullish FVG becomes a bearish IFVG (resistance); a sliced bearish FVG becomes a bullish IFVG (support). A 'close through' by body is the likely test; the wick-only case is not stated.
- Midpoint (CE) = (top+bottom)/2. Quadrants are 25% bands of the zone.

3. Reaper (2023 form): find an impulsive leg that breaks structure (MSS, a swing sequence break) and its breaker. The breaker is the last opposite-colour candle or order block that failed, created after a sweep of a high or low. Then require a bullish-context IFVG whose zone lies in the discount half (below 50%) of that impulsive leg's range. For shorts, the IFVG lies in the premium half. This needs swing and leg detection and is the most subjective part.

4. Reaper variant (2026 form): require an IFVG and an FVG of the opposite polarity overlapping or adjacent in the same price region (the 'nested' pair). The IFVG is the one that was inverted; the FVG is the 'first utilization'. For shorts, price should rally back into the IFVG from below.

5. Trigger (objective once the zone exists): after price retraces into the IFVG, the candle body closes inside the near half of the IFVG and outside the paired FVG. For shorts that is the lower half; for longs, the upper half by symmetry (not stated). The following candle must confirm: for a short, close below the trigger candle's low; for a long, close above its high. 'Immediate feedback' has no numeric definition.

6. Entry: at or on the retest of the IFVG's near quadrant, around the CE. The trigger body close is the filter, with execution on the 1m.

7. Stop: beyond the zone or the short-term swing extreme (the short row says 'above short-term swing high'; no long initial stop is quoted). Trailing rule: once price takes out the previous candle's high, move the stop to the low of the HTF imbalance.

8. Target: the HTF volume imbalance (the low or CE of it for longs), or sell-side liquidity or the session low for shorts. Scale partials and leave runners for the final level.

9. Invalidation and filters: a close through the IFVG's CE or far side (inferred, not quoted). Price returns to the target imbalance too fast (less bullish, soft). Too many candles pass with no progress (N not given; treat as a tunable parameter).

Subjective or unspecified: bias, breaker identification, 'impulsive leg', 'nested', 'opposing', 'immediate feedback', the stagnation count, and the initial stop distance.
reaper.changes_over_time:
Only three dossiers mention the Reaper, spanning almost three years, with nothing in between: cgsltOB736E (2023-07-19), kzeFqGK9gCQ (2026-06-08) and 18vX-vv2bsg (2026-06-10).

1) 2023 definition: the Reaper is an Inversion FVG nested inside a Breaker Block, in the discount of a bullish breaker's impulsive leg (premium for a bearish one). It is a purely conceptual unveiling, with no trades. Emphasis is on bias, the CE of the Reaper as a defended level, and rebutting the 'Three Indians' and supply/demand comparisons.

2) 2026-06-08 (the dossier calls it 'ICT Reaper FVG'): the dossier describes a bullish FVG plus a bullish IFVG below relative equal lows, after a sweep, into a Daily volume imbalance. There is no breaker and no discount/premium-of-leg condition in the dossier. The execution is 20 contracts on the 1m, with a stop trailed to the low of the daily VI and partials scaled.

3) 2026-06-10: he calls it 'a variant of a reaper': an IFVG nested with an opposing FVG, on the 1m, with an hourly IFVG as context. This is the first source that states the opposing-FVG form ('both sides of the equation'), and again there is no breaker.

Net change: the breaker-block host is no longer mentioned in the 2026 videos. The model is now defined by two nested gaps of opposite polarity plus an HTF imbalance draw, and the lecture-style CE defense rule gives way to execution detail (lower-half body close, next-candle confirmation, trailing to the HTF imbalance low).

Possible conflict: whether the 2026 trades are the same 'Reaper' or a different variant is unclear, because he says 'variant' only once. The dossiers are summaries, so an omitted breaker could just be an omission. The quote in the 2023 file is a spliced fragment with '...' markers; only the contiguous segments were used. No timestamp-bound entry price or numeric stop distance is quoted for either trade. The dossier trade rows (not quotes) supply the entry and stop descriptions.
reaper.markets: NQ (E-mini Nasdaq-100 futures) only. The 2023 lecture is on NQ at 15m/5m/1m, with no trades. The 2026-06-08 long is NQ on the 1m, with a Daily volume imbalance as the objective. The 2026-06-09/10 short is NQ on the 1m, with an hourly IFVG as context. The only other instrument in those videos is CL (crude oil), and it is analysis, not a Reaper.

rules.rule: Purpose of the Reaper: a precision method to exploit a shifted sentiment, deliberately different from retail S/R or 'Three Indians' patterns.
rules.quote: I wanted to create and codify a method to go in and capitalize on precision, take advantage of shifted sentiment and go under the radar of everybody else out there.

rules.rule: A Reaper is only taken with a directional bias; the same structure is mirrored for longs and shorts.
rules.quote: So all of these things are completely reversible, but the context is you have to have a bias.

rules.rule: 2026 long: the HTF draw is a daily volume imbalance above price, with the trade aimed up into it. This quote is the bias or draw; the daily VI as the exit is covered under target.
rules.quote: This dipped down in here. This is that daily volume imbalance I said we would likely trade up into

rules.rule: 2023 definition: the Reaper is an Inversion FVG sitting in the discount half of the impulsive leg of a bullish breaker. Bearish version: the IFVG sits in the premium half of the impulsive leg of a bearish breaker.
rules.quote: A Reaper is a fair value gap in a discount of the impulsive price leg of a bullish breaker. Reverse it: a bearish ICT Reaper Inversion Fair Value Gap would be a bearish breaker that would have a fair value gap in the premium side of the impulsive price leg.

rules.rule: The CE (50%) of the Reaper is the level that validates a support/resistance zone. An S/R level without an FVG is not confirmed.
rules.quote: Classic support resistance is only confirmed if it has one of my fair value gaps, and look what it has right there: consequent encroachment of that Reaper.

rules.rule: 2026 variant (no breaker mentioned): an IFVG is nested with a second FVG of the opposite polarity, 'both sides of the equation'. In a bearish context the IFVG is treated as the inversion zone and the other FVG opposes it.
rules.quote: nested first utilization and then the other fair value gap will oppose that. So you're getting both sides of the equation here buy side imbalance sell side inefficiency when we're bearish it should treat it as inversion fair value gap

rules.rule: An IFVG is created when price slices through a volume imbalance (gap between one candle's close and the next candle's open) or an FVG; the sliced zone is then treated as an inversion FVG. His example is an hourly volume imbalance.
rules.quote: We slice through it here. We treat it as what? Inversion fair value gap

rules.rule: Trigger candle (short): after the retest, the candle body closes inside the lower half of the IFVG and outside the opposing bearish FVG.
rules.quote: where does the body close? It closes inside the lower half of the inversion fair value gap and outside of this bearish fair value gap.

rules.rule: Entry is on the retest of the IFVG, in its lower quadrant for the short. The dossier trade row says 'lower quadrant of hourly IFVG / 1m FVG retest', entry on the 1m. For the long, the dossier trade row gives a sweep of relative equal lows and a bullish FVG plus bullish IFVG as the entry area, but no quote states the long entry.
rules.quote: touching right here, the lower quadrant of it.

rules.rule: The long's stop is trailed up in steps. After price clears a candle's high he moves the stop to the low of the daily volume imbalance. No quote states the initial stop; the dossier's short trade row says 'above short-term swing high'.
rules.quote: let's see if we get any kind of discount sensitivity off of that to the upside, clear this candlestick's high. If it does, then I'm going to run the stop loss right to the low of the daily volume imbalance.

rules.rule: Long target: the low of the daily volume imbalance, with its CE near 29,560 on NQ. He scales out partials of a 20-lot and leaves the last runners to be stopped at that level. Short target (dossier trade row only, no quote): sell-side liquidity and the session low.
rules.quote: with a stop loss that would get me out at the low of the daily volume imbalance. So, that's not a bad target for being forced out of the final two contracts of a 20 lot

rules.rule: The next candle after the trigger should confirm the trade immediately. If it does not, the setup is suspect.
rules.quote: The next candle should give you immediate feedback that you're on side.

rules.rule: Protect open profit: don't let a winner turn into a loss, and lock it by moving the stop, scaling partials and exiting the final runners.
rules.quote: Now, we don't want to see it go to a loss. We don't want to see this fill back in

rules.rule: Soft warning: if price rushes straight back to the imbalance it targets, the long is less bullish. This is a quality filter, not a hard invalidation level.
rules.quote: I don't want to see it come back immediately for that volume imbalance. I I don't want to see that because if it's in a hurry to get back to that inefficiency, that's kind of a little less bullish.

rules.rule: Stagnation or time-stop: if the trade spends too many candles without progress, it has to start running or it is failing. The number of candles is not given.
rules.quote: It's already spent too many candles without going higher, so it needs to start running higher.

osok.summary: One Shot One Kill (OSOK) is ICT's once-a-week swing model. He reads the higher-timeframe draw, waits for a Monday-to-Wednesday manipulation of the weekly high or low (a Judas swing from the weekly open into a premium or discount PD array), and takes one entry from an internal-range FVG, OB or OTE. He targets external range liquidity (50 to 100+ pips on forex), manages the trade, and is done for the week.
osok.needs_clock: Partly. Day-of-week and session timing is part of the forex weekly-profile version. That includes the weekly open as reference price, the Monday or Tuesday London manipulation, Wednesday and Thursday expansion, Friday settlement, and the 70%-Tuesday statistic. The 2020 killzone teaching and the 2026 lunch-macro window (11:30 to 13:30 NY, setup usually in the first hour) also need a clock. The structural core uses price delivery only and could run on 24/7 synthetic indices if you define a synthetic period (N bars) and use its open as the reference. That core is: a higher-timeframe draw, a counter-bias run past the period open into a premium or discount array that sweeps liquidity, displacement with an FVG or OB, an internal-range entry, and an external liquidity target. The Tuesday and London filters, DXY SMT confirmation and news context would not carry over. The weekly structure would then be a bar-count convention, not a documented ICT rule.
osok.how_to_code:
Weekly-profile OSOK, short side shown (mirror for longs). Items marked [S] are subjective in his teaching.
1. Reference levels. Record the weekly open (Sunday 18:00 NY, or Monday 00:00). Maintain the daily and weekly swing highs and lows, unmitigated daily and weekly FVGs, and old highs and lows such as the 20-week one in Model 9.
2. Bias. Pick the draw on liquidity: the nearest untested external low or unmitigated daily FVG or discount pool, with price in premium of the higher-timeframe dealing range (above 50%). Bias is the direction of that draw. [S] Which draw he picks is discretionary. Code it as nearest unswept pool plus premium/discount.
3. Manipulation window. From Monday through Wednesday (Monday or Tuesday London in 2022, Tuesday or Wednesday in Model 2, Monday to Wednesday in Model 9), look for price to trade above the weekly open into a premium PD array (daily or 4h bearish OB or FVG) and sweep a prior swing high or equal highs (Judas swing or Turtle Soup). Monday is optional because Tuesday is the extreme about 70% of the time. [S] Which Judas swing is the real one is only known in hindsight, so use the first sweep that meets step 4.
4. Trigger. After the sweep, require displacement: a strong candle or leg that breaks the last short-term swing low (market structure shift) and leaves an FVG or OB. Optional confirmation is SMT divergence against a correlated instrument (DXY against GBPUSD or EURUSD). It needs a second symbol and he calls it a confirmation tool, not a timing tool.
5. Entry. Limit order in the displacement's FVG or OB (internal range array), or in the 62 to 79% OTE zone of the leg from the sweep high to the displacement low. The dossiers show this on 15m or 1h for the 2022 model, 5m at the NY open for Model 9, and 1m or 3m on NQ. One trade per week: after a fill, no further new setups that week. Optional pyramiding adds are allowed only while price is above equilibrium of the trade's dealing range.
6. Stop. Above the manipulation high (the Judas swing high), or the fixed Model 2 values of 25 pips (50 on the alternative entry). Model 9's 8.5-pip stop was a tight one on a 5m FVG.
7. Targets. TP2 (runner) is the opposing external range liquidity: the old low, sellside pool, daily FVG low or weekly low, typically 50 to 100+ pips on forex and 359 handles on NQ. A separate TP1 order at the Model 8 bread-and-butter objective is documented in Model 9. The 2026 minimum target is the nearest old low or the daily discount wick's consequent encroachment.
8. Management. After the first retracement and expansion (Wednesday), move the stop to protect capital and take a partial. The 25-50-75 trail is: at 25% of expected profit move the stop up 25% of its distance, at 50% move it 50%, and at 75% move it to break even. [S] The dossier's phrasing is ambiguous. For NQ he trailed the stop behind sellside purges overnight.
9. Exit and invalidation. Hold until the target is hit or until price stops making new lows in the bias direction (weekly profile broken). Flat by the end of Friday if still open. After a delivered trade, stand aside for the rest of the week.
Subjective parts: choice of draw on liquidity, what counts as a premium PD array and as energetic displacement, which sweep is the Judas swing, SMT confirmation, and the exact trailing-stop arithmetic.
osok.changes_over_time:
Teaching changes over time.
1. 2017 (nHUtxQj5jks) and 2020 (cwoBv5aI0Vk): OSOK is a philosophy of patience, one good setup a week, with the dossier tying it to killzone trading. The nHUtxQj5jks summary says 80 to 120 pips, but that comes from the dossier's own summary text and the only quote says 'one of these a week'.
2. Oct 2022, Month 07 (LBlK6JB0QS0): the full weekly-profile model. Target is 50 to 100+ pips. The weekly high forms Monday or Tuesday in London, the Judas swing goes above the weekly open into a premium PD array, and there is one trade, entered on an OTE retest and held to Friday. Caveat: the quotes in this dossier read as polished summaries, not raw transcript, and its trade row has no price levels.
3. Jan to Feb 2024, Charter Models 2 and 9: the pip target drops to 50 to 75 per week, and the weekly-extreme day shifts from Monday or Tuesday London (2022) to Tuesday and/or Wednesday (Model 2) and then Monday through Wednesday, with Tuesday about 70% (Model 9). Model 9 adds the internal-to-external range engine, a twin-order structure (a Model 8 order plus a runner), pyramiding above equilibrium, 20-week old highs as targets and DXY SMT at the NY open. Model 2 adds the 25/50 pip stops, the 25-50-75 trail and the one-trade-per-week cap. Pyramiding and twin orders sit awkwardly with a strict single shot.
4. Sept 2024 (N9RW9v2kOoY): same name applied to an NQ index-futures swing. It is a Turtle Soup short at a bearish OB with 14 contracts in 3 tranches, held 18+ hours, stop trailed overnight and exit at a daily FVG low. The target is in handles and dollars, not 50 to 75 pips.
5. Jul 2026 (zq4hz_XiTRE): a 'short-term' one shot one kill that he says to look for every month, every trading day and every week. It is an intraday NQ premium-inefficiency short on 1m, with a lunch-macro window (11:30 to 13:30), first-presented-FVG consequent encroachment and a low-hanging-fruit target. That is far from the Monday-to-Wednesday weekly model. His stated rule is to stop trading once the weekly target is hit.
6. Stop sizes conflict by variant: 25 or 50 pips (Model 2), 8.5 pips (Model 9 GBPUSD), above the Tuesday high (2022), and about 20 NQ handles above the blended entry (Sept 2024).
7. Evidence caveats: all 8 trades shown are winners. Several rule rows carry the dossier's own paraphrase, not his words. The weekly-profile quotes come mostly from LBlK6JB0QS0, whose wording looks cleaned up. The twIPoG2TZ1o 04:30 quote says 'higher low', a long-side wording that doesn't match the bearish examples. No dossier gives an explicit entry trigger quote for the weekly model. The entry and trigger parts above are the closest verbatim statements (the internal-range entry line and the SMT line), and the OTE retest and displacement trigger come from trade tables and chart descriptions.

GBPUSD (3): Model 9 short (+75 pips, twIPoG2TZ1o), NY-open DXY-SMT short (126.4 pips against an 8.5-pip stop, 14.87 R, YIxurbDNrWM), FOMC-week long (hit the weekly target, i8xt0EQDjNY). Counting caveat: 7 are named OSOK or Model 9 in their dossier. KQdsa7S1LoQ is Model 2, which its overview calls Short-Term Trading (One Shot - One Kill). Direction split is 6 shorts and 2 longs, and every trade shown is a win. nHUtxQj5jks, cwoBv5aI0Vk and qstxYesCTQk show no trades. rules.rule: Use it as a once-per-week swing model. Stalk one high-probability setup per week worth 50 to 100+ pips with minimal drawdown, instead of intraday scalping (Month 07, 2022).
rules.quote: The One Shot One Kill model is designed to find one high probability setup per week that can capture 50 to 100 or more pips with minimal draw-down.

rules.rule: Charter Model 9 (2024) sizes the same model at 50 to 75 pips per week.
rules.quote: this is a one shot one kill model and it is specifically dealing with stocking 50 to 75 Pips per week

rules.rule: Earliest form (2017): the idea is to catch one good setup a week and manage equity well, not to trade often.
rules.quote: On a One Shot One Kill basis, if you catch one of these a week with the right amount of equity management, you can build a massive trading career.

rules.rule: 2020 philosophy version: be patient and wait for the one particular setup. This is the sniper idea, not yet the weekly-profile mechanics.
rules.quote: Wait for that one particular setup. That's the One Shot, One Kill model.

rules.rule: Bias comes from the higher-timeframe draw on liquidity. In the Month 07 example price is heading for an untested discount liquidity pool on the daily chart, so the week is bearish and the short is the trade.
rules.quote: Prices going lower, why? Because they're reaching for the discount liquidity pool on the daily chart that has not been tested yet.

rules.rule: Foundation principle (2017): smart money buys when price is falling into discount and sells when it is rising into premium. Take the weekly order flow side.
rules.quote: Smart money buys in down markets, and they sell in up markets. That is the fundamental understanding you must have.

rules.rule: Core weekly-profile setup. Price runs above the weekly opening price in a Judas swing into a premium PD array (mirror for longs). That run forms the high of the week on Monday or Tuesday.
rules.quote: How I knew that the high could most likely be formed on Monday or Tuesday is by looking at the weekly opening price and the Judas swing above it into a premium PD array.

rules.rule: Model 9 differs from Model 8 because it explicitly hunts the weekly high or low.
rules.quote: what we said about the model number eight, where we didn't require or even concern ourselves with hunting the weekly high or low, this model we are.

rules.rule: Delivery engine. Entries from internal range liquidity (FVG, OB, void) tend to run to external range liquidity (old highs and lows).
rules.quote: Most of the time you're going to find that internal range liquidity entries will run to external range liquidity.

rules.rule: Confirmation, not timing: an SMT divergence (for example DXY against GBPUSD) is used only to confirm a narrative already built from the higher-timeframe draw and the weekly profile. It is not scanned for on its own. The Model 9 GBPUSD trade used DXY SMT at the NY open. The dossier's OSOK trade row for this video (a GBPUSD long) is the only one that links SMT to OSOK.
rules.quote: smt is not a timing tool it's a confirmation tool okay it confirms something that you were already expecting anyway

rules.rule: Enter from an internal-range PD array (order block, fair value gap or void) formed by the reversal after the manipulation. The dossiers show the entry as an OTE retest or 5m FVG, in the London kill zone or at the NY open. OTE is a chart description in the dossier, not a quoted rule.
rules.quote: That means you're going to see order blocks, fair value gaps, or voids be your entry and it'll expand outside of the present short-term dealing range to external range liquidity.

rules.rule: Model 2 teaches a 25-pip stop on the standard entry and 50 pips on the alternative (delayed) entry, placed beyond the swing extreme. Dossier trade rows show other stops: above Tuesday's high, 8.5 pips on the Model 9 GBPUSD trade, and 20 NQ handles above the blended entry (initial stop 19,165.00).
rules.quote: you're going to use a 25 pip stop loss it'll be a 50 pip stop loss if you use the alternative entry

rules.rule: Primary target is external range liquidity: the old swing low or high, the sellside or buyside pool, a daily FVG or the weekly extreme.
rules.quote: it'll expand outside of the present short-term dealing range to external range liquidity. And that is your low resistance liquidity run.

rules.rule: Hold the weekly profile until it stops making new lows (for a short) and let the bulk of the move deliver into Friday.
rules.quote: Stick to the weekly profile until it no longer makes lower lows. Let the smart money deliver the bulk of the move into Friday.

rules.rule: 2026 NQ version: a minimum 'low hanging fruit' objective is the nearest old low or the consequent encroachment of the daily discount wick.
rules.quote: What would be a low hanging fruit objective? Just getting to that low. Or as I mentioned in the analysis and commentary, this would be a low hanging fruit objective if it could just get down to that.

rules.rule: Once the retracement is followed by an expansion (Wednesday in the example), move the stop to protect capital and take a partial profit.
rules.quote: Once we have a retracement and then an expansion underway on Wednesday, you move your stop to protect capital and take a portion off the table.

rules.rule: Model 2 trailing-stop protocol is 25-50-75. The dossier reads it as: at 25% of expected profit the stop drops 25%, at 50% it drops 50%, and at 75% it goes to break even. The first fragment names the protocol.
rules.quote: my stop loss protocol management the trailing stop-loss is 25 50 75

rules.rule: Break-even is only reached at 75% of the expected move.
rules.quote: 75% of what you're expecting then break even

rules.rule: Pyramiding is allowed only while price is still on the premium side of equilibrium of the trade's dealing range (for shorts). Stop adding once price trades to equilibrium.
rules.quote: as long as we're above equilibrium on the framework that's used for the trade I will pyramid

rules.rule: Twin-order structure. Every OSOK trade gets a separate order that only targets the Model 8 bread-and-butter objective, and the other order is held for the full OSOK extension.
rules.quote: I want to do a separate trade where I'm only trying to get what would be described as model number eight it's a complete trade all together by itself its own

rules.rule: Do not day-trade it. One clean trade held for two or three days is the goal.

rules.rule: Once the weekly shot has delivered, stop trading for the week (2026).

rules.rule: Swing-hold example: the NQ short in the Sept 2024 OSOK video was held about 18 hours through the PM chop and overnight session. The stop was trailed to 18,999.25 after a sellside purge, and the full position closed at the Aug-13 daily FVG low (18,765.25). The quote supports only the hold duration. The stops and exit come from the dossier's trade table.

rules.rule: The weekly-profile premise holds only while price keeps making new lows (for a short). Once it stops, the profile is done and the trade is over.
rules.quote: Stick to the weekly profile until it no longer makes lower lows.

rules.rule: One shot per week. If Tuesday gives the trade, take it and do not trade Wednesday. If Tuesday gives nothing, Wednesday is the day.

rules.rule: Recommended markets from the dossiers: EURUSD, GBPUSD and DXY (as SMT reference) on the 2022 and 2024 forex versions, and NQ on the 2024 and 2026 versions. Timeframes are weekly and daily for the draw, 1h or 15m for the Month 07 entry, 5m at the NY open for the Model 9 GBPUSD trade, and 1m or 3m on NQ. The only quote on markets is the NQ line here.

rules.rule: Month 07 weekly profile: the weekly extreme is expected to form in the London session on Monday or Tuesday. Entry is in the London kill zone. Wednesday and Thursday are the expansion days and Friday is the settlement.
rules.quote: If we're looking for lower prices as we're going to justify in this lesson, we anticipate the high of the week to form on Monday or Tuesday in London.

rules.rule: Model 9: Tuesday makes the weekly high or low about 70% of the time, so it is fine to skip Monday and wait for Tuesday or Wednesday.
