weekly_profiles.summary: Weekly range profiles and weekly bias: set the week's direction from the weekly chart (buy at or below the weekly open in a bullish week, sell at or above it in a bearish one), expect the weekly low/high on Tuesday (London) or by Wednesday NY open after a Judas swing against the bias, skip Monday, take one trade, then expect a 20-30% TGIF retracement of the weekly range on Friday.
weekly_profiles.needs_clock: Mostly yes. The core of the model is calendar time. The weekly open is Sunday 18:00 ET, the weekly extreme is expected between Monday close and Wednesday 07:00 NY open (Tuesday London most often), Monday is skipped, and Friday has a hard 17:00 ET close. The profile also depends on the economic calendar (Thursday/Friday news, NFP weeks), which price cannot see. On 24/7 synthetic indices there is no Sunday gap, no Friday close, no London/NY sessions and no news, so the day-of-week edge ('Tuesday 70%', Monday sit-out, TGIF at the Friday close) has no basis there. Only a price-only version could be tested: define an arbitrary 'week' of N bars, mark the period open, and look for a Judas sweep against the bias followed by a reclaim of the open and a retracement entry. Do the same for exhaustion: after a long one-directional run, fade a 20-30% retracement of the run's range, invalidated at 40%. He says price action is fractal across timeframes (Sb9m_dxr4bI 01:22), but he never claims the 70% or TGIF numbers hold on a synthetic feed. Treat the clock-free port as an untested analogue, not as his rule.
weekly_profiles.how_to_code:
Three modules. Thresholds marked [subjective] are not given as numbers in the dossiers.

0) Calendar. weekly_open = first price after Sunday 18:00 ET (2026 usage; the 2017 videos say 'Sunday's opening'). Day index Mon=1..Fri=5 in New York time, with Wednesday 07:00 ET as the cut-off. Track running weekly high/low, the day and time each was set, and the Monday range.

1) Weekly bias (price-only proxy, [subjective]).
- Bullish if the weekly chart shows an un-swept old high or an imbalance above and the higher-timeframe structure is trending up.
- Bearish if the same applies below.
- Otherwise no-bias: skip the week, or scalp only (VdGihxSuSRk 01:26).

2) Classic Tuesday/Wednesday module (Model 2 / One Shot One Kill).
- Skip day 1 (Monday), except the NFP-week Monday if you choose to model it.
- Bullish week, Tue 00:00 to Wed 07:00 ET:
  - Price trades below weekly_open.
  - It sweeps a Monday or prior swing low or equal lows. Trigger: a sweep of 10-30 pips (FX) or about 0.2-0.5 ATR [subjective].
  - It shows displacement up, closing back above the sweep and ideally above weekly_open.
- Entry: limit at the 62-79% OTE of the displacement leg, or at weekly_open minus 25-30 pips (Yqio1Ja0lIQ 24:34). Use a 25-50 pip stop beyond the swept low, or 150 pips for the 2017 swing variant.
- Bearish weeks mirror this.
- One trade per week (set a flag).
- Invalidation, checked on every bar:
  - A new low below the candidate weekly low before Wednesday 07:00 ET: cancel and stand aside for the day.
  - A Wednesday close back through weekly_open against the bias (line in the sand).
- Targets: expansion away from the open toward the draw on liquidity, or until Thursday NY open (Model 2).
- Management: partial 50-80% at +100 pips, then stop to breakeven. Alternative: the 25-50-75 trail (KQdsa7S1LoQ 01:02:17). Do not hold large size over the weekend.
- Wednesday reversal variant: Mon/Tue trend against the eventual bias into an HTF array, then Wednesday breaks a short-term opposing swing (jvc105qaCJs 00:17:24). Treat as the same module with the extreme allowed on Wednesday.

3) TGIF module (Friday).
- Preconditions:
  - Mon-Thu closed directionally, with the week's close beyond weekly_open in the bias direction.
  - The high/low of the week is printed Friday morning (new weekly extreme, usually a sweep of Thursday's extreme).
  - The market is not at an all-time high, which he says to disregard.
- R = weekly_high - weekly_low at the time of the trigger.
- Zone: for a short after a weekly high, level_k = weekly_high - k*R for k = 0.20 to 0.30. 0.40 is the outer limit he gives in 2025.
- Trigger: 1-5m displacement through a swing low that leaves an FVG (the '2022 model'). Enter on the FVG retrace. Stop above the Friday high.
- Target: the 20-30% zone (his Friday-close settlement).
- Invalid if price retraces at least 40% of R, or at the 17:00 ET close. Be flat before the weekend.

4) Friday Asian Range (low confidence).
- Source quotes: only 7SUa7lw2zTw 24:15 and YYsfAvz0c3o 07:15 and 14:30 are genuine quote lines. The Asian window 19:00-00:00 EST and the 11:00-13:00 ET exit time come from the dossier's own summary text, not from ICT quotes. Do not code them as his rules.
- Gate: bias underway and weekly range not exhausted.
- Mark the Asian range. Wait for a London sweep of one side and a fade; do not buy the breakout.
- Target: 2-3x range projection from the range edge.

Subjective parts: bias, sweep size, 'displacement', 'weekly range exhausted', and the profile labels (classic / Wednesday reversal / consolidation / seek-and-destroy). He never gives thresholds for them.
weekly_profiles.changes_over_time:
Source quality. The stated 70% tendency and the polished 'profile' wording appear in dossiers that read as machine-written summaries: wFjeUzJys7w, LBlK6JB0QS0, 7SUa7lw2zTw, YYsfAvz0c3o, PBzd2u4AgbE, _9QfSbpZTZA, 3B7Reg2Yiqs, KrGTimL3YRQ, jvc105qaCJs. The lower-case run-on quotes (Yqio1Ja0lIQ, Sb9m_dxr4bI, 5_l311HP87c, BZ4HVsArJBE, GVx-yJkehtA, KQdsa7S1LoQ, s1gCDuzcukU, YIxurbDNrWM, koN1ge8bewI) and the 2025-26 quotes (b4DOrfGau8w, NPU4gsM9jqA, rtIcbG6twrI, iSWZOe3aUFE) read like real transcripts. He never shows a sample behind '70%'. Number given: bearish Tuesday high, 2020 (_9QfSbpZTZA); Tuesday low in London, 2022 (wFjeUzJys7w); 'high or low', 2024 (YIxurbDNrWM). The 85-minute 2026 'Week in the Life Cycle of Price' (dmHSwlmS9iY) has only four sparse rule lines and no trades.

Evolution by year:
- 2017: the weekly open is the anchor (buy at or below it when bullish). The weekly low is expected from Sunday open to Wednesday NY open (highest odds Tue London to Wed NY open). Wednesday is the 'line in the sand', and a new low before Wednesday NY open cancels the trade. The swing version uses a 150-pip stop for 150-300 pips. Partials come at every 100 pips. Monday is sat out about 90% of the time.
- 2020: 'Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday are best entry days' in large expansion weeks (PBzd2u4AgbE), alongside the 70% Tuesday-high claim. The Friday Asian Range lectures appear only in November 2020; nothing later in the dossiers uses that name, and TGIF replaces it as the Friday concept.
- 2021 (Market Maker series): the midnight-open rule applies only Mon-Wed, not Thu/Fri. Thursday can hold the weekly high (MMSM), and Friday trades back into the weekly range with no percentage given.
- 2022-2023: a profile taxonomy (classic Tuesday extreme, Wednesday reversal, mid-week consolidation, expansion) tied to the Sunday calendar. TGIF is formalised as a 20-30% retracement of the weekly range, with 40% or more treated as a reversal.
- 2024 Charter Models 2, 9 and 10: the anchor can form Mon/Tue/Wed, but the model hunts Tuesday and Wednesday. One trade per week. Stops are 25/50 pips and the trail is 25-50-75, or a two-partial-then-collapse rule in Model 10. Targets are 50-75 pips per week.
- 2025: the TGIF range is widened to 20-30% and 'as much as 40%', and TGIF is disregarded at all-time highs. Thursday can print the weekly high or a fake high (dA2CHAN1DzY).
- 2026: Monday guidance is 'try not to trade Mondays', with the NFP-week Monday as the exception. In iSWZOe3aUFE he says 'ICT teaches never trade on Mondays. That's not true.' NFP-week students stop after Wednesday 11:00 ET. Weekly range percentage levels (20% / 30%) are used as live targets. 'Match models to the weekly profile' is stated but not specified (dmHSwlmS9iY).

Direct conflicts:
- Window for the weekly extreme: Tue London to Wed NY open (2017) versus Mon-Wed (2020, 2024) versus Thursday possible (2021, 2025).
- Monday: 'miss it on purpose' versus 'best entry days' (2020) versus 'we trade every Monday of NFP week' (2026).
- Reference open: the weekly open, the midnight NY open (Mon-Wed only), and '400 opening price' in Model 2 (24:13). The last may be a transcription of 04:00 or something else.
- Stop size: 150 pips (2017 swing) versus 50 (Model 2) versus 25/50.
- Partials: every 100 pips (2017) versus 25-50-75 trail (2024) versus two partials and collapse (Model 10).
- Friday Asian Range, between the two 2020 dossiers: trade the London expansion through the range (7SUa7lw2zTw) versus don't buy breakouts above the range and expect a sweep and reversal (YYsfAvz0c3o). Exit time also differs: 11:00-12:00 ET versus before 13:00 ET.
- TGIF: 20-30% (2023), up to 40% (2025), none stated (2021). The percentage is presumably measured down from the weekly extreme as a share of the weekly range; this is not stated explicitly.
weekly_profiles.markets: Count of 10 is trades in the dossiers tied to a weekly-profile, one-shot or TGIF setup. Yqio1Ja0lIQ has 2 (EURUSD long, USDCAD short), wTR-vhOdMgo 1 (NQ TGIF short), NPU4gsM9jqA 1 (NQ TGIF short, +45 pts), -Qag-99u_BM 1 (NQ NFP-Friday short into the 20% weekly-range level), KQdsa7S1LoQ 1 (EURUSD short, +160 pips), s1gCDuzcukU 1 (EURUSD/GBPUSD Model 2 short), LBlK6JB0QS0 1 (EURUSD short, +110 pips), GVx-yJkehtA 1 (GBPUSD Tuesday London OTE long), BZ4HVsArJBE 1 (GBPUSD Friday retracement short). About 5 more loosely related trades (twIPoG2TZ1o, YIxurbDNrWM x2, Sb9m_dxr4bI, nNEt9QTCTtk, which repeats the Yqio1Ja0lIQ examples) are not counted. The two taxonomy lectures, wFjeUzJys7w and dmHSwlmS9iY (85 min), show no trades. Markets: 2017-2024 FX (EURUSD, GBPUSD, USDCAD), 30m for the weekly study and 15m/1h for execution. 2023-2026 NQ futures (ES for comparison) on weekly, then 1m/5m. Classic profiles are recommended mainly on EURUSD and GBPUSD (Month-07 dossiers).

rules.rule: On Sunday read the economic calendar; it decides which weekly range profile (classic Tuesday extreme, Wednesday reversal, mid-week consolidation, etc.) is expected for the week.
rules.quote: You must look at the economic calendar on Sunday. The calendar dictates which weekly range profile the algorithm will most likely deliver.

rules.rule: If high-impact news sits on Thursday/Friday, expect Mon-Wed to be a sluggish consolidation (do not expect the classic Tuesday expansion).
rules.quote: If high impact news is scheduled for Thursday or Friday, Monday through Wednesday will frequently form a Consolidation Mid-Week profile.

rules.rule: Friday Asian Range is only used when a directional higher-timeframe expansion (weekly bias) is already underway; not in a consolidating week.
rules.quote: The Friday's Asian Range is only useful if a bias is underway. That means are we in a clear directional expansion on the higher timeframe charts?

rules.rule: Non-farm-payroll weeks: late-week profiles are unreliable; be done by Wednesday 11:00 ET and stay out Thursday/Friday (stated for students).
rules.quote: hopefully you learned why I tell you to avoid non-farm payroll weeks after 11:00 a.m. Wednesday Eastern time.

rules.rule: Weekly bias is read from the weekly chart as a draw on liquidity: does price look headed to an old low, old high, or an imbalance above/below. He explicitly rejects forcing a fresh bias every day.
rules.quote: i'm not trying to get a daily bias every single day i'm trying to determine the likely weekly expansion and again what is that i utilize a weekly chart and i studied that

rules.rule: Weekly bias is expressed against the weekly (Sunday) opening price: bullish week = buy at or below it; bearish week = sell at or above it.
rules.quote: if we know that our analysis leads us to a bullish weekly perspective we're gonna be focusing on buying at or below the weekly opening price when bullish and when we're bearish on a weekly we're gonna be focusing on selling short at or above the weekly opening price

rules.rule: Bullish-week profile: Monday, Tuesday and early Wednesday run in the bias direction until the draw on liquidity is reached.
rules.quote: if i'm bullish for the week i'm expecting monday and tuesday and early parts of wednesday to be bullish until we get to an area where the draw on liquidity is reached

rules.rule: If no weekly bias is clear he waits (Monday action, even mid-week) and only scalps; he does not force a weekly bias.
rules.quote: sometimes I have to wait for Monday's trading, sometimes I have to wait for maybe the middle of the week before I can get the information or may not even have it at all this week and it forces me to do just small little scalps.

rules.rule: Weekly Judas swing: the week opens and price is driven away from the weekly open against the bias (below it in a bullish week) to trap early traders; this is the manipulation leg that sets the weekly extreme.
rules.quote: the new week we would expect to see the opening price that drop down which is a Judas swing this engineered move is to knock individuals are already out long or drive individuals that are not in the marketplace that want to sell short to entice them to do so

rules.rule: Classic profile: the low (bullish) or high (bearish) of the week forms Tuesday London; the 70% figure is his stated tendency, not measured.
rules.quote: The Classic Tuesday Low of the Week profile forms the low of the week in London on Tuesday roughly 70% of the time in bullish trending conditions.

rules.rule: Bearish mirror: weekly high forms Tuesday (70% claim), else Wednesday if Tuesday only consolidates.
rules.quote: I teach that when we're bearish, there's a 70% likelihood that the high of the week will form on Tuesday. If it doesn't form on Tuesday, it will occur on Wednesday

rules.rule: Wednesday reversal profile: when an intraweek reversal into a higher-timeframe array is expected, the weekly extreme is delayed to Wednesday London/New York.
rules.quote: When you anticipate an intraweek market reversal, look for the high or low of the week to be delayed until Wednesday London or New York session.

rules.rule: Late-week variant: in a strongly bullish week the weekly high can form Thursday, or Thursday prints a fake high that is later run.
rules.quote: when we have a really bullish week, as we've seen so far this week, it tends to create these either the high of the week forms on Thursday or it'll create these fake highs of the week and then it'll come back raging and blow out the high

rules.rule: Thursday/Friday role: after the Mon-Wed accumulation and expansion, smart money distributes into Thursday/Friday highs and price then trades back into the week's range.
rules.quote: this is where smart money they distribute their longs on thursday and friday if it offers higher prices and then you expect price to come off that and trade back down into the range which is the highest high formed intra-week to the low

rules.rule: TGIF premise: a week that expanded Mon-Thu often prints its extreme Friday morning; once set, price gravitates into internal range liquidity.
rules.quote: once that high of the week is established, it's absolutely controlled, the market will just simply gravitate into internal range liquidity.

rules.rule: Friday Asian Range: a protraction (false break) beyond the Asian/Friday extreme is an engineered move to draw in breakout traders before the real move the other way.
rules.quote: During consolidation here, the market had a protraction above Friday's high. That's an engineered move to draw in buyers before the true move down.

rules.rule: Wednesday reversal profile trigger: a Wednesday break of a short-term high (after the Mon/Tue decline into the HTF array) confirms the intraweek reversal.
rules.quote: Now Wednesday breaks a short-term high. That break of structure is the signal that the intraweek reversal has been confirmed.

rules.rule: TGIF trigger on a lower timeframe: displacement through a swing (swing low for a short after a weekly high) that leaves a fair value gap; then aim at the 20-30% level.
rules.quote: wait for it to give you your 2022 model: displacement, breaking a swing low, creating a fair value gap, then target that 20 to 30 percent weekly level.

rules.rule: Model 2 (weekly short-term) entry: buy under the opening price on Tuesday or Wednesday (bullish week) with a 50-pip stop, hold to Thursday New York open. Note the dossier text reads '400 opening price' (dossier summary says 04:00); the exact reference open is ambiguous.
rules.quote: buy under 400 opening price on Tuesday or Wednesday using 50 pip stop loss holding for Thursday's New York open

rules.rule: Swing version (2017): buy about 30 pips below the weekly open in a bullish week with a wide 150-pip stop; targets 150-300 pips. Short-term version uses the OTE retracement on Tue/Wed instead.
rules.quote: buy 30 pips below the opening price on Sunday and use a hundred and 50 pips stop this is for swing traders not short-term traders and let that go and see if you don't get 150 to 300 pips

rules.rule: Standard short-term entry uses a 25-pip stop; the alternative (delayed) entry uses a 50-pip stop beyond the swing extreme.
rules.quote: you're going to use a 25 pip stop loss it'll be a 50 pip stop loss if you use the alternative entry

rules.rule: Weekly expansion runs away from the weekly open after Wednesday and has only until Friday's close to deliver.
rules.quote: the algorithm will want to expand away from this opening price after Wednesday because it only has New York opens time period to Friday's close

rules.rule: TGIF target: a retracement of 20-30% of the completed weekly range, not a full reversal.
rules.quote: The TGIF trade is going to look for a retracement back into 20 to 30 percent of whatever that weekly range has done

rules.rule: 2026 TGIF description: price trades back below Friday's midnight open and settles between 30% and 20% of the weekly range into the Friday close.
rules.quote: trades back down below Friday's midnight opening price and then we settle in in TGIF between the 30 and 20% of the weekly range and close right there. Brilliant, isn't it?

rules.rule: 2021 version of Friday behaviour (no percentage given): after pressing higher every day, the last day trades back into the weekly range.
rules.quote: now we have pressed every single day higher now we're on the last day of the week the algorithm will likely trade back into the weekly range

rules.rule: Friday Asian Range target (2020 dossier): a displacement through Friday's extreme projects to about three Asian-range standard deviations; take profit there.
rules.quote: A displacement lower running out Friday's lows projects right down to three Asian range standard deviations. That's where you take your money off the table.

rules.rule: Scale out: bank 80% as a day trader, at least half as a short-term trader, because the weekly can change gears mid-week (partials roughly every 100 pips).
rules.quote: as a day trader you certainly want to be banking 80% of your position and if you're a short-term trader you want to be at least half your position out because the weekly can change gears midweek

rules.rule: After the first ~100-pip partial, move the stop to breakeven.
rules.quote: if it allows you to make a hundred pips when you take your first partial off and put your stop at breakeven you're in a beautiful position

rules.rule: One shot per week: if the Tuesday trade triggers do not trade again Wednesday; Wednesday is only the execution day if Tuesday did not offer the setup.
rules.quote: looking at a selling opportunity on Tuesday and or Wednesday so if we get a trade on Tuesday we don't trade on Wednesday

rules.rule: Once the Wednesday retracement-then-expansion is underway, protect capital by moving the stop and taking a portion off.
rules.quote: Once we have a retracement and then an expansion underway on Wednesday, you move your stop to protect capital and take a portion off the table.

rules.rule: Do not carry heavy risk over the weekend close.
rules.quote: you do not want to be carrying heavy risk into the weekend close.

rules.rule: If price trades beyond the Tuesday/Wednesday extreme (below the low formed by Wednesday NY open in a bullish week) the weekly low is not in: cancel the trade and sit out the day.
rules.quote: if we go lower than the low formed on Wednesdays New York open you have to nix the trade and go to the sidelines on the day

rules.rule: Wednesday line in the sand: in a bullish week, once Wednesday trades above the weekly open it must not return to the open.
rules.quote: Wednesday is the line in the sand if it trades above the opening price when we're bullish we do not permit it to come back down to the opening price

rules.rule: TGIF invalidation: a retracement of 40% or more is a reversal question, not a TGIF rebalance.
rules.quote: If it retraces 40 percent or more, that's more of a conversation for reversals

rules.rule: TGIF is disregarded when price is at all-time highs; the 2025 version also widens the retracement to as much as 40%.
rules.quote: Obviously when we're at all-time highs, we want to disregard the TGIF because it can keep going and keep going and keep going

rules.rule: Friday is time-limited: do not expect far liquidity pools to be reached late Friday.
rules.quote: Don't expect these relative equal highs to be taken before the draw on liquidity because it's Friday. It only has a little bit of time.

rules.rule: 2017 weekly profile examples: EURUSD (and USDCAD) on the 30-minute chart with the weekly open extended to Friday and an OTE fib.
rules.quote: go through that fib that low to this high you get an optimal trade entry beautifully lined up

rules.rule: 2021 teaching used GBPUSD with a weekly chart for the weekly draw and daily/1h/15m for execution.
rules.quote: weekly chart of the british pound versus us dollar

rules.rule: 2026 TGIF and weekly-profile material is on NQ index futures, weekly chart for the profile and 1m for execution.
rules.quote: weekly chart of the NASDAQ composite and NQ futures

rules.rule: The weekly low/high is expected between Sunday open and Wednesday New York open (07:00 NY), with highest odds Tuesday London to Wednesday NY open.
rules.quote: what we're looking for is the weekly low to form between Sunday's opening and Wednesday there high odds or the weekly low to form before Wednesday's New York open or would be otherwise 7:00 a.m. New York time the odds further increase between Tuesday and Wednesday focusing on Tuesday's London to Wednesday's New York open

rules.rule: Tuesday London open is the usual weekly-extreme time.
rules.quote: primarily I want you to be thinking how Tuesday to Wednesday in that time period that's when the weekly low is gonna form many times it's going to be Tuesday's London open

rules.rule: Monday sit-out (2017): about 90% of weeks that make their low on Monday he misses it on purpose; he uses Monday's range and acts Tuesday.
rules.quote: about 90% of the time if the week makes its low on Monday I'm missing that because I elect to sit many times on the sidelines because I want to use the range of Monday to give me insights so on Tuesday I like to get hopefully a lower low when I'm bullish and then I'll buy in here

rules.rule: Monday sit-out (2021): leave Monday to others, study it, and treat Tuesday as the action day.
rules.quote: i wanna study on monday what they do and then on tuesday generally that's my action day

rules.rule: Monday sit-out rationale (2024): because Tuesday forms the weekly extreme about 70% of the time, skipping Monday costs little.
rules.quote: 70% of the time Tuesday makes the high or low of the week so if there's a lot of opportunity or odds that Tuesday creates the high or low of the week is it really that big of a deal if you don't take a trade on Monday in my opinion my view is no

rules.rule: Monday sit-out (2026): Monday is the accumulation/manipulation part of the week.
rules.quote: which is the reason why I tell students try not to trade on Mondays cuz Mondays are the manipulation and accumulation part of the week, the first day of the week.

rules.rule: Monday exception (2026): NFP-week Monday is traded; the sit-out is not absolute.
rules.quote: We trade every single Monday of non-farm payroll week.

rules.rule: The weekly-open reference is only used Monday to Wednesday for entries, not Thursday/Friday.
rules.quote: we're not going to reference the opening price on thursday because we're so late in the week we're focusing primarily on buying below the opening price in bullish weeks on monday tuesday and wednesday bearish weeks we're looking to sell short on monday tuesday and wednesday above the opening price on thursdays and fridays we're not factoring that in

rules.rule: TGIF timing: the extreme of a strong trending week is expected Friday morning (London / early NY).
rules.quote: We anticipate that high forming Friday morning

rules.rule: Friday time budget: the market only has until the 5 PM ET close, so TGIF settles into the 20-30% zone and stops.
rules.quote: You got to think about how much time because time is the most important factor. Time you have to consider it only has Friday because when we close at 5:00 Eastern time, it's then you go into the weekend

london_cbdr_profile.summary: London day trade on one of four daily profiles (normal or delayed protraction, buy or sell): the prior 2-8 PM NY CBDR must be under 40 pips (ideal 20-30) and gives a 1-4 SD grid; after the midnight NY open the Judas swing runs against the day's daily bias by 1-2 SD (starts at midnight for normal, at or after 2 AM for delayed) into a discount or premium PD array; buy below the midnight open or just under the Asian low, stop 50% of 5-day ADR beyond the Asian extreme, target the opposite-side SD levels and ADR, take 60-80% off at the 60-minute equilibrium, expect the day to be capped by about 2 PM NY.
london_cbdr_profile.needs_clock: Yes, it is clock-dependent at every step. CBDR is defined as 14:00-20:00 New York, the Asian range as 19:00-24:00 New York, the reference open is the midnight New York price, normal versus delayed protraction is decided by whether the Judas starts at midnight or at about 02:00, the London kill zone is 01:00 (or 02:00) to 05:00, a day with the move done before 10:00 triggers the 80% rule, London lunch 05:00-07:00 is dead, and 14:00 caps the day. The edge claim is tied to interbank (IPDA) time and London liquidity, so it cannot be validated on 24/7 synthetic indices. A reduced price-only version could run there by substituting a fixed anchor: a prior 6-hour body range as the CBDR proxy, a prior 5-hour range as the Asian proxy, the anchor-time price as the open, then the same SD grid, a sweep beyond the range by 1-2 SD, and ADR-based stop and targets. That version tests only the geometry, not his claim, and he explicitly does not endorse synthetic markets.
london_cbdr_profile.how_to_code:
Inputs: 15m bars (5m for refinement), converted to America/New_York with DST, pip size per symbol, 5-day ADR in pips.
1) Day D reference values. CBDR: use candle bodies (max/min of open and close) of bars from D-1 14:00 to 20:00 NY; top, bottom, width W in pips. Asian range: bodies from D-1 19:00 to D 00:00 NY; AH, AL, width A. Midnight open M: first price at D 00:00 NY. ADR5: mean daily range of the last 5 days.
2) Day filter. Hard: skip if W > 40 pips (JKzEhfwV1dY, nI1AMOC1pro); treat 20-30 as ideal and >30 as degraded; one lesson uses 50 (stK2gNqhLaM). Prefer A <= 20; if A > 40 allow only the delayed profile. Skip the day after an FOMC (2 PM release) and other flagged news. 2024 Model 5 variant: require W >= 15 or A >= 20, else use the float.
3) SD grid: for k in 1..4, up_k = top + k*W and down_k = bottom - k*W. Optional second grids from A (Asian) and from half the float range.
4) Bias: an external input (daily order flow, DXY, HTF PD arrays). It is subjective; the code should take it as a parameter (+1 buy day, -1 sell day).
5) Profile classification. Normal protraction: after 00:00 price starts moving against the bias (below M on buy days, above M on sell days) and prints the extreme between about 02:00 and 04:00. Delayed: price stays inside a narrow band around M from 00:00 to 02:00 and the counter move starts at or after 02:00. The consolidation band size is not given, so choose a parameter. Anything else = no trade.
6) Judas measurement: on a buy day J = M (or bottom) minus the lowest low since 00:00; express J in W units. Valid zone is the price trading between roughly down_1 and down_2 (up to down_3 at the outer end), below M, and ideally at or below AL minus 5 pips. Arms the setup only if a discount PD array (order block or fair value gap, HTF) overlaps that zone; the array detection is subjective and the mirror holds for sells.
7) Entry: limit or market buy at AL - 5 pips, or at the overlap of down_1/down_2 with the array. Never buy above M. If missed, a 5m retrace into the array after a structure shift is allowed. The exact signal that the Judas is finished is not stated mechanically; pick one (close back above AL, or 5m shift) and flag it as a free parameter.
8) Stop: AL - 0.5*ADR5 for buys, AH + 0.5*ADR5 for sells (5Z_3NbclMSY). Dossier trade tables also show a stop below the Judas extreme; that is an alternative, not a quote.
9) Targets: opposite-side levels of the same grid (up_1..up_4 on a buy day), the Judas size J used as a multiplier, ADR high (low + ADR5), the HTF opposing liquidity; prefer levels that overlap a PD array. Tolerance for counting an SD hit: 1-5 pips.
10) Management: first objective: take 50-80% and move stop to breakeven + 1 pip. Take 60-80% at the 50% level of the 60-minute range. If the ADR is reached before 10:00 NY take 80%. Keep a runner for double ADR. Flat or stalled by 14:00 NY, no new entries 05:00-07:00 NY.
Subjective parts that cannot be coded from his words: the bias, which PD array counts, the exact consolidation threshold for delayed protraction, the end-of-Judas confirmation, and whether the SD level and the array overlap.
london_cbdr_profile.changes_over_time:
Counts: 7 trade rows in the starter set and the bread-and-butter sell lesson (eU8WcUftUtY, 5Z_3NbclMSY, zanmou0ic5U, OVfn-gDk2dE, -oMtfDvc18Y, cqf8nH54bb8, 2fgXDt3T3XE). Most are generic summaries with no date or price; only cqf8nH54bb8 (EURUSD, about +100 pips) and 2fgXDt3T3XE (EURUSD short 1.1558 to 1.1495, +63) are priced. nI1AMOC1pro and JKzEhfwV1dY show no trades but about 7 chart days used as projection examples (GBPUSD 15m: a 13-pip CBDR day hit 2 SD up at the London high, a 58-pip day was skipped, a 19-pip and a 16-pip day gave London lows at 1 SD and 2 SD down, and in JKzEhfwV1dY a low was projected at 1.2440 and missed by one pip).

london_cbdr_profile.markets: Forex majors only. GBPUSD (Cable) on the 15-minute chart is the worked example in the CBDR and projection lessons (nI1AMOC1pro, JKzEhfwV1dY); EURUSD in the day-trade routine and the 2024 Model 5 lecture (cqf8nH54bb8, 2fgXDt3T3XE); AUDUSD, USDCAD, USDJPY appear in the 2017 Judas-swing lessons and in the recommended-market tables of the 2022 lessons; DXY is used only as a bias check. rules.rule: The model is a London day trade that must fit one of exactly four daily profiles: London normal protraction buy or sell, or London delayed protraction buy or sell. Anything else is not this model.
rules.quote: I'm only looking for four types of profiles: London normal protraction buy or sell, or London delayed protraction buy or sell. That's it, nothing else is slipping through the cracks.

rules.rule: CBDR width is the day-quality gate. About 20-30 pips is ideal because it is roughly one third of a 100-pip average daily range.
rules.quote: one third of that is around 33 pips so that's why I give about 20 to 30 pips ideal scenario.

rules.rule: Higher-timeframe daily directional bias must exist first; without it the intraday Judas/SD setup is not to be taken.
rules.quote: If you don't have higher timeframe directional bias from the daily chart, you have no business taking day trades. You are simply gambling on noise.

rules.rule: Midnight New York price is the day's reference open (IPDA true day starts at midnight NY). Bullish day: wait for price to trade below it. Bearish day: wait for price to trade above it. 2017 teaching: draw it forward to about 11:00.
rules.quote: whatever the opening price is exactly at midnight New York time I draw that out to around 11 o'clock in the morning

rules.rule: CBDR = high to low of the 2:00 PM to 8:00 PM New York window (prior evening), measured in pips. Under 40 pips, preferably 20-30.
rules.quote: The time period that frames the Central Bank dealers range is 2:00 PM to 8:00 PM New York time. The ideal range is less than 40 pips, preferably the range should be no more than 20 to 30 pips in total range high to low.

rules.rule: Measure CBDR (and the Asian range) with candle bodies, not wicks, because wicks carry broker spread noise.
rules.quote: I like to use the bodies predominantly because the wicks are always going to show erroneous price because of your dealing spread through your broker

rules.rule: Standard-deviation grid: one SD equals the CBDR width, added above the CBDR high and subtracted below the CBDR low; further SDs repeat the same width.
rules.quote: one standard deviation above and below would be the same range added to the high of the Central Bank dealer's range and subtracted from the low.

rules.rule: Asian range window is 7:00 PM to midnight New York time (same window in the 2017 and 2020 lessons).
rules.quote: 7:00 PM Eastern Standard Time in New York time begins the Asian range. Every day at midnight Eastern Standard Time New York ends the Asian range.

rules.rule: Asian range compression filter for the Asian-range version of the model: 20 pips or less going into Frankfurt/London.
rules.quote: We're going to demand that the Asian Range is in a 20 pip range or less ahead of Frankfurt and London

rules.rule: Alternative SD unit when CBDR/Asian range are unusable: the Float (written flout in 2024); half of the float range is one SD unit.
rules.quote: The equilibrium of the float range to the low of its range is counted as one standard deviation

rules.rule: Two buy-side delivery types for the Judas leg: offset accumulation (run below an old low) and re-accumulation (retrace into a discount fair value gap without taking the old low). Bread-and-butter sells are the mirror image.
rules.quote: engineering sellside liquidity to offset long positions. Re-accumulation: IPDA reprices lower to a discount Fair Value Gap to reaccumulate new long entries.

rules.rule: 2024 Model 5 qualification (reverses the 2022 maximum into a minimum): CBDR at least 15 pips, or Asian range at least 20 pips, otherwise use the flout.
rules.quote: 15 Pips Central Bank dealers range minimum doesn't do it we Asian range 20 pip or more if it doesn't do it then we use the flout

rules.rule: The Judas swing is the protractionary move away from the CBDR and counter to the intended direction of the day; its size in SD is what you measure.
rules.quote: We're looking specifically at the range that IPDA will go into protractionary state and move counter the direction of the intended direction of the day in other words it's the Judas swing.

rules.rule: The Judas extension does not have to be known in advance; measure how far it went after it has happened and use that distance as the unit.
rules.quote: We don't necessarily have to know beforehand to the pip what the extension is going to be away from the Central Bank dealers range we just need to know what it is after the move has already ensued

rules.rule: Bullish trigger: price must move down below the midnight open by some measure of Asian-range or CBDR standard deviations (he cites about 33 pips as the SD size in that example).
rules.quote: and if I'm bullish I want to see a move down below that opening price to some measure of standard deviations of the Asian range or Central Bank Dealers Range

rules.rule: Normal protraction: CBDR under 40 pips, Judas swing starts right after midnight and reaches 1 to 2 SD (down for a buy day).
rules.quote: look for that Judas swing to reach down 1 to 2 standard deviations.

rules.rule: Delayed protraction: price sits through midnight to 2:00 AM and the Judas move only begins at or shortly after 2:00 AM New York time.
rules.quote: In delayed protraction, IPDA will enter a protraction stage at or shortly after 2:00 AM New York time

rules.rule: Where the Judas extreme (high of day on sell days, low of day on buy days) usually forms: from the CBDR out to 3 SD.
rules.quote: Typically most sell days will create the high of the day from the Central Bank dealers range up to three standard deviations. Most buy days will create the low of the day from the Central Bank dealers range down to the third standard deviation.

rules.rule: Ideal case is tighter: sell-day high no more than 2 SD above CBDR, often only 1 SD.
rules.quote: Ideally sell days create the high of a day no more than two standard deviations above the Central Bank dealers range, many times just one standard deviation.

rules.rule: 2017 sell-side anatomy (the only verbatim sell-side midnight-open statement): tight Asian range, quick drop, then a run above the Asian high and above the opening price is the Judas swing.
rules.quote: asian range small tight consolidation we want to see it drop down trip traders in right away then run on the other side of the asian range high that movement above the opening price above the asian range high that is the Judas swing

rules.rule: 2017 buy-side anatomy: pop above Asian high, then drop below the midnight open and below the Asian low.
rules.quote: what we're looking for is the element of a bullish Judas swing is a pop above the Asian range high then a drop below the opening price at midnight and then below the asian range low when that occurs that's the actual Judas swing

rules.rule: Buy on the Judas swing down, below the midnight open; do not buy above the open.
rules.quote: You want to be buying on the Judas swing down or below the opening price and don't chase price

rules.rule: Buy just under the Asian range low, plus 5 pips for spread (mirror for sells above the Asian high).
rules.quote: I like buying under the Asian Range plus 5 pips for the spread

rules.rule: Entry zone is 1 to 2 SD of the Asian range (or CBDR) coinciding with a discount PD array (premium array for sells).
rules.quote: look for one or two standard deviations in the Asian Range coupled with a discount PD array.

rules.rule: Entry precision matters most at the low on buy days and the high on sell days.
rules.quote: Let me remind you that the precision really is on the entry side of the low on the buy days and the high on the sell days

rules.rule: Require confluence of SD level, ADR, and a PD array before taking the routine trade.
rules.quote: Once we have those confluences of standard deviations, Average Daily Range (ADR), and a PD array

rules.rule: If the ideal Judas entry is missed, a later 5-minute retracement can still be taken.
rules.quote: Even after the ideal Judas entry point has passed, a 5-minute retracement can be scalped

rules.rule: Protective stop is 50% of the 5-day ADR away from the Asian range extreme (subtract from the Asian low on buys; add to the Asian high on sells). Example: 100-pip ADR gives a 50-pip stop.
rules.quote: take 50 pips minus the Asian range low, whatever that price is, that's what your stop loss has to be.

rules.rule: Target is to fill four SD levels of the CBDR; four is a rule of thumb and can extend one more.
rules.quote: look to fill four Central Bank Dealers Range projections or standard deviations

rules.rule: The SD size of the Judas swing becomes the multiplier for the rest of the day's projection.
rules.quote: How much of a standard deviation did we see? Because that becomes the known range to work with and it becomes our multiplier as well. So when the market looks to fill the numbers

rules.rule: SD projections are only a guide; the PD arrays decide, and the best targets are where SD level and PD array overlap.
rules.quote: While there still may be some range permitted based on the projections, it's the PD arrays that call the shot. These projections will lead you to an overlap of time and price.

rules.rule: Tolerance: an SD level counts as hit within 3 to 5 pips in forex (2024); earlier examples claim within 1 pip.
rules.quote: remember standard deviations are within 3 to five Pips that's considered precision in Forex

rules.rule: At the first objective take 50% to 80% off and move the stop to breakeven plus one pip.
rules.quote: Once price moves in your favor and hits your first objective, you must take off 50% to 80% of your position and move your stop to breakeven plus one pip to eliminate risk.

rules.rule: Take 60 to 80 percent off at the 50% equilibrium of the 60-minute range being traded.
rules.quote: At the equilibrium of the price range you are trading inside of on a 60-minute chart, take or have taken 60 to 80 percent off

rules.rule: If the ADR high (or low) is reached before 10:00 AM New York, take 80% off.
rules.quote: If ADR high is reached prior to 10 AM, take 80% off of your position.

rules.rule: Leave a runner for days that deliver double ADR.
rules.quote: you leave runners to capture these double ADR days.

rules.rule: CBDR wider than 40 pips: stand aside, do not use this model that day.
rules.quote: We move to the sidelines and we do not look to trade with the Central Bank dealers range in our repertoire when the range is greater than 40 pips.

rules.rule: Soft width limit: CBDR above 30 pips is already less fruitful for projections (hard cap is 40).
rules.quote: Range is larger than 30 pips can tend to be unfruitful for projections.

rules.rule: Looser variant of the CBDR cap given in the avoid-London lesson: CBDR over 50 pips, skip London entirely.
rules.quote: If the Central Bank Dealers Range is greater than 50 pips, I'm already knowing firsthand I'm possibly going to pass on a London

rules.rule: Asian range over 40 pips: only consider the delayed protraction profile, otherwise sit out London.
rules.quote: If the Asian Range is greater than 40 pips, I'm going to consider the delayed protraction profile

rules.rule: No London trade after an FOMC release the previous afternoon.
rules.quote: Avoid trading London open after FOMC events that create whipsaw

rules.rule: If the day does not fit one of the four profiles, the trade is missed and must be left alone even if it becomes a big day.
rules.quote: It could be a 150 pip day and you aren't getting in with either one of these profiles, and guess what that means? That's a trade you missed and you leave it alone.

rules.rule: Do not force the SD grid every day; it fails without a 20-30 pip CBDR.
rules.quote: where this will get you in trouble is you're going to try to apply the standard deviations every single day and you're going to forget about the importance of having a range between 20 and 30 pips for the Central Bank dealers range.

rules.rule: Forex majors for the Judas swing: EURUSD, GBPUSD, AUDUSD, USDJPY (2017 list).
rules.quote: euro dollar Cable Aussie dollar dollar yen there's four markets if you just watch those it'll give you a wide array of potential scenarios where this type of thing forms

rules.rule: 15-minute chart for day-trade projections; lower timeframes skew the SD levels (2024 Model 5).
rules.quote: day-by-day basis I've seen the most consistency using the 15-minute time frame

rules.rule: 2025 statement on the related Midnight Opening Range model: works in forex and futures, not crypto; he separately says he has no experience with synthetic markets.
rules.quote: It works obviously in Forex and it works in Futures, it works in every asset class with the exception of crypto.

rules.rule: Use New York clock times exactly as he gives them.
rules.quote: If you're ever questioning what I'm referring to in terms of the beginning and endings you have to have a New York time clock

rules.rule: London kill zone 1:00 AM to 5:00 AM New York (the dossiers for other 2022 lessons use 2:00-5:00 AM).
rules.quote: Every day at 1:00 AM Eastern Standard Time New York begins the London Kill Zone. Every day at 5:00 AM Eastern Standard Time New York ends the London Kill Zone.

rules.rule: IPDA true day runs from midnight to 3:00 PM New York.
rules.quote: Every day at 12:00 AM midnight New York time begins the IPDA true day this is the beginning of the 24-hour interbank trading day. Every day at 3:00 PM New York time ends the IPDA true day 24-hour interbank trading day.

rules.rule: 2017 Judas window: from the midnight open to 5:00 AM New York.
rules.quote: you start hunting the Judas swing at midnight New York time okay so this is a New York opening price and it ends at 5:00 a.m. New York time and that's basically the entire five hour window that would be utilized for anticipating this price move

rules.rule: London close kill zone 10:00 AM to 12:00 noon New York, where the daily extreme is often completed on trend days.
rules.quote: Every day at 10:00 AM Eastern Standard Time New York begins the London close Kill Zone. Every day at 12:00 PM noon New York time ends the London close Kill Zone.

rules.rule: Hard time cap: 2:00 PM New York usually caps the high or low of the day, so exit or expect stall by then.
rules.quote: Even in a really long winded trending day, 2:00 PM usually caps the high or low of the day if we continue through London Close Kill Zone

rules.rule: No new trades in London lunch (5:00 to 7:00 AM New York).
rules.quote: Be mindful that between 5:00 AM and 7:00 AM New York time is London lunch. We don't take new trades in that window; the market goes into consolidation or retracement.

rules.rule: Day of week: Tuesday and Wednesday predominantly form the high or low of the week.
rules.quote: The day of the week is paramount in understanding about day trading because Tuesday and Wednesday form the high or low of the week predominantly.

charter_models.summary: Index of 13 distinct Charter Mentorship price-action trade plans (27 Dec 2023 to 16 Feb 2024: day, short-term, swing, position, buy/sell-side market-maker, 6%-per-month, one-shot, scalp, and the 2022 model), all built on bias, internal-to-external liquidity run, OB/FVG/OTE entry, fixed-pip stop, pip or liquidity target and staged risk management.
charter_models.needs_clock: Partly. Not one model, so it varies. Clock-dependent: Model 1 (07:00-10:00 NY), Model 13 (07:00-10:00 NY FX, 08:30-11:00 index, plus PM catalysts), Model 5 (Tue-Thu, no Mon/Fri, London/European open, CBDR and Asian range), Model 2 (Tue/Wed, 04:00 open price, 06:00 European open filter), Models 9 and 10 (weekly anchor on Mon-Wed), Model 11 (London low into NY open), plus seasonal tendencies in Models 3 and 4 (April-May strong, July-August scale back). Price-delivery only, so usable on 24/7 synthetic indices: the Model 6/7 market-maker buy/sell fractals (stated to apply on all timeframes), Model 12 (OB, then displacement, then FVG pullback with a fixed pip target), the internal-to-external liquidity run of Models 9/10/11, IPDA 20/40/60 lookbacks (as bar counts), Model 3 and 4 swing and position logic, and all the money-management rules (sizing, 25/50/75 ladder, risk halving, pyramiding). On synthetics, replace weekday, session and CBDR/Asian-range gates with a rolling-range or bar-count proxy (or drop them) and rescale the pip distances (5, 15, 20, 25, 50) to the instrument's volatility, for example as ATR multiples.
charter_models.how_to_code:
The index is a family of 13 plans, so code it as one shared pipeline with per-model parameter sets, not a single detector.

1) Structure primitives. Confirmed swing highs and lows (3-bar fractals) on the bias and execution timeframes. Dealing range = highest high and lowest low over N bars (the 20/40/60-day IPDA lookbacks become bar counts). Equilibrium = 50 percent of the range, premium above it and discount below. External range liquidity = old swing highs and lows beyond the short-term range, equal highs or lows, and previous-day or week extremes. Internal range liquidity = unmitigated FVGs, order blocks and voids inside the range. FVG (3-candle): bullish when low[i] > high[i-2], bearish when high[i] < low[i-2]. Order block = the last opposite-colour candle before a displacement leg that breaks a swing.

2) Bias (the least mechanical step). Bullish when price on the bias timeframe has closed beyond the last confirmed swing high (Model 1 daily rule), or the current higher-timeframe candle is expanding up (Model 11 weekly). Require the entry array to sit in discount (long) or premium (short) of the lookback range. Take the next external liquidity pool in the bias direction as the draw.

3) Setup and trigger. M12/M13 core: a liquidity sweep or order-block tag, then displacement (body larger than k times ATR, or a leg that breaks structure) that leaves an FVG. Reject any FVG with no preceding OB or sweep plus displacement. M6/M7: original consolidation, then a sweep and reversal low or high (SMR), then a low-risk entry, then reaccumulation OBs and FVGs, with the original consolidation extreme as the Terminus (+/-10, 20, 30 pip grades). M5 adds a session-range gate: CBDR at least 15 pips, or Asian range at least 20, else the flout.

4) Entry. Limit order at the near edge of the FVG on the pullback (do not market-chase the expansion). Alternatively OTE at 0.62 to 0.79 retracement of the displacement leg, nested in the OB or FVG (M1). Cancel the order if price goes through the far side or the window closes.

5) Stop. Per model: swing +/-5 pips (M1), 25 pips (M2/M3), swing +/-15 pips (M4/M5), 20 pips (M8, M10-M12), or the extreme of the FVG-forming candle with no padding (M13).

6) Target. External liquidity or a fixed pip count: 20 (M12), 25/week (M8), 30 (M11), 50 to 75 (M3, M9, M10), Terminus plus grades (M6/M7), symmetrical swing extension (M1).

7) Management. Size = equity times risk percent divided by (stop pips times pip value), rounded down. Ladder: at 25 percent of the distance to target cut the stop distance by 25 percent, at 50 percent by 50 percent, break even only at 75 percent. Or take partials: M8 (first partial, then break even), M10 (two partials, third closes all), M12 (80/20). Halve risk after a full loss until 50 percent of it is recovered, and after five wins in a row. Pyramid only in premium for shorts or discount for longs, with total risk across adds within 1 percent.

Subjective parts needing a rule or a human choice: the bias call (institutional order flow, weekly expansion direction), which candle counts as the order block, what counts as energetic displacement, SMR identification, SMT divergence against DXY, seasonal and COT filters, 'old lows take precedence', and which of the 13 plans to run.
charter_models.changes_over_time:
1) Thirteen separate plans, not one model. Day trading: Models 1, 5 and 11. Short-term/weekly: Models 2 and 9. Swing: Models 3 and 10. Position: Model 4. Market-maker buy side (6) and sell side (7). Bread-and-butter 25 pips/week, 6% a month: Model 8. Scalp 20 pips: Model 12. Model 13 is the 2022 YouTube model codified. The sequence runs 27 Dec 2023 to 16 Feb 2024.
2) Stop sizing changes over time. M1 uses 5 pips beyond the swing (29 Dec). M2/M3 use 25 pips (4-6 Jan). M4/M5 use 15 pips beyond the swing (11-18 Jan). Feb models use 20-pip examples, and M12 says his own minimum is about 15 and he keeps students near 20. M13 (16 Feb) says put the stop exactly at the extreme of the FVG candle, 'not one tick above', which contradicts the fixed buffers.
3) Break-even handling disagrees. M2, M4 and M5 use the 25/50/75 ladder ('not rushing to get Break Even'). M8 says move to break even at the first partial. M10 takes two partials and closes on the third target. M12 sells 80 percent at 20 pips. M7 says flatten everything at the final objective.
4) Risk per trade. 1 percent in M10, M11 and M12, and as the aggregate cap in M4 pyramiding. M7 and M8 use a 1.5 percent worked example ($300 on $20k). M13 allows '2% or less', and M6 has a 2 percent budget split over four orders. Halving after a loss is in M1, M2, M5 and M7. Halving after five wins appears only in M7 and M8.
5) Timeframe. M5 insists on 15m and says lower timeframes skew projections. M1 executes on a 5m OTE, M12 scans 15m and executes 5m, and M13 watches 5m down to 1m.
6) Weekly extreme. M8 does not hunt the weekly high or low. M9 does (Mon-Wed, Tuesday about 70 percent). M5 skips Monday and Friday. M2 trades Tuesday or Wednesday only. M13 drops weekday logic for time-of-day catalysts.
7) Session gate wording. JN_uaDDZ0rc says CBDR must exceed 15 pips. 2fgXDt3T3XE adds an Asian range of 20 pips or more, otherwise use the flout.
8) Dossier quality. The trade tables are curated walkthroughs, all wins, with neat prices, and some do not match the stated rules (for example the M12 rows in 3xgtrXok-xs and xi0N9BG1Qvs show 5 to 12 pip stops against a 20-pip rule, and the M8 row shows a 15-pip stop against 20). Several Rules-table quotes join two fragments with an ellipsis, so where needed I quoted only a contiguous piece (kNlySn81dmo 06:30 and 14:00, 3xgtrXok-xs 17:01 and 21:10, NB7Bku099tU 11:23, JN_uaDDZ0rc 27:53, 4f1vjQMlV50 25:03, twIPoG2TZ1o 10:30). atm_method.summary: A standalone hourly-chart stop-run pattern: price takes out a short-term high (ideally the second push of a two-stage run), immediately breaks market structure, and you enter on the retest of the broken level with the stop 1-2 pips beyond the rejection extreme. You target the resting stops beyond the opposite swing, and can drill down to 15m or 5m OTE to cut risk (65 to 20 pips, 140 to 20 pips) while keeping the full reward. It is bearish as taught, with a bullish mirror.
atm_method.needs_clock: No. Nothing in the video ties the pattern to a time of day, killzone or session (the Session column is N/A on every row). It is defined only by price: swing highs/lows on the hourly, a sweep of a short-term high, a structure break and a retest. It could run on 24/7 synthetic indices using only price delivery, building 60m bars (and 15m/5m) from elapsed time. The 60-minute bar boundaries are arbitrary on a 24/7 feed.
atm_method.how_to_code:
Bearish version; the bullish version mirrors it. Only the source video 30petm6SZz0 teaches this model.

1. Build 60m candles and mark swing highs and lows with a fractal rule of N bars each side. N is not given, so it is a parameter.
2. Stop run: price trades above a prior short-term swing high H1. Optional quality filter, since he says "ideally" and "stronger if": the up-leg contains two successive sweeps of short-term highs (a two-stage move). The final sweep high H2 is the "key / rejection high".
3. Structure break: within a few bars after the sweep (his word is "immediately", with no bar count), price closes below the most recent swing low L that sits under H2. This is the market structure break. The level L is the broken support that becomes resistance.
4. Entry (1h version): price retraces back up to L. Place a limit at L, or enter on first touch or rejection.
5. Stop: H2 plus a 1-2 pip buffer. On synthetic indices, scale the buffer to the instrument, for example a fraction of ATR.
6. Target: the sell stops resting under the swing low. In code, use the next lower swing low at or below L; which swing he means is subjective. The dossier trades table says a 300% Fibonacci extension below the swing low for the 15m version. That is table text and not in the quoted rules, so treat it as optional.
7. Drill-down (risk reduction): once the 1h setup is armed, switch to 15m or 5m. Find the lower-timeframe down-leg that breaks structure and wait for the retracement into its OTE zone. Enter there, put the stop above the lower-timeframe swing high, and keep the same target. Stop pips shrink from 65 to 20 and from 140 to 20. OTE zone limits (62-79% in ICT's other material) are not stated in this video, so they are an outside assumption.
8. Reward-to-risk is computed from the target distance over the refined stop (225/20 is about 11:1 in his bullish example).

Subjective or unspecified: fractal size N; wick versus close for the sweep; how many bars count as "immediately"; whether the two-stage condition is required or just a score booster; exact retest tolerance (touch versus zone); which swing low is the target; the pip buffer; the OTE band; whether the lower timeframe is 15m or 5m.
atm_method.changes_over_time:
No evolution over the years can be reported. The case-insensitive grep for "atm method" across all 884 files hits only 20171216-30petm6SZz0.md (Dec 2017, Market Maker Primer Course) and catalogue.csv. Other "atm" hits are false positives: At-The-Money options in 20221022-cv-fwKKXrwQ, and "symmetrical", "algorithmic" and "Datum"-type substrings in 20171010-aQrd75xwBS4, 20201218-RLDLuYaZYI4 and 20230930-MPIhoDIb-v0. This dossier has a Rules table and a trades table but no separate "Verbatim Quotes & Timestamps" section, so every quote comes from the Rules table. Several table cells contain "..." gaps, and I used only contiguous stretches with no gap.

Caveats on the source:
(1) The 07:39 quote mixes "above the key high or the rejection high" (a bearish stop) with "buy stops above here" (a bullish target). It looks like a caption or transcript blend, so the target quote reads as bullish while the dossier's bearish trade row says sell stops below the swing low.
(2) The two-stage condition is optional ("ideally", "stronger"), not required.
(3) The video states no invalidation rule other than the stop, no time-of-day rule, no HTF or daily bias rule, no fib band for OTE, and no maximum risk.
(4) The 300% extension target appears only in the trades table.
(5) The trades table has 4 rows but only 2 distinct trades (one bearish with a 65-pip stop, one bullish with a 140-pip stop). Each is shown on the 1h and again drilled down to 15m or 5m.
(6) Both examples are hindsight chart walk-throughs with no dates or pair names, and results are all winners (+65 pips and +225 pips).

htf_swing_position.summary: Top-down Monthly > Weekly > Daily > 4H PD-array nesting: with the higher timeframes aligned (or a daily/weekly correction), buy daily/4H discount arrays (sell premium arrays) that sit at or inside weekly/monthly arrays, risk 1-1.5% for 3:1 to 10:1, hold weeks to a quarter toward the opposing HTF array; the stock/options version adds Feb-May seasonal windows and index-SMT relative-strength watchlists.
htf_swing_position.needs_clock: The core 2022 model does not need an intraday clock. It runs on Monthly/Weekly/Daily/4H candles, so it needs only candle boundaries (the daily close for the limit-order version). Calendar months are optional filters: equity Feb-May and Oct-Dec, summer reduction, quarterly shift every 3-4 months, plus the seasonal, COT, open-interest, rate-differential and SMT confirmations. The 2024 Charter Model 4 variant adds early-week (Mon/Tue) manipulation and, per the dossier overview only, a London Open kill zone. It could run on 24/7 synthetic indices using only price delivery if "monthly/weekly/daily/4H" are replaced by synthetic resampled windows (for example 30d/7d/1d/4h) and the non-price filters are dropped. Those filters are most of his hallmark list, so a price-only version is a reduced form of the model. Expect very low frequency, about 6 to 12 setups per year per instrument.
htf_swing_position.how_to_code:
1) Resample the price feed into M, W, D and 4H candles. Classify each timeframe as bullish, bearish or correcting from swing structure plus displacement: a close beyond the prior swing high/low with an above-average-range candle and ideally an FVG. Displacement size and swing length are SUBJECTIVE and need tuned thresholds. Also test "trending vs range-bound" over the last 9-18 months of M/W (no displacement means skip).
2) Direction filter:
 - If M, W and D agree, trade every daily/4H array in that direction.
 - If M and W agree but D corrects, require the entry array to overlap a W array.
 - If W and D both correct against M, require overlap with an M array (nesting test = zone overlap).
3) Build the arrays. All of these are subjective in practice:
 - Dealing range: point of origin to intermediate-term high of the last impulse; discount is below 50%, premium above.
 - Bullish OB: the last down-close candle before displacement. Use the body, with the open and mean threshold (50%) as reference.
 - Bearish OB: the mirror of the above.
 - Others: FVG (3-candle gap), liquidity void, breaker (an OB or swing that failed and flipped), mitigation block, rejection block (long wick, trade beyond the bodies), old highs/lows.
4) Entry: either (a) a 4H reaction/displacement off the nested array, or (b) the Month 05 limit order, a buy limit at the close of a completed daily down-close candle when that candle is inside a daily PD array and M/W flow is up (mirror for shorts). Alternative (c), the 2024 Model 4 entry at the open of a monthly bearish OB, is a limit at the OB's open price.
5) Stop: beyond the HTF array or swing. Examples given are 50-70 pips on the 4H, or 5-day average daily range from the entry (60-100 pips). Risk 1% (position) to 1.5% (Month 06 example). If pyramiding, keep aggregate risk under 1%.
6) Targets: the opposing HTF array (old high/low, OB, FVG, void, monthly/weekly imbalance), with equilibrium (50%) as the first draw. Reject if reward:risk is below 3:1. Take partials at intermediate arrays (about 50%), trail behind daily swing lows/highs, and add only on a retracement into premium (shorts) or discount (longs).
7) Invalidate/skip:
 - A rejected daily/weekly higher high (or lower low) with a structure break, i.e. a bearish (or bullish) breaker forming against the trade.
 - No trend on M/W.
 - Reward:risk below 3:1.
 - Account risk limit already used.
Non-price filters you cannot code from price alone: COT, open interest, rate differentials, seasonals, fundamentals, headline sentiment. SMT can be approximated with two correlated instruments. The subjective part is the "leaps off the chart" test; the dossier says to pass on anything ambiguous.
htf_swing_position.changes_over_time:
Timeline of changes:
- 2017-12: "Secrets to Swing Trading" is a different tool set. A daily 10/20 EMA "stacking" filter gates 1h OTE entries (9 AUDUSD examples), targets are the symmetrical swing and 200% extension, the stop is not trailed until price leaves a consolidation, and about 50% comes off at the first objective. Another 2017 video gives a weekly-open swing model: buy 30 pips below the Sunday open with a 150 pip stop for 150-300 pips.
- 2020-02: the swing premise is Daily/4H/1H and position is Monthly/Weekly/Daily, and he advises beginners to avoid position trading.
- 2022 Core Content (Months 05, 06, 10-12) is the PD-array nesting model above. Month 06 says setups come from M/W/D with execution on the 4H. The Month 03 dossier (paraphrase only, no usable quote) says position = monthly chart and swing = weekly chart with 1-2 setups per quarter.
- 2023-12: swing stop left unchanged after 3 partials. The dossier tags this IMPLIED with no verbatim quote, so I did not quote it.
- 2024-01 Charter Model 4 (position trading): entry at the monthly OB open, 20/40/60-day IPDA ranges, 1% aggregate pyramid cap, graduated stop reduction, scale back in July/August. The Model 4 dossiers disagree on duration (multi-month vs multi-day plus London kill zone and Mon/Tue manipulation).
- Charter Models 3 and 10 call themselves swing models but are short-term (25-pip stop, 50 pip first target; 50-75 pips per week; two partials then close on the third). They belong on other cards.
- 2026 "swing trader's model" is an intraday ES fulcrum measured move, a different meaning of "swing".

Internal conflicts:
- Risk: 1% max (Month 05, Model 4) vs 1.5% (Month 06 example).
- Break-even accuracy at 3:1: 34% (Xs1i0aIeTME) vs 30% (JAjL7rUX2Iw) vs 25-30% (Month 05 money-management overview).
- Frequency: "one to two swing trades per every four to six weeks" (about 9-26 a year) vs "Six trades" a year vs 1-2 per quarter.
- Stop handling: don't trail (2017), trail behind daily swing lows (Month 05), leave unchanged (2023), graduated reduction (2024).
- Entry style: 4H reaction nested in HTF arrays (Month 06) vs daily-close limit (Month 05) vs monthly OB open with no LTF confirmation (2024).

Reliability warnings:
- Many Month 10-12 dossiers (options, commodity/forex/stock/bond mega-trades, long-term top-down) list rules as paraphrase without quote marks, and their trade rows are generic templates (for example "+500 to +1,500 pips"). I omitted those rather than quote them.
- The Million Dollar Swing dossier (VL4YLTRerHY) gives very prescriptive rules (4 pillars, daily MSS + 62-79% OTE, 30/30/40 scale-out, EUR/USD long 1.0820 -> +430 pips) that no other Month 06 dossier corroborates. Treat it as low confidence.

Trade count (12): Million Dollar EURUSD 1 (low confidence), stock longs AAPL/BA/HD/MCD 4, stock shorts AXP/CAT/CVX 3, Model 4 GBPUSD + EURUSD pyramid + EURUSD 3, euro futures open-interest long 1. Not counted: worked case studies without tickets (EURUSD 2011 70-pip stop / 585-pip move, USDJPY 2016 ~1,200 pips, AUDUSD ~1,200 pips, Silver, CHF), about 11 templated rows in Months 10-12, and the 9 AUDUSD 1h EMA-stack swings from 2017.
htf_swing_position.markets: FX majors and crosses (EUR/USD, GBP/USD, USD/JPY, AUD/USD, USD/CHF, NZD/USD, USD/CAD) with the DXY as anchor; metals (silver, gold); commodity futures (grains, cattle, cotton, crude); index futures (Dow, ES, NQ); single stocks from the Dow 30 (AAPL, BA, HD, MCD longs; AXP, CAT, CVX shorts); bond futures (ZB, ZN); and call/put options or LEAPS on stocks and indices. Core Month 06 teaching is FX-centred (pips). The stock, options, commodity and bond lessons are mostly paraphrased in the dossiers, with no verbatim rule quotes.

rules.rule: Swing only markets that are trending on the higher timeframes; skip range-bound ones.
rules.quote: If the aim in swing trading is to position ourselves in moves that are likely to move a large distance, we should be looking for markets that are trending.

rules.rule: Do not marry a favorite pair; re-scan every quarter for where the new trending opportunity is.
rules.quote: You want to be avoiding favorite markets in general for swing trading purposes.

rules.rule: Market-selection filter: at least 2 of the 4 asset classes (stocks, commodities, currencies, rates) must be trending (one of stocks/commodities and one of currencies/rates).
rules.quote: We want at least to have at least half of the four or two of them showing a profile where there's trending environments underway.

rules.rule: Stack the hallmarks (HTF trend, clear order flow, rates, COT, opposing PD arrays, seasonals, intermarket/SMT); more confluence, higher odds. Mostly non-price filters.
rules.quote: The larger amount of things on this list that I can accumulate to build the idea that my trade is valid, the more likely the trade does pan out.

rules.rule: Stock/call-option version, filter 1: the broad index must be poised to rally before any single stock is bought (the sell-watchlist video gives the mirror rule for shorts/puts).
rules.quote: Filter number one: the stock market as a whole must be poised to rally higher.

rules.rule: Equity seasonal buy window is February to May (calendar filter, not a clock). The seasonals dossier adds Oct-Dec bullish and May-Oct low magnitude, so cut leverage and option activity then.
rules.quote: we look for February to May for our buy programs for buying stock or stock options.

rules.rule: Highest-probability swing direction = Monthly, Weekly, Daily and 4H all aligned (all moving away from discount for buys / premium for sells).
rules.quote: When we're swing trading, the easiest and the most probable direction setups are when all monthly, weekly, daily, and four hour are in alignment.

rules.rule: On Monthly/Weekly classify the last 9-18 months as trending vs range-bound consolidation before looking for a setup.
rules.quote: On the monthly and weekly, you're looking for the 9 to 18 month market profile: are we in a trending environment or are we in a range-bound consolidation?

rules.rule: Draw on liquidity rule: whichever PD array spectrum price most recently reacted from, price is expected to seek the opposite spectrum (discount support -> premium targets).
rules.quote: The PD arrays that have been traded to or executed on most recently indicate the opposite PD array Spectrum will be reached for.

rules.rule: Directional side is taken from monthly market structure first.
rules.quote: You're going to be consulting the market structure on the monthly chart to determine what side of the marketplace you're going to be looking for.

rules.rule: For position trades the four asset classes (stocks, rates, commodities, currencies) should all confirm the outlook (intermarket filter; not price-only).
rules.quote: All four of them together (the stock market, interest rates, commodities, and currencies) should be confirming your general outlook on the marketplace.

rules.rule: A seasonal tendency only counts if the last two years' weekly price direction agrees with it; seasonals are a roadmap, not a trigger.
rules.quote: Look at these last two years: what was the underlying price direction on the weekly chart? Was it bullish or bearish? That's what qualifies the seasonal tendency.

rules.rule: Three-stage lifecycle: condition (HTF alignment + impulse/displacement away from a point of origin), staging (retracement into the dealing range), execution (expansion).
rules.quote: There is a condition first, then there's the stage portion of taking the trade, and then there's the execution when the market expands up to higher prices.

rules.rule: Bull market, M/W/D bullish: buy every daily (and equivalent 4H) bullish discount array: mitigation block, breaker, liquidity void, FVG, bullish OB, rejection block, old low/high.
rules.quote: You're going to buy all daily bullish discount arrays: that is a bullish mitigation block, bullish breaker, liquidity void, fair value gap, bullish order block, rejection block, and or an old low or high.

rules.rule: Nesting rule 1: if monthly+weekly bullish but daily is correcting, only buy daily discount arrays that sit at or inside a weekly discount array.
rules.quote: You're going to be buying daily bullish discount arrays at or nested in weekly discount arrays.

rules.rule: Nesting rule 2: if weekly is also correcting, the daily array must sit at or inside a monthly discount array.
rules.quote: Buying daily bullish discount arrays at or nested in the monthly discount array

rules.rule: Bear mirror of nesting rule 1 (monthly and weekly bearish, daily rallying): sell daily bearish premium arrays only at or inside weekly premium arrays.
rules.quote: When the monthly is bearish, the weekly is bearish, and the daily is bullish, that means there's a correction underway on the daily chart. You're going to sell daily bearish premium arrays at or nested in weekly premium arrays.

rules.rule: Bear mirror of nesting rule 2 (weekly and daily both rallying inside a bearish monthly): sell only at or inside monthly premium arrays.
rules.quote: The monthly being bearish, the weekly being bullish, and the daily being bullish: you're going to sell all daily bearish premium arrays at or nested in the monthly premium arrays.

rules.rule: Dealing range = point of origin to intermediate-term high of the impulse; the discount side of that range is where the buy arrays are taken.
rules.quote: We have our range defined by our point of origin and the intermediate term high prior to the retracement

rules.rule: Order-block definition used for the arrays: down candles = bank accumulation (bullish OB), up candles = distribution (bearish OB).
rules.quote: we measure bank accumulation by buying at down candles, and we measure bank distribution at up candles as resistance.

rules.rule: Frame swing levels on monthly and weekly PD arrays only; lower timeframes are used just to time entry.
rules.quote: With swing trades we're only focusing on framing the monthly and weekly levels ideally.

rules.rule: Trigger = price reaches a discernible discount array and shows displacement up off it (subjective: what counts as displacement).
rules.quote: What you're looking for is a discount array that has shown to induce buying and it's going to be evidenced by price moving higher

rules.rule: Month 05 limit-order variant: needs a fully CLOSED daily down-close candle (up-close for shorts) aligned with HTF flow; invalid while the candle is still forming.
rules.quote: The daily should post a bearish candle. The daily chart must close the candle with a down close, and it is not valid while the daily chart candle is trading and or forming.

rules.rule: Time the entry on the 4H chart at the monthly/weekly level to keep the stop small and maximize R.
rules.quote: Timing a four-hour entry on higher timeframe levels, that offers the maximum R multiples

rules.rule: LOW CONFIDENCE (single dossier, not corroborated by the other Month 06 dossiers): 'Million Dollar Swing' trigger = daily market structure shift with displacement.
rules.quote: Wait for the daily market structure shift. Do not try to catch the exact tick low. Let the market break a swing high with energetic displacement.

rules.rule: 2024 Charter Model 4 variant: early-week manipulation against the expected long-term road map is the convergence trigger (needs a weekday clock).
rules.quote: look for a convergence of both manipulation and price opposite to expected long-term road map

rules.rule: Timeframe split: setups and targets from Monthly/Weekly/Daily, execution on the 4H chart.
rules.quote: We're going to look for the setups on monthly and weekly and daily, but we'll execute on four-hour charts.

rules.rule: Buy limit placed at the close of the closed daily down candle (sell limit at the close of an up candle in a bearish trend).
rules.quote: And the buy limit is going to be placed at the bearish candle's close

rules.rule: Rationale: next session price is expected to dip below that close, so the limit fills at a deep discount.
rules.quote: When we use a buy limit entry at the close, what we're doing is the very next day or the next candle when it opens up, we're expecting price movement to move below that down candle's close

rules.rule: The limit candle must coincide with a daily PD array (OB, FVG traded into, liquidity void); no limits on random candles.
rules.quote: These conditions are best suited when we align them with a daily PD array: in other words if there's a bearish order block, if there's a gap that it's traded into, if it's filled in a void.

rules.rule: 2024 Model 4 position entry: sell at the OPEN of the monthly bearish order block, no lower-timeframe confirmation, during a bearish seasonal window.
rules.quote: bearish order Block in this case we're actually going to use the open to sell

rules.rule: LOW CONFIDENCE (uncorroborated): Million Dollar Swing entry on a daily retracement into the 62-79% OTE after the daily MSS, stop below the swing low.
rules.quote: Enter on the daily retracement into an Optimum Trade Entry (62% to 79% Fibonacci level), place your stop below the swing low, and let the trade run for weeks.

rules.rule: Use the 4H chart to shrink the stop (example 50-70 pips) while the target is the 200-600 pip monthly/weekly objective.
rules.quote: By having a four-hour, it reduces the ranges to a smaller, more conservative number in terms of what we can frame our risk around.

rules.rule: Month 08 variant for HTF entries: stop = 5-day average daily range from the entry (about 60-100 pips); no tiny stops on HTF ideas.
rules.quote: a 90 to 100 pip stop is relatively insignificant because you're looking for higher timeframe setups.

rules.rule: Position trade risk cap is 1% of equity per trade.
rules.quote: How much money should you be risking? No more than 1%

rules.rule: Month 06 sizing example: 1.5% risk, about 50 pip stop, 3:1 leverage, six trades a year (conflicts with the 1% cap).
rules.quote: Six trades, that's it. Six trades risking 1.5%, using 3 to 1 leverage, and about a 50 pip stop, you're more than doubling your equity every single year.

rules.rule: 2024 Model 4: when pyramiding, aggregate risk across all adds must stay under 1%, so the first entry risks less than 1%.
rules.quote: you don't want to exceed 1% that means if you have intentions of potentially adding to the position then you have to use less than 1% on your first entry

rules.rule: Longs target one of the opposing premium arrays (list in the quote); shorts mirror to discount arrays.
rules.quote: The idea is we're looking for something down in this list of arrays to target one of the premium arrays: mitigation block, breaker, liquidity void, fair value gap, bearish order block, rejection block, old high or historic low.

rules.rule: First draw from a deep discount/premium is equilibrium (50% of the recent range); many trades are just discount to equilibrium.
rules.quote: When markets are at a premium or at a discount, they're always going to initially look to rebalance, that means the equilibrium price point between the last recent range.

rules.rule: Monthly/weekly imbalances (price not traded at for weeks or months) are high-draw targets.
rules.quote: Price not traded at in recent weeks or months left in imbalance basis monthly and weekly: those levels are going to be a high draw on price.

rules.rule: Minimum reward:risk of 3:1 (prefers 5:1 and up); a separate Month 06 video says 30% accuracy is enough at 3:1.
rules.quote: Limiting setups to 3 to 1 reward to risk permits as low as 34% accuracy to be net profitable

rules.rule: 2024 Model 4 short targets old lows as the discount PD array.
rules.quote: using the same liquidity based Concepts looking at Old lows as our discount PD array

rules.rule: Bear leg objective is a discount array (bullish OB, FVG, old low).
rules.quote: anything that would be viewed as a discount or a buying scenario, that's what price will be looking to seek to find as a downside objective.

rules.rule: Trail stop behind intermediate swing lows on the daily chart as price expands (swing highs for shorts).
rules.quote: Trailing stops: as price continues to expand, you lock in profit by trailing stops behind intermediate swing lows on the daily chart.

rules.rule: Take partials at intermediate PD arrays and re-enter or pyramid on later daily retracements.
rules.quote: Scaling out: when price achieves intermediate-term PD arrays, you take partials and look to re-enter or pyramid on subsequent daily retracements.

rules.rule: Do not pick tops/bottoms; sync with the 3-4 month quarterly shift and take the middle (biggest) portion of the move.
rules.quote: We are trying to get in sync with that quarterly shift to get the meat in between, in other words the biggest portion of the move.

rules.rule: 2024 Model 4 pyramid rule: add only when price retraces to the dealing-range midpoint or into premium (shorts) / discount (longs).
rules.quote: at the midpoint or higher when price is in a premium and you can only pyramid in a premium

rules.rule: Take a partial on every pyramided tranche when the major liquidity objective is reached, then trail behind swing structure.
rules.quote: this would be where you take a partial on all three of them

rules.rule: 2024 Model 4 graduated stop reduction: at 25% of expected profit cut risk 25%, at 50% cut 50%, at 75% stop to breakeven.
