rules.quote: when we are in profit 25% of our expected objective stop loss can be reduced by 25%

rules.rule: 2017 variant (1h OTE swings): do not trail the stop; take partials and only trail once price leaves a consolidation.
rules.quote: leave your stop down here okay do not trail your stop-loss you want to be taking partials okay

rules.rule: 2017: swing trades bank about 50% at the first objective (day trades 75-80%).
rules.quote: for a swing trade you can take off like 50% leave the remaining 50% on

rules.rule: LOW CONFIDENCE (uncorroborated): Million Dollar Swing 30/30/40 scale-out with a daily-swing-low trail.
rules.quote: Scale out 30% at the first weekly objective, 30% at the second, and hold the remaining 40% with a trailing stop behind daily swing lows until the macro target is reached.

rules.rule: Do not buy daily arrays after a higher high is rejected with a market-structure break (bearish breaker forming).
rules.quote: If you see a daily post a higher high and then it's rejected and it breaks down with its market structure, you're probably looking at a development of a bearish breaker and you do not want to be buying against that type of condition.

rules.rule: Mirror: do not sell daily premium arrays after a lower low is rejected (bullish breaker).
rules.quote: You're going to avoid selling daily premium arrays if the daily has just posted a lower low and rejected — this is going to be seen as a bullish breaker.

rules.rule: Same breaker test on the weekly: skip weekly discount arrays after a rejected weekly higher high.
rules.quote: Avoid buying weekly discount arrays if the weekly has just posted a higher high and rejected that price high

rules.rule: Obvious trading range = no directional edge; skip.
rules.quote: If a market is confined to an obvious trading range, this does not indicate it has high odds for a directional setup.

rules.rule: Fail any static filter and the trade is passed on, no exceptions.
rules.quote: when the trade setups fail the filtering process, the trade is passed on. Period. No exceptions.

rules.rule: Swing holding period is two weeks or longer (same lecture states 200-500+ pip objectives).
rules.quote: swing trading is a form of intermediate term trading with trade durations of two weeks or longer in time.

rules.rule: Position-trade horizon is about one quarter (the 3-4 month quarterly shift).
rules.quote: As I mentioned in this mentorship, my time horizon is about three months. I think it's pretty much as realistic as you're going to get for position trading.

rules.rule: 2020 variant of the timeframe matrix: swing = Daily/4H/1H premise (position = Monthly/Weekly/Daily); differs from the Month 06 swing matrix.
rules.quote: as a swing trader your premise for breaking down market structure will be comprised of a look at the daily the 4-hour and the one-hour chart

rules.rule: 2017 swing method (daily 10/20 EMA stacking, 1h OTE entries) was claimed to work on all pairs/markets/asset classes.
rules.quote: I'm going to be using this currency pair this works on all currency pairs all markets all asset classes as well

rules.rule: Stock sell-watchlist: narrow the Dow 30 to 2-4 names (lower highs while the index rallies, weekly trending down); buy-side mirror uses higher-low stocks.
rules.quote: We'll be trying to narrow the selection down to two to four companies during the stock selection process.

index_bond_session.summary: ICT's Oct 2022 (Month 10) clock-based session framework for ZB and ES/NQ/YM: mark the 60-minute opening range and pre-market extremes, expect the AM session to print the day's high or low, enter stop-run (Turtle Soup) or SMT-divergence reversals, hold the AM leg to about 10:30-11:00 and the PM leg toward the 3:00 PM bond close, and read the day type (trend, consolidation, or one of the projected-range profiles) from higher-timeframe PD arrays and the economic calendar.
index_bond_session.needs_clock: Yes, heavily. Every component is defined by New York clock times: the 08:20 CME open, bond AM 07:00-12:00 and PM 12:00-15:00, the index true day 09:30-16:00, the opening range 09:30-10:30, the 05:00-09:30 pre-market reference window, the AM high around 10:30-11:00, the lunch lull 11:00-13:00, the PM leg 13:00-16:00, the noon-3 PM SMT window and the 3:00 PM bond close. It cannot run on 24/7 synthetic indices as designed, because those have no cash open, no bond close and no real participation volume. The premise that the AM session has the largest volume and therefore forms the high or low of the day does not exist on a synthetic feed. Only the price-delivery sub-pieces could be ported: a range-extreme sweep followed by a run to the opposite extreme; SMT-style divergence between two correlated synthetic series; a volatility squeeze followed by range expansion; a 50% equilibrium target; premium/discount array nesting. They would need an arbitrary session definition (for example a fixed UTC reset) and would have to be tested rather than assumed. The volume-divergence rule needs real exchange volume, and the calendar-based day-type filter has no equivalent.
index_bond_session.how_to_code: 1) Clock: convert to America/New_York. Bonds: CME open 08:20, AM 07:00-12:00 (it may end about 11:00), PM 12:00-15:00, hard end 15:00. Indices: day 09:30-16:00, opening range (OR) 09:30-10:30 with the 09:30-10:00 sub-window as the volume node, lunch 11:00-13:00, PM 13:00-16:00, SMT window 12:00-15:00. 2) Levels: ORH/ORL = highest high and lowest low of the 5m bars in [09:30,10:30) for indices (the dossier describes ZB as 60 minutes from 08:20, i.e. [08:20,09:20), without a verbatim quote, so treat that as unconfirmed). Pre-market PMH/PML = relative swing highs and lows of ES/NQ/YM in [05:00,09:30). 3) AM setup (indices): after 09:30, flag a sweep when one index trades beyond a prior swing low (the pre-market low or ORL) while at least one of the other two holds a higher low. Entry A (aggressive): buy the sweeping index at or after the breach of the old low (Turtle Soup). Entry B (conservative, from the dossier overview and trade table only): a buy stop above the high of the last down-close candle on the stronger index after the SMT is confirmed. Mirror for shorts. 4) PM setup: same SMT test on swing extremes formed between 12:00 and 15:00, executed on ES only. 5) Bond volume divergence: at a new swing low or high compare that bar's volume with the previous extreme bar's volume. If it is lower or not higher, flag exhaustion and look for a run toward the OR boundary stops. Thresholds are not given. 6) Stops (from the dossier trade tables, not quoted): a few ticks beyond the sweep wick (for example ZB entry 154'21 with the stop at 154'18, and entry 153'29 with the stop at 153'25), or beyond the down-close candle low. 7) Targets (partly quoted): the opposite OR boundary, an overhead FVG fill (ZB 154'13), the 10:30-11:00 time exit for AM trades, 50% of the day's range on consolidation days, and the 15:00 bond close for PM or trend holds. 8) PM target filter: if the AM extreme touched or sat on a 4h/daily array, do not use it as a PM sweep target and use only the lunch highs or lows. If it did not, the PM may run the AM extreme and reverse. 9) Day type (partly subjective): squeeze = N consecutive daily bars with small range after a tap of an HTF discount/premium array, which implies a trend-day expansion. A high-impact report on a later day, price sitting at an HTF array or at the dealing-range equilibrium, or neutral daily/4h flow implies a consolidation profile and should skip trend entries. Classify AM and PM extremes into the six named profiles (the other two of the stated eight are not in the dossier). Subjective parts: how obvious an SMT must be, what counts as a relative high or low, identification of HTF PD arrays, the squeeze's N and range threshold, the meaning of an energetic ZB move, the day-type classification, and the cutoff for 'volume lower than the prior extreme'.
index_bond_session.changes_over_time: 1) Opening-range length changed. In Oct 2022 (ORbtHOUzAIM) the index opening range is 09:30-10:30, with the first 30 minutes as the volume node. By April 2024 (evM3prB_JR4) he says "the opening range is between 9:30 in the morning and 10:00 a.m. eastern standard time" (the dossier says he rejects 5/15-minute windows). In March 2026 (6DuByzKLDsc) he says "The first 30 minutes is opening range" and calls 09:30-10:30 "your first hour's dealing range". So the 2022 60-minute opening range is later split into a 30-minute OR and a 60-minute first-hour dealing range. The 2026 videos also add a RTH Opening Range Gap with consequent encroachment (RY67bW2UhxY) and a 10:00-11:00 Silver Bullet window, which are separate models. 2) AM/PM boundaries differ by market. Bonds: AM 07:00-12:00 (it may end about 11:00) and PM 12:00-15:00 (JpV-J31mxhg). Indices: AM trend 09:30-11:00, lunch 11:00-13:00, PM 13:00-16:00 (qZg_5bac518, yWBxZsbmK1U). Feb 2023 (ALMsQytQ1fg) puts the PM expansion at 13:30-15:00. The 2023 workshop dossier (rx15_eN9sxI) puts the ZB focus at 07:00-09:30. The 2020 ZB trade dossier (YMt87VQRpNM) shows 08:30-11:00, and in 2017 (uE-aaP16nOw) he said "the New York is going to be seven o'clock in the morning to ten o'clock in the morning". 3) 'True day' is used differently. Month 10 ORbtHOUzAIM defines the index true day as 09:30-16:00. Month 8 (_2nUKLAD9ig) says "Every day at 12:00 AM midnight New York time begins the IPDA true day", ending at the 3:00 PM bond close. 4) The 3 PM close is described two ways. qZg_5bac518 says the market makes its high or low at the 3:00 PM bond close relative to the AM session. The same dossier's paraphrase says the 15:00-16:00 final hour delivers the opposite extreme into the close, which sits uneasily with that. Month 8 (_2nUKLAD9ig) calls post-3 PM something to avoid. 5) The lunch hour is avoided in 2022 (yWBxZsbmK1U, per the dossier paraphrase) but in 2023 he describes it as a trading window: "all my focus goes to New York lunch hour, trading the run-on stops taking place on stock index futures" (rx15_eN9sxI). 6) The projected-range lecture (P5pyzmgZA1s) says "eight ways" but the dossier names only six profiles. Its trade table also calls the June 22, 2017 short a consolidation AM rally / PM decline, while the entry is described as made during the morning rally into a premium array. 7) Dossier quality caveat. In the Month 10 dossiers only some 'Rules He States' cells contain real quotation marks. Several key rules are dossier paraphrase with no verbatim text: the ZB 60-minute opening range from 08:20, trend vs consolidation session continuation or reversal, the reversal trigger condition, the bond timeframe hierarchy, and the FVG exit rule. No stop-loss rule has a verbatim quote at all, so stops come only from the trade tables. Many quoted cells contain '...' gaps, so parts were quoted from one contiguous side of each gap, and a few lose the second half of the sentence. 8) Volume statements are exchange-futures specific. CGbSpa_9Z9Y contrasts them with spot FX, and a model relying on volume cannot be reproduced on feeds without real volume.
index_bond_session.markets: 30-Year Treasury Bond futures (ZB; 1/32 tick = $31.25) and the equity-index triad E-mini S&P 500 (ES, 'spoos'), Nasdaq 100 (NQ) and Dow (YM). The triad is used for SMT confirmation, with execution usually in the S&P. Intermarket confirmation comes from DXY and USD/JPY (bond-trend video). The 13 trades counted come from the dossier trade tables: 4 ZB (CGbSpa 1 long, JpV 1 long, RgpxhuVp5Xg 1 range-scalp short, S0ouOvtjV2I 1 long) and 9 index (ORbtHOUzAIM 2, qZg_5bac518 2, wWCKTEhVp2o 2, P5pyzmgZA1s 1, yWBxZsbmK1U 2). A further stand-aside example (pre-FOMC, RgpxhuVp5Xg) is not counted as a trade. Most examples are illustrative; two are dated live reviews from June 22 and 23, 2017 (ES short, consolidation AM rally / PM decline). Bond Mega-Trades (At43V93rnDQ) is a separate multi-month model and is excluded.

rules.rule: Bond trend-day precondition. A run of small daily ranges (volatility squeeze) that has just traded down into a higher-timeframe discount array is the trigger to expect range expansion and professional accumulation. The dossier overview says discount or premium, so the short side is the mirror. Do not fade the breakout from the squeeze (dossier warning, not quoted).
rules.quote: if these small ranges have just recently traded down to a discount array, that's our trigger

rules.rule: Bond consolidation-day filter. High or medium impact US reports due on a later trading day create a dead space in ZB (the consequence is stated in the second half of the sentence, not quoted). Expect chop around the 50% equilibrium, do not chase breakouts, and stand aside.
rules.quote: Economic calendars: if we see high to medium impact U.S. reports due to release on another trading day later

rules.rule: Index days are pre-classified into one of his projected-range profiles before trading. The dossier says eight but names only six: two-session up close, two-session down close, AM rally/PM reversal, AM decline/PM reversal, consolidation AM rally/PM decline, consolidation AM decline/PM rally. The profile depends on daily and 4h order flow and on whether the AM session reaches an opposing HTF PD array (these conditions are dossier paraphrase, not quoted).
rules.quote: By far and large these eight ways of projecting the range that I'm going to show you in this teaching will pretty much fit the bill on most days.

rules.rule: Index futures: the first 30 minutes of cash trading (09:30-10:00 NY) carries the largest morning volume, so expect the high or low of the day to be set there.
rules.quote: 9:30 to 10:00 has the largest volume of the day typically for the morning session, and that creates usually the high or low of the day.

rules.rule: Bonds: the AM session has the largest volume of the day. The second half of the same sentence (not quoted) says it therefore generally forms the high or low of the day, so the AM session is where to look for the daily extreme.
rules.quote: The AM session has a built-in advantage because it generally will see the largest volume of the day

rules.rule: Intermarket bias. ZB leads. When the rate market moves energetically it triggers sponsorship in the other markets. The dossier says a ZB rally (falling yields) lines up with a weaker DXY and a falling USD/JPY, which is paraphrase and not quoted.
rules.quote: when the interest rate market kicks off and it's allowed to move energetically, that's going to be the trigger for sponsorship.

rules.rule: Consolidation-day bias. After price reaches a higher-timeframe PD array, do not assume an immediate reversal. Expect digestion at the midpoint or a retrace to equilibrium.
rules.quote: don't always expect an immediate reversal; price can consolidate at that midpoint or retrace back to an equilibrium price point.

rules.rule: Index opening range = 09:30-10:30 NY (60 minutes). Its high and low are the stop pools that get raided. For ZB the dossier overview describes a 60-minute range from the 08:20 CME open, but that carries no verbatim quote.
rules.quote: We're delineating the opening range: 9:30 to 10:30 AM New York time

rules.rule: Pre-market reference. Mark the relative highs and lows between 05:00 and 09:30 NY on each index (ES, NQ, YM) and compare them across the three. These are the liquidity levels the 09:30 open runs.
rules.quote: Between the 5:00 AM New York time and 9:30 equities open New York time you're going to be looking for relative lows and relative highs and just compare them.

rules.rule: Intraday index logic is stop-hunting. Map where the stops sit (opening-range extremes, pre-market and lunch highs and lows, prior session extremes) and expect price to be delivered to them.
rules.quote: On an intraday basis you have to understand it's all about liquidity and where the stops are

rules.rule: AM SMT trigger. Among ES/NQ/YM, the index that trades below the old low while the others hold higher lows is the Turtle Soup candidate (bullish). Mirror for highs.
rules.quote: your eye should go right to that one that's making a lower low and identify that as Turtle Soup

rules.rule: PM SMT trigger. Between noon and 3:00 PM NY, one index failing to confirm the other indices' lower low is the divergence signal. The bracketed 'or higher high' in the dossier is the mirror.
rules.quote: one index is going to fail to confirm a lower low

rules.rule: Bond volume divergence. A lower low should come with a higher volume bar. When it does not, expect exhaustion and a reversal. The dossier trade table pairs this with a stop run beyond the opening range. It needs real exchange volume.
rules.quote: price making a lower low, that lower low should have been met with a higher bar on volume. This is a sign of impending reversal.

rules.rule: Aggressive entry: buy the stop-running (lagging) index below the old low, i.e. Turtle Soup. The conservative entry (a buy stop above the last down-close candle on the stronger index after SMT is confirmed) appears only in the dossier overview and trade table with no verbatim quote.
rules.quote: buy it below the old low.

rules.rule: Use the triad only as confirmation. Once the crack appears across all three, take the trade in the S&P only, not in the Dow or the Nasdaq.
rules.quote: If I see that crack among all three, my trade's going to be taken in the S&P

rules.rule: Wide opening range: after one side is raided, the objective is the stops on the opposite end of the opening range (boundary to boundary).
rules.quote: With the extension or long wide ranges in opening range for spoos, that will give us a range to reach back into and look for stops on the opposite end.

rules.rule: Time target for a full-day trend hold: the 3:00 PM bond close.
rules.quote: At least try to aim for holding until three o'clock Bond close New York time if at all possible.

rules.rule: The 3:00 PM bond close is where the day's high or low, relative to what the AM session printed, usually forms. Treat it as the PM exit or reversal time.
rules.quote: As soon as the bond market closes at 3:00 PM New York time, that's usually when the market makes its high or low in respective terms to what was seen in the AM session.

rules.rule: PM liquidity target depends on the AM session. If the AM session reached an HTF premium array, the PM will probably only run the lunch-hour highs. The other branch (not quoted here) is that without an HTF array tag, the PM can run the intraday high and then reverse.
rules.quote: If there's a higher time frame premium array that AM session hit, then it's likely that it won't go back up there because they've already defended that level and it may just want to run the lunchtime hour highs

rules.rule: AM trade: hold ideally to 10:30-11:00 NY, then expect consolidation or retracement into the lunch hour. The text after 'morning New York time' (not quoted) says to anticipate that.
rules.quote: We'll be holding for again ideally around 10:30 to 11:00 o'clock in the morning New York time

rules.rule: PM trade: after the 1:00 PM rally begins, hold at least until about 2:00 PM.
rules.quote: holding for again around two o'clock minimum.

rules.rule: On consolidation days or news dead spaces, stand aside. Accept missed moves in order to preserve capital for the expansion that follows.
rules.quote: You already should have given yourself permission to miss moves

rules.rule: No SMT unless the divergence is obvious. Do not force a Turtle Soup when the three indices move in lockstep.
rules.quote: When it's not obvious, assume it's not there

rules.rule: Nested HTF filter for PM stop-run trades. If the AM low is anchored to a 15m/60m (and HTF) discount array, do not expect the PM to take out the AM low, so a PM trade that depends on that sweep is invalid. The opposite branch (not quoted) is that if the AM low formed above an HTF discount array, expect a lower run in the PM.
rules.quote: If the AM session bounces into the lunch off of a higher time frame nested level that's also seen on a 15 or a 60 minute discount array, then we don't expect the intraday low to be taken out in the afternoon session

rules.rule: Markets and order of the day (2023 recollection): FX overnight, then ZB in the morning session, overlapping with index futures, then lunch-hour index stop runs, then the PM index session. The dossier lists charts on 5m and 15m for index examples and daily, 4h and 2h for bond context, but the timeframe-hierarchy rule has no verbatim quote.
rules.quote: My trading day would move from Forex overnight and then go into bond trading in the morning session, and then I would either do an overlap with index futures or finish my day in Forex.

rules.rule: His two home markets are ZB and S&P futures (spoos). He rarely traded both at once (the rest of the sentence, not quoted, says they are diametrically opposed).
rules.quote: I started as a Treasury bond trader and SP futures trader those were my two markets of choice

rules.rule: Bond clock anchor: the 08:20 NY CME open is the start of heavy New York bank and trader order flow in ZB.
rules.quote: 8:20 AM is the CME opening

rules.rule: Bond split session: PM session = 12:00-15:00 NY. The dossier gives the AM session as 07:00-12:00.
rules.quote: The New York PM session is defined by noon New York time to 3:00 PM New York time

rules.rule: Bond AM session ends at noon, but can end as early as about 11:00.
rules.quote: noon ends the AM session, just know that it can end earlier around 11:00 AM.

rules.rule: Index futures true day = 09:30-16:00 NY cash session. Do not use 24-hour Globex bars as the day.
rules.quote: True day for the Nasdaq / S&P E-mini futures is the same: beginning at 9:30 AM and closing at 4:00 PM New York time.

rules.rule: The AM trend starts looking for index setups at the 09:30 cash open. The rest of the sentence (not quoted) says the highs form around 10:30 NY.
rules.quote: At 9:30 AM the equities market open, that's when we start looking for our indices

rules.rule: Index PM trend window runs from about 13:00 to the 16:00 close. The lunch lull is roughly 11:00-13:00 (per the yWBxZsbmK1U dossier summary).
rules.quote: It begins around 1:00 PM New York time and extends all the way to 4:00 PM at the close.

rules.rule: PM SMT window: compare the index highs and lows formed between noon and 15:00 NY.
rules.quote: We're looking for the highs and the lows between noon and 3:00 PM New York time

rules.rule: After 13:00 NY the PM leg starts. Compare SMT at the highs (or lows) at that point.
rules.quote: After one o'clock is seen in New York, we would anticipate some measure of a rally again and we would be comparing SMT divergence at the highs

micro_scalping.summary: Sub-minute (5s to 1m) limit-order scalps on index futures: buy or sell a fresh order block, FVG or volume imbalance, with a tiny stop (about 1.25 to 4 handles), aiming at the nearest liquidity pool. Add size (usually 5 to 6 contracts per add, up to 15 to 18 in total) when displacement runs away, then recover costs with a partial or a stop move and trail the rest.
micro_scalping.needs_clock: The core mechanism is price-only, so it could run on 24/7 synthetic indices. It needs displacement, a fresh OB/FVG/volume imbalance, an equal-high/low or swing liquidity target, pyramiding on new arrays, and a costs-covered stop. Time is context, not a rule. The videos ran at 06:50 to 08:50 ET and at 12:04 ET, with no stated killzone (only the pinball drill uses 9:30 to 10:00). The Calub trade also used the New Week Opening Gap and pre-market buyside, which depend on the calendar. On synthetics these would be replaced by swing or equal highs and lows, and the 15 to 20 handle room would be scaled by ATR. Costs are part of the model (costs-recovered partial), so the spread must be modelled. Dossier text says quick scoping is for active volatility, which can be coded as an ATR or displacement filter.
micro_scalping.how_to_code: 1) Work on a 5s, 15s, 30s or 1m series. 2) Detect displacement: a run of 1 to 3 same-direction candles with body above k times ATR(n) that leaves a 3-candle FVG (gap between candle 1 and candle 3) or a volume imbalance between consecutive bodies. Mark the last opposite-close candle or series before it as the OB, with its mean threshold at 50%. 3) Pick the target: the nearest opposing liquidity, meaning equal highs or lows within a tick tolerance ('too smooth'), a swing high or low, or a session extreme. Require reward of at least about 3x the stop. For Calub's model, also require roughly 15 to 20 NQ handles of room, scaled by ATR. 4) Entry: a resting limit at the OB mean threshold, just inside the candle body, or at the FVG edge. Triggers are a retest of the array, an immediate rebalance (a one-candle retracement into the new gap), or a change in state of delivery at the array. 5) Stop: beyond the OB mean threshold, the FVG high or low, or the sweep candle's extreme. In the videos this was 1.25 points in ES and 1.75 to 4.25 handles in NQ. 6) Pyramid: while open and in profit, when a new displacement leg prints a new OB or FVG in the trade direction, or the price reclaims an FVG, place an add limit there. Adds were 5 or 6 contracts on a base of 5 to 12, giving a total of 1.5x to 3x. After the add, move the stop to the FVG high or the add and blended price plus costs. 7) Exit: take a partial that recovers costs when the first structural low or high breaks. Take tiered limits at liquidity pools (for example 10 of 15, with 2 to 5 runners). Trail the stop beyond each new FVG, OB or inversion FVG. Hit-and-run mode exits everything at the first pool. 8) Invalidation: a body close beyond the CE of the supporting gap or inversion FVG (a wick is allowed, the 'Mohawk'), the stop being hit, or choppy tape without displacement. Subjective parts: what counts as displacement and 'speed', which candle is the OB, how smooth 'too smooth' is, which pool is the first logical target, when to add, and how much size to leave as runners. The 15 to 20 handle figure is ambiguous.
micro_scalping.changes_over_time: 1) Evolution. Dec 2022 'quick scoping' is a 1m FVG scalp after a sweep (flNNEKKcYkM). Its rule rows are dossier paraphrases (for example 'Operational scalping rule'), not his words, so none are quoted. In 2022 episodes 2 and 3 he says high-frequency algorithms work on 1 to 3 minute charts, and that sub-minute charts are 45, 30 or 15 seconds. Sep 2023 shows 15s entries with a pyramid to 3 contracts. Jan 2024 uses a 5s chart. May 2024 is 'micro-scalping without bias' on 15s, and the 30s premium-wick short follows 2 days later. Aug 2024 brings the Calub's Model range note, and Sep 2024 brings 1m grey pools (volume imbalance) with 'Costs & Risk Covered'. In 2026 he teaches Calub with a 1m inversion-FVG long and a 15s ES review where bodies respect the OB and the inversion FVG CE 'to the tick'. 2) Bias. May 2024 says trade without a bias, while the Sep 2024 micro-vs-mini lecture dossier row warns that 15s charts are only for entry refinement inside higher-timeframe PD arrays, not standalone. 3) Partials. aaKO-eu-tQ4 gives two legitimate styles: hit-and-run takes no partials, a model trader scales out and trails. Trade rows show both (flNN exits fully; HUxK takes 13 of 15 off). 4) Stop handling. In 2024 the stop goes to costs-covered within minutes. The dossier summary of the 2023 'One Trading Setup For Life' video (vuBRMFhFZAY, a summary, not a verbatim quote) says not to trail stops tightly behind shallow 15s wicks and to keep the stop below the structural low. Stop anchors also differ: OB mean threshold, FVG high, or under the inversion FVG. 5) Calub/Caleb's model. The 2024 range note says 15 to 20 handles, and it is ambiguous whether this is a minimum. A 2026 dossier (e6XwTK4hVqI) quotes 'at least 30 to 40 handles' for high-resistance scalping, but the speaker context is unclear. The 2026 Caleb's model rule there is about the first presented FVG after displacement versus the 9:30 candle. 6) Evidence quality. Most start videos are unvoiced, so their 'Verbatim Quote' cells are chart annotations (short phrases, some ending in '...' in the source). 'Mohawk' means a small wick past CE in VElIka5sk0E and kRShZKZlvJ4, but the AxNoqk5Vx8o dossier uses 'Mohawks' as a label on volume-imbalance boxes. 7) Trade-table values (stops, targets, P&L) come from dossier tables and carry some inconsistencies (for example My9wQ8 initial stop 5184.50 versus 5185.00).
micro_scalping.markets: NQ futures (mostly), ES futures once at midday (My9wQ8_UtZk, 12:04 to 12:18 ET), and MNQ in the micro-versus-mini lecture. Chart timeframes are 5s, 15s, 30s and 1m. Nothing was shown on forex, crypto or single stocks, and in 2022 he declined to co-sign crypto. Trade count of 11: the 8 start videos give 9 (My9wQ8 1, aaKO 2, HUxK 1, zKCC 1, AxNo 1 pyramided position, tjnir 1, flNN 1, k2QL 1), plus VODMCdDnMs8 (5s) and the DnuCB5Stk-0 pinball drill row. Adjacent sub-minute pyramid trades that no keyword hit (fRS8m-wShIo 30s, CRE7Pmch5G0 15s, vuBRMFhFZAY 15s, HM2M9a4OEFQ 15s) are not counted.

rules.rule: Calub's Model (NQ, 15s) is only worth taking when there is roughly 15 to 20 handles of room between the entry array and the liquidity target. His own on-chart note, not a spoken rule. It is ambiguous whether this is a minimum or just the range of that trade: entry 19,590.75 to buyside 19,606.00 is 15.25 handles.
rules.quote: The 'Range' between Entry to Liquidity is 15-20 handles in NQ

rules.rule: No higher-timeframe directional bias is needed. Trade the two-way liquidity that is on the chart, buying one side then reversing to the other.
rules.quote: so you can trade without a bias you can trade the liquidity that's available

rules.rule: Work between opposing local liquidity pools. Buy a discount array to run the buyside, then sell short a premium array to run the sellside beneath. Reverse straight away after the first target.
rules.quote: buying in here running the buy side there then going back in selling short and getting the liquidity under

rules.rule: Clean, 'too smooth' equal highs or lows are engineered retail stop pools. They are read as the magnet or target, not as support or resistance. Annotation on the ES 15s chart.
rules.quote: Too Smooth

rules.rule: Price changes direction at a PD array (an order block retest). He calls this the change in the state of delivery, and it validates the immediate re-entry.
rules.quote: that's the change in the state of delivery right here

rules.rule: On the 15s chart, a one-candle retracement into a freshly formed gap (an immediate rebalance) is the low-risk trigger just before momentum accelerates. It is also the point where he adds.
rules.quote: that's an immediate rebalance watch how it runs up

rules.rule: Use resting limit orders, not market orders. Place them at or just below the candle bodies of the reference array, not out at the wick extremes.
rules.quote: that's the reason why I'm drawing my limit order just below the bodies of these candles

rules.rule: On a 5s chart, enter at the 50% mean threshold of the order block. Shorts go at a bearish OB, and the ES 15s short also went off a bearish OB.
rules.quote: mean threshold of the order block and we'll do extensions

rules.rule: Variant: on the 30s chart, short inside the upper wick of a prior high, because wicks are treated as gaps (premium wick). NQ pre-market, 15 contracts at 18,178.00. Annotation only.
rules.quote: Wicks are 'Gaps'

rules.rule: For an order-block entry, put the stop just beyond the order block's mean threshold (50%). The risk on these trades was 1.75 to 4.25 handles in NQ and 1.25 points in ES.
rules.quote: the stop below mean threshold that would be here

rules.rule: After pyramiding into a runaway move, anchor the stop on the breakaway FVG high (ES short, stop 5184.25). The wording in the dossier is 'Stop Loss Is FVG High'.
rules.quote: Stop Loss Is FVG High

rules.rule: Aim for the nearest opposing liquidity pool, such as the 5m smooth lows. Delivery into it should show speed and not creep.
rules.quote: Looking for speed as it probes the 5 minute Smooth Lows For Sellside Liquidity

rules.rule: Two exit styles. A pure hit-and-run scalper takes no partials and exits everything at the first logical liquidity level. A model trader scales out and trails runners.
rules.quote: if you are going to be hard and fast and you want to be a surgical hit and run type scalper you don't take any partials you just take the first logical level of liquidity

rules.rule: Size on: add contracts when price reclaims a bearish FVG and accelerates into a low. Pyramids seen: 5 to 10 to 15 in ES, 12 to 18 in NQ 1m, 10 to 15 in NQ 30s.
rules.quote: I'll add more there because that's just too good to pass up: reclaim bearish fair value gap for those who are wondering, should be breaking this low accelerating pretty hard

rules.rule: Size off: when the first structural low breaks, take off enough to recover costs (5 contracts) and leave the rest open to run into the breakaway.
rules.quote: I'm going to take off five there because we broke a low and costs are recovered; I want to see this one stay open because that'll be breakaway

rules.rule: After adding, raise the stop to the blended or add price so that costs and risk are covered. NQ 1m: stop moved to 19,708.25 after the 6-lot add (annotation).
rules.quote: Costs & Risk Covered

rules.rule: Trail the stop to just beyond the inversion FVG that is supporting the trade. If price comes back to that level the thesis is gone, so get out. 1m NQ long, 2026.
rules.quote: Raise the stop up just underneath this inversion fair value gap now, cuz if it goes there, I don't want to be a part of this anymore.

rules.rule: Candle bodies must not close beyond the 50% (consequent encroachment) of the supporting gap. A wick through it is allowed.
rules.quote: And there's the halfway point right there consequent encroachment. It can wick down below it. We don't want to see it leave a body down there. Otherwise, it makes it more difficult for the market to continue

rules.rule: An inversion FVG should defend its boundary and never reach its halfway point. Reaching it makes the array suspect.
rules.quote: Inversion fair value Gap it should never reach the halfway point but defend the boundary.

rules.rule: A small wick past consequent encroachment is the 'Mohawk', and it is permissible. Only a body beyond it (per the 2026 rule above) breaks the array.
rules.quote: Here's consequent encroachment in the fair value Gap it dropped down into it hit it went a little bit past that what's the Mohawk it means it's permissible we allow for that.

rules.rule: The charts are sub-minute. High-frequency algorithms use market structure on 3, 2 and 1 minute charts and often on 45, 30 and 15 second charts.
rules.quote: high frequency trading algorithms will use market structure on a three minute two minute and one minute chart many times sub one minute that would be like 45 second 30 second 15 second intervals

rules.rule: A 5s chart is not random noise. A short at the OB mean threshold with pyramiding on that chart made more than 10:1 on about $150 of risk.
rules.quote: I'm looking at this little area right there on a 5-second chart that's supposed to be just noise; that's funny

rules.rule: The 15s chart gives plenty of FVGs to get into a move with precision, as a refinement inside higher-timeframe arrays (MNQ/NQ lecture).
rules.quote: With a 15-second chart there's plenty of fair value gaps to get into the move with precision.

rules.rule: ES is preferred for clean body-respect on the 15s chart, and NQ is his usual vehicle. The micro-scalps were shown on NQ and ES futures only.
rules.quote: More professionals trade S&P than the Nasdaq, simply because it's much more cleaner in terms of its price action

rules.rule: Only the pinball-drill variant has a stated clock: use the first presented FVG between 9:30 and 10:00 as the entry framework. The recorded micro-scalps ran from 06:50 to 12:18 ET with no stated session rule.
rules.quote: First present the fair value gap between 9:30 and 10:00 then using that as your entry framework.

news_trades.summary: Trade the delivery that follows scheduled high-impact news (NFP/CPI/PPI at 08:30 NY, FOMC at 14:00 and 14:30, Jackson Hole) by letting the first spike sweep one side, then entering a retest of an inversion FVG or first-presented FVG with a far target and early partials. The 2023 Ma Deuce variant instead sits in an IFVG before 08:30.
news_trades.needs_clock: Yes, heavily. The trigger is a scheduled external event, so it needs a calendar and a New York clock: 08:30 for NFP/CPI/PPI, 14:00 statement and 14:30 conference for FOMC, 10:00 for Fed-chair or data events. It also uses fixed windows: the 07:00-08:30 range anchor, a 15-20 minute post-release wait, the 14:40-14:50 FOMC sweet spot, the 10:00 resume, the 09:30 open, and the Wednesday 11:00 NFP-week lockout. It cannot run unchanged on 24/7 synthetic indices, which have no news events. Only the price-delivery core could be ported: a range, a first sweep (Judas/first run), a body-close inversion of a prior FVG, a retest entry, a far target, partials and a ratcheted stop. For synthetics the 'event' would have to be a proxy such as a volatility-expansion bar or a fixed clock bar. The dossiers give no evidence that this works without a real news catalyst.
news_trades.how_to_code:
Inputs: a calendar of event timestamps in NY time (NFP/CPI/PPI 08:30; FOMC statement 14:00 and conference 14:30; FOMC minutes 14:00; Jackson Hole days and any 10:00 Fed-chair speech), 1m OHLC for NQ, and daily/4H/15m for context.

1) Pre-event frame. Take the highest high and lowest low of the 1m bars from 07:00 to the event minute (08:30). Mark them as buy-side and sell-side liquidity. For FOMC also mark the unraided daily highs/lows of the last 2 days. Extension levels are fib standard deviations of the 07:00-08:30 range at -1.0, -1.5, -2.0 and -2.5, drawn low to high. Event Horizon is the 50% of two chosen swing extremes. Subjective: which swings he picks, and the required confluence.

2) Stand-aside gating. No entries from the event minute for 15-20 minutes (2026), or until 09:30 (2022) or 10:00 (2023). For FOMC, no entries 14:00-14:40; the practical entry window is 14:40-14:50 (2023 said wait to 14:45). No trading Thursday/Friday of NFP week or after Wednesday 11:00; Monday of NFP week is allowed. Do not use pre-release entries except the Ma Deuce variant.

3) First-run / Judas detection. After the event bar, price takes one side of the pre-event range, wick or body. Then it closes back inside the range or into a fresh FVG against the sweep. Trade direction is opposite the first run unless the higher-timeframe draw says otherwise. Subjective: the higher-timeframe bias and whether a poke is a 'sweep' or a 'run'.

4) Setup arrays. FVG: 3-candle gap. IFVG: a prior FVG whose far boundary is closed through by a candle body (a body close is required; wicks do not count). First-presented FVG: the first FVG formed after the event minute or 09:30. Entry trigger is a retest of the IFVG or first-presented FVG in which bodies hold the gap's lower/upper half and fail to reach its consequent encroachment (50%). Place a limit entry inside the gap, with an optional lower-timeframe confirmation. Subjective: whether a gap 'qualifies', and body-versus-wick tolerance (he allows a one-tick overshoot).

5) FOMC two-stage logic. Stage 1 = the move after 14:00: pierce of the daily high or low, then a reversal and a short or long off the first FVG after 14:00. The stop is beyond the 14:00 extreme and the target is a daily volume imbalance. Stage 2 = after 14:30, the reversal from that imbalance toward the opposite intraday extreme. The Sept 2026 variant instead takes a single 14:40-14:50 entry on a retest of an inefficiency that existed before the 14:00 sweep.

6) Stop. Beyond the IFVG or gap far edge, or beyond the swing or news extreme; a 4H FVG boundary on high-volatility news. After displacement, move to break-even plus costs, then trail beyond wick consequent encroachment, the IFVG, or the new swing. Never move the stop back.

7) Targets and sizing. First partial at the 50% (CE) of the dealing range or the Event Horizon midpoint; second at the 25% quadrant; the remainder at an opposing array such as an hourly BISI low, daily volume imbalance or 'extreme' liquidity target. Never take a partial below halfway. Cut size after a stop-out (the Dec 2023 video shows a 50% re-entry, flagged as implied only). Use one micro contract if trading NFP at all.

8) Jackson Hole seek-and-destroy. On day 1 and day 2 of the symposium, flag seek-and-destroy: at least 2 alternating sweeps of opposite range extremes, with the range expanding (megaphone). No breakout entries. Trade an IFVG retest after a sweep, trail the stop, and exit before a scheduled speech (10:00).

9) Ma Deuce (the only pre-news model). Before 08:30, with the daily bias and structure in agreement, find an IFVG (a bullish BISI broken lower on the 5m). Short a retest into it with the stop above the IFVG high. Take partials at CE, at the 25% quadrant, and at a discount array (shown to 15,175 and the hourly BISI low).

Subjective parts overall: the bias, which swings define the range and Event Horizon, 'meaningful retracement', 'qualifies as IFVG', the 'sweet spot', and the target distance. There is no numeric rule for the post-release wait other than '15-20 minutes'.
news_trades.changes_over_time:
1) Pre-release positioning changed repeatedly. Nov 2017: a USDCAD OTE short was held through the NFP print (silent video, +100 pips). Jan 2018: 'NFP Friday. Not for professionals.' 2020-2022: avoid or watch only. Sept 1 2023 (NQ NFP short) and Sept 8 2023 (Ma Deuce): positioned ahead of 08:30 with limit orders inside an IFVG. Dec 2023 and Feb 2024: enter after the release. Sept 2024: 'manual intervention', do not trade into it. Jan 2025: a pre-NFP micro short was stopped out, then a 3-micro re-entry won. Oct 2026: 'don't position ahead of NFP, wait 15-20 minutes', yet the live fade was scaled in at 09:05-09:13. Ma Deuce appears in exactly one dossier (1PkTGkOjoGo); its pre-news entry contradicts the 2024-2026 teaching.

2) Which FOMC stage is tradeable is inconsistent. 2021: do not trade FOMC while developing. May 2022: ahead of FOMC is a 'gambler's setup' and the real move is around 2:30. Feb 2023 and May 2024: stage 1 is the fake and the real move is the 2:30 conference, so wait until about 2:45 or stand aside at 2:00. July 2023 dossier: the conference itself has a sweep up then a reversal down. The 7pW4 video (dated 20250101 in the catalogue, but NQZ2025 levels near 24,400 suggest late 2025 or later): trades stage 1 off the first FVG after 2:00 and calls the conference 'untradeable'. Apr 2026: be done by 10:30 and let the day cook. Sept 2026: trades a 14:43 'sweet spot' entry that falls inside the conference window.

3) NFP-week schedule: 2017 'Wed-Fri iffy'; 2022 'trading done by Wednesday'; Oct 2023 'no trading Thu/Fri, resumes after 10:00 on NFP day'; 2026 lockout after 11:00 Wednesday, but 'we trade every single Monday of non-farm payroll week'.

4) Jackson Hole: Aug 2020 (EURUSD, Powell speech) taught sit-on-hands; Aug 2026 trades it on NQ (day 1 long, short, day 2 long) but avoids heavy size.

5) Source quality. Many 2023-24 dossiers (QOogqHrBzeY, h0yOpwSilnE, _ZOFkSXfvsg, 25PzvOjgJZY, UMcebJiqAUI, 7IttD8JmDIo) contain only IMPLIED/visual rule rows with no spoken quotes, so no quotes were taken from them. Silent videos (f6KC4m4zNgc, sUGuNE31lG0, S8ztuGt29FM) have no spoken rules; their trade tables are used only for the trade count. jBCdc2vsmNE (2021) reads as synthesized, so its quote is low confidence. The QOog/h0yO and 59Elm/f6KC pairs are the same trade, counted once.

6) Trade count: 33 = trade-table rows with news-event trades across about 28 dossiers (8 in the starting eight videos, 25 elsewhere). It excludes: the 08:30 AM 'Model 2022' trade in 7pW4, the Dec 6 2023 NFP-week Wednesday trades, and the next-morning post-FOMC trade in sUGuNE31lG0. The 10:00 housing-sales trade (Nov 2023) is included, so the true count of NFP/CPI/PPI/FOMC/Jackson Hole trades is somewhat lower.
news_trades.markets: NQ (E-mini Nasdaq) is the main vehicle and appears in every 2023-2026 teaching video; entries are on the 1m chart, with 5m in the Ma Deuce lesson and daily/4H/15m for context. ES (S&P) was used for 2022-Jan 2024 news trades. Micro NQ (MNQ) was used for the May 2022 FOMC scalp and the Jan 2025 NFP micro trades. Earlier FX examples: GBPUSD (FOMC 2017, 2021), USDCAD (pre-NFP short, Nov 2017), EURUSD (Jackson Hole 2020, FOMC reference). In the FOMC two-stage video he says he dislikes yen crosses and calls GBPUSD choppy (markets table, no timestamp). A 2026 video also warns against retail CFDs (US100/US500) versus CME futures. The model is applied to 08:30 data (NFP/CPI/PPI), 10:00 data, FOMC statement and conference, FOMC minutes, and Jackson Hole.

rules.rule: NFP, CPI and PPI: do not trade ahead of the release; trade after the news driver has injected volatility (2024 statement of the general rule).
rules.quote: Look at payroll, look at CPI, PPI, those types of events, you always want to trade after those news drivers because you know the volatility will be established.

rules.rule: FOMC is a two-stage delivery. Stage 1 is the sell-off or spike at 2 pm. The press-conference stretch is called untradeable. Stage 2 runs from the stage-1 extreme to the buy side of the intraday high.
rules.quote: This is the first stage delivery where it sells off at 2 p.m. beginning of FOMC and then during the conference portion basically is untradeable. And this is the second stage here from the low up to the buy side running the [intraday high].

rules.rule: Jackson Hole Symposium day 1 is the highest-likelihood seek-and-destroy day. If it does not form on day 1 it can still form on day 2.
rules.quote: Day one of Jackson Hole Symposium is the highest likelihood of a seek and destroy day. It doesn't mean it if it doesn't form on day one that it can't do it on day two.

rules.rule: On medium and high impact news, the first run on liquidity goes to the side that would have been the winning side, so the first spike points the wrong way. The real move comes after that side is taken. Direction therefore comes from the higher-timeframe draw, not from the spike.
rules.quote: So it's the first run on liquidity on medium or high impact news drivers that tends to be the side that would be the winning side if they wait!

rules.rule: Ma Deuce is an inversion-FVG model used around 08:30 news. In the dossier's case study a bullish BISI is broken lower and becomes resistance for a short, with structure and daily bias in agreement.
rules.quote: Ma Deuce is simply a model utilizing an inversion fair value gap

rules.rule: Before an 08:30 release, mark the range from the highest high to the lowest low between 07:00 and 08:30 NY. This is the baseline for the news reaction and its projections.
rules.quote: highest high and lowest low of the range prior to 8:30 release. So, 7:00 in the morning starts the time. Go through up to the point of 8:30, which is here.

rules.rule: Before FOMC, map the untouched daily highs and lows (back-to-back inside days) as the pools to be raided. The first stage pierces them.
rules.quote: at this moment, we had yet to trade above Tuesday's high or Monday's high, or below Monday and or Tuesday's respective daily lows

rules.rule: Project the 7:00-8:30 range with a negative 2.5 standard-deviation extension, fib drawn low to high. Its confluence with the Event Horizon (50% between two swing extremes) marks the fade level in the Oct 2026 NFP short.
rules.quote: So it's 2.5. Make sure it's negative on your fib and you're drawing it from low to high.

rules.rule: A level needs confluence with other smart-money arrays to count. An isolated standard-deviation level is not tradeable.
rules.quote: Not interested at that level because it's by itself. It's isolated. Isolated levels are useless. There has to be a convergence of several things that I teach in terms of smart money concepts that makes the level viable

rules.rule: Seek-and-destroy profile on Jackson Hole: price alternates sweeps up and down in an expanding (megaphone) shape to clear stops on both sides. Do not trade breakouts of it.
rules.quote: seek and destroy likely. So, it's going to go up, down, up, to clear stops, down to clear stops

rules.rule: At 08:30 the first run is usually the Judas swing. When several reports drop together, wait for the burst to exhaust.
rules.quote: High impact news driver at 8:30 usually it's the first run that is your Judas swing but because we have multiple reports at 8:30 give it a minute.

rules.rule: FOMC stage 1: after the 2 pm statement, price trades up into the first presented FVG and then drops. This is the stage-1 short trigger.
rules.quote: Price trades up into the first present fair value gap post 2 p.m.

rules.rule: After the 2 pm pierce of the daily high and a re-rally above it, return to the inefficiency that formed before the sweep. It becomes the inversion FVG to trade (Sept 2026 FOMC).
rules.quote: And then once it took out this high, we want to go back in and look at any inefficiency that formed prior to that because it's going to act as an inversion fair value gap

rules.rule: IFVG signature: candle bodies respect the gap and wick midpoints. The open cannot even reach the consequent encroachment of the gap or wick, and price breaks down.
rules.quote: Volume balance at the low to the wick low. Draw that out. Body respected lower half. Open couldn't even touch consequent encroachment or consequent encroachment of that wick. Broke down. They are absolute characteristics of an inversion fair value gap

rules.rule: Confirmation after the news candle: an FVG that fails to reach its midpoint, with the next candle trading lower, is confirmation of a smart-money short.
rules.quote: fair gap and you see it fail to get to the midpoint here and it trades lower in the next candle

rules.rule: Post-CPI: a candle that closes outside the first-instance FVG qualifies it as an inversion FVG. A body close beyond the gap is required.
rules.quote: respecting this as an inversion fair value gap because we had a close outside of it right there.

rules.rule: Ma Deuce (Sept 2023): with an 08:30 delivery expected, enter inside the inversion FVG before the news. This is the only pre-release entry taught as a named model.
rules.quote: we're expecting an 8:30 delivery we can get in here and use this and get ahead of yes get ahead of and enter before the news it's like an x-ray view

rules.rule: Oct 2026 NFP: do not position ahead of the release. Wait about 15-20 minutes after 08:30, see which liquidity is left, then enter. The live fade short was scaled in between 09:05 and 09:13.
rules.quote: you got to wait a little bit. Wait about 15 minutes, 20 minutes into the session and then you'll see what liquidity, what type of things will be left in its wake

rules.rule: For PPI, CPI and NFP, let the news do its move, then enter on a meaningful retracement back into the range.
rules.quote: wait for them to throw out there whatever they're going to do and then when you see a meaningful retracement

rules.rule: Dec 2023 NFP long: place the stop at the boundary of the 4-hour FVG so noise does not hit it. The trade table shows the stop at 16,335, below entry at 16,365.
rules.quote: place my stop loss right at the high of the 4our fair value Gap so it's not going to get hit by noise

rules.rule: Trail the stop to just beyond the inversion FVG once the bodies have spent time inside it (Jackson Hole day 1 long).
rules.quote: Bring the stop up again. Now the stop here is below the inversion fair value, guy, because we've spent a lot of time with the bodies in there

rules.rule: Always use a hard stop on news trades, since you cannot know the outcome. Size small enough that it can be taken.
rules.quote: You aren't going to know. That's why you have to use a stop loss. That's why you don't over leverage

rules.rule: On news-driven trades put the final take-profit far beyond what you expect the trade to do. Take partials on the way.
rules.quote: whenever I trade events where it's news driven, I always put an extreme target for my takerit, the final one, way beyond what I think the trade's going to do personally

rules.rule: Ma Deuce three tiers. First partial at the consequent encroachment of the range, second at the lower 25% quadrant, remainder at another discount array. The third tier comes from the dossier's rule row, not this quote.
rules.quote: first partial would be here at consequent encroachment and you let it run some more to get down to the lower quadrant

rules.rule: Post-CPI: measure the Event Horizon between two swing lows. The algorithm is likely to reach the halfway point, which is the first partial target.
rules.quote: between this low and this low, the algorithm will likely reach to halfway of that.

rules.rule: On FOMC day, hold for more only selectively. Be surgical about the objective (the Sept 2026 short targeted a daily suspension block).
rules.quote: You can hold for lower, but it's FOMC day. So, you want to be very surgical about what you're looking for

rules.rule: Bank partials along the way, because unrealized NFP profit can disappear quickly.
rules.quote: but being mindful that you got to take partials along the way because NFP can take it quickly away from you if it's unrealized profit

rules.rule: Never hold full size with no partial taken.
rules.quote: the trade you've taken no partial you are hoping and praying please start taking partials

rules.rule: Once price expands in your favor after the news, roll the stop to break-even plus commissions.
rules.quote: roll my stop to break even plus commissions plus

rules.rule: Never move a raised stop back. A secured profit is not to be given up (Jackson Hole day 1).
rules.quote: never never never want to pull the stop back. I've secured a payday

rules.rule: At the first FOMC with a new Fed chair he expected more give and take, so he took partials and did not reach for the far target (Monday's low).
rules.quote: it was the first FOMC conference with the new Fed chair. So, I was expecting a little bit of you know, give and take a little bit more than normally. So, I was more inclined to take off partials and not reach for Monday's low

rules.rule: Take the partial in the premium half of the dealing range, not below halfway (Aug 2026 NFP long).
rules.quote: I just don't want to take a partial below halfway. So, everything here is germane. I'm taking a partial in in the premium side of the low where I longed from

rules.rule: If you insist on trading NFP, use one micro contract. You will be wrong often.
rules.quote: trade with one micro contract. That way when you're wrong—and you're going to be wrong more times than you ever thought you would be—it won't hurt you that bad.

rules.rule: 2022 FOMC position rule: be out of the trade before the release. A missed trade does not break the system.
rules.quote: I would have been completely out of the trade ahead of the release. It doesn't mean the system is flawed if a trade misses; it means you protect your capital.

rules.rule: Oct 2026 rule: positioning ahead of NFP (and CPI/PPI) is guessing. Stand aside until the move is out.
rules.quote: Now, you shouldn't try to position yourself ahead of non-farm payroll. That's guessing. That's gambling

rules.rule: Sept 2024: NFP, like FOMC, is a manual intervention that overrides normal flow. Do not trade into the release.
rules.quote: it's like FOMC, a manual intervention where they literally override normal flow. You're encouraged not to try to trade it going into the release.

rules.rule: 2021 baseline (dossier reads as synthesized; low confidence): do not gamble on the print. Wait for the dust to settle and for spreads to normalize.
rules.quote: The professional trader isn't trying to gamble on what the government numbers are going to say. We wait for the dust to settle, the spreads to normalize, and let the algorithm show us who took control.

rules.rule: Avoid NFP weeks after 11:00 a.m. Wednesday ET. Thursday and Friday of NFP week are no-trade days.
rules.quote: hopefully you learned why I tell you to avoid non-farm payroll weeks after 11:00 a.m. Wednesday Eastern time.

rules.rule: FOMC is traded on NQ (Dec 2026 contract) on the 1m chart, with daily context. He shows a 15-contract scale-in.
rules.quote: take a quick look at FOMC for September 2026 for Nasdaq

rules.rule: Jackson Hole seek-and-destroy is traded on NQ at the 1m level in the NY AM session.
rules.quote: trading Jackson Hole and it's a seek and destroy profile

rules.rule: FOMC sweet-spot entry window is 14:40-14:50 NY (the Sept 2026 short was filled at 14:43).
rules.quote: when you're trading FOMC I believe that at 2:40 to 2:50 p.m. Eastern time that's usually when the sweet spot entry forms

rules.rule: FOMC has two phases: rate statement at 2:00 and press conference at 2:30. In 2024 he said the real move comes with the conference. In the 2025/26 teaching the stage-1 short comes right after 2:00.
rules.quote: FOMC generally is a two-stage event what that means is there's going to be the rate announcement at 2:00 and then the press conference at 2:30

rules.rule: Feb 2023: the 2:00 move is not the real move. Wait until about 2:45 NY before acting (a developing-trader rule).
rules.quote: Can you trade it after like 2:45 New York local time? I believe you can, but I don't think anyone should be doing anything with it right now

rules.rule: 2023 NFP rule: after 10:00 NY on NFP day, normal trading resumes.
rules.quote: after 10:00 of non-farm payroll everything resumes and you can be a Trader after that.

rules.rule: 2022 NFP rule: if the 08:30 release does not take the expected liquidity, wait for the 09:30 open to do the sweep before entering.
rules.quote: if the 8:30 AM news release fails to take out expected liquidity, wait for the 9:30 AM open to perform the sweep before entering

rules.rule: Apr 2026 FOMC-day protocol: finish trading by 10:30, then let the day develop until the 2:30 conference.
rules.quote: We got FOMC today. So protocol is you want to be trading by 10:30 or sooner. And then let the rest of the day cook until they go out and they do their read announcement statement and their conference call 2:30.

rules.rule: The FOMC influence window is 14:00-15:00 NY, ending when bonds close.
rules.quote: The last hour 2:00 to 3:00 PM New York time will always encapsulate any movement that's related to FOMC.

bridge_builder.summary: IPDA delivers price for two reasons only, to rebalance inefficiency (FVG, voids, order blocks inside the range) and to take resting stop liquidity outside the range. The "bridge" is trading from an internal-range array out to the opposing external-range liquidity, then back again, without needing the range to break.
bridge_builder.needs_clock: The core is price-only. Detecting a dealing range, external swing highs and lows, internal FVGs and order blocks, a sweep of one side, and the run to the other side needs no clock, so it could run on 24/7 synthetic indices. He says "time is the first measure" (qQvEV2dTTW8), but the Bridge Builder dossier gives no hours, only "kill zones" in the dossier's own gloss. A clock appears only in the 2024 variants: weekly bias, a Monday-Wednesday anchor high or low, and London or New York open. On synthetics those would be lost or replaced by a bar-count or session-length proxy, and the pattern would run as pure price delivery.
bridge_builder.how_to_code:
Detection is mostly mechanical, with a few subjective inputs.
1. Swings: compute fractal swing highs and lows (N-bar pivot) on a context timeframe. Subjective: N, and the tolerance for equal highs or lows.
2. Dealing range: take the latest swing high and low pair where both sides have been swept (2020 definition), or the highest high and lowest low of a fixed lookback such as 20 days (2024). Equilibrium is 50% of the range. Subjective: which definition and lookback to use.
3. Mark external range liquidity (ERL) as unswept swing highs and lows or equal highs and lows at or beyond the range extremes. Mark internal range liquidity (IRL) as unmitigated 3-candle FVGs, liquidity voids and validated order blocks inside the range. An FVG is bullish when the low of candle 3 is above the high of candle 1, and bearish in reverse. An order block is the last opposite-colour candle before the displacement, valid only after a later candle trades through its high or low. Subjective: what counts as displacement (for example body size above k times ATR plus a swing break).
4. Cycle state: when price takes an ERL pool (wick through a swing, then displacement back inside), set the target to the opposing ERL. Expect a retracement into an IRL array first, preferring discount (below 50%) for longs and premium for shorts.
5. Entry: a limit order at the FVG edge or consequent encroachment (50% of the gap), or at the order block open or high, after the sweep and displacement.
6. Stop: beyond the sweep extreme or the array's far edge. The dossier states only "below swing low wick", or a fixed 20 pips in the scalp model.
7. Target: the nearest unmitigated opposing ERL.
8. Filter: low resistance, meaning no unmitigated opposing HTF array or consolidation between entry and target. Subjective: what counts as an obstacle.
9. Management: raise the stop to just below the order block's 50% mean threshold after price leaves; optionally take partials at new short-term extremes and close all at the third target.
10. Invalidation: no displacement after the sweep, a body closing beyond the order block's 50% (this comes from dossier text, not a quote), or a cluttered path.
11. Wiring check: a quote-free state machine (ERL taken, then displacement, then IRL retrace, then IRL entry, then opposing ERL) can be run bar by bar with no session logic.
Subjective parts: range selection, equal-level tolerance, displacement threshold, obstacle definition, and the HTF bias source. The Bridge Builder dossier states no bias rule beyond "bridge HTF dealing range to LTF execution".
bridge_builder.changes_over_time:
1. The name "Bridge Builder" appears only in qQvEV2dTTW8 (Oct 2022). That dossier is thin: three rule quotes and one composite trade with no prices, for a 97-minute video, so the stop, entry and management details come from related videos.
2. Range definition changed. In 2020 (_9QfSbpZTZA) the dealing range is the swing that has run both buy-side and sell-side liquidity, and the dossier text there calls the sell stops below an old low "Internal Range Liquidity". The 2022 lecture (npL3ZXJ5zOU) fixes it differently: buy-side above the range high and sell-side below the range low are both external, and internal means FVGs, voids and order blocks inside. In 2024 (pblXxWhnRz4) the range is a 20-day highest-high and lowest-low lookback.
3. Direction of the bridge. The 2022 lecture and Models 9 and 11 enter at internal arrays and target external pools. In the 2021 scalp video (F-0G6IGTXHg), a scalp enters on 1m or 5m and exits at internal range liquidity, while a day trade holds for the daily range. Model 10 (CTS27DsveNs) goes external-to-external: enter on a stop run past an old high or low and exit at opposing stops, which he calls counterparty liquidity theory. Model 9 (twIPoG2TZ1o) also contrasts turtle soup entries at external highs targeting internal arrays with internal entries targeting external pools. Later videos also say the cycle runs both ways, external to internal and internal to external, on every timeframe.
4. Time: the 2022 video says time precedes price, but gives no hours in its dossier. The 2024 Charter models add weekly bias, a Monday-Wednesday anchor, 20-day lookback and London or New York timing. The 2023 TGIF video (wTR-vhOdMgo) has an external-to-internal version: after the weekly high or low forms on Friday morning, price gravitates back into internal range liquidity (20-30% of the weekly range).
5. Risk: the 2022 trade row stops "below swing low wick", but Model 12 uses a fixed 20-pip stop (about 15 at his smallest) and Model 11 uses 20 pips above the OB. The management examples (stop to just below the OB 50%, two partials then close all) come from the 2022 order block video and the Model 10 swing video, not from the bridge-builder video.
6. Some quotes in the card come from videos outside the grep set (BZ4HVsArJBE from 2021 and 54yWnOON0zQ from 2019), flagged in the rule text. Two quoted rows in the qQvEV2dTTW8 table contain mid-quote ellipses; the card uses only the contiguous segments on one side of the ellipsis.
bridge_builder.markets: The Bridge Builder video (qQvEV2dTTW8) shows ES and NQ index futures (daily, 1h, 15m, 5m) and FX majors (5m, 1m). It recommends index futures and major currencies and warns against indicator-heavy retail systems such as Market Profile and Volume Spread Analysis. Its trades table has one composite long on "Index Futures / FX Major", with no prices and only a vague "multi-handle / multi-pip expansion" result. The ERL/IRL lecture (npL3ZXJ5zOU) uses monthly USDJPY, EURUSD, GBPUSD and DXY, and has no trades table. The same internal-to-external pattern appears under other names in these videos, which add eight more trade rows: twIPoG2TZ1o (GBPUSD short, Model 9), CTS27DsveNs (two GBPUSD shorts, Model 10), E57WWIEjhvU (ES long), UtdXo9HJHKU (NZDUSD shorts, Model 11), pblXxWhnRz4 (AUDUSD long), xi0N9BG1Qvs (USDCHF long) and V1thfpo-R9U (ES long). The strict count for the Bridge Builder video proper is 1, a composite example.

rules.rule: Only take trades whose path to the target is clean (low resistance): no opposing PD arrays or obstacles between entry and the liquidity pool.
rules.quote: You as a trader want your trades to be in low-resistance conditions. In other words, you don't want to have any resistance in your path of profitability.

rules.rule: Inside the dealing range, ask which old low or old high price is likely to be drawn to next, and choose that as the draw on liquidity.
rules.quote: Inside this Dealing Range we look for the next draw on liquidity. Where is Price likely to trade to next, below which Old Low, above which Old High?

rules.rule: 2024 Model 11 variant: a directional bias comes first, from the expected direction of the next weekly candle, and trades go only that way.
rules.quote: Identify the likely or most probable direction the next Weekly bar or candle will expand in a directional sense

rules.rule: Core premise: price delivery has two objectives only, inefficiency and fair value, and liquidity.
rules.quote: The algorithm is seeking inefficiency and fair value, and it's seeking liquidity. Period

rules.rule: Define the dealing range from the swing that has run liquidity on both sides, buy-side above and sell-side below.
rules.quote: Once you have arrived at a particular swing that has done both, that is your dealing range.

rules.rule: External range liquidity = buy stops above the range high and sell stops below the range low, which price runs to in order to pair with pending orders.
rules.quote: External range liquidity: the current trading range will have buy-side liquidity above the range high, and sell-side liquidity below the range low. Runs on liquidity seek to pair orders with pending order liquidity.

rules.rule: Internal range liquidity = the inefficiencies inside the range (liquidity voids, fair value gaps, and order blocks) that price fills while the range holds.
rules.quote: Internal range liquidity: when the current trading range is likely to remain, liquidity voids will fill in, and fair value gaps will also fill in

rules.rule: Internal versus external is relative to which swing pair you call the range. The same leg is internal in one range and external in another.
rules.quote: In the context from this high to this low, it's internal range liquidity. But from this low to this high, it's external range liquidity

rules.rule: The bridge can be worked entirely inside a dealing range, trading internal arrays, without the range ever being broken.
rules.quote: we can work inside dealing ranges and never see those ranges broken, navigating an old range of data.

rules.rule: Once one side's external liquidity has been taken, expect price to seek the opposing external liquidity.
rules.quote: once that's purged, price seeks Buyside External Range Liquidity

rules.rule: General delivery law: take liquidity, then look for opposing liquidity. (From a related 2021 video found outside the grep set.)
rules.quote: the algorithm will seek liquidity take that liquidity once that liquidity has been taken it will look for opposing liquidity

rules.rule: If the internal array is an order block, it only counts once a later candle trades through its high with displacement.
rules.quote: Validation of a bullish order block is when the high of the lowest down candle or price bar is traded through by a later formed candle or price bar.

rules.rule: Enter at an internal-range array (order block, FVG or void) in the direction of the expected run to external liquidity.
rules.quote: Most of the time you're going to find that internal range liquidity entries will run to external range liquidity. That means you're going to see order blocks, fair value gaps, or voids be your entry

rules.rule: Use internal range liquidity pools for the entry and the opposing external pools for the exit.
rules.quote: Utilize Internal Range Liquidity Pools to facilitate an entry in the direction of the Weekly Expansion & exiting on opposing External Range Liquidity Pools.

rules.rule: Definition of the bullish order block used as an internal entry array: the lowest down-close candle with the most open-to-close range, near support.
rules.quote: Definition of a bullish order block is the lowest candle or price bar with a down close that has the most range between open to close and is near a support level.

rules.rule: The risk level must be visible before you act. No trade until the condition points to where the market is going.
rules.quote: You're going to be able to see where the loss would be, but you're not taking a trade until the condition points to where the market is going.

rules.rule: Model 12 scalp variant: keep the stop around 20 pips (his own floor is about 15). In the bridge-builder video itself the stop is only 'below swing low wick' in a table, with no quote.
rules.quote: personally my lowest is about 15 Pips but as a mentor I'm trying to keep you around that 20 pip threshold for stop

rules.rule: The target is the opposing external range liquidity beyond the short-term dealing range, ideally a low-resistance run.
rules.quote: and it'll expand outside of the present short-term dealing range to external range liquidity. And that is your low resistance liquidity run.

rules.rule: Aim for a known level of external liquidity above (long) or below (short) the entry array.
rules.quote: we're looking for an expansion up into a known level of what's up there: external range liquidity.

rules.rule: When choosing the external pool, old lows or highs to the left outrank freshly made short-term ones. (Model 10 swing model.)
rules.quote: old lows to the left take precedence over new short-term low

rules.rule: After price runs away from the order block, raise the stop to just below 50% of the order block range to reduce risk.
rules.quote: Just below the 50% of the order block total range is also considered to be a good location to raise the stop loss after price runs away from the bullish order block to reduce risk.

rules.rule: Model 10 swing variant: at most two partial exits, and the third take-profit closes the whole position.
rules.quote: in your rules you want to say that two partials on the third take profit all your position comes off it's as simple as that

rules.rule: Skip or abandon when the path to the pool is cluttered (a high-resistance run). This is the inverse of the low-resistance filter. The quote is from a 2019 video outside the grep set.
rules.quote: High resistance liquidity runs make it very hard for markets to find sustainable moves. The market has to fight through every single level, chewing up stops in both directions.

rules.rule: The internal-to-external swing works on every timeframe, so it can be used fractally.
rules.quote: Internal range to external range. External range to internal range. Every time frame, I don't care what time frame

rules.rule: 2021 scalp version: on a 1-minute or 5-minute chart, take internal range liquidity for 15 to 30 pips and exit there. The target is internal here, unlike the later models.
rules.quote: A scalp in forex is generally 15 to 30 pips. You are getting in on a one-minute or five-minute chart, taking internal range liquidity, and getting out.

rules.rule: Time is the first element of the algorithm: ask when a move is likely to occur before judging price. The dossier gives no concrete hours in the bridge-builder video.
rules.quote: Time is the first measure in algorithmic principles in theory

rules.rule: Model 11 variant: the day's low forms in the London open and runs into the New York open. Session timing is an overlay from the 2024 models, not part of the 2022 bridge-builder video.
rules.quote: trades right up into the New York session open creating that 30 pip expansion

smt.summary: Compare the same swing extreme across two correlated markets (DXY vs a USD pair, or ES/NQ/YM). When one market takes the new high or low and its partner refuses to, treat the partner as the relative-strength leader and take the trade in that direction. It only confirms a setup you already expect; it does not time the entry. The Sick Sister variant has a laggard index catch up to the leader.
smt.needs_clock: The core detector needs no clock. It compares the same swing extreme (same reference candles) in two correlated price series, so it uses only price. His teaching ties it to windows: index SMT at the 8:30 and 9:30 NY events and in the AM (9:30 to 11:00) and PM (noon to 3 PM) windows. FX/DXY versions on 1h, daily or weekly are session-agnostic. Dossiers also say to avoid Fridays and holiday sessions when decoupled. Running it on 24/7 synthetic indices with price only is possible in principle, but this is my inference and not in the dossiers. It needs two genuinely correlated or inverse series, and most synthetic indices are independent generators. It is only meaningful with a true correlated pair.
smt.how_to_code:
1) Inputs: series A (traded) and B (reference), same timeframe and aligned bars. Mark inverse pairs (DXY vs USD-quoted FX) and map B to -B so highs and lows swap. Use LOW for lows and HIGH for highs, never close (MdYrslpUezU 06:48).

2) Swings: find pivot lows and highs with N bars each side. N is subjective (his dossiers give none). Per isXicdayBwA 05:07, take the previous swing low (L1) and the new low (L2) on A at candle times t1 and t2, and read B's low at the same two candles.

3) Bullish SMT: A.low(t2) < A.low(t1), A takes the liquidity (prior swing, session or day low, or equal lows), and B.low(t2) >= B.low(t1) (a higher low). B is the leader. Bearish mirror: A makes the higher high and B makes a lower high. For DXY vs FX: DXY higher high with FX failing the lower low is bullish FX; DXY lower low with FX failing the higher high is bearish FX.

4) Triad (ES/NQ/YM): flag when at least one index fails to confirm and at least one confirms. Leader = the index with the shallowest sweep. The non-confirming one is the leader for longs. For shorts he picks the weakest of the three (the one with the lower high), per G9mVorSyvR0 00:33:45.

5) Qualifier, not signal: output a boolean plus leader and laggard. Require a narrative (HTF bias or draw on liquidity) and an obviousness threshold (for example B's offset >= k ticks or a fraction of ATR). Then run the entry model: MSS or displacement, then a close-proximity FVG/IFVG limit, with the stop beyond the swing or FVG candle and the target at the opposing liquidity pool. Take a partial at the first pool; pyramid on a new MSS and FVG.

6) Filters: skip if the swings are symmetric (both confirm). Skip when decoupled: no common direction across the three averages, or a rolling correlation below a threshold (the threshold is mine, not his). Skip Fridays and holidays if you want to follow him strictly.

7) Sick Sister lag entry (low confidence, summary-style dossiers): leader (NQ) breaks and displaces through buy-side liquidity; the laggard (YM or ES) has not taken its matching pool. Long the laggard at a discount array (FVG or OB) to its unrun buy-side pool, or hold the leader.

Subjective parts: the swing definition, the same reference candle (time shift between markets), what counts as obvious, the narrative, what counts as deep discount, the decoupling threshold, and which instrument to trade (leader vs laggard).
smt.changes_over_time:
Caveat on dates: a file's date is the upload date. Several 2022 Month-0x dossiers (GuycI8XubgE, ygtvWKyOzHQ, wWCKTEhVp2o, qZg_5bac518, yWBxZsbmK1U) are re-uploads of 2016-17 material, and yWBxZsbmK1U shows a June 23, 2017 example. Several dossiers (fz9ZDU6bKIc, GuycI8XubgE, gGxVE8zUIRQ, VSSwM6rDIg0, LN1nfYp4dBw, n37ozsUreR0) are summary-style with possibly reconstructed quotes. The Sick Sister lag-entry rule rests on two of those (gGxVE8zUIRQ, VSSwM6rDIg0) and should be treated as low confidence. The raw-transcript style files are isXicdayBwA, i8xt0EQDjNY and the 2022 Mentorship episodes.

Evolution:
- 2017 (isXicdayBwA): DXY vs FX pairs on 1h and daily. Terms are symmetrical market, cracked correlation, teeter-totter. SMT is paired with a 70.5% OTE entry and a -300% extension target. Also applied to bonds and grains.
- 2021 (i8xt0EQDjNY): SMT is a confirmation tool, not a timing tool. It needs a narrative, and retail indicator divergence (RSI) is rejected. It is used at HTF key levels (daily sell-side raid) and for weekly One Shot One Kill GBPUSD.
- 2022 Mentorship (Eps 7, 22, 28, 29, 35, 38): ES/NQ/YM intraday on 1m and 5m, built into the 2022 Model (SMT, then MSS, then FVG). He buys the relative-strength leader and uses the Low setting on overlays. News events at 8:30 and 9:30 create the divergence.
- 2022 Month 10 index lessons: AM and PM windows, with the index that trades below the old low treated as a Turtle Soup buy. A single execution instrument is chosen.
- 2023: Sick Sister (Apr and May), decoupled-index caution (Apr 11), 3-averages SMT on the 15m chart, 1m ES/NQ SMT with MSS.
- Dec 2023 to Feb 2024 (Charter models): back to DXY vs EURUSD/GBPUSD for FX day and swing trades.
- Oct 2024 (xUWonBnfYOk): decoupled markets. The dossier overview says to cut leverage in half or stay flat, but that is a paraphrase, not a quote.
- 2026: SMT is "a qualifier, not a selection tool". It is used as narrative context for IFVG/CE entries, with a Friday caution.

Conflicts:
1. Which market to trade. Eps 28/38, fz9ZDU6bKIc and LN1nfYp4dBw say buy the relative-strength leader; Ep 28 says avoid buying the weaker index making the lower low. The Sick Sister dossiers (VSSwM6rDIg0 etc.) say position in deep discount of the lagging index and do not chase the leader. wWCKTEhVp2o says buy the index that sweeps the old low via Turtle Soup for speed, versus buying strength on a stop. qZg_5bac518 says take the trade in the S&P only.
2. Trigger vs qualifier. 2017 sets trade as SMT plus OTE. 2021 and 2026 say qualifier or confirmation only. Eps 29/35 embed SMT inside a model.
3. Clock dependence. Index SMT is tied to 8:30/9:30, AM and PM windows, but FX/HTF versions are clockless.
