4. Decoupling. Sometimes the divergence is the signal; sometimes decoupling means stand aside. The distinction (one clear leader vs. chaos across three averages) is subjective.
5. Count of indices. In 2022 two indices (ES, NQ); in 2022 Month 10 and 2023, three averages including YM.

rules.rule: SMT is a confirmation of something already expected, not a timing tool. Never go hunting for divergence without a plan.
rules.quote: smt is not a timing tool it's a confirmation tool okay it confirms something that you were already expecting anyway

rules.rule: Later (2026) restatement: divergence only qualifies a setup. It is not a selection tool.
rules.quote: divergence there which is a qualifier. It is not a selection tool.

rules.rule: Have a logical narrative or draw on liquidity first. Without it the divergence can vanish.
rules.quote: you have to have logic and some measure of a narrative behind what it is you're looking for otherwise the divergence could be there momentarily and then completely evaporate

rules.rule: Higher-timeframe (daily) order flow sets direction. SMT must agree with it.
rules.quote: never fight the order flow on the daily chart Banks and largest institutions will dictate where price goes

rules.rule: 2026 example: an index running above a prior high (Monday's all-time high) that the partner fails to confirm becomes the bearish narrative.
rules.quote: within the context and narrative of looking for lower prices because of SMT because we traded above Monday's old all-time high again.

rules.rule: Baseline expectation: correlated or inverse partners confirm each other's extremes (a symmetrical market). Confirmation means the trend continues and reversal hunting is not wanted.
rules.quote: in a symmetrical market where everything is as it should be when the market creates a lower low and for instance in the Aussie dollar the dollar index should make a comparable higher high

rules.rule: Index version: one index takes the old extreme (a stop run) while the partner does not. The partner is the weak one on a bearish idea. Mirror this for lows.
rules.quote: so if we're bearish and we're expecting lower prices and we see this but the s p doesn't do it that's showing you that this is a stop run and it shows that s p is really weak

rules.rule: DXY/FX version: DXY takes a new low at face value looks like dollar weakness, but the USD pair (cable) fails to make the matching higher high. That is a cracked correlation, so the move was not real weakness.
rules.quote: the dollar index here makes a lower low here so face value it looks like dollars weak at the same time the cable market you can see is not making a higher high as you would expect it to do so this is a cracking correlation

rules.rule: Bullish index case: ES prints the lower low while NQ refuses. The refuser is the leader.
rules.quote: we have a low and a lower low in es on NASDAQ we're seeing a Divergence

rules.rule: Sick Sister setup: one index leads and the other lags in a consolidation. Evidence is a summary-style dossier, so lower confidence.
rules.quote: The Sick Sister approach occurs when one market leads and the other lags in consolidation

rules.rule: Sick Sister mechanism: the index lacking strength lags at first, then catches up in sympathy with the leader. Often YM lags NQ.
rules.quote: One of them is sick—it doesn't have the strength to perform the same way the leader did like the Nasdaq. But given enough time, it heals, gets its strength, and moves in sympathy.

rules.rule: The leader drags the lagging index up, which is the catch-up run behind the lag entry.
rules.quote: The strong one pulls this one up—grabs a hold of it by its hair and drags its rear end up higher with it.

rules.rule: Trigger, DXY higher high with the FX pair failing to make a lower low (partner in an inverse pair fails to confirm). The pair is then being accumulated, which is bullish for it.
rules.quote: we have the dollar index making a higher high but now in this case if this was representing the Aussie dollar the Aussie dollars failing to make a lower low so this is suggesting that Aussie dollar is being bought up

rules.rule: Compare both charts at the same timeframe and the same reference candles.
rules.quote: looking at exactly the same timeframe at exactly the same reference points or candles

rules.rule: Mechanics for comparing: when overlaying correlated markets, compare lows using the Low price, not Close.
rules.quote: when comparing lows between two correlated assets using an overlaid comparison line chart, the comparison line must be plotted on the 'Low' price setting rather than the default 'Close'

rules.rule: The pair should mirror each other. If both do not make the matching extreme, that is the cracked-correlation signal.
rules.quote: i'm comparing the price of one benchmark currency the dollar versus another currency pair and they should be mirroring one another so if this is high or high this should be low or low if it doesn't do that that to me indicates as a cracking correlation

rules.rule: Worked statement of the bullish signal on DXY vs GBPUSD: DXY higher high while cable fails to make the lower low.
rules.quote: where it went high higher high low failed lower low so it's telling the traders without really broadcasting it that okay cable's gonna start going higher because it failed to make that lower low where the dollar made the higher high so this is smt divergence

rules.rule: Index example: S&P (ES) fails to go lower when NQ does, so it is the leader.
rules.quote: s p failed to go lower that's an smt divergence okay smt smart money technique

rules.rule: Trade the market that held. Buy the relative-strength leader of the ES/NQ pair on a bullish SMT. This is an on-screen annotation in the dossier.
rules.quote: I am buying the Relative Strength Leader between the ES & NQ contract

rules.rule: 2022 Model execution after SMT: SMT, then MSS, then a close-proximity entry in or near the new FVG on the 1m chart.
rules.quote: close proximity entries that means either inside the Fair Value Gap or in close proximity to it

rules.rule: PM-session variant: after the SMT and lunch sweep, enter long on a retrace into a 15m FVG sitting in discount of the dealing range.
rules.quote: enter long when price retraces into a 15-minute Fair Value Gap that is located within a Discount (below 50% equilibrium) of the current Dealing Range

rules.rule: 2026 variant: with the SMT narrative, short at the consequent encroachment of an inversion FVG.
rules.quote: the fill on the short is right at the consequent encroachment of the inversion fair value gap

rules.rule: For shorts, choose the weakest of the three averages. It retraces least against you.
rules.quote: When we're looking for a weak market across the three averages, you're looking for ideally shorting in the weakest one because it's going to have very little retracements against you.

rules.rule: Sick Sister lag entry (summary-style dossier, lower confidence): do not chase the leader. Position long in deep discount of the lagging index and expect catch-up. This conflicts with 'buy the leader'.
rules.quote: you don't chase the leader; you position in deep discount of the lagging sister, anticipating catch-up delivery.

rules.rule: Long: stop just below the relevant low (in the Ep.7 NQ trade, one tick below the NQ swing low). The dossier gives no SMT-specific stop rule beyond that.
rules.quote: stop loss placed right below that low

rules.rule: Index longs: take the full position at buy-side liquidity pools resting above the morning swing highs.
rules.quote: full position profit targets for intraday index futures trades should be anchored to significant buy-side liquidity pools resting above morning swing highs

rules.rule: FX swing version: after SMT, price reaches for the buy stops on the weekly or daily chart.
rules.quote: in a market that's shown a willingness to be bullish because of smt the low sell side liquidity pool in the daily chart it's wanting to go higher is clearly reaching for some measure of buy stops and we've outlined that on the weekly chart

rules.rule: 2026 NQ short: the lunch-macro low is the draw on liquidity he used.
rules.quote: this has got a longer wick. So I would use this as a lunch macro low as a draw on liquidity.

rules.rule: Pyramid: add a second position on a new MSS and retrace into the new FVG.
rules.quote: after an initial long position is established from an FVG retracement, a second position may be placed when price forms another bullish market structure shift and retraces into the newly formed Fair Value Gap

rules.rule: Take a first partial when the sell-side or buy-side liquidity is purged (NQ short, 2022).
rules.quote: That's your short for Nasdaq right there—sell-side liquidity purged, first partial locked in.

rules.rule: Trail the stop under the recent swing lows as price advances. This is on-screen chart management in the dossier.
rules.quote: Trailing stop loss placed below recent swing low and raised as price advances

rules.rule: No obvious divergence means no SMT. Do not strain to find it or force it.
rules.quote: When it's not obvious, assume it's not there

rules.rule: If the pair confirms each other (symmetry), the trend persists and reversal setups are not wanted.
rules.quote: When the dollar index makes a lower low and foreign currencies make a higher high, this confirms current price action and the underlying trend is likely to continue. The idea of stalking reversal patterns in this condition is not highly probable

rules.rule: Do not trade against an established divergence, especially on a Friday.
rules.quote: Not on a Friday. Not against the divergence that's been created, not against the gap that hasn't been really traded into deep enough.

rules.rule: Decoupled indices: when the three averages each do their own thing, setups degrade. Stand down or reduce.
rules.quote: Because they're all doing whatever they want to do opposed to one another, it makes trading much more difficult because everything is decoupled.

rules.rule: Decoupled-markets lecture: decoupling makes conditions problematic. Only a fragment is quoted in the dossier.
rules.quote: Decoupled all day and make very problematic conditions for trading.

rules.rule: After entry, exit the remainder if the supporting array (bullish OB) fails.
rules.quote: kill the remaining portion of a long trade if price trades through a bullish order block that was supposed to act as support

rules.rule: Primary FX pairing: DXY against the foreign currency pairs (AUDUSD, GBPUSD; also EURUSD in later years).
rules.quote: one of the most powerful ones that I use is the relationship between a dollar index itself versus foreign currency pairs

rules.rule: Primary index pairing: ES with NQ, usually on 1m to 5m intraday.
rules.quote: these are closely correlated assets the s p 500 stocks composite and in nasdaq 100 stocks composite they generally move together in tandem

rules.rule: Watch the whole ES/NQ/YM triad even if you only trade one.
rules.quote: these averages tend to move in tandem so that means they generally move in the same direction so I'm looking at the Dow even though you don't see me trading it I'm looking at it

rules.rule: 2026: execute on one market and use the others for context.
rules.quote: By narrowing your focus to one market, it does a great deal in terms of controlling your expectations and your attention span.

rules.rule: Charter Model 1: EURUSD against DXY on daily/hourly, with DXY unwilling to make a comparable extreme.
rules.quote: you'll see the dollar Index was unwilling to make a comparable high or low

rules.rule: Index SMT appears around the 8:30 and 9:30 NY news and open events.
rules.quote: 8 30 9 30 at news events being released they'll create this divergence

rules.rule: PM window: compare highs and lows between noon and 3 PM NY.
rules.quote: We're looking for the highs and the lows between noon and 3:00 PM New York time

rules.rule: AM window: compare pre-market highs and lows (5:00 AM to 9:30 AM NY) across the indices.
rules.quote: Between the 5:00 AM New York time and 9:30 equities open New York time you're going to be looking for relative lows and relative highs and just compare them.

rules.rule: Second SMT checkpoint after 1 PM NY on the PM leg (Month 10 index lesson).
rules.quote: After one o'clock is seen in New York, we would anticipate some measure of a rally again and we would be comparing SMT divergence at the highs

opening_gaps.summary: ICT plots fixed gap levels (NWOG: Fri 17:00 ET close to Sun 18:00 open; NDOG: 17:00 close to 18:00 open; RTH ORG: prior 16:14 ET settlement to the 09:30 open), halves each into a consequent-encroachment (CE) line, expects price to revisit and respect the CE with candle bodies, and (from Sep 2024) claims the ORG half-gap is tagged about 70% of the time in the morning, usually the first 30 minutes.
opening_gaps.needs_clock: Yes. The model is defined by exchange-clock boundaries, so it cannot run on 24/7 synthetic indices using price delivery alone. NDOG needs the 17:00-18:00 ET daily break. NWOG needs Friday 17:00 ET to Sunday 18:00 ET (17:00 for forex). RTH ORG needs the prior-day 16:14/16:15 ET regular-hours settlement and the 09:30 ET cash open. The 70% claim is tied to the first 30 minutes (09:30-10:00) or 'by 10:00' (Onca4KgfQB4 says the morning session). A continuous synthetic feed has no close-to-open discontinuity, so every gap would be zero and the model is undefined. Only the generic parts port: CE of an FVG, body-versus-wick respect, first FVG after an arbitrarily chosen 'session open', and levels from prior sessions. The 70% half-gap statistic would have to be re-measured. Applying it to Jump-style discontinuities is my speculation and is not taught in the dossiers.
opening_gaps.how_to_code:
Inputs: 1-minute OHLC in America/New_York time for NQ/ES/MNQ that includes both electronic and regular hours.

1) NDOG: for each day, close = last price at or before 17:00:00 ET, open = first price at or after 18:00:00 ET. hi = max, lo = min, ce = (hi+lo)/2. Keep the gap if hi > lo. The Feb 2023 teaching accepts one tick; the Aug 2024 teaching requires over 20 NQ handles for the CE to be annotated. Extend the levels forward in time. The dossiers say to keep roughly 3 to 5 recent NDOGs (dossier rule for eYYyonGwTRs, not a quote).

2) NWOG: the same construction with close = Friday 17:00 ET and open = Sunday 18:00 ET (forex 17:00 ET). Keep at least the last 4, and keep them for months until price has traded through them repeatedly. Never build the gap from daily bars.

3) RTH ORG: close = the prior regular-hours settlement, using the close of the 16:14 ET 1-minute bar (he labels it 4:14 PM, some dossiers say 4:15). open = first print at 09:30:00 ET. Do not use ETH data. Set hi/lo/ce. Quadrant lines are at 25% and 75% in 2024-25. Octants every 12.5% and a -2.0 standard-deviation projection of the gap appear in 2026. Premium if open > settlement, discount if open < settlement.

4) Half-gap model: after 09:30, for a discount gap watch for high >= ce, and for a premium gap watch for low <= ce. Score a hit if it happens by 10:00 (the 2026 statement) or by about 11:30 (the Sep 2024 'morning session'). Parameterise the window and measure the hit-rate yourself, because the 70% figure is his claim and it is stated differently over time (see variants). Treat the 20-75 handle band as 'CE or full fill after a pre-market sweep'. Treat gaps over 120 handles on NQ as runaway: no fill, only a shallow move into the 25% quadrant. Convert the handle thresholds to a percentage or ATR multiple for other instruments.

5) Entry: find the first 3-candle FVG formed after 09:31 and before 10:00 in the direction of the CE. Place a limit inside it. Body-respect check: the candle bodies close inside or beyond the near edge, with wicks allowed outside. For NDOG and NWOG reactions, enter on a touch of the CE or edge and confirm with a close on the respecting side. The CE-touch tolerance he cites is one tick.

6) Stop: beyond the FVG candle, or just beyond the CE of the higher of two gaps (Two Gap Rule), or just below/above the ORG CE for the probe trades.

7) Targets and management: first target is the ORG CE. The dossier says to take a partial there and then run to the gap edge, the next NDOG/NWOG, or about 100 handles (these are dossier summaries, not quotes). Exit if bodies stay on the wrong side of the CE or the 9:30 open.

8) Invalidation filters: runaway gap over 120 handles; a gap-down open that cannot reach the lowest quadrant or octant; an NDOG retested repeatedly without displacement; three or more NWOG CE touches by Wednesday (dossier rule: treat the week as consolidation); price trapped inside overlapping prior ORGs.

9) Impeding barriers: build a list of horizontal levels (prior settlement, 9:30 open, ORG high/low/CE, NDOG/NWOG edges, inversion FVGs). Classify an approach as deflect (wick rejection with bodies respecting) or absorb (bodies close through). This is my interpretation of a dossier summary and is not directly taught in the quotes.

Subjective parts that need a human or a parameter choice: what counts as displacement; the exact first-presented FVG on a given chart; whether bodies are respecting a level; how many NDOG retests are too many; which older gaps to keep; handle thresholds on other instruments; whether the 4:14 or 4:15 print is the settlement; the impeding-barrier definition.
opening_gaps.changes_over_time:
1) Early versions. 2020-08 (2mtzC7ajUew 04:38): on Mondays he wants the Sunday gap filled, then trade in the gap's direction. 2022 (t8flQP5jy-Q 00:35, 10:28; jXBuSFBUs2w): the Sunday 18:00 gap is plotted for that trading week as support/resistance and as a discount anchor, with a week-long life. Feb-Mar 2023 formal NDOG/NWOG with acronyms and CE (GFdWahZUNOw 11:02, 7RiUUCqQ3SY, KXx07qzW5u0, SSWN6YSVyFY, WKKnlIIkBTk). May-Jun 2023 extends NWOG life to weeks and months while ORG and NDOG are called intraday (BM1mqQv-ypk 08:23, V0uV6lcgobQ 10:31).

2) Anchor conflict. The 2023 videos (and ul6x6BwOg6M, Aug 2024) define NDOG/NWOG from the 17:00 close to the 18:00 open. The Sep 2024 dossiers differ. The l7eu9yvUUtg dossier says NWOG must be anchored to the Friday 4:14 PM settlement and warns against Sunday/electronic prints, but its only verbatim line (00:48:02) is about Friday 4:14 settlement dashed lines. The -M-RAtxB-bE overview (not a quote) says NDOG runs from the 4:14 PM settlement to the open. The Jan 2025 videos return to ETH definitions (x_44mMI7YqU 00:58; uIvlS330qrA 07:19 says ORG is RTH only and ETH gaps are NDOG/NWOG). These dossier claims are likely over-readings or generation errors. The safe reading is NDOG/NWOG = ETH (17:00/18:00) and ORG = RTH (about 16:14/09:30). Settlement is labelled 4:14 in most dossiers and 4:15 in a few (LMi_mO3AP08, Onca4KgfQB4).

3) ORG reference. Jun 2023 (Sf_uYZBWTrA 11:06) measures premium/discount against Friday's close. From Aug 2024 it is the previous day's settlement. 2023 also frames trades with Silver Bullet and the 09:50-10:10 repricing macro, while 2024-26 uses the first presented FVG in 09:30-10:00.

4) The 70% half-gap statistic keeps shifting. Aug 27-29, 2024: appears only in dossier summaries (yOZHawAE8QI, NMCy1H2_Wr8). Sep 4 and 9, 2024: verbatim half-gap, 'morning session', and the Sep 4 summary says discount gaps (Ipjk9S8HTbA, Onca4KgfQB4 27:25). Oct 17, 2024 (akfEjsn4adk 00:22:56): a gap higher comes all the way back to settlement 70% of the time in the first 30 minutes, with the dossier tying it to gaps of 75 handles or more. Jan 2025 (uIvlS330qrA, pM8oWrcIJqU): 20-75 handles gives a pre-market sweep then CE/fill, and over 120 handles is runaway and not likely to fill, with only a move to the 25% quadrant. Jun 2025 (ixKzHykP0CY 00:29:35) restates 70% to CE. Sep 2025 (OC-ilNjtYsM 04:15) applies 70% to the CE of the 30-minute opening range, which is a different object. 2026: Half Gap Model (1X0A-Lgf9RY 00:20:58, V4KPpX-CWXk 00:38:08), a daily SOP and 'by 10:00' (5ycp9oGKPms 01:25:41, BD7kqmgdBU8 11:16, 2H_qpeIp2rY 04:36), while Onca4KgfQB4 80:15 accepts a later arrival. The window tightened from 'morning session' (2024) to 'first 30 minutes' or 'by 10:00' (2026).

5) Full fill versus half. The 2024 dossiers list 'never assume 100% fill' (DRuEMX4RhMw rules list, Ipjk9S8HTbA) and a terminus at a new NDOG/NWOG (Ipjk9S8HTbA 60:15). Oct 2024 targets the settlement. 2026 treats CE by 10:00 as low-hanging fruit and still tracks full closure later (5ycp9oGKPms, 12:50-1:10 macro).

6) Grid and tools. 25/50/75 quadrants (DRuEMX4RhMw, vfqyx8BYdNo, r-9jSs1Oq_c) later become octants and a -2.0 standard-deviation projection of the ORG (UVVmS0de0g0 28:22; 54kzPj03Rkg). The Event Horizon zone around gaps (kuURDD1ajdQ 30:11) is used in 2026 scaling (2H_qpeIp2rY).

7) NDOG filters. One tick is enough in Feb 2023 (SSWN6YSVyFY) but over 20 handles gets the CE in Aug 2024 (ul6x6BwOg6M). In 2023 (Sh-bDHWNpsk) he dislikes NDOGs retested too often, while in Aug 2024 (hdSscxZgE58) old NDOGs keep being revisited after being filled.

8) Impeding barriers appear only in the Aug 2024 lecture iLe_4m84_yw (with cross-references in vfqyx8BYdNo and yOZHawAE8QI). Only 22:30 ties the term to inversion FVGs, and the transcript spells it 'impending'. The settlement/ORG-edge/NDOG definition is the dossier's summary.

9) Dossier reliability. The 2023 'Rules He States' tables (WKKnlIIkBTk, BM1mqQv-ypk, Sh-bDHWNpsk, Sf_uYZBWTrA) read as tidy sentences that may be paraphrased. The 2025-26 'Exact words' tables look more transcript-like (r-9jSs1Oq_c has speech-to-text errors). Use the 2025-26 statements for thresholds and confirm the 2023 ones against the video.
opening_gaps.markets: NQ is dominant from 2024 to 2026, with MNQ micros in the 2026 tape readings. ES was the main market in 2023 (NWOG, NDOG, ORG lectures). DXY and EURUSD appear in the Feb 2023 NWOG review (7RiUUCqQ3SY). GBP/USD appears in the Jan 2025 forex NWOG trade (x_44mMI7YqU). YM is listed only in a dossier markets table (WKKnlIIkBTk), not in a quote. Trade count: 57 tabulated trade rows name an opening gap as entry context, target or stop reference, across 53 videos (17 in 2023-24, 11 in 2025, 29 in 2026). Seven of the eight designated teaching videos show one trade row each, and uIvlS330qrA shows none. Most rows use the gap as a target or confluence, and few use it as the sole trigger. The rows are dossier summaries, so entries and P&L are approximate.

rules.rule: He calls the daily gap-midpoint routine his standard operating procedure: look for it every day until price shows it will not happen. The referent of 'that' is inferred from the dossier overview, which ties the SOP to the RTH ORG and its 70% CE rule.
rules.quote: That's everyday operation protocol. That's a SOP, standard operating procedure. That's a 100% I'm looking for that every single day until proven it's not going to do it.

rules.rule: NDOG size filter (Aug 2024): when the 17:00-18:00 gap on index futures is over 20 handles, always keep its midpoint CE annotated.
rules.quote: if it's over 20 handles then I'm going to probably have the midpoint consequent encroachment annotated

rules.rule: Feb 2023: even a one-tick NDOG is worth plotting because most people miss it. This conflicts with the later 20-handle filter.
rules.quote: The distinction between where we closed for the one-hour break and when we opened back up at six o'clock—it's very little change, in fact it's only one tick.

rules.rule: Jan 2025: the moderate RTH opening range gap band on NQ is 20 to 75 handles. In that band he expects a pre-market liquidity sweep and then a move back toward CE or the settlement.
rules.quote: If we are trading in between 20 and 75 handles with an opening range gap

rules.rule: NWOG is the gap between Friday 17:00 close and Sunday 18:00 open (electronic session).
rules.quote: Whatever the separation is between Sunday's open at 18:00 and Friday's close at 17:00, that is the true New Week Opening Gap.

rules.rule: NDOG is the 17:00 close versus the 18:00 open (New York time). Extend it through the day.
rules.quote: The New Day Opening Gap is the closing price at 5:00 PM and the opening price at 6:00 PM New York local time. Extend that out through the time of the trading day because the algorithm will reprice back to it multiple times.

rules.rule: The ORG is defined from regular trading hours only. Gaps seen once electronic hours are shown are NDOG or NWOG.
rules.quote: The opening range gap is defined by regular trading hours only. As soon as you start showing electronic trading hours, what you're looking at there is New Day Opening Gaps and/or New Week Opening Gaps.

rules.rule: ORG anchor (Oct 2024): yesterday's regular-hours settlement (dossiers label it 4:14 PM ET, sometimes 4:15) becomes one edge of the gap, the 9:30 open the other.
rules.quote: The settlement price is now becoming what the opening range Gap low it still will always be a constant yesterday's settlement price at regular trading hours close.

rules.rule: Halve the gap to get consequent encroachment (CE). Candle bodies tend to rest there.
rules.quote: Take that range, divide it in half, and you'll get the consequent encroachment, which you won't be surprised I'm sure to see that's where all these bodies are resting.

rules.rule: Extend the NWOG range through the whole week because it draws price back.
rules.quote: We always extend that range throughout the week because it will act as a magnet—it'll draw price back to it

rules.rule: An ORG is a true liquidity void (no prints at all), not a BISI/SIBI. Price eventually wants to rebalance it.
rules.quote: Eventually price will want to rebalance all of this here because it's inefficient, because there's no price at all, zero. So this is an actual liquidity void. It's not a buy-side imbalance sell-side inefficiency, it's an actual liquidity void.

rules.rule: Do not confuse the RTH ORG (a price range) with the opening range (the 09:30-10:00 time window).
rules.quote: That's the regular trading hours or RTH O RG open range gap, not to be confused with the opening range, which is the first 30 minutes of trading from 9:30 to 10:00 Eastern time

rules.rule: Do not delete old NWOGs when the week ends. Smart money keeps using them as reference points.
rules.quote: It's engineered, it's designed, and then smart money uses these old reference points

rules.rule: Keep at least four weekly gaps on the chart.
rules.quote: Maintain a minimum four new week opening gaps on your chart

rules.rule: Shelf life: NWOGs last weeks to months.
rules.quote: New week opening gaps I can hold on to them and use them for weeks, months

rules.rule: Shelf life: ORG and NDOG are short-term imbalances that matter intraday.
rules.quote: Opening range gaps and new day opening gaps, their short term imbalances with an intraday shelf life.

rules.rule: NDOG and NWOG are the more influential draws on liquidity. Keep them mapped and active.
rules.quote: The larger draw the more influential draw on liquidity are new day opening gaps and new week opening gaps that's the real hidden that's the magnet on price

rules.rule: Overlapping NDOGs (a cluster) are a defended zone.
rules.quote: When multiple NDOGs cluster together, expect aggressive institutional defense.

rules.rule: Layered NDOG and NWOG levels produce high-resistance runs (choppy, friction), so adjust targets.
rules.quote: these layered new day opening gap and new week opening gap levels, that's what causes high resistance liquidity runs.

rules.rule: 2026 grid: prior-day RTH ORGs are graded into octants plus CE, and price is expected to return to those levels.
rules.quote: Highest octant, consequent encroachment, lowest octant, and the low of Thursday's opening range gap, regular trading hours opening range gap

rules.rule: IMPEDING BARRIER (the only verbatim tie in the dossiers): an inversion FVG acts as a barrier price must respect. The transcript spells it 'impending'. The dossier's wider definition (prior settlement, 9:30 open, ORG high/low, unfilled NDOGs within about 100 handles) is a summary, not a quote.
rules.quote: there's logic behind this, this is why I said anybody talks about inversion fair value gaps, you must understand their behavior as an impending barrier.

rules.rule: Barrier example: price trapped between an older NDOG and the ORG. The dossier says the ORG high plus the settlement line acted as barriers that day.
rules.quote: bang around between new day opening gap of August 21st and the opening range gap.

rules.rule: 2023 premium/discount classification of the opening gap, measured against Friday's close (later versions use the prior day's 4:14 PM settlement).
rules.quote: Whenever there's an opening range gap lower than Friday's close we are opening with a discount opening range gap. If we are opening with a gap that's above Friday's close we're opening with an opening range gap premium.

rules.rule: The half-gap draw is the session bias: gap down means look up to CE, gap up means look down to CE, on the strength of the 70% claim in the first 30 minutes.
rules.quote: 70% of the time, the first 30 minutes, a half gap gets traded to. Now, that's a huge advantage for bias for session.

rules.rule: Trading the discount-ORG reprice to the midpoint needs no higher-timeframe bias.
rules.quote: it matters not for a bias, you don't need a bias.

rules.rule: NWOG low as a bias filter: once price has worked below the NWOG low, drop the upside idea (dossier: long ideas abandoned).
rules.quote: Running up on the short-term buy side liquidity there and I'm not interested in needing it to see it go above here because we've already worked below the new week opening Gap low.

rules.rule: Two NWOGs, one above and one below, bracket price and define the range.
rules.quote: If you have a new week opening gap above you and a new week opening gap below you, they bracket price.

rules.rule: Reaction at an NDOG CE: the wick may enter the CE, but candle bodies must respect the gap.
rules.quote: price may wick into the CE, but candle bodies should respect the gap.

rules.rule: A CE holds if bodies do not close through it. A wick through is allowed, a close beyond it ends the validation.
rules.quote: Consequent encroachment: it can wick below, but it cannot close below consequent encroachment to keep this validated

rules.rule: Judge the CE by bodies, not wicks.
rules.quote: it's okay for these wicks to trade through it, that's what wicks do, but the bodies are showing you the narrative.

rules.rule: At the NWOG edge, wicks probe liquidity but bodies respect the gap.
rules.quote: candle wicks probe the liquidity, but bodies respect the institutional gap.

rules.rule: NDOG CE holding price is the reaction signal (Sep 2024 tape reading).
rules.quote: Consequent encroachment of the New Day Opening Gap holding price to the tick.

rules.rule: Tolerance on a CE reaction: one tick off is acceptable. This is the only numeric tolerance in the dossiers.
rules.quote: And that price is 342.50 in the high. Comes in at 342.75, so it's one tick off. So, that's good enough for government work.

rules.rule: If the gap opens higher, he likes to see a run to the pre-market range (06:00-09:30 ET liquidity) first, before the retrace into the gap.
rules.quote: if it opens higher I like to see it trade to a pre-market session

rules.rule: A morning move away from the ORG is treated as a Judas swing, and he anticipates repricing back into the gap (the 09:50-10:10 macro in this 2023 example).
rules.quote: I'm going to anticipate the algorithm repricing back down into the opening range gap

rules.rule: The model chain is FVG entry, then partial at mid-gap, then terminus at the NDOG.
rules.quote: We saw the fair value gap here to mid-gap, that's one setup that could be your model. You could go fair value gap, partial at mid-gap, terminus new day opening gap.

rules.rule: Entry uses the first fair value gap after the open, with a resting limit order inside it.
rules.quote: Wait for that first fair value gap to form and have your limit order sitting in that fair value gap

rules.rule: The FVG to use is the very first presented one in the first 30 minutes (09:30-10:00).
rules.quote: The very first presented fair value gap during the opening range first 30 minutes

rules.rule: Inside the entry FVG, wicks may poke out but bodies should stay respectful.
rules.quote: wicks can come outside of that fair value gap, but the bodies tend to be more respectful.

rules.rule: The Half Gap Model trade example uses a Model 2022 entry: the FVG on the right side of a swing high, with the half gap as the objective.
rules.quote: I like the fair value gap on the right side of a swing high which is your model 2022 setup

rules.rule: Entry confluence (2023 NDOG video): an NDOG edge or CE aligned with a 62%-79% retracement (OTE). The dossier wording looks polished and may be paraphrased.
rules.quote: that's Optimal Trade Entry (OTE). Confluence between an NDOG and a 62%–79% retracement creates maximum probability.

rules.rule: Retracement tolerance: price may come back from the NWOG low up to its CE and still continue lower (short example, Jan 2025).
rules.quote: Using that new week opening gap low into consequent encroachment of that new week opening gap, that's a permissible range and then drops aggressively.

rules.rule: 2023 version: frame the move with Silver Bullet rules (range low to high, equilibrium, discount PD array below 50%) and target the ORG.
rules.quote: I just used the simple Silver Bullet rules that I taught you which would be take the low to the high, find equilibrium, what PD array would be a discount array below 50%

rules.rule: Two Gap Rule (2023): with two gaps, use the higher gap and put the stop just beyond its CE.
rules.quote: I'm finding half of that or 50% of it, consequent encroachment, and I place my stop loss just above that

rules.rule: A long off the RTH ORG CE puts its stop just below that CE.
rules.quote: stop loss is just below consequent encroachment and the regular trading hours opening range gap mid gap level uh CEs

rules.rule: A short puts its stop just above the CE of the wick or gap.
rules.quote: place the stop just above consequent encroachment. Look at how many times price gives you very clear signatures

rules.rule: Sep 2024 statement of the half-gap rule: about 70% of the time the half-gap level is traded to in the morning session.
rules.quote: the rules I'd live by is 70% of the time that half-gap price level gets traded to and repriced to in the morning session.

rules.rule: Jan 2026 Half Gap rule: price reaches for half of the ORG about 70% of the time.
rules.quote: About the opening range gap? Half of that gap's range. 70% of the time you're going to see it reach for half of that gap.

rules.rule: Minimum objective is a return to the gap CE by 10:00 (low-hanging fruit).
rules.quote: anticipating very minimum trying to get back to the gap consequent encroachment by 10:00

rules.rule: Half Gap Model sizing: look for about a hundred handles on NQ, anchored to the opening range gap.
rules.quote: Half gap. That was our model. That was one of the things I had for my son. All he has to do is look for a hundred handles.

rules.rule: 2026 shorthand: half gap is traded to by 10:00.
rules.quote: Consequent encroachment is here. So half gap 70% of time gets traded to by 10:00

rules.rule: NWOG as the draw: a market maker buy model delivers price up into the new week opening gap (2023).
rules.quote: Trading on the premise that it's a market maker buy model and sending price up into the new week opening gap, which is what I'm looking for.

rules.rule: After a premium rejection, aim for sell-side equal lows and the opening range gap below.
rules.quote: What you're going to aim for: sell side relative equal lows and or the opening range gap below

rules.rule: After NDOG defence, expect expansion to pre-set buyside liquidity.
rules.quote: Expansion out of the NDOG support matrix into predetermined buyside liquidity.

rules.rule: Oct 2024 variant of the target: a gap-up open comes all the way back to the prior settlement 70% of the time in the first 30 minutes. The dossier ties this to gaps of 75 handles or more.
rules.quote: Essentially 70% of the time okay in the first 30 minutes a gap higher opening is coming all the way back down to previous settlement price at 414 eastern time.

rules.rule: Scale out at the old low, halfway to the prior-day ORG CE, and just beyond that CE (3-contract example, Jul 2026).
rules.quote: I did event horizon, so I took a partial of the three contracts I was short. I took one right there, one halfway between this low and Monday's consequent encroachment, and then I took it right at a move just below regular trading hours opening range gap consequent encroachment from Monday's trading.

rules.rule: Event Horizon: the shaded zone around an NDOG or NWOG that price crosses before expanding.
rules.quote: That little pink shaded area is my Event Horizon. Whenever you have a New Day Opening Gap or New Week Opening Gap, price crosses that threshold and expands.

rules.rule: Exit criterion for a long into the ORG: bodies not closing at or above the 9:30 open or the ORG low means get out.
rules.quote: It did not close with a body at or above 9:30 opening price. It did not close with a body at or above the low of the regular trading hours opening range gap.

rules.rule: Bank partials as price enters the NWOG and leave a runner to the limit (2023).
rules.quote: We've taken partials as we enter that new week opening gap

rules.rule: Several visits to the NWOG CE in one week signal consolidation, so stay nimble and intraday.
rules.quote: One of the classic telltale signs that you are in a consolidation that's most likely going to continue is if we see price come back to it multiple times in a week.

rules.rule: Chart hygiene: yesterday's ORG is enough, and today's did not need annotating that session.
rules.quote: Using just yesterday's opening range gap is sufficient enough

rules.rule: Probe a gap-CE idea with one contract, and if the probe fails, look for the opposite side (Jul 2026).
rules.quote: I did the probe of one contract, see if it can get that run up in towards gap closure. And then when it failed, I knew what I was looking for as the opposite side.

rules.rule: Risk cap he cites in a barrier-dense Aug 2024 session: about one quarter of 1%.
rules.quote: and if I'm not risking but one quarter of 1% by the end of the day, you stay protected.

rules.rule: Runaway gap on NQ: with a very large gap he expects continuation and no fill back to settlement. The numeric threshold (over 120 handles) is in the dossier tag line; the quote carries the logic.
rules.quote: With such a large gap like that the rules I employ is that it's probably going to keep going in the direction of an extreme gap like that

rules.rule: An opening range gap greater than 120 handles on NQ is not likely to fill.
rules.quote: How much of a range was that opening range gap? It was greater than 120 handles, wasn't it? So what does that mean? It's not likely to fill in. Go back and watch the logic.

rules.rule: Breakaway gap: price leaves the opening range gap at the open and never tags mid-gap or closes the gap.
rules.quote: what happens if that's a breakaway gap? Starts right out the gate straight up, no full closure.

rules.rule: An NDOG retested too often without displacement loses value (2023).
rules.quote: but I generally don't like to see those types of new day opening gaps retested too frequently without displacement.

rules.rule: A gap-down open that tries to rally into the gap but cannot reach the lowest quadrant level is a bearish signature. The half-gap long idea is off.
rules.quote: Gaps lower, tries to go higher into the gap, fails to trade to the lowest quadrant level

rules.rule: Mid-NWOG test (Feb 2026): if bodies cannot even get back to the CE, that is weakness (short confirmation).
rules.quote: The bodies, notice that they cannot even get back to consequent encroachment

rules.rule: Stand aside when price is trapped inside overlapping prior-day opening range gaps (Apr 2026 neutral stance, per dossier overview).
rules.quote: All of this market structure this way right here, all of this tells me don't touch it.

rules.rule: Locate the NWOG on a lower-timeframe chart (15m or 5m) and never on the daily chart.
rules.quote: you don't want to use your daily chart because the daily chart is going to blend the data.

rules.rule: Forex NWOG is Friday close to Sunday open at 5:00 PM Eastern (GBP/USD, Jan 2025). Futures use the 18:00 open.
rules.quote: Notice right over here, you see this, that is the Friday close, Sunday opening 5:00 p.m. Eastern Time. So that is your new week opening gap.

rules.rule: Chart both RTH and ETH sessions (ES, Jan 2023) or the gaps are invisible.
rules.quote: If you look at the market with just electronic trading hours only, you miss the gaps like this up in here.

rules.rule: Demonstrated on the MNQ 1-minute chart: mark the ORG and its half gap.
rules.quote: There's your opening range gap for today. There's half gap right there, okay?

rules.rule: The 70% criterion is met when price trades into the gap CE before 10:00 ET.
rules.quote: It does so before 10:00, so there's our 70% likelihood of happening.

rules.rule: Sep 2024 nuance: the half-gap can be reached after the first 30 minutes and still count as the rule working.
rules.quote: And there you go, there's your half-gap. Did it happen in the first 30 minutes? No, but it did trade down to mid-gap

gradient_grid.summary: Grade any dealing range, gap, imbalance or wick into octant/quadrant/CE levels; a PD array only counts when it forms and is touched on one of those levels with bodies respecting it, then manage price hand-offs (chain of custody) to the next array's CE or the Event Horizon (midpoint between two liquidity pools).
gradient_grid.needs_clock: Partly. The core geometry is price-only: grid lines, wick CE (longest wick), FVG/IFVG/OB/volume-imbalance edges, the body-versus-wick respect test, the one-tick tolerance, Obsidian, Hangman, shadow overlap, Event Horizon (midpoint between two pools) and the chain-of-custody sequence all need only OHLC and swing/liquidity detection, so they could run on 24/7 synthetic indices using price delivery alone. What needs a clock is the way he mostly anchors the grid in 2026: the RTH opening range gap (prior day 4:14 pm ET settlement to 9:30 ET open), the 70%-by-10:00 base rate, the 9:30-10:00 opening range, New Day/Week Opening Gaps, the 7:00-9:00 pre-market range, and the macro windows (xx:50 to xx:10, e.g. 9:50-10:10, 10:50-11:10, 7:50-8:10, 3:50-4:00 MOC). He says time is only a booster (4SJlJdIANCo 36:06 'You don't have to take trades only in macro time'; gDFZ4p1BI1c 09:10 'if you apply time... further increases the likelihood') even though he also calls the technique 'time and price'. For synthetics, drop the session-gap grid and use swing ranges, imbalance boundaries and wicks as the graded ranges, optionally using the daily open/previous close as a stand-in gap.
gradient_grid.how_to_code:
1) GRID(lo,hi): step=(hi-lo)/8, lines k=0..8 at lo+k*step. Name by position (nearest the high = upper), not by fib number. His spoken order (BD7kqmgdBU8 19:17) is high, upper octant, upper quadrant, octant, CE, octant, lower quadrant, octant, low, i.e. 0.125/0.375/0.625/0.875 = octant lines, 0.25/0.75 = quadrant lines, 0.5 = CE; the '.625' (La2fTewydjw 25:25) and '0375' (C7CwjBOtHwM 15:22) mentions confirm odd eighths are octant points (that mapping is inferred). Before Mar 2026 only 25/50/75 was used.
2) Ranges to grid (objective once chosen): (a) RTH opening range gap = [min,max] of previous 16:14 ET settlement and 09:30 ET open, kept on the chart for days; (b) edges of a daily/60m FVG, BISI/SIBI, volume imbalance or suspension block; (c) a wick = body edge to wick tip, CE = midpoint, quarters at 25/75; among adjacent same-side wicks at a turn use the longest/most elongated; (d) NWOG/NDOG, 7:00-9:00 range, first 30-min and first-hour range; (e) an intraday swing high-low (subjective: 'frame the high and low correctly').
3) Anchor test for a candidate PD array (FVG, OB, breaker, IFVG, volume imbalance, suspension/rejection block): a key price of the array (edge, open, CE) lies within about 1 tick of a grid line, or the array lays on it. Anchored = high-probability; add score for being inside a higher-timeframe array, sitting in a macro window, or coinciding with an Event Horizon.
4) Respect test: after the touch compute body_hi=max(open,close), body_lo=min(open,close); 'respected' = no body beyond the level (wicks ignored). Bias = bodies confined to one half of the gap after leaving it (lower half = bearish); invalidation = a body left beyond the CE/level.
5) IFVG: a 3-candle FVG whose far edge is later closed through by a candle body (one tick beyond is enough); entry on the retest with bodies holding outside.
6) Order-block trigger / change in state of delivery: last up-close (down-close) candle at the level, signal when price trades through that candle's open (no close needed). Stop at that open (Dj0663u7VRc 27:06) or at the extreme +1-2 ticks; target the next array CE, the RTH gap CE, relative equal highs/lows or the highest/lowest octant.
7) Obsidian: two opposing wicks (upper wick of one bar, lower wick of another) within one swing; zone between their two midpoints; short on a close below the zone, long on a close above. Subjective: 'within a narrative' and which two wicks.
8) Hangman: at least 2 bars with bodies just on one side of a CE, then a bar whose wick crosses the CE and whose body returns to the other side; trade the rejection. Only one lecture; the bar count and 'just above' are undefined.
9) Shadow: intersect the price range of a newer imbalance with an older one (the 'pink area'); grid the overlap and require a later PDA to touch its lines. Thin evidence (pq9WuZ9q4Bg 36:36, MB7clEZvF7s 54:47).
10) Event Horizon: EH=(A+B)/2 where A is an old low/high or the near pool and B the next pool, old high/low or target; compute it before entry from the unrealized range; take 25% of the remaining (w2zTfhjScDg) or 1 of 3 contracts (2H_qpeIp2rY) at EH and run the rest to B. On news days he stacks it with the -2.5 standard deviation of the 7:00-8:30 range (59Elm8myGEc 13:54).
11) Chain of custody = state machine over validated, anchored PD arrays in time order: custody belongs to array X while bodies respect X; hand-off when a body/CISD breaks X; the expected next stop is the CE of the next array (IFVG to RTH gap CE, daily BISI CE, relative equal lows). He pyramids at each validated array.
12) Context: 70% RTH-gap-CE base rate, daily draw, avoid CPI/PPI/NFP prints.
Subjective parts: which dealing range, which wick is 'the one', 'narrative', how many bodies count as respect, shadow/Obsidian pairing, first-touch versus wait-for-reaction entry, partial size at Event Horizon.
gradient_grid.changes_over_time: Terminology drift: 2017-2020 dossiers use 'Fibonacci gradients' (OTE 62/70.5/79, 162/200 extensions); 2019-2022 dossiers use 'quadrant' loosely for premium/discount halves; 2023 introduces weekly wick quadrants (uzPM1CuSSx8, IU673ZUGuxI); Aug-Oct 2024 uses 25/50/75 'quadrants' on opening range gaps and FVGs (vfqyx8BYdNo, DRuEMX4RhMw, akfEjsn4adk) and in PFUe6OKmKuk 07:29 he says 'quarters theory is a joke'; Sep-Oct 2025 adds wick grading (8DWi2wLWv30, N4gTPOnZIYw, rxot6S73Lvs); Feb 2026 says 'gradient levels' anchor to the RTH gap (FBxxYUvNaY4); the word 'octant' first appears Mar 2026 (54kzPj03Rkg, sPKglrJAVFY 'These levels are your gradient levels'); the 8-tier octant grid is stated Jul-Aug 2026 (BD7kqmgdBU8, 4SJlJdIANCo). Quadrant labels flip between dossiers: 0.25 is called the upper quadrant in vfqyx8BYdNo but the lower quadrant in DRuEMX4RhMw, depending on fib direction, so code by price position. Event Horizon: the 2024 dossier (kuURDD1ajdQ 30:11) says it is a pink shaded zone around NDOG/NWOG where price commits to a run; every 2026 source (w2zTfhjScDg, k2QLuxMIZio, bUN_f8U_1Eg, EZB4vBUFdHw, 2H_qpeIp2rY, IF7dEkgWoO0) defines it as the 50% point between two liquidity pools/old low and target, so use the 2026 meaning and treat the 2024 one as an outlier (sUGuNE31lG0 only has an unspoken chart label 'Event Horizon Between REHs & Friday High'). Event Horizon partial size varies: 25% of the remainder (w2zTfhjScDg) versus 1 of 3 (2H_qpeIp2rY) versus 3 off of 9 (EZB4vBUFdHw 08:23). Wick selection hardened: Sep 24 2025 'One wick will be respected and it's your job to determine which one' and 'not a hard and fast rule' (8DWi2wLWv30 02:40), then Oct 1/3 2025 'longest wick' / 'most elongated'. Stop on an inversion FVG: Oct 2025 'Never, never, never' trail under it until structure breaks (rxot6S73Lvs 25:26) versus Jun 2026 'Raise the stop up just underneath this inversion fair value gap' (k2QLuxMIZio 05:33). Wick versus body: wicks may do damage and may exceed the level (2L88yH3LKcs 18:05, k2QLuxMIZio 09:21, one-tick tolerance LBrsLPKXZ2E 17:46) but pq9WuZ9q4Bg 36:36 and dYQSUCSbYn8 37:18 want the array to touch or lay on the level. rules.rule: A PD array is only recognised as an ICT PD array when it anchors to one of the octant or quadrant levels of the graded range.
rules.quote: the technique I teach you when it has to anchor to one of the octants or quadrant levels. That's how you know an ICT PD array

rules.rule: Bias is built top-down: daily chart first, then down to the 1m; never decide from the 1m chart alone.
rules.quote: working with the hierarchy of working from daily chart down to the smaller time frames. Not just looking at a smaller one minute chart

rules.rule: The octant and quadrant levels of the daily imbalances are projected down onto the 1m chart and used as the anchors.
rules.quote: anchored to? The daily. So the daily chart has these octant and quadrant levels

rules.rule: Base-rate bias for the day: about 70% of the time the half-gap (CE) of the RTH opening range gap is traded to in the first 30 minutes.
rules.quote: 70% of the time, the first 30 minutes, a half gap gets traded to. Now, that's a huge advantage for bias for session.

rules.rule: Read direction from which half of the gap/block price can occupy: if price works only in the lower half and cannot get into the upper half it is bearish (mirror for bullish).
rules.quote: Notice how we were working only in the lower half of that. So if it can't get in the upper half, is that bullish or bearish? It's bearish.

rules.rule: Frame the dealing range by its correct high and low; an arbitrary range is not the one.
rules.quote: dealing range, okay? Any old range is is not what we're looking for

rules.rule: Grade the unrealized (not yet delivered) dealing range with the grid; choosing the right range is the skill.
rules.quote: You don't see anybody grading an unrealized dealing range. They don't even know how to pick the right one.

rules.rule: The RTH opening range gap is measured between the prior day's 4:14 pm ET settlement and the 9:30 open.
rules.quote: That's the settlement yesterday at 4:14 p.m. Eastern time. And then 9:30 opening price this morning

rules.rule: The RTH opening range GAP (a price zone) is not the opening RANGE (the 9:30 to 10:00 window); do not mix them.
rules.quote: That's the regular trading hours or RTH O RG open range gap, not to be confused with the opening range, which is the first 30 minutes of trading from 9:30 to 10:00 Eastern time

rules.rule: The grid is nine lines in a fixed order: low, lowest octant, lower quadrant, octant, CE (50%), octant, upper quadrant, upper octant, high.
rules.quote: And that's these levels, the high quadrant, I'm sorry, upper octant, upper quadrant, octant, consequent encroachment, octant, lower quadrant, octant, and then the low

rules.rule: Once the RTH opening range gap exists, every intraday gradient level and fair value gap is anchored to its grid.
rules.quote: Once you have that opening range gap, every one of these gradient levels on your chart anchors to it.

rules.rule: Grade a swing with octants/quadrants to know where PD arrays should form; arrays that form on a gradient level are validated and high probability.
rules.quote: that's how we determine where PD arrays should form and should they form at that gradient level or looked at level. Then they're perceived as high probability. They're validated, if you will.

rules.rule: Wick grading: when several wicks cluster at a turn, take the consequent encroachment of the longest wick only; do not average or use the smaller ones.
rules.quote: Consequent encroachment of the longest wick. Don't use this one, don't use that one, this is the longest one so consequent encroachment is right there.

rules.rule: Wick selection: pick the most elongated wick.
rules.quote: Why am I picking this one? Because this one is the most elongated

rules.rule: Earlier, softer version of wick selection: plot every available wick, price will respect one, and the trader must work out which while it is delivering.
rules.quote: One wick will be respected and it's your job to determine which one that is while price is delivering and before the next move happens

rules.rule: A wick is treated like a gap: a balanced price range that takes precedence (the dossier example is wick over order block).
rules.quote: whenever you have that, just like a gap, wicks take precedence. Why? Because they're balanced price ranges.

rules.rule: A wick is gridded like any range: its low, lower quadrant, CE, upper quadrant and high are the reaction levels.
rules.quote: This is the low of it. Lower quadrant. Consequent encroachment and then the upper quadrant and the high of that wick

rules.rule: Shadow PD array: an imbalance that casts its shadow over another imbalance; this overlap is what a later PDA must be measured against.
rules.quote: A PD array simply called a shadow because it's casting a shadow over top of another imbalance

rules.rule: Obsidian PD array: two opposing wicks within a narrative, each split in half; the consequent encroachment levels between the two wicks are the reaction zone.
rules.quote: Obsidian is is two opposing wicks within a narrative and you split those wicks in half and between those two wicks consequent encouragement levels

rules.rule: Hangman PD array: bodies sit just above a consequent encroachment (suggesting continuation), then one candle wicks past the level and rejects back outside.
rules.quote: The bodies are just above consequent encroachment, which would indicate what? Continuation is likely, but then we move back down outside of it. It just goes up there, wicks past it, and then rejects.

rules.rule: Event Horizon (2026 definition): the halfway point between a nearer liquidity pool and the next, larger pool or old high.
rules.quote: We're inside that fair value gap we're going to see event horizon, which is again the halfway point between the 1-hour minor buy side liquidity pool and then the old high here.

rules.rule: Event Horizon is projected from an old low (or high) to the next target or pool of liquidity and used as an approximate anchor, also on BTC.
rules.quote: since we have this old low, this is where you would use my event horizon concept, which is an old low down to a next target or pool of liquidity and we'll just ballpark it.

rules.rule: Chain of custody: study how price is handed from one PD array to the next, not buying and selling pressure.
rules.quote: what we're doing is we're studying the chain of custody from one PD array to the next. We're not studying buying and selling pressure

rules.rule: Chain of custody framing: the question is how price moves from one PD array to the next.
rules.quote: the topic I've been focusing on which is the chain of custody for price. Okay, so how does price move

rules.rule: Every time price reaches an octant or quadrant level, watch for a PD array to form there.
rules.quote: Every single time we get to an octant or a quadrant level, you're looking for a PDA to form.

rules.rule: The PD array must touch or lie on the grid level to be valid.
rules.quote: It's got to touch or lay on it to validate this PD array to be perfect.

rules.rule: Tolerance is about one tick: a wick one tick beyond the level is still accepted.
rules.quote: The high on this candlestick comes in at 29,943. So, went one tick higher, which is fine. It's completely permissible.

rules.rule: A rally that stalls dead on the lower octant, into a bearish suspension block, is the sell location.
rules.quote: High comes in at 966 half and that's the lower octant level. Stopping right there dead in its tracks

rules.rule: Order block at the level is confirmed when the candle trades through its opening price (it need not close beyond): that is the change in state of delivery.
rules.quote: As soon as this candlestick trades down through the opening price, it need not close below it. As soon as it does that, that validates this as a change in the state of delivery

rules.rule: Inversion FVG is validated by a candle body close just one tick beyond its edge.
rules.quote: So it's one tick below. So it validates this as an inversion fair gap.

rules.rule: Obsidian trigger: a close beyond the midpoints of the two opposing wicks.
rules.quote: we want to see a close below obsidian which is two opposing wicks midpoints.

rules.rule: Hangman trigger: bodies imply continuation, then a small wick beyond the level and the rejection finishes the move.
rules.quote: that's the hangman. Okay? This little wick above when the criteria is the bodies are suggesting maybe continuation, but then we get this. Then it's done. It's over.

rules.rule: Sell short at the grid-anchored order block and add (pyramid) there for a larger position.
rules.quote: that's where you can sell short or add and build a premium entry pyramiding for a larger position to go lower. So, what we're seeing is the chain of custody and control of price. It's not buying and selling pressure.

rules.rule: Long entry on an inversion FVG that is anchored to an octant of an earlier RTH opening range gap.
rules.quote: I'm going to go long on this inversion fair value gap. It's anchored to this octant from Tuesday's trading hours open range cap.

rules.rule: Entry at the consequent encroachment zone of a graded wick.
rules.quote: that gives me an opportunity to trade at the consequent encroachment zone.

rules.rule: Do not take the first hit at the level; wait for the reaction and the break, then look for the next array beyond it.
rules.quote: Don't take first hit to go short. Look for it to go there and then break down and then start looking for something extra past the reaction

rules.rule: Stop at the open of the candle the setup is built on; if price goes there he is out.
rules.quote: I'm stopping on the stop loss that I put just at this candlestick's open. Okay? So, I felt that if it was going to go there, it warrants me being out. I don't want to hold on to any more risk.

rules.rule: Short stop: the candle high plus a tick or two.
rules.quote: candlestick's high plus a tick or two. That's a really good place to put a stop loss.

rules.rule: Long stop below the low of the range/array the entry rests on, even if wider than usual.
rules.quote: The original stop has to be below that low right there. So, buying it here, stop loss down there.

rules.rule: First objective: the CE of the RTH opening range gap is expected by 10:00 (the 70% case).
rules.quote: So we traded up into that gap or consequent encroachment. It does so before 10:00, so there's our 70% likelihood of happening.

rules.rule: Target the consequent encroachment of the RTH opening range gap.
rules.quote: the midpoint or consequent encroachment of regular trading hours opening range gap for Monday's trading.

rules.rule: Bullish target can be the highest octant of a 60m imbalance.
rules.quote: It's going to go right back up into that 60-minute buy side imbalance sell side inefficiency. And trades right to the highest octant

rules.rule: Event Horizon scaling: take about 25% of the remaining position off at the Event Horizon and let the runner reach for the rest.
rules.quote: Take about 25% of the remaining portion off when you're at event horizon

rules.rule: Take one contract off when price reaches the Event Horizon vicinity.
rules.quote: this is an old low down to there. Okay? So, if it gets in this vicinity here, I'll take one off cuz that's event horizon.

rules.rule: With three contracts: one partial at the old low, one halfway to the next target (Event Horizon), the last just below the gap CE.
rules.quote: I did event horizon, so I took a partial of the three contracts I was short. I took one right there, one halfway between this low and Monday's consequent encroachment

rules.rule: Trail the stop only behind verified PD arrays (e.g., wick CE) so a retrace cannot get below them.
rules.quote: So I can actually bring my stop up and lock in a little bit more juice out of this lemon because if it's going to retrace, it shouldn't find its way below this wick's consequent encouragement.

rules.rule: Exit long when bodies fail to close at or above the 9:30 open and the RTH gap low.
rules.quote: It did not close with a body at or above 9:30 opening price. It did not close with a body at or above the low of the regular trading hours opening range gap.

rules.rule: Oct 2025 rule: do not trail the stop under an inversion FVG until structure has broken.
rules.quote: if you're long and you rolled your stop loss just below the inversion fair value gap: Never, never, never do that until it breaks structure and leaving it

rules.rule: Jun 2026 rule: raise the stop to just under the inversion FVG once price is away from it.
rules.quote: Raise the stop up just underneath this inversion fair value gap now, cuz if it goes there, I don't want to be a part of this anymore.

rules.rule: Wicks may pierce the CE but a body left beyond it makes continuation harder; bodies decide.
rules.quote: We don't want to see it leave a body down there. Otherwise, it makes it more difficult for the market to continue

rules.rule: Bodies, not wicks, tell the story: a bearish read holds while bodies do not touch the CE or lay on the octant.
rules.quote: the bodies are not touching consequent encroachment. The wick can, but the wicks are allowed to do damage. The narrative and volume is really shown in the bodies.

rules.rule: Bearish wick-CE read is void if price closes above that wick's consequent encroachment.
rules.quote: it would have to close above this wick's consequent encroachment. You see a theme here how I'm teaching you to use these wicks. It's giving you discount sensitivity validation for continuation going lower.

rules.rule: Nasdaq (NQ) only, kept simple; he says the teaching applies to other markets.
rules.quote: looking at the NASDAQ again. Keeping things simple. Not a long list of markets to look at. Everything I'm teaching here is applicable to everything else.

rules.rule: Do not put real risk on a 1m idea that the daily chart does not support.
rules.quote: if there's nothing supporting the idea on the daily chart, it's not going to be helpful to you to place so much risk

rules.rule: Grid has two axes: price levels (octants/quadrants) horizontally and macro start times vertically.
rules.quote: That is the grid aspect horizontally. Vertically, the vertical axis is the macro start time

rules.rule: Example of a macro-time low: the lowest candle of the 9:50 to 10:10 macro.
rules.quote: it's occurring during 9:50 to 10:10 macro. What's the lowest candle here? 10:10.

rules.rule: Entries need not be inside macro time; shorting just ahead of the macro is acceptable.
rules.quote: you can short it just ahead of the macro. You don't have to take trades only in macro time.

rules.rule: Time is a booster: a gradient level sitting with a FVG/OB/breaker raises sensitivity, and a macro window raises it further.
rules.quote: if that is sitting right with a PD array like a fair value gap, an order block, a breaker, it supercharges the likelihood that it's going to be very sensitive. And if you apply time

rules.rule: Example: pre-market 7:50 to 8:10 macro trades down into a quadrant level and stops on the tick.
rules.quote: we come back right back down in during the macro 750 Eastern time to 8:10 that's my macro time. This trades right down into a quadrant level

fvg.summary: A fair value gap (BISI/SIBI), volume imbalance or liquidity void left by displacement is the pullback entry zone: price returns to its edge or 50% consequent encroachment, candle bodies must respect that level, and the trade runs to opposing liquidity.
fvg.needs_clock: The core pattern needs no clock. FVG (BISI/SIBI), consequent encroachment, volume imbalance, BPR, immediate rebalance, inversion and wick CE are defined only by candle highs, lows, opens and closes, so they could run on 24/7 synthetic indices using price delivery alone. The clock enters in four places. (1) Silver Bullet: retracement entry into a FVG between 10:00 and 11:00 New York time. (2) 'First presented FVG': the first gap after the 9:30 ET open candle, the 9:31 candle being the stated minimum, within the first 30 minutes. (3) Macro windows (9:50-10:10, 2:50-3:10 London) and Model 13 sessions (7-10 for FX, 8:30-11 for index futures). (4) Opening range gap, NWOG and NDOG voids, which need a session close-to-open break and do not exist on a continuous 24/7 feed. For synthetics, drop the clock gates and replace 'first presented' with the first qualifying gap after a defined anchor such as a swept swing or a fixed bar-count reset. My own caveat, not his teaching: volume imbalance and body-gap voids depend on how candles are built. If each open equals the prior close there are none; if built from ticks a one-tick gap always appears, so a minimum-size filter is needed.
fvg.how_to_code:
1) Gap scan on closed bars (candle 1 = i-2, candle 2 = i-1 displacement, candle 3 = i). BISI/bullish: low[i] > high[i-2], zone = [high[i-2], low[i]]. SIBI/bearish: high[i] < low[i-2], zone = [high[i], low[i-2]]. CE = zone midpoint; quadrants at 25/75 percent of the zone. Candle 1's high (short) or low (long) is the stop anchor.
2) Displacement filter (SUBJECTIVE, never given as a number): candle 2 has a large body relative to its range and recent ATR, and/or its close breaks the last swing (market structure shift). Ignore gaps below a minimum size.
3) Disqualify: the three candles sit inside a prior overlapping-wick range or inside an existing BPR (Apr 2025 rule); for shorts the gap must lie above 50 percent of the displacement leg, for longs in discount (2022 rule); no displacement means no setup. Context from the 2022 model: a sweep of a swing or equal highs/lows, then displacement breaking the opposite swing, then the gap. Bias or draw on liquidity must exist (SUBJECTIVE).
4) Gap state machine: ACTIVE -> TOUCHED (record depth: near edge, short of CE, at CE, beyond CE) -> RESPECTED (candle bodies stay on the origin side of CE; wicks through are allowed) or FAILED (a body closes beyond CE). If a body closes through the whole gap it INVERTS (IFVG) and the direction flips.
5) Entry: after formation, price retraces into the zone. Variants he taught: limit at CE (the default 2020 to 2025), partial fill short of CE (IOFED), 'close proximity', or wait for a confirming 3-candle swing (2022). Never enter on the expansion candle itself.
6) Stop: beyond candle 1's extreme. Padding is contested: 1 to 2 ticks (2022), zero (Feb 2024), one tick (Feb 2026). Tighter variants put the stop just beyond the CE (Venom/BISI, trailing on first presented FVG). With two stacked gaps use the CE of the higher one.
7) Target and management: nearest opposing liquidity (swing, equal highs/lows, prior session or day extreme) or an opposing PD array. Partials at CE and quadrants. Trail the stop to the gap edge or CE. Pyramid on a new gap in the same direction.
8) Variants. Volume imbalance (bullish): min(open,close)[i] > max(open,close)[i-1] while low[i] <= high[i-1], zone is the body gap, CE its midpoint. Immediate rebalance: bar i+1 trades back to bar i's high or low (touch only, no 3-candle gap) and bar i+2 expands; time-stop if no run by the next bar. BPR: intersection of an earlier bearish gap and a later bullish gap (or the reverse) covering the same prices; price should not re-enter it. Liquidity void: a run of same-direction long-bodied bars with no body overlap, or an opening-range gap; closes when returning bodies trade through it. Breakaway gap: a gap out of a consolidation or HTF-array CE that price never retraces into while running to the HTF draw; it can only be labelled after the fact, so code it as 'hold, do not wait for fill'. Wick CE: for a long wick measure open to extreme and take 50 percent. First presented FVG: first qualifying gap after an anchor event (9:30 ET candle), so it needs a clock or a substitute anchor.
Subjective parts: what counts as real displacement, which gaps matter (obvious/protracted, nested with an order block, 'willingness to stay open'), the narrative and draw on liquidity, premium/discount location judgement, and whether a wick over a gap makes it a suspension block instead.
fvg.changes_over_time:
Timeline from the dossiers. Sept 2020: volume imbalance introduced (body gap with overlapping wicks) and consequent encroachment already used as the 50 percent threshold. 2022: Month 04 lectures (uploaded Sept 2022) define the FVG and liquidity void on USD/JPY daily; the 2022 mentorship model is sweep, displacement, retrace into the FVG, with first-gap-found top-down on 5 to 1 minute. 2023: SIBI/BISI naming in the dossiers, immediate rebalance (from Feb 2023), BPR (from Jan 2023), breakaway gap and gap theory (June 2023), Silver Bullet 10 to 11. 2024: FVG selection protocol (displacement, narrative, not every gap), strict mean threshold versus CE wording (Sept to Oct 2024), low resistance runs where the gap should stay partly open, 'first fair value gap between 9:30 and 10:00' appears Aug to Sept 2024. 2025 to 2026: first presented FVG, suspension block and Venom (BPR), disqualifying gaps inside a BPR (Apr 2025), 'willingness to stay open' (Feb 2026).
Conflicts and changes:
(1) Stop padding. Apr to May 2022: 'at minimum above the candle's high' and '1 to 2 ticks above' (CnTXwAuDi9Y 42:15). Feb 2024 (kNlySn81dmo): exactly at the candle high, 'not one tick above it'. Feb 2026: 'one tick above' candlestick number one. 2025: above the first candle of the SIBI, or just below the BISI's CE for Venom. Jun 2023: above the CE of the higher of two gaps. Sept 2022 (SO3SJFNRim8) used a fixed 4-point stop and picked the gap that allowed it.
(2) Entry depth. 2022 (nv0ey5UyOmY 36:09): anywhere between the gap's low and high is sufficient. Dec 2022 (_GKZoHIJpj0): in a strong trend it only taps the edge and will not fill. Aug 2023 IOFED: shallower than the CE. 2020 to 2025: wait for the CE. Late 2025: stay in the upper or lower half and it is 'better that it doesn't' touch the midpoint (wcSH7zlQ1Zc); Oct 2025: does not like buying a full closure.
(3) Blind limits. May 2022 (OYNpIeu9czw 07:02): do not place a blind limit inside an FVG, wait for a confirming 3-candle swing. 2025 dossiers show limit fills at CE and 'hit that limit order'.
(4) Gap should stay open versus gap should be closed. Month 04 and the void lecture (HTQgH11W37o) trade a counter-move that closes the gap or void, then reverses. Oct 2024 (svYZKOrWPRo), Feb 2026 and the breakaway-gap teaching want the gap left partly open and not filled. Treat them as two trade types, rebalance at an old gap versus continuation off a fresh one.
(5) Virgin gaps. Sept 2023 (LPmMtq9jLm8): a gap can be revisited and need not be fresh. Jan 2025 (b4DOrfGau8w): the third touch will break through. 2025 to 2026 emphasis is on only the first presented gap after 9:30.
(6) Mean threshold versus CE. Jan to Aug 2023 dossiers use 'CE / mean threshold' and '50 percent CE' of order-block bodies loosely; from Sept 2024 (fhBnnU44A6E, svYZKOrWPRo) and Feb 2025 (7cYwwE1GoV8) mean threshold is only for order blocks and CE only for gaps, wicks and inefficiencies.
(7) 'Liquidity void' means different things: Sept 2022 a large one-sided displacement range closed by bodies (HTQgH11W37o); Jan 2023 a gap between a candle's high/close and the next low/open (ZrZJmwrMxFY); 2025 an opening-range gap with no price traded, explicitly not a BISI/SIBI (uIvlS330qrA); Sept 2022 'vacuum block' for news gaps (shPGUz9pU-A).
(8) Immediate rebalance wording. Apr to Sept 2023: not a three-candle gap, just touching the prior candle's high or low in the same or next candle. The May 2023 dossier summary (ZtLMTXv-Dr0) paraphrases it as backfilling the range in a candle or two; the May 2025 version is the next candle opening and retesting the displacement candle's high, then a run.
(9) Wick over a gap. Jan 2025 (5N4QHrY6DRc 18:48): a gap with a wick lying over it is a reclaimed FVG revisited about 90 percent of the time. Sept 2025 (-Td-D-vKJDg 10:54): that picture is a suspension block 'you would never look at as a fair value gap'. The 2020 volume imbalance is the same wicks-overlap, bodies-gap shape.
(10) Small timeframes. 2022 first gap top-down on 5 to 1 minute; Jun 2023 warns new traders off seconds charts; Sept 2024 uses a 15-second chart for entries.
(11) Quote reliability. Several 2022 table cells (36184dDAqtM, QkokVv0owSE, 8z6My18WZqA) read like summarised rules rather than raw speech, so treat them as lower confidence than the 2024 to 2026 cells.
fvg.markets: Mostly NQ (Nasdaq futures) and ES (S&P futures). Also forex (EUR/USD, GBP/USD, USD/JPY daily in the Month 04 lectures, a few JPY crosses), DXY used for bias and inversion gaps, and one-off crude oil (CL) and Dow (YM). Count method: I parsed every 'Trades Taken or Shown' table in the 884 dossiers (about 960 trade rows in all). 367 rows in 331 dossiers name an FVG, imbalance, CE, BISI/SIBI, volume imbalance, liquidity void, BPR or breakaway gap in the entry or setup description. By market (rows can list more than one): NQ about 227, ES 78, EUR/USD 22, GBP/USD 15, DXY 3, CL 2, YM 1, 18 unlabelled. By dossier year: 2022 76, 2023 64, 2024 71, 2025 81, 2026 72, plus 3 earlier (2017, 2020, 2021). These are dossier summaries (live executions, demos, case studies), not a verified trade log.
