rules.rule: Only act on a fair value gap that has real displacement behind it (Sept 2024 NQ lesson); a three-candle gap without displacement is not tradeable.
rules.quote: Waiting to see if we get a fair value Gap with real displacement behind it.

rules.rule: Do not trade every FVG. Protocol (Model 12, Feb 2024): order block or PD array is hit, an expansion swing follows, the FVG forms on that expansion, then entry on the pullback into it.
rules.quote: bearish order block hits it expansion price swing we're looking for the fair value Gap then that's the protocol so we're not to look for every potential fair value Gap and I'm going to trade it no you don't do that

rules.rule: 2026 quality filter: the best gap shows a willingness to stay open (price reacts at it and leaves it unfilled instead of closing it in).
rules.quote: My fair value gap, okay, it needs to show a willingness to stay open. That's the highest probability fair value gap.

rules.rule: A gap does not have to be virgin or fresh and can be revisited, but it must be engaged at the right time of day (Sept 2023).
rules.quote: The fair value gap needs to be engaged at the right time of day, even if it's been traded to before! A fair value gap doesn't need to be the first visit, it doesn't have to be a 'virgin' level

rules.rule: Needs a bias and a known draw on liquidity (stops or inefficiency to rebalance) first; an immediate rebalance alone does not help without it (May 2023).
rules.quote: If you don't know what the draw on liquidity is or where the market's likely to reach to, whether it be for stops or inefficiency for the purposes of rebalancing or repricing, the immediate rebalance isn't going to help you all that much.

rules.rule: Location rule for longs (2022): FVG sits in discount, below 50% of the current dealing range, on the 15-minute; mirror for shorts in premium.
rules.quote: enter long when price retraces into a 15-minute Fair Value Gap that is located within a Discount (below 50% equilibrium) of the current Dealing Range

rules.rule: 2022 short rule: the FVG must sit above the 50% equilibrium of the displacement leg's high-to-low range.
rules.quote: for a bearish displacement leg to qualify for a short entry setup, the resulting Fair Value Gap must be located above the 50% equilibrium level of that displacement leg's high-to-low range

rules.rule: Trade FVGs in line with higher-timeframe order flow; a small FVG that nests inside a higher-timeframe imbalance is preferred (May 2023).
rules.quote: look for a fair value gap to trade into aligned with higher-timeframe order flow.

rules.rule: In bullish order flow every fair value gap and down-close candle acts as support (July 2026).
rules.quote: And bullish order flow, every fair value gap and down close candle starts supporting price.

rules.rule: 2022 model sequence: run above old or equal highs (reverse for lows), short-term lows taken out with displacement, then retrace through the displacement leg into a FVG to short.
rules.quote: to run above an old high or relative equal highs and if you're bearish that short-term lows taken out with displacement and then you go back through that displacement leg looking for a fair value gap to short into

rules.rule: A broken level is not a trade by itself; a valid entry needs an FVG formed during displacement through the level and entry on the retracement into that FVG (2022).
rules.quote: when price breaks a prior support/liquidity level, do not trade the level simply because it broke; a valid short entry requires an FVG to form during displacement through the level, and entry must occur upon retracement into that FVG

rules.rule: Month 04 lecture: after liquidity is run the market returns to close a fair value gap; the bearish USD/JPY daily example is mirrored for buy-side runs (gap below market).
rules.quote: Everything shown here is reversed for buy-side liquidity runs where the market will come back and close in a fair value gap below the marketplace.

rules.rule: FVG, order block or void is an internal-range entry; it runs to external range liquidity (the low resistance liquidity run).
rules.quote: Most of the time you're going to find that internal range liquidity entries will run to external range liquidity.

rules.rule: Venom sub-model (May 2025): a SIBI must come first, then a single-candle sweep of sell-side stops, then a BISI departing it.
rules.quote: You have to have a cibby first and then a bissy leaving it or it's not a venom.

rules.rule: PD array matrix (Sept 2022): liquidity void and fair value gap are premium arrays, ranked with mitigation block, breaker, order block, rejection block and old highs.
rules.quote: The idea is we're looking for something down in this list of arrays to target one of the premium arrays: mitigation block, breaker, liquidity void, fair value gap, bearish order block, rejection block, old high or historic low.

rules.rule: Liquidity void teaching (Month 04): price is delivered in stages and closing the void completes the rebalance.
rules.quote: Pricing in on an institutional level has to happen in stages, and closing the void completes that rebalancing.

rules.rule: Month 04 definition: a range (about 25 pips on USD/JPY daily) left with no trading outside the displacement candle; the gap is left open.
rules.quote: About 25 pips: that is our fair value gap, and it's been left open. There's been no trading outside of the movement of that range except for that down candle.

rules.rule: 2022 trigger: after the high is taken, watch the candle; as it closes and the next opens, check whether the sequence created a fair value gap.
rules.quote: once that candle closes and this candle opens you're gonna monitor this candle and you want to see as soon as this candle closes does it create that fair value gap

rules.rule: 2022 checklist: swing level broken, move energetic, FVG present; then price trades down into the gap and you buy.
rules.quote: we have a swing high right here it breaks it does it trade above that yes was it energetic yes does it have a fair value Gap yes so now the market trades down into it here

rules.rule: Naming: SIBI (sell-side imbalance, buy-side inefficiency) is the bearish FVG; BISI is the bullish one.
rules.quote: The classification is SIBI (Sell-side Imbalance Buy-side Inefficiency)

rules.rule: Volume imbalance (Jan 2023): two candle bodies that do not touch while the wicks overlap.
rules.quote: A volume imbalance is where one candle's body and another candle's body doesn't touch, but there are wicks that overlap in between.

rules.rule: Volume imbalance origin (Sept 2020): no wick crossover would be a normal gap; here the wick crosses but open and close differ, and that body difference is the imbalance.
rules.quote: When we look at a gap in price, usually there is no wick, no body crossover. But here, the candle's low crosses over, but there's a difference between its open and close.

rules.rule: Immediate rebalance (Apr 2023): no three-candle gap needed; the candle just touches the prior candle's extreme and runs.
rules.quote: Immediate rebalance is my concept when it doesn't require three candles to make what you would expect as a fair value gap. It just touches the prior candle and runs.

rules.rule: A FVG is a deferred rebalance (price comes back later); an immediate rebalance returns to the prior candle's high in the same or next candle.
rules.quote: This is a deferred rebalance: a fair value gap is a deferred rebalance, it's going to be referred to at a future time.

rules.rule: Consequent encroachment is the 50% midpoint of a gap, inefficiency or wick.
rules.quote: That's the halfway point. So if we're looking at an inefficiency or a wick, it's always called consequent encroachment. Consequent encroachment is the midpoint of an inefficiency or gap.

rules.rule: Oct 2024 terminology: mean threshold is the midpoint of an order block; consequent encroachment is only for gaps and inefficiencies.
rules.quote: half of that order block is a mean threshold reference point it's not consequent encroachment consequent encroachment is gaps or inefficiencies.

rules.rule: Wick CE: treat a long wick as a gap; measure open to extreme and take 50% as its consequent encroachment (Apr 2025).
rules.quote: And what I like to do is I like to measure from the open down to the low. 50% of that is consequent encroachment because I teach you that a wick whether it's below or above a candlestick is to be treated as a [gap].

rules.rule: 2025 usage of liquidity void: an opening range gap (no price traded at all) is a true void, distinct from BISI/SIBI.
rules.quote: Eventually price will want to rebalance all of this here because it's inefficient, because there's no price at all, zero. So this is an actual liquidity void. It's not a buy-side imbalance sell-side inefficiency, it's an actual liquidity void.

rules.rule: Balanced price range (Apr 2023): a buy-side imbalance that price later trades back through becomes a BPR and stops price like a brick wall.
rules.quote: that buy-side imbalance sell-side inefficiency becomes a Balanced Price Range. That means it's going to stop like a brick wall standing in the way of price action!

rules.rule: Entry reaction level is the consequent encroachment, the midpoint of the gap (Silver Bullet context, Oct 2023).
rules.quote: it found its opportunity to drop down into consequent encroachment which is midpoint of that Gap here

rules.rule: On a first presented FVG formed after a liquidity raid, wait for consequent encroachment to be tapped before entering (May 2025).
rules.quote: you wait for consequent encroachment to be tapped.

rules.rule: 2022 model: enter inside the FVG or in close proximity to it.
rules.quote: close proximity entries that means either inside the Fair Value Gap or in close proximity to it

rules.rule: Never chase the expansion swing; wait for the FVG to form and for price to come back into it (for a short, back up to the candle high that is the gap low).
rules.quote: this is where we do not Chase it we just simply wait for the fair value Gap to form

rules.rule: IOFED (Jan 2025): limit-order entry into a partial fair value gap, expecting expansion away.
rules.quote: That's institutional order flow entry drill, which is an entry into a partial fair value gap and we should see expansion to the downside and hit that limit order.

rules.rule: IOFED as defined in Aug 2023: a shallower entry, less than half of the inefficiency (before the 50% CE).
rules.quote: Institutional order flow entry drill which is a partial entry but less than half of the inefficiency or consequent encroachment, that is institutional order flow entry.

rules.rule: Immediate rebalance entry (May 2025): the next candle opens, trades back to the displacement candle's high, then price runs on the following candle.
rules.quote: Through it here and then the next candle opens, trades right back down. That candle's high. That's an immediate rebalance. And then the next candle after that price will start running.

rules.rule: Oct 2025: on a buy-side continuation he does not want a full closure of the gap; he wants a partial.
rules.quote: I do not like to buy a full closure of a fair value gap when it's a buy side and continuation

rules.quote: Closing right up on that 104.76 level: the ultimate draw on price was to close that liquidity void.

rules.rule: 2022: stop at minimum above the high of the candle that formed the FVG (for shorts).
rules.quote: your stop loss has to be at minimum above the candle's high that formed the fair value gap

rules.rule: Model 13 (Feb 2024): stop sits at the high (or low) of the candle that forms the FVG edge used for the setup.
rules.quote: stop loss is placed at the high of the candle that forms the high of the Fair Value Gap used for the setup

rules.rule: Model 13 (Feb 2024), same sentence continued: no padding, which contradicts his 2022 (1 to 2 ticks) and 2026 (one tick) wording.

rules.quote: I'm finding half of that or 50% of it, consequent encroachment, and I place my stop loss just above that

rules.rule: Venom long (Apr 2025): stop just below the consequent encroachment of the BISI; a deeper retest means the BPR failed.
rules.quote: Because this venom model is a balanced price range and it should not come back down here. If it does, it's not a venom and it's probably going to be a wrong trade

rules.rule: Enter from internal range liquidity (OB/FVG) and exit at opposing external range liquidity pools.

rules.rule: After the void is closed, price reprices to the opposing equal lows (December 15th lows in the example).

rules.rule: Breakaway gap: leave it open and aim for the higher-timeframe draw on liquidity; do not expect it to fill.
rules.quote: it becomes a breakaway gap; you wait for it to trade to the higher timeframe draw on liquidity and do not expect it to fill.

rules.rule: Once liquidity and inefficiency have both been delivered to, price runs for the opposing side of liquidity.
rules.quote: It has balanced this out here, and then it starts its run for the opposing side of liquidity.

rules.rule: Model 13: take profits at opposing PD arrays (discount arrays near equilibrium, previous session or day lows).
rules.quote: Profit Taking Logic: We are looking to take profits at opposing PD Arrays

rules.rule: Trail the stop to the CE of the first presented FVG formed 9:31 to 10:00 ET (Feb 2025).
rules.quote: raise the stop up so now I have the stop at the middle or consequent encroachment of the first presentive fair value Gap that occurs between 9:31 and 10:00 always eastern time.

rules.rule: Ma Deuce scaling (Sept 2023): first partial at consequent encroachment, next at the lower quadrant, remainder at another discount array.
rules.quote: first partial would be here at consequent encroachment and you let it run some more to get down to the lower quadrant

rules.quote: And there's a partial again. and I lowered the stop right above the high of that fair value gap because if it's now going to trade back to it, it's going to go higher.

rules.rule: Immediate rebalance time stop: if price does not go by the next candle it consolidates or reverses, so abort the trade (Sept 2023).
rules.quote: If it doesn't do it by the next candle after the immediate rebalance, you're going to consolidate or reverse.

rules.rule: 2022: add a second position when a new market structure shift retraces into the newly formed FVG.

rules.rule: Sept 2022 live trade: want the gap to stay open so it acts as a breakaway gap.
rules.quote: I want to see that stay open, that would act as a breakaway gap.

rules.rule: Breakaway gap (June 2023): a SIBI/BISI that supports being on side and that you do not want to see filled.
rules.quote: something that supports the idea that you're on side and you don't want to see that gap filled, so you treat it as a breakaway gap.

rules.rule: Sept 2025 identification: a gap left out of a consolidation at the CE of a higher-timeframe PD array is classed as a breakaway gap.
rules.quote: It's leaving a consolidation in consequent encroachment of a higher time frame PD. So any gap left there, that's an easy way of classifying it as a breakaway gap

rules.rule: Mar 2026: wick below CE is allowed; a body close below CE invalidates the gap.
rules.quote: Consequent encroachment: it can wick below, but it cannot close below consequent encroachment to keep this validated

rules.rule: Jan 2023: price should not trade through the midpoint; going below it compromises the premise.
rules.quote: Consequent encroachment, remember we don't want to see it trade through the midpoint

rules.rule: Jan 2025: wicks may trade through the level, the bodies show the narrative.
rules.quote: it's okay for these wicks to trade through it, that's what wicks do, but the bodies are showing you the narrative.

rules.rule: Live trade (Sept 2022): if the BISI's consequent encroachment loses ground, kill the trade.
rules.quote: We had consequent encroachment of this buy-side imbalance sell-side inefficiency, don't want to see it lose any more ground here. If it does, I'll just kill it and be content.

rules.rule: Apr 2025: disqualify a first presented FVG that forms inside an existing balanced price range (overlapping wicks, no real breakaway).
rules.quote: Why is it not a valid first presented fair value gap? Because you need to look at where it is in proximity to the candles that formed just before it.

rules.rule: 2022: a short setup into a FVG below 50% of the displacement is invalid.
rules.quote: if the FVG is below 50%, the short setup is invalidated

rules.rule: Aug 2023: after price passes through and leaves a gap it becomes a BPR; price is not expected to trade through it again.
rules.quote: when the market comes back up to it here and passes through and leaves it now this becomes a balanced price range we do not expect it to go through it

rules.rule: 2022: no displacement breaking a short-term swing means there is no setup.
rules.quote: if price trades through an old swing level or Fair Value Gap and fails to produce displacement breaking a short-term swing low/high, no trade setup exists

rules.rule: Month 04: the wick may trade through; the candle bodies must close in and respect the gap.
rules.quote: The wick trades through the body, but the bodies of the candle completely close in here

rules.rule: Sept 2025: once price breaks down through the gap's CE and out of it, the gap has failed and flips to an inversion FVG.
rules.quote: Once we trade down below it and hits the consequent encroachment and breaks outside of it, that means it's likely to trade lower to trade to inversion fair value gap

rules.rule: June 2026: a candle must close outside the gap to validate it as inverted; a wick through is not enough.
rules.quote: We have a candlestick close outside of this buy side imbalance sell side inefficiency which validates this becoming an inversion fair value gap.

rules.rule: 2022 top-down strip: step down 5, 4, 3, 2, 1 minute and use the first FVG found; stop descending once one is found.
rules.quote: the first fair value gap we come to if we find one on a four minute you don't need to go down to a three you don't need to go down to a two you don't need to go down to a one

rules.rule: Jan 2025: use the 5, 4, 3, 2 or 1 minute chart that has the cleanest inefficiency.
rules.quote: timing is based on either a 5 minute 4 minute 3 minute 2 minute or one minute chart whichever one has the cleanest inefficiency that you can work with

rules.rule: Sept 2024: on a 15-second chart there are plenty of FVGs for precise entries.
rules.quote: With a 15-second chart there's plenty of fair value gaps to get into the move with precision.

rules.rule: June 2023: he works seconds charts but advises new traders not to, because small-timeframe gaps mislead.
rules.quote: I go into these lower timeframes, even sub-one-minute like in the seconds charts, but I don't advise new people to do that

rules.rule: Jan 2025: it works on Forex (London 2:50 to 3:10 AM macro), buying inside a reclaimed BISI FVG.
rules.quote: We're presently inside of the 2:50 AM 3:10 AM macro, and yes it works on Forex. So I'm going to be buying here inside of a reclaimed BISI fair value gap.

rules.rule: Model 13 time of day: 7am to 10am EST for Forex, 8:30am to 11am EST for index futures.
rules.quote: We use Time Of Day - 7am to 10am EST for Forex and 8:30am to 11am EST for Index Futures.

rules.rule: Silver Bullet (Mar 2023): between 10:00 and 11:00 New York time a displacement creating a FVG forms every day.
rules.quote: between 10:00 o'clock New York local time and 11:00 o'clock New York local time, there will be a displacement in price creating a Fair Value Gap. That is why I call it the Silver Bullet.

rules.rule: Oct 2023 clarification: the FVG may form earlier; only the retracement entry must fall between 10 and 11.
rules.quote: the fair value Gap does not need to be inside of 10 to 11 the setup is a retracement into a fair value Gap between 10 and 11

rules.rule: Sept 2024: first FVG presentation between 9:30 and 10:00.
rules.quote: First fair value Gap presentation between the 9:30 and 10:00 window.

rules.rule: Nov 2025: the 9:31 candle opening is the minimum criterion for a first presented FVG.
rules.quote: This right here 931, that's the minimum criteria for a first presented fair value gap. So you have to see that 931 candlestick open up.

rules.quote: The very first presented fair value gap during the opening range first 30 minutes

order_block.summary: Order block family: the last opposite-close candle (or run of them) before a displacement that trades through its high/low and leaves an imbalance is the footprint of a change in state of delivery. Trade the retest of its high/open toward the mean threshold (50 percent of the candle) for a move to external range liquidity. Variants: propulsion block (second down-candle into a prior OB), mitigation block (last down-candle at a failed-swing low), rejection block (long-wick body-to-wick zone), reclaimed block (old curve candles reused), vacuum block (true session or news gap).
order_block.needs_clock: Core family needs NO clock. Order block, propulsion block, mitigation block, rejection block and reclaimed block can all be detected from OHLC sequence alone (swing structure, displacement, FVG, candle open/close/high/low), so they could run on 24/7 synthetic indices using price delivery only. Clock-dependent add-ons that are optional: the 2022 Episode 18 rule to pull an unfilled limit order at 11:30 New York, kill zones, the 2024 Lecture #1 claim that a valid order block must form after 8:30 (this comes from the dossier summary and from a quote cell that contains ellipses, so it is not quoted here), macro windows, and midnight/08:30 open filters in his 2022 combined models. The vacuum block is different: it is defined by a true discontinuity at a session open or close, a weekend break or a news release such as NFP. A continuously quoted synthetic index has no sessions or news, so it will rarely produce one; only a spike or jump gap in the series could stand in, and he never taught that.
order_block.how_to_code:
Common helpers: swing highs and lows (3-bar fractals); displacement = a 1 to 3 candle leg whose range or body exceeds k times a rolling median (k is a free parameter) and closes beyond the prior short-term swing; FVG = candle1.high below candle3.low for bullish (mirror for bearish); mean threshold MT = (open+close)/2 of the block candle body (2024 to 2025 wording; 2016 wording says the total range, so keep a flag); premium/discount = above or below 50 percent of the current dealing range.
ORDER BLOCK (bullish; bearish is the mirror): 1) detect a displacement leg up that takes out a prior short-term high; 2) candidate = the last down-close candle before the leg, or the whole run of consecutive down-close candles (treated as one compound block, dossier 2024-04-30); the 2016 version prefers the one with the largest open-to-close body near a swing low; 3) validation = a later candle's high exceeds the candidate's high (2016) and, for the 2022 form, the leg left an FVG; optional strict flags: the leg swept a prior low first (liquidity taken), the block sits in discount of the dealing range; 4) zone = from candidate high down to its open (sensitive zone), MT = 50 percent of the body, low = candle low; 5) entry = limit at the high (aggressive), open (standard) or MT (deep), after price returns into the zone; 6) stop = below the candle low (2016) or below MT (2022 to 2023); 7) target = nearest external liquidity (old swing high or equal highs) or opposing PD array; 8) management = once price displaces away, trail the stop to just below MT; 9) invalid if a candle body closes below MT (2016 to 2025 wording) or, in the strictest 2024 wording, if any candle trades down through MT; cancel the order if it is never touched before the next leg forms.
PROPULSION: after a bullish OB at A, find a later down-close candle B whose low trades into A's range (B.low <= A.high) and whose body stays above its own MT; zone is B's high down to B's MT; entry on first return to B.high with a stop under MT(B); valid once price trades above B's open; fail on a close (or trade-through) below MT(B).
MITIGATION (bearish): swing low A, rally to a lower high B that does NOT exceed the previous high (failure swing), then a break below A (market structure shift); the block is the last down-close candle at A; enter short on return into its body; invalid if bodies close above its high. If B made a higher high first, it is a breaker, not a mitigation block.
REJECTION (bearish): a swing high with one or more long upper wicks; zone = highest candle body edge (max of open or close in the swing) up to the highest wick; entry = limit at the body edge, or a sell stop just below the body edge after price pokes above it without a higher wick high; take profit near the lowest body rather than the wick extreme.
RECLAIMED: store the down-close candles that formed during the sell-side leg of a curve (each one followed by a minor bounce); when price later rotates up and returns to those same price levels, treat each as a long zone (mirror for shorts). Needs a defined MMBM/MMSM curve, so it is the most subjective.
VACUUM: gap between consecutive bars where no price traded (low[n] > high[n-1] or high[n] < low[n-1], measured at session open, weekend or news bar); zone = the gap; enter only if price returns to the edge and bounces immediately; otherwise stand aside.
Subjective parts: what counts as displacement; 'near support'; narrative and draw on liquidity; which candle of a consecutive run is the block; body versus total range for MT; whether trading through or a close is needed; how the dealing range is chosen; 'immediate feedback'; and the parent versus child timeframe.
order_block.changes_over_time: 1) What validates it. 2016 core content (re-uploaded Sept 2022): a later candle trades through the high of the down-close candle. April 2022: 'Without the imbalance, there is no order block' and 'an order block is a change in the state of delivery'. 2023 to 2024: also needs a narrative and a draw on liquidity ('every down-closed candle doesn't make it an order block'). Aug 2024 Lecture #1 dossier summary adds: formed post-8:30, took liquidity, energetic displacement. 2025 to 2026: the key level becomes the OPEN of the candle or of the lowest-open run (CISD), and he says it need not close beyond it (dYQSUCSbYn8, KHkUPAsdyfk, and June 2026 'Order block does not require close', which sits in a cell with ellipses so it was not quoted). 2) Zone definition. 2016 mentions 50 percent of the 'total range'; 2021 says high to open, not the entire range; 2024 to 2025 say real body, with mean threshold for order blocks and consequent encroachment for gaps (Sept to Oct 2024, Feb 2025). In 2023 he still used 'mean threshold' for imbalances (20230130-eTMS36H7HA0, 20230119-cWekmMLqiNM), so the terminology drifted. 3) Entry level. 2021: high or open, high is easiest. Jan 2024: enter at the mean threshold of a bearish OB (VODMCdDnMs8). Aug 2024: deep inside the body ('nice deep premium inside the body'), buy below the body into the discount wick (ul6x6BwOg6M), sell on an uptick at the open (woAQ1XJeD7Y). 2025: bearish block's key level is the lowest open of the consecutive up-close run. 4) Stop. 2016: below the block low, then raise to just below 50 percent. Feb 2022 and 2023: below mean threshold or the candle low. April 2022 bearish model: above the intermediate-term high with the imbalance. Aug to Sept 2024: stop at the rejection block wick or referenced to the open. July 2026: expect overshoot, 'it's going to dig down underneath it a little bit' (J9G1j3-e1GU, quote cell has ellipses). 5) Close versus trade-through on the 50 percent: 2022 Month 04 dossiers imply bodies must not close beyond; Aug 2023 'if we close below that'; Sept 2024 'I don't want to see any candlestick after it forms trade down through the mean threshold' (wEBlRM7whoI, ellipses); Sept 2025 propulsion 'trades down to halfway but doesn't close below'. 6) Propulsion block: 2016 'never see the mean threshold break'; 2023 'not below the midpoint'; 2026 dossier summary says it is validated when price trades above the open of the order block candle. 7) Mitigation block: 2016, 2020 and Mar 2024 show it as an entry (5m limit with 11-pip risk; short at a mitigation block on MNQ), but July 2023 says he uses mitigation blocks as targets more than entries because they can be traded through (vN2BkfyRWE4, quote cell has ellipses). 8) Rejection block role changes: 2016 entry zone (body to wick); Feb 2023 'the rejection block only acts as a target' (kFIOp8Tprdc); 2023 to 2024 used as a stop reference or trail point (3FGFEuaDSOc, 7iRB5uc1KYk, hdSscxZgE58). 9) Reclaimed: 2016 means re-using old candles across the MMBM/MMSM curve; in Aug 2024 'reclaimed bearish order block' is tied to 'digging into the original order block' (yOZHawAE8QI), which sounds closer to a propulsion block, and from 2023 on 'reclaimed' mostly means reclaimed FVG, not order block. 10) Vacuum block appears in a single video (2016 content) with no trades and no later mention. 11) Premium/discount filter appears only from 2024 (down-close candles in premium are not bullish order blocks, joqM_Z96vtM). 12) Data caveat: for the Month 04 re-uploads (taught Dec 2016) the dossier text that says bodies must close above the 50 percent mean threshold is analyst summary, not a verbatim quote; only the stop-raise to just below 50 percent is quoted from PIYh0CxoY9c.
order_block.markets: Count method: regex over the trade tables of all dossiers, about 131 rows matched; 19 were dropped because the block was only a target or stop reference, or the row was a reclaimed FVG/CIBI rather than a reclaimed OB. That leaves about 112 rows, roughly 95 plain order block, 6 rejection block, 4 to 5 propulsion block, 3 to 4 mitigation block, 0 vacuum block and 0 reclaimed order block. Many of the rows combine the block with an FVG, OTE or a market maker model, so pure order-block-only trades are fewer. The 8 seed teaching videos show no live trades. Markets: forex (EURUSD, GBPUSD, USDCAD, AUDUSD, USDCHF, NZDUSD, GBPJPY, 2017 to 2024 and 2025 reviews); DXY as confirmation; index futures (ES/MES, NQ/MNQ) dominate from 2020 and almost entirely from 2022 to 2026; ZB bonds, soybeans, cotton and single stocks (AAPL, MCD, CAT) in the Oct 2022 swing and position-trade series; a Bitcoin chart in 2018. Timeframes run from monthly and weekly (position trades) through daily, 4H, 1H, 15m, 5m, 1m, down to 15-second charts in 2024 to 2025. Vacuum block was taught only on EURUSD-type forex and index futures (NFP gaps, session opens and weekend gaps).

rules.rule: Colour of the candle is not enough; a down-close or up-close candle is only a block in the right context.
rules.quote: Every down candle is not a bullish order block and every up candle is not a bearish order block.

rules.rule: A candle only counts as an order block if price trades down into it after displacement and there is a narrative behind it.
rules.quote: Down-closed candles are supposed to support price, but every down-closed candle doesn't make it an order block! It has to trade down into it after displacement, and it has to have a narrative behind it. That's what makes it an institutional array.

rules.rule: With a bullish higher-timeframe read, buy the daily bullish discount arrays (order block is one of them); bearish is the mirror.
rules.quote: You're going to buy all daily bullish discount arrays: that is a bullish mitigation block, bullish breaker, liquidity void, fair value gap, bullish order block, rejection block, and or an old low or high.

rules.rule: A bullish day narrative is what makes the down-close candle an order block; the candle alone is not the reason.
rules.quote: See how that overlaps with this down close candle's high? That's an order block. It's not just a down close candle that makes it an order block. It's the narrative that it's a bullish day.

rules.rule: When price is at a higher-timeframe bullish order block mean threshold, stop selling and prepare for the reversal.
rules.quote: When you see the market low form and it's trading at a daily bullish order block mean threshold, you do not look to sell short anymore. You prepare for the reversal.

rules.rule: Candle selection (2016 core content): lowest down-close candle with the largest open-to-close range, near support. Bearish is the mirror.
rules.quote: Definition of a bullish order block is the lowest candle or price bar with a down close that has the most range between open to close and is near a support level.

rules.rule: Zone is the high down to the open of the (consecutive) down-close candles, not the whole range; higher probability when price first takes out sell stops and then returns to the block.
rules.quote: the high to the opening price now why not the entire range like a supply and demand zone would be well this is not supply and demand so it's the high down to the opening price extend it out in time and the market drops down into that that's a bullish order block and it's taking out sell stops so a high probability order block is when it takes out stops and returns down to the order block itself

rules.rule: 2022 rule: the displacement must leave an imbalance (FVG) or there is no order block.
rules.quote: Without the imbalance, there is no order block.

rules.rule: 2022 redefinition: the order block marks a change in the state of delivery.
rules.quote: What is an order block? It's a change in the state of delivery.

rules.rule: Mean threshold is the half-way point of the order block, a reference point distinct from consequent encroachment, which is reserved for gaps.
rules.quote: We don't use this Wick this is your order block right there so half of that order block is a mean threshold reference point it's not consequent encroachment consequent encroachment is gaps or inefficiencies.

rules.rule: Validation (2016): the block is valid only once a later candle trades through the high of the down-close candle (bullish case). Trading through is enough; a close is not stated.
rules.quote: Validation of a bullish order block is when the high of the lowest down candle or price bar is traded through by a later formed candle or price bar.

rules.rule: Validation (2026), bearish case: price trading down through the open of the up-close candle validates it as a change in state of delivery; no close needed.
rules.quote: It's got to touch or lay on it to validate this PD array to be perfect. So, open on up close candle when you go bearish. As soon as this candlestick trades down through the opening price, it need not close below it. As soon as it does that, that validates this as a change in the state of delivery

rules.rule: Same 2026 point stated again: passing through is enough; a candle close beyond is not required.
rules.quote: Once it passes through it right on that candle it need not like it does here close below it. We don't need to see that. You see these guys teaching my order block theory or attempting to and they're saying it's got to get a close. No, it does not.

rules.rule: Buy the high or the open of the consecutive down-close block; the high is the easiest and the stop absorbs the adverse move.
rules.quote: the order block is the consecutive down close candles all three of them make up the order block but the sensitive price point is the high and the opening so you can be a buyer at the high or at the opening price the easiest one is using the high and allowing your stop to absorb any adverse price movement

rules.rule: Stop beneath the mean threshold of the order block candle (2023 live scalp).
rules.quote: the stop below mean threshold that would be here

rules.rule: 2022 model, bearish order block: stop above the intermediate-term high that carries the imbalance.
rules.quote: This is an intermediate term high, swing high because it has the imbalance. It should not trade higher than a high. That's the reason why I'm telling you you can put your stop loss there.

rules.rule: Order block is internal range liquidity; the draw is external range liquidity (old highs or lows) outside the short-term dealing range.
rules.quote: Most of the time you're going to find that internal range liquidity entries will run to external range liquidity. That means you're going to see order blocks, fair value gaps, or voids be your entry and it'll expand outside of the present short-term dealing range to external range liquidity. And that is your low resistance liquidity run.

rules.rule: After price runs away from the block, raise the stop to just below the 50 percent of the order block range.
rules.quote: Just below the 50% of the order block total range is also considered to be a good location to raise the stop loss after price runs away from the bullish order block to reduce risk.

rules.rule: 2022 Episode 18 model: the order is time-limited; pull an unfilled limit order after 11:30 New York rather than leaving it good till cancel.
rules.quote: Now, what happens if it doesn't fill you by 11:30? Pull the order. It's it. Don't put it you know, good till cancel. Just pull it because you want to be entering on the day that it creates this

rules.rule: If price trades back down into the level that was meant to hold, the idea is wrong and the stop is accepted.
rules.quote: now i have six contracts long and i'll move my stop up just a little bit underneath that low right there it should not trade back down into that if it does i'm wrong and that's fine

rules.rule: Mean threshold test (2026): price must not breach or go below the halfway point of the order block.
rules.quote: Does it breach or go below mean threshold? Mean threshold is the halfway point of an order block. It doesn't do that.

rules.rule: Wicks may trade outside the block; only the bodies are judged against the range.
rules.quote: The bodies are respecting this range here, the wicks are permitted, they're always permitted to trade outside the lines because that's where the damage is done.

rules.rule: Weekly order blocks taught as a higher-timeframe anchor (2017).
rules.quote: This is Volume 2 of the precision concepts series. In the initial video we discussed weekly order flow and the inherent advantages of understanding long-term order flow. Now we're going to be focusing on specific order blocks on a weekly chart.

rules.rule: Same logic is used on a 15-second chart pre-market on NQ (2025).
rules.quote: This is the smaller 1-minute time frame. This is the pre-session pre-market session. I did a 15-second order block long here and I showed that on the Telegram channel reaching for this buy side here.

rules.rule: Placing the order inside the kill zone is what matters; the fill does not have to happen inside the window.
rules.quote: Kill zones are when you determine your entry, and you place your orders, and you walk away. You don't need to have your entry filled inside that kill zone window. Your order idea and your order placement need to be considered at that time.

rules.rule: [Propulsion block] Definition: a candle that has traded down into a down candle or bullish order block and takes over as support.
rules.quote: A propulsion block is a candle or bar that has previously traded down into a down candle or bullish order block and takes over the role of price support for higher price movement.

rules.rule: [Propulsion block] Another down candle trading into a previous down candle while the underlying context is bullish.
rules.quote: When this candle creates the down close and closes, this becomes a propulsion candle. What makes it a propulsion candle is that we are trading another down candle into a previous down candle when the underlying context is bullish.

rules.rule: [Propulsion block] Price normally only trades down into the high of the propulsion candle and then explodes, so entry is at that high with a very tight stop.
rules.quote: Most likely it will never do that, it just trades down into the high of the candle and immediately explodes.

rules.rule: [Propulsion block] Expect immediate responsiveness and very little drawdown; if it does not respond you have your answer early.
rules.quote: That's why I gave you the name: it's a propulsion candle because it propels price quickly and suddenly and it gives you immediate feedback, very little drawdown, immediate price responsiveness.

rules.rule: [Propulsion block] Retracement must not go below the midpoint of the propulsion candle (2023).
rules.quote: We have a higher down-closed candle here—this is a propulsion block. So any retracement here should be kept at bay; it should not go below the midpoint of that candle. That's the rules for a propulsion block, meaning that if this is going to rally, it should not go halfway more.

rules.rule: [Propulsion block] 2025 wording: trading down to halfway is allowed, closing below halfway is not.
rules.quote: This is the order block here but then this candle is higher trades down to halfway but doesn't close below the halfway and that's a definition for propulsion block

rules.rule: [Mitigation block] A break below the old low is the market structure shift that confirms sellers are willing to drive price lower.
rules.quote: A net shift in market structure is seen here with a break below that old low. That gives us confirmation that the market does in fact have participants on a large scale willing to drive prices lower.

rules.rule: [Mitigation block] Frame the last down candle at the low, where the buying took place before the short-term rally.
rules.quote: Inside that low, what we're going to be focusing on is the last down candle, because the last down candle is where the buying took place right before that little short-term rally up.

rules.rule: [Mitigation block] Sell short when price returns to that candle, where trapped longs mitigate their losses.
rules.quote: This is a mitigation block: everything that was used to drive price higher, once it's traded below here, it's underwater. They're going to want to mitigate those losses at that candle, sell short.

rules.rule: [Mitigation block] The body of the candle must not be violated.
rules.quote: Notice the body of the candle is not violated. This is hallmark characteristics of a mitigation block.

rules.rule: [Rejection block] Candles with long wicks at a swing; sell above the bodies of those candles.
rules.quote: Rejection blocks: candles that have real long wicks, we're going to look to try to sell above the bodies of those candles.

rules.rule: [Rejection block] If price trades above the level but not to a higher wick high, sell on a stop below that level (sell on weakness).
rules.quote: If it trades above that particular level and it does not trade to a higher wick high, you could be a seller on a stop below that level so that way you can be selling on weakness.

rules.rule: [Rejection block] Do not demand a full wick sweep; the bodies are the nearest thing to institutional levels.
rules.quote: Don't always demand that price gets below the wicks; it's really the bodies of the candle that is the closest thing to institutional understanding you're going to get.

rules.rule: [Reclaimed block] Bullish: an old down candle used to buy that saw a bounce is reclaimed for new longs on the buy side of the curve.
rules.quote: A bullish reclaimed block is a candle or bar that was previously used to buy price and a short-term bounce confirms minor displacement. In the buy side of the curve, these old blocks or down candles will be reclaimed for new longs.

rules.rule: [Reclaimed block] Bearish mirror: old up candles used to sell are reclaimed for new shorts on the sell side of the curve.
rules.quote: A bearish reclaimed block is a candle or bar that was previously used to sell price and a short-term decline confirms minor displacement. In the sell side of the curve, these old blocks will be reclaimed shorts or new entries for short positions.

rules.rule: [Vacuum block] A discontinuous gap from session opens and closes or an instant central bank repricing.
rules.quote: This could be if we're trading futures contracts where they have session opens and closes where there's no trading, or an instant central bank repricing.

rules.rule: [Vacuum block] News events such as Non-Farm Payroll create the gap, so the model is tied to the release clock.
rules.quote: Non-Farm Payroll: it can gap sometimes 30, 50, 60 pips from where it was trading right before the numbers released. They do a quick repricing at the central bank.

rules.rule: [Vacuum block] Price returns, bounces and leaves the gap intact; only buy with immediate feedback.
rules.quote: Bounce there and leave that little gap opening still intact, but this could potentially be a buy. If you're looking for this to occur, you'd have to see immediate feedback.

rules.rule: [Vacuum block] The bounce itself leaves a small fair value gap that can be used later.
rules.quote: Price comes to that level, stops trading lower, and rallies higher leaving a small gap which would be classified as a fair value gap we can use at a future time.

suspension_block.summary: A suspension block is an FVG-like imbalance with a wick lying over it (later also: a candle bracketed by volume imbalances at its high and low, or an inefficiency-to-inefficiency range). He treats it as an HTF or intraday PD array whose CE and quadrants split bullish from bearish. Bodies staying in one half show the order flow, and entries are retests into the block with a one-tick tolerance.
suspension_block.needs_clock: The core does not need a clock. Detection (a wick-over-gap block, or a candle bracketed by volume imbalances), CE, quadrants and octants, the lower-half or upper-half body test, the one-tick retest tolerance and the body-outside-the-block invalidation are all price-only, so they could run on 24/7 synthetic indices. The caveats: (1) the 'daily' block needs a day boundary, so on synthetics define it as a fixed bar-count aggregate such as 1440 x 1m, which is an assumption, not his rule; (2) several of his uses are time-gated and cannot be ported: the London 1:30-2:00 AM first-presented FVG (Zm9Q0NDRxoY), the 9:30 bell stop buffer and pre-market entries (Jxl5UJk_ylc), the FOMC 2:40-2:50 PM window (50VbES10ULs), the post-CPI/PPI/Fed 10:00 trades, and NWOG and opening-range-gap targets. He also says time is the algorithm in the Zm9Q0NDRxoY video, so the original is clock-aware. Drop those gates for a pure price-delivery version.
suspension_block.how_to_code: Reconstructed from the trades tables and quotes, because the dossiers never give exact candle-level geometry. Steps: (1) Volume imbalance (VI): two consecutive candles whose bodies do not overlap while their wicks do. (2) Block candidate, daily or intraday: a candle (or a short run of candles) with a VI on its low side and another on its high side, so it is bracketed by a lower and an upper VI (486N8ow3U2A 00:26, -Td-D-vKJDg 14:40, N3qz13Hl-gg 06:28). Alternatively a plain 3-candle FVG where a wick overlaps the gap range (-Td-D-vKJDg 10:54). Block range = the high/low of that candle, or from the lower VI to the upper VI; both are subjective, because he never fixes which. (3) Levels: CE = 50%, quadrants at 25%, octants at 12.5% steps. (4) Bias: over a window of bars after the block forms, if candle bodies close only in the lower half or below the CE and never reach the upper half or premium quadrant, then bearish; mirror for bullish (3Uu2IB6kI28). Wicks are ignored for bias. If bodies stay below the CE but price is just oscillating, treat it as range and stand aside (zyKAPNk_prA). (5) Entry (subjective): price returns into the premium bracket (shorts) or the discount wick (longs), allows a one-tick overshoot (LBrsLPKXZ2E), and an inversion trigger fires, meaning a candle closes through a gap inside the block (IFVG flip). (6) Initial stop from trade tables: just above the block high (shorts) or below the wick low (longs); 6VaEdP4TYe8 uses 'no body closes outside the block' as a soft stop. (7) Management: move to breakeven or loss cover when time or distance permits, trail only after a closing basis break of a minor swing, partial on each new extreme. (8) Targets: next opposite liquidity pool, lower or discount block, CE of a pre-market block, or the daily block if entering above it. Subjective parts: how many candles can form the block, whether a wick must fully cover the gap, 'reversed/down-close' strength, the definition of 'first instance' FVG, the narrative filter, which timeframe, and the stop distance.
suspension_block.changes_over_time: 1) Date conflict: Zm9Q0NDRxoY (file dated 2025-01-01) already calls a first-presented FVG a 'bearish suspension block', yet -Td-D-vKJDg (2025-09-30) says 'my first mention of it in public. I've never taught it before'. The January file date is probably a placeholder, but it is unresolved. 2) The definition drifts. Sept 2025: an FVG with a wick laying over it (not to be read as an FVG). Jan 2025 file: an inefficiency-to-inefficiency range respecting the CE. Feb 2026: a daily candle with volume imbalances at both its low and high. Jul 2026: 'Volume imbalance. Volume imbalance.' and a 'first instance FVG' called a suspension block. These do not share one geometric rule. 3) Role drift: an intraday entry array with quadrants (Sept 2025); a daily reference and ceiling (Jan-Apr 2026); a range-containment boundary via its CE (Jan 2026); a retest-short zone after news (Jul 2026, with a one-tick tolerance and octant halts); a target and CE draw (pre-market block CE, Sept 2026; daily block as FOMC exit, Sept 2026). 4) Bias reading: 3Uu2IB6kI28 says bodies only in the lower half means bearish, while zyKAPNk_prA says below the CE just means hammering in a range, so lower half alone does not give a trade. 5) Stop style: Sept 2025 table says above the block high; Apr 2026 (6VaEdP4TYe8) says wicks may poke through the block high and only bodies outside collapse the trade; Jan 2026 trails on closes and covers loss at breakeven before the bell. 6) Several dossier items are summary-level, not his words, and were not used as quotes: the 'volume imbalance ceiling' and 'do not chase above daily blocks' claims in V4KPpX-CWXk, the shaded-block target in yqBvOeOKcBM, and the block-labelled entry in fFi2QEApVGM. 7) 6VaEdP4TYe8 23:47 and 12:10 talk about 'that wick' and its CE, but it is unclear whether that is the block's wick, so they were left out.
suspension_block.markets: All NQ (E-mini Nasdaq-100) futures, plus one trade on MNQ (micro Nasdaq). Timeframes: the block is marked on the daily (also 1h and 15m), and 1m intraday blocks are used for entries. ES and YM appear in the April 14, 2026 tape reading, but no block trade is shown there. Nothing on forex, metals, or crypto. Trade count of 9 distinct rows whose title or table names the block: -Td-D-vKJDg 14:40 (short, from a Twitter/X review); Zm9Q0NDRxoY 10:45 (conceptual short); 486N8ow3U2A 05:30 (short, analysis review only); Jxl5UJk_ylc 03:08 (live long, held through the bell); 6VaEdP4TYe8 00:17 (MNQ short, scaled out, remainder stopped on stall); IF7dEkgWoO0 02:28 (post-CPI short, +$16,080); LBrsLPKXZ2E 15:10 (post-PPI short, +72 pts); 50VbES10ULs 12:14 (FOMC short exiting at the daily block, +$33,800); VBgfJRMVCaI 10:20 (post-holiday short to the pre-market block CE, a win). The same trade as 9W4YpyAg5RY 20:08 is counted once. Only 6 have stated outcomes, and all of those are wins or partial wins. Borderline and not counted: fFi2QEApVGM 02:20 (chart row says 'inversion FVG / suspension block' but the trade is titled an IFVG short) and N3qz13Hl-gg (names a block verbally; the trade is titled a trailed buy-stop sweep). Not one of the 9 is a clean, repeatable entry-to-exit walk-through with a stated stop. Entry, stop and target come from trade-table cells, not from quotes.

rules.rule: The block is strongest when it is a reversal (down-close) candle and the narrative and order flow already point toward discount arrays (bearish case). Subjective: 'reversed' and 'narrative' are not defined.
rules.quote: the suspension block is extremely bullish or bearish if it's reversed and it's a down close candle and you have narrative and orderflow moving is lower reaching [for discount arrays]

rules.rule: While price sits below the CE of the block it is just range-bound chop. He wants price to start moving out of that range before he is interested.
rules.quote: I need this to start moving out of this range here for me to really be interested

rules.rule: Daily suspension block split into halves or quadrants. If price works only in the lower half and cannot get into the upper half, the bias is bearish. The mirror (only the upper half is respected means bullish) is implied but not quoted.
rules.quote: Notice how we were working only in the lower half of that. So if it can't get in the upper half, is that bullish or bearish? It's bearish.

rules.rule: The block's consequent encroachment (CE) is the pivot. Staying below it means containment and hammering inside the range, not directional expansion.
rules.quote: as long as we stay below the consequent encroachment of this suspension block, then we're probably just going to hammer around inside the range

rules.rule: Candle BODIES, not wicks, prove direction. Bodies that do not touch the premium level (or the upper half) are the footprint of smart money, so bearish.
rules.quote: It's bearish because the bodies are not touching that level. So, if this is a premium level and the bodies are not touching it, that's the signature that the algorithm lays down for smart money.

rules.rule: Original 2025 definition: an FVG with a wick laying over it is not treated as a plain FVG. It is a suspension block (candle geometry not spelled out).
rules.quote: first introduction to my first mention of it in public. I've never taught it before. I've never given it to anybody. This is my ICT suspension block. And you'll see it with this wick laying over top of it. So you would never look at that as a fair value gap

rules.rule: Daily-chart anatomy: a candle with a volume imbalance (bounce) at its low and another at its high is a suspension block.
rules.quote: positive balance outside efficiency with a volume bounce at the low and a volume bounce at the high which makes this a suspension block

rules.rule: Alternative wording: a block runs from one inefficiency to the next. A first-presented FVG that changes structure is a (bearish) suspension block and respects its equilibrium (CE).
rules.quote: changes market structure bearish and now we can use this inefficiency to inefficiency which is what suspension block. Now this first presented fair value gap is a bearish suspension block and it reacts and respects the equilibrium point

rules.rule: Two stacked volume imbalances equal a suspension block. Bodies staying below the gap and the high confirm it.
rules.quote: Volume imbalance. Volume imbalance. That's a suspension block. We nailed the low of that.

rules.rule: The block is subdivided into upper and lower quadrants. Later teaching adds octants (lower octant, 12.5% steps) and a shaded daily box.
rules.quote: these are just the upper and lower quadrants respectively into this suspension block

rules.rule: A new week opening gap that opens inside the premium part of a daily block uses the block as supply.
rules.quote: we are opening up with a new week opening gap in a premium portion of this suspension block

rules.rule: Reaction trigger: an FVG inside the block that gets traded through flips to an inversion FVG (IFVG), and the CE of the flipped gap drives price in the new direction.
rules.quote: That inversion fair value gap was a SIBI. Now it's a bullish inversion fair value gap. Consequent encroachment sends it higher

rules.rule: Short trigger in the Post-CPI block short (the chart row calls it 'Tuesday's first instance FVG suspension block'): a candle closes below the first-instance FVG, which then acts as an inversion FVG.
rules.quote: See that candlestick closed below first instance of fair value gap

rules.rule: If he is bearish and a gap sits in the premium of the block, it should act like an inversion FVG (resistance).
rules.quote: if we're bearish this is going to act like a inversion fair value gap

rules.rule: Short entry: after a breakdown and a reversal, price comes back up into another suspension block bracketed by a lower and an upper volume imbalance. Enter the retest into the upper (premium) bracket.
rules.quote: market breaks down, comes back up one more time into another suspension block. See this lower volume imbalance, upper volume imbalance, but because we had a reversal

rules.rule: Judas-swing fade: sell short inside the last suspension block (a bullish up-close candle), expecting a run to the sell side.
rules.quote: selling short inside of that last suspension block. It's a bullish up close candle

rules.rule: Retest of a bearish block: price runs up into the 'bear suspension block' (after halting at the lower octant) and stops dead at the block, to the tick. Short from there.
rules.quote: open trade right up into the bear suspension block there. Right to the tick. Stops dead in its tracks.

rules.rule: Tolerance: a one-tick overshoot of the block level on the retest is still valid, so a one-tick poke is not a failure.
rules.quote: The high on this candlestick comes in at 29,943. So, went one tick higher, which is fine. It's completely permissible.

rules.rule: Stop is trailed only after a close through a minor swing high or low. Roll it to just beyond that level, and only on a closing basis with a strong showing. Initial stop levels (above block high for shorts, below the wick low for longs) come only from the trade tables, not from a quote.
rules.quote: if it can take out this high here on a closing basis, then I'll roll the stop up to just below here. I like to see it really make a strong showing above this minor short-term high

rules.rule: Target in the Judas-swing fade: the sell side (sell-side liquidity and the Monday opening range gap, per the trade table). Other trade-table targets: a lower block, the CE of a pre-market block, the daily block as an exit, and a discount liquidity pool.
rules.quote: I think that they're going to go for that sell side

rules.rule: Loss covering: with 4.5 minutes to the bell, move the stop above entry. He identifies the green shaded zone on the chart as the daily chart's suspension block (a long entered inside the block's discount wick).
rules.quote: We have 4 and 1/2 more minutes before the opening bell, so I'm going to take the stop above entry. Just as a loss covering. So, this green shaded area here, that is the daily chart's suspension block

rules.rule: Run down equity: take a partial whenever price makes a new extreme (new low for a short) and no partial has been taken yet. This was a short whose target was the pre-market block CE, so the quote is not block-specific.

breaker_unicorn.summary: A breaker is the last opposite-colour candle at a swing that was swept and then broken with displacement (bullish: low, high, lower low, then up through the high; bearish: the mirror). Price is expected to return into that candle and reverse. A Unicorn (2026 name) is a breaker with a fair value gap at the same location.
breaker_unicorn.needs_clock: The breaker and the unicorn are pure price structure: swing, sweep, displacement break, a candle zone, and an FVG overlapping it. The pattern needs no clock and could run on 24/7 synthetic indices using only price delivery. His examples are mostly in clock contexts (London killzone, 8:30 and 9:30 NY, the 5:50 AM macro, a 1:30 PM trade). In 2020 and 2026 he mentions the time overlap as a bonus. In 2025 he says macro time "further increases the likelihood". He never states time as a requirement for the breaker. The 2024 clock rules (post-8:30 order blocks, the 30-minute opening range) are for order blocks and the opening range, not breakers. The 2020 "killzone requirement" in the HRIXsFHYVmw dossier is the dossier's own summary, not a quote. Clock-dependent parts to replace on synthetics: targets such as the RTH opening range gap, NDOG octants, session highs/lows and midnight open. Substitute swing highs/lows, equal highs/lows, fib or standard-deviation projections, or the opposite array. The higher-timeframe bias can be built from aggregated candles and does not need time of day.
breaker_unicorn.how_to_code:
Mechanical detection (bearish breaker; swap high/low and up/down for bullish):
1. Detect swing points with a fractal of n bars (n is a parameter, subjective). Find the sequence H1, L1, H2 with H2 > H1 and L1 between them. H2 must take out H1: a wick beyond H1 counts as the liquidity run. If H2 does not exceed H1, label it a mitigation block, not a breaker.
2. Confirmation: a later candle BODY closes below L1 (market structure shift). It should be a displacement candle, for example range above k times ATR, or it leaves an FVG. Until then the breaker is not armed.
3. Zone: the lowest down-close candle (close < open) at L1, the last candle before the rally to H2. Its full high-low range is the zone. The most sensitive part is the lower half or body. The zone midpoint can be used as the mean threshold. For bullish: the highest up-close candle at H1, before the drop to L2.
4. Unicorn: find a 3-candle FVG with gap_high > gap_low whose price span overlaps the breaker zone. Two versions appear in his teaching. (a) 2024 "inversion" version: a bullish FVG formed in the run-up from the breaker candle to H2, which price then closes below, flipping it into an IFVG. (b) 2026 version: any FVG that formed at the same location as the breaker. Use an overlap test with a tolerance, with the FVG within or abutting the breaker range, and optionally require the overlap to be at least x percent of the FVG height. Mirror for bullish.
5. Entry: arm a limit order, or enter on first touch of the zone after step 2. Limit levels: the breaker midpoint, the FVG consequent encroachment (CE), or the FVG edge nearest the zone. Variant (2023): place the order inside the zone before step 2 completes.
6. Stop: just beyond the breaker candle extreme (above the high for shorts). Alternatively beyond the sweep extreme H2 (his earlier and wider variant), or beyond the unicorn FVG and breaker union.
7. Invalidation: any candle body close beyond the far side of the zone (above the breaker high for bearish). Wicks are tolerated. Cancel the pending order if price makes a new extreme beyond the sweep before the entry fills.
8. Targets: the opposite-side liquidity pool (prior lows or equal lows), the opposing array (bullish breaker or FVG), or standard-deviation or fib projections of the leg. Add a partial at the first objective and trail the stop above recent candle highs or the breaker edge.
9. Context filter: HTF bias from higher-timeframe swing structure; require longs in discount and shorts in premium of the dealing range; skip if an opposite HTF breaker is forming (osRUnIpGIJ0).
Subjective parts to parametrise or fix: the fractal length, what counts as displacement, whether the zone is body or full range, how much overlap counts as "same location", the HTF bias definition, and the target choice.
breaker_unicorn.changes_over_time:
1. Naming. "Unicorn" appears only in the 2026 dossiers (JmAJfuSkY1g, bz4QNPcpmWE; P8Pn8DHFSW8 says "breaker and fair value gap together"). The idea is older: 2022 (4m FVG with a bearish breaker), Jan 2023 (volume imbalance, bullish breaker and a 5m FVG), Jul 2023 ("Reaper": an FVG in the impulsive leg of a breaker), 2024 (breaker plus inversion FVG as a premium array). Also, "Unicorn" in 20200929-nz7Y5lrAqgM is an unrelated joke about losses.
2. Candle selection drifts. UrS 2016 content: the highest up-close candle at the swing, using the entire range. 2017: "the high between the low and the lower low", with price going to the middle of the breaker. 2022: price mostly stays in the lower half of the breaker candle. 2023: use bodies; wicks do the damage and are allowed outside. 2024: the most sensitive part is the last up-close (or lowest down-close) candle. 2025: use the entire range, not just the body, and not the wicks of other candles. Body versus full range is unresolved.
3. Retest requirement. 2016-2022: enter when price returns to the broken swing after the break. 2023 (1HtRfFYiwO0): "not a break and retest", and you can trade inside the breaker before it breaks. Both styles coexist.
4. Stop. 2016-2017: beyond the swing extreme, or the true high ignoring wicks. 2022: just beyond the breaker candle. 2024: a tight stop at a rejection block, but that is for order blocks. 2026: trailing above prior candle highs. No verbatim stop rule for the unicorn exists. Trade tables only show "below breaker swing low" (bz4Q) and "above bearish order block high" (JmAJ).
5. Breaker versus mitigation block. 2016-2017 and 2022-2024 all require the liquidity sweep. In 2020 (AoXOBI0PqCE) he says a mitigation block is "close to, but not the same as" a breaker. In 2024 (0OIplRTKYOA) he marks a failed higher high as "NOT a -Breaker. Mitigation Block."
6. Source quality. Dossiers from about 2018 onward are largely AI summaries, with some paraphrased text inside the quote cells. Examples: the q1vrarNcnfU and HRIXsFHYVmw summaries call the bullish breaker candle "down-close" or "up-close" inconsistently. The UrS-mtGHtAA quotes (up-close for bullish, down-close for bearish) are the authoritative definition. The stop-above-the-breaker-not-the-FVG rule (hQ379EuyNKQ) is a dossier paraphrase; only the "breaker is the factor" line is verbatim. The 2020 "killzone requirement" is also dossier-authored.
7. Targets moved from Fibonacci extensions and symmetrical swing projections (2017), to standard-deviation projections (2023), to liquidity pools, opening-gap octants and the Event Horizon (2026).

rules.rule: Use a real breaker (liquidity swept, then broken) as an entry array. A mitigation block (no sweep) can be traded through, so it is better as a target than an entry.

rules.rule: Higher-timeframe bias filter: when the higher timeframes are bullish, buy the daily/4H bullish discount arrays, and a bullish breaker is one of them. The sell side mirrors this with bearish premium arrays including the bearish breaker.

rules.rule: Bullish breaker structure: swing low, swing high, then a lower low that runs the sell stops. The breaker is the up-close candle (range) at the most recent swing high, before the old low was violated.
rules.quote: for a bullish breaker it's a bullish range or up close candle in the most recent swing high prior to an old low being violated

rules.rule: Bearish breaker structure (mirror): the down-close candle at the most recent swing low, before the old high was violated by a run on buy stops and the market then broke down.
rules.quote: a bearish breaker is a bearish range or down close candle in the most recent swing low prior to an old high being violated

rules.rule: Hard prerequisite: the extreme must have purged liquidity before the displacement. A level that merely turned the market (supply/demand flip) is not a breaker.
rules.quote: That is not what a breaker is. A breaker requires a purge of liquidity before displacement.

rules.rule: Why the sweep matters: the stop run traps the other side below the old low, which creates the later need to mitigate.

rules.rule: Optional confluence at the sweep: SMT divergence between correlated indices (ES makes the lower low, NQ will not). It was shown on the 2023 bullish breaker long and is not required.

rules.rule: Pattern shorthand: bearish breaker = high, low, higher high, then a break lower (bullish = low, high, lower low, then a break higher). The price sequence alone defines the pattern.

rules.rule: Which candle (2016 mentorship content published 2022): the highest one just before the drop, and the entire range of that candle is used.

rules.rule: Which candle (2024): the most sensitive part is the last up-close candle before the stop sweep, though the whole range counts as the breaker.

rules.rule: Which candle (2024, bearish): the lowest down-closed candle before the run-up. The most sensitivity is inside that candle.
rules.quote: The bearish breaker is this candle and this candle the most sensitivity is going to come inside of the lowest down closed candle prior to the run up

rules.rule: Which candle (2023): select by candle bodies (lowest close). Wicks do the damage and are not used to define the block.

market_structure.summary: Read price as a fractal hierarchy of 3-candle swings (short-, intermediate-, long-term). After a liquidity sweep, treat a displacement-driven break of the relevant short-term swing that leaves an FVG as the Market Structure Shift. From 2025 the entry reference is the CISD: price trading through the opening price of the up-close (or down-close) candle run, used as the order-block level.
market_structure.needs_clock: The core is pure price/OHLC and could run on 24/7 synthetic indices: 3-candle swings, the STH/ITH/LTH hierarchy, an MSS (displacement through a short-term swing that leaves an FVG), and CISD (price crossing the open of the up-close or down-close candle run). The clock appears only as filters and anchors. These are the 2017 killzones (London 02-04, NY 07-10), the 2020 killzone premise, the 2020 Friday/late-day filter, the 2022 noon-1pm no-trade rule and 8:30/9:30 sweep anchors, and 2025-26 context (7-9am pre-market, plus a 10:50-11:10 macro that appears only in the vgG9JAKwng4 dossier summary, not in any quote). Calendar-based reference levels (midnight or 8:30 open, session highs/lows, previous day high/low, NWOG/ORG) would need rolling or synthetic daily boundaries on a 24/7 market. In Jan 2025 (vgG9JAKwng4) he says the algorithm refers only to time and OHLC, so candle opens are legitimate price-only inputs.
market_structure.how_to_code:
SWINGS (price only, any timeframe). STH: bar i with high[i] > high[i-1] and high[i] > high[i+1] (3-candle, candle colour ignored); STL is the mirror. ITH: an STH whose previous and next STH in the STH series are both lower, OR an STH formed when price rebalances (returns into) an FVG (8GkQfdAXZP0). LTH: an ITH flanked by lower ITHs. Build each level by running the same pivot test on the level below (fractal). Lows mirror this. When two similar extremes compete, take the more extreme one (g8bhZReDK-Q).

STOP RUN vs FAILURE SWING. Stop run: a swing extreme is exceeded, then price rejects back inside. Failure swing: the next swing fails to exceed the prior extreme (lower high or higher low).

BEARISH MSS (bullish mirrors). (1) Sweep: an STH, ITH, relative equal highs or a session/daily high is traded through; record the sweep high. (2) Reference low: the most recent STL formed in the advance into the sweep high (on a higher timeframe, the ITL; the conservative grade waits for the ITL). (3) Trigger: a later bar breaks below that low with displacement. Practical definition: body beyond the swing (not wick only), body size >= k x average body (k about 1.5-2; this is subjective), AND the leg leaves a 3-candle bearish FVG (candle1.low > candle3.high). For shorts the FVG should sit above 50% of the leg's range (QkokVv0owSE). Reject: wick-only break, break through overlapped candles with no FVG, engulfing alone, break inside a conflicting opposite imbalance.

ENTRY / STOP / TARGET. Entry: limit at the FVG near edge (candle-3 level) or its CE (50%) on the retrace; alternatives are the breaker or order block, or the 2017-2020 version, which is an OTE retrace of 62-79% on the body-to-body leg. Stop: above the sweep high or displacement swing high, candle 1 of the FVG, or the ITH. Target: opposing liquidity (swing low, equal lows, previous day low). The first objective is the 50% equilibrium. Projections are -1.0/-1.5/-2.0/-2.5 SD anchored from ITH to swing low. Trail the stop above lower intermediate highs. Add on a new same-direction MSS plus FVG.

CISD (bearish; bullish mirrors with down-close candles). Find the run of consecutive up-close candles immediately before the decline. Level = the lowest open of that run (Jan 2025). Variants: the open of the sweep candle (Venom, Apr 2025) or the open of the last up-close candle (Sep 2025). Trigger: the first later bar whose low trades below the level. A close below is not required (Jul 2026); require a close below only as a stricter option. Confirm that the move left an FVG (eai0nHhAC8w: 'Without the imbalance, there is no order block'). Entry: the retest up into that order-block zone (CISD level up to the run's high). Stop above the run's high. Pyramid on later up-close runs that break lower (PPCVZ2m3Dk8).

BIAS. Take the direction from the HTF swing sequence: lower ITHs mean sell-side draw. Combine with premium/discount of the current dealing range (50% of ITH-to-swing-low).

SUBJECTIVE PARTS (need parameters or discretion): displacement size; which short-term low is the one to break; which candle run defines the CISD; the 'first presented' or 'respected' gap when several exist; the FVG-rebalance ITH variant; whether an HTF PD-array context is required (dossier paraphrase only).
market_structure.changes_over_time:
1) Same words, different concepts. 'Institutional market structure' in GuycI8XubgE (Nov 2016 material, re-uploaded 2022) means inter-market symmetry or SMT between DXY and foreign currencies, not a single-chart swing read. 'Institutional swing points' in xRjKtUEKkSE means only two kinds (stop run or failure swing). From 2020 the swing hierarchy STH/ITH/LTH (xGFCIUFxsbw, 8GkQfdAXZP0, PPCVZ2m3Dk8) is the structural tool. Code the 2020+ definitions and treat the other two as context. The 'Key Swing Points' video T0JyGdJ28fM is about session-time swing points (Asia, London, NY), not the fractal hierarchy.

2) Swing wording is ambiguous. uE-aaP16nOw (2017) says 'only three candles or three bars' at 18:13 but also 'a high that has two lower highs on either side' at 20:02. N29ZJ-o31xs (2022) gives a one-candle-each-side 3-candle pattern. The 2025 ITH is 'two lower short-term highs to the right and left'. ITH versions: 2020 'lower highs on either side'; 2022 'flanked by lower short term highs OR forms at an FVG rebalance'; Sep 2024 summary 'subordinate to a higher swing'; the Oct 2022 core-content summary (Ad-votrg6WQ) says it must form inside an HTF PD array. That last point is unquoted paraphrase and was not used as a quote.

3) The MSS got stricter and the entry tool changed. 2017-2020: a break of the short-term high or low (MSB/MSS), then a Fibonacci OTE retrace of 62-79% (70.5% sweet spot), with the leg measured body-to-body. 2022: displacement is mandatory, an FVG must be left, and a limit goes in the FVG ('no displacement, no trade'). 2023: overlapped candles with no FVG are not an MSS (uzPM1CuSSx8). 2025-26: a wick inside a conflicting imbalance and an engulfing candle are not an MSS (b4DOrfGau8w, Rwao8f6oD0Q), and candle bodies matter. In Oct 2022 core-content summaries the same words (Daily/Weekly MSS plus OTE) are used for multi-week swing trades.

4) CISD evolved, and the reference candle differs by video. Apr 2022 (eai0nHhAC8w): 'an order block ... is a change in the state of delivery' (an imbalance is required). Sep 2023 and Aug 2024: price changing direction at a PD array or an order block activating. Jan 2025 (vgG9JAKwng4): the lowest open of consecutive up-close candles. Apr 2025 Venom: the open of the sweep candle. Sep 2025: the open of an up-close candle. Jul 2026: crossing the open is enough, no close needed. The vgG9JAKwng4 dossier summary adds 'confirmed when price closes below' and ties it to a 10:50-11:10 macro, but neither point is in the quoted text, and the 2026 quotes contradict the close requirement. CISD is a candle-open cross, not a swing break. In the Sep 2025 'Model 2022' sequence it comes after the MSS and breaker, as the order-block level. WVIjXP26AhQ ('PreSession CISD', Feb 2026) is silent, so it is evidence of a trade only, with no rule text.

5) Stops moved from 'at the swing low, 1-2 pips beyond' (2017) to above the sweep or displacement high or candle 1 of the FVG (2022), the ITH (2022-24), the order-block high (2025), or below the order block's mean threshold (Sep 2023 HFT video, tjnir-o4rsQ).

6) Clock tension. 2017 and 2020 are killzone-driven, and 2020-10 adds a Friday filter. The 2022 mentorship adds the 8:30/9:30 sweeps and the noon-1pm ban. In 2025 he says the algorithm sees only time and OHLC, not stops or volume, while the 2017-2022 language leans heavily on stop runs and liquidity. The structure definitions themselves never need the clock.

7) Source reliability. Many dossiers are generated summaries. The Sep-Oct 2022 'Core Content' items are re-uploads of 2016 teaching, and some of their 'Rules' tables mix paraphrase with quotes without quote marks (Ad-votrg6WQ, Oec_0NM_OeY, which has a paraphrased killzone-only MSS filter). Unquoted paraphrase was excluded from the parts. VL4YLTRerHY (Million Dollar Swing Setup) has suspiciously precise numbers, so treat it as low confidence. The uzPM1CuSSx8 quote is a garbled auto-transcript, so its meaning comes from the dossier note.
