rules.rule: Do not enter just because price has reached a target or PD level. Wait until the market itself signals a shift, meaning displacement plus a Market Structure Shift.
rules.quote: wait for the algorithm to communicate a shift through displacement and Market Structure Shift

rules.rule: A hard sell-off or rally after a liquidity sweep is not tradeable unless it prints the model criteria: an MSS that leaves an imbalance (FVG).
rules.quote: if price sells off or rallies aggressively following a sweep but does not print the required mentorship model criteria (market structure shift with an imbalance / Fair Value Gap), do not trade the move

rules.rule: Structure is read around key higher-timeframe support/resistance levels. Without them there is no directional bias whatever model you use (2020 'Essentials' lecture).
rules.quote: support resistance trumps everything without the understanding of key support resistance levels you're not going to get to a directional bias regardless of what trading model you're using

rules.rule: Take the direction of the highest timeframe in your chosen three-timeframe stack.
rules.quote: the highest probability trades are made in the higher time frame direction

rules.rule: Swing-hierarchy bias: successive lower intermediate-term highs confirm the delivery is reaching for sell-side liquidity (mirrored for higher intermediate-term lows).
rules.quote: If intermediate-term highs keep creating lower intermediate-term highs, it confirms the algorithm is reaching down for sell-side liquidity.

rules.rule: 2017 daily-swing bias: once a daily swing high is traded through you are on bullish alert and wait for the next swing low to form (mirrored for bearish).
rules.quote: and if price trades through the swing high you are now on bullish alert you wait for the swing low the form

rules.rule: VARIANT MEANING (2016 Month 03 lesson): 'institutional market structure' meant inter-market symmetry between DXY and foreign currencies, not a single-chart swing read. Symmetry means continuation. A non-confirming (SMT) swing means reversal.
rules.quote: When the dollar index makes a lower low and foreign currencies make a higher high, this confirms current price action and the underlying trend is likely to continue.

rules.rule: Only two kinds of institutional swing point exist: a stop run (swing extreme exceeded, then rejected) or a failure swing (swing extreme not exceeded).
rules.quote: I want you to understand that there's really only two forms of swing points in the marketplace as it relates to institutional trading: it's in the form of a stop run or a failure swing. That's it, there's nothing else.

rules.rule: Short-term swing high = 3-candle pattern (middle high higher than the candle on each side). Candle colour is irrelevant. Buy-side liquidity rests above it.
rules.quote: swing high as this it's a candle with a lower high to the left of it and a lower high to the right of it three candle pattern okay it does not matter if the candles are up or down closes you're just looking for a swing High because above that's it's going to be buy side liquidity

rules.rule: Short-term swing low = 3-candle pattern (middle low lower than the candle on each side).
rules.quote: swing low is a candle with a higher low to the left of it and a higher low to the right of it three candle pattern

rules.rule: Intermediate-term high (ITH) = a high flanked on both sides by lower short-term highs, OR a swing high that forms when price rebalances an FVG. The low side mirrors this.
rules.quote: intermediate term high is flanked by lower short term highs on both sides or forms at an FVG rebalance

rules.rule: Long-term high (LTH) = a high flanked on both sides by lower intermediate-term highs. The hierarchy is fractal: STH, then ITH, then LTH.
rules.quote: long term high is flanked by lower intermediate term highs

rules.rule: 2025 restatement of the ITH: a high with two lower short-term highs either side of it. It applies on any timeframe because the structure is fractal.
rules.quote: Intermediate term high is any high that has two lower short-term highs to the right and left of it. And we also have it in the smaller scale here because it's fractal

rules.rule: When two candidate swing lows compete, use the one that reached the lowest price. Anchor the dealing range to that extreme (mirror for highs).
rules.quote: why am I using this one not that one? Because this one went lower.

rules.rule: Before the shift, expect a stop hunt. A move down is preceded by a short-term high being taken out (buy stops). A move up is preceded by a short-term low being run out.
rules.quote: anytime a significant price move lower is expected always anticipate some measure of a stop hunt on buy stops or a short-term High being taken out obviously it's reversed when you're looking for higher prices generally you'll see a short term low run out

rules.rule: 2017 definition: a break in market structure = the short-term high is broken. The swing low-to-high that results is then used for the Fibonacci (OTE) measurement.
rules.quote: when it's high is broken that's a break in market structure okay so you want to use the low to the high that forms once this high is taken out so we'll bring in our Fibonacci

rules.rule: 2017 bearish version: a short-term high is taken out (stop run) and then immediately broken back down. That is the break in market structure.
rules.quote: we have taken out a short term high but immediately after that short term high is violated it's broken down so in essence this is a break in market structure here

rules.rule: 2020 MSS definition: the short-term swing low on the highest timeframe of your model breaks. That is the catalyst for looking for the optimal trade entry.
rules.quote: this short-term swing low on the highest timeframe for your particular trading model once that breaks this would be the catalyst for you to say okay this is probably going to be an optimal trade entry

rules.rule: 2022 Model (bearish): price runs above an old high or relative equal highs, then short-term lows are taken out WITH displacement. You then go back through the displacement leg for an FVG to short into.
rules.quote: to run above an old high or relative equal highs and if you're bearish that short-term lows taken out with displacement and then you go back through that displacement leg looking for a fair value gap to short into

rules.rule: Running through the short-term low is what he calls displacement.
rules.quote: run through this short term low we have displacement

rules.rule: Displacement must be energetic: a move that leaves the area quickly. Hesitant drift does not qualify.
rules.quote: hasn't really shown me what displacement something energetic where it moves away

rules.rule: 2023 tightening: breaking a swing high or low is not enough. If the break runs through overlapped candles and leaves no fair value gap, it is not an MSS (auto-transcript is garbled; meaning taken from the dossier note).
rules.quote: We have the low high lower low we moved above it it's a shift in Market structure no there's no fair value Gap in here because we've had all this overlapped Candlestick run running all the way over top this range.

rules.rule: 2024: the MSS is an energetic break below the swing low, and it creates an active bearish breaker.
rules.quote: notice the energetic break below the swing low during the opening range, creating an active bearish breaker.

rules.rule: 2025 'Model 2022' sequence on NQ 1m: buy side taken, then shift in market structure, then a retrace up into a premium FVG, then a break lower that forms a bearish breaker.
rules.quote: this is model 2022 because we had buy side taken here shift in market structure trade back up into a fair value gap that's in a premium and then breaks lower here's is a breaker.

rules.rule: CISD in the same sequence: the bearish order block is the change in the state of delivery.
rules.quote: And we have an order block that's bearish, which is change in the state of delivery

rules.rule: CISD level for a short: a run of consecutive up-close candles is the bearish order block, and the delivery changes at the open of that run.
rules.quote: consecutive of closed candles is your bearish order block and changes the delivery at that candle's open.

rules.rule: CISD level (Jan 2025): the LOWEST opening price among the consecutive up-close candles, not a supply zone.
rules.quote: it's the change in the state of delivery which is the lowest opening price of these consecutive candlesticks

rules.rule: CISD = the opening price of an up-close candle (for shorts). Price at or below that open is then delivered toward lower discount/sell side.
rules.quote: Change in the state of delivery is the opening price of an upclose candle. It was rallying here, the algorithm changes gears and anything at that price or lower it will spool and reach for lower discount or sell side

rules.rule: CISD is validated as soon as a candle trades down through the opening price of the up-close candle (bearish case). A close below is NOT required.
rules.quote: So, open on up close candle when you go bearish. As soon as this candlestick trades down through the opening price, it need not close below it. As soon as it does that, that validates this as a change in the state of delivery

rules.rule: Same pass-through rule restated in Jul 2026: crossing the open is enough. No candle close is needed.
rules.quote: Once it passes through it right on that candle it need not like it does here close below it. We don't need to see that.

rules.rule: 2017 entry on a break of structure: wait for a retest of the broken level, where old support becomes resistance (bearish case).
rules.quote: all we're doing is waiting for a retest of that same old support level now becomes resistance

rules.rule: 2017 OTE entry after the break: go long as price retraces to the 62% level of the swing (62-79% band, 70.5% sweet spot).
rules.quote: as price hits this 62% tration level right there that's all it would be necessary you can go long on that

rules.rule: 2022 entry: after the old high is violated and the swing low breaks (bearish MSS), short the retrace up into the fair value gap.
rules.quote: now you have a opportunity does price draw back up into the fair value Gap after this candle breaks below here and giving you a bearish market structure shift yes it trades up in the ne value Gap you can go short there

rules.rule: Two entry grades: aggressive = first lower-timeframe FVG inside the HTF order block. Conservative = wait for the MSS that breaks the intermediate-term low.
rules.quote: aggressive entry is getting in on the first lower-timeframe FVG inside higher-timeframe order block; conservative low-risk entry waits for market structure shift breaking the intermediate-term low

rules.rule: A level break alone is not an entry. A valid short needs an FVG created during the displacement through the level, and you enter on the retrace into that FVG.
rules.quote: do not trade the level simply because it broke; a valid short entry requires an FVG to form during displacement through the level, and entry must occur upon retracement into that FVG

rules.rule: If you miss the move, do not chase. Wait for the next little swing point to break, then look for the retest.
rules.quote: If I miss it and it takes off, it's no problem; I'm waiting for this little swing point here to be broken. Once that high is broken, we look for the retest.

rules.rule: Do not wait for price to return to the exact stop-run level. A secondary retracement into a fresh order block is a valid entry.
rules.quote: We can be a buyer here with the exception that there may be a bullish order block over here. It doesn't have to come back down to this level.

rules.rule: Swing-trade scale: after a daily MSS, enter on the daily retrace into the 62-79% OTE. Stop below the swing low. (Lower-confidence dossier: the 'Million Dollar Swing Setup' summary reads as generated.)
rules.quote: Enter on the daily retracement into an Optimum Trade Entry (62% to 79% Fibonacci level), place your stop below the swing low, and let the trade run for weeks.

rules.rule: Short stop goes above the intermediate-term high (the swing high that has the imbalance). It should not be exceeded.
rules.quote: This is an intermediate term high, swing high because it has the imbalance. It should not trade higher than a high. That's the reason why I'm telling you you can put your stop loss there.

rules.rule: Long stop sits just below the swing low formed when sell-side liquidity was taken.
rules.quote: place the protective Stop Loss just below the Swing Low that was formed when taking out the sell-side liquidity

rules.rule: Short stop sits above the newly formed swing high that swept the liquidity.
rules.quote: stop loss placed above the newly formed swing high that swept the liquidity

rules.rule: FVG-based stop: above candle 1's high of the bearish FVG, chosen for safety while learning.
rules.quote: you want a lot of safety so place your stop above candle number one's high

rules.rule: 2017 OTE long: stop is at the swing low. Wicks through the OTE zone are tolerated.
rules.quote: price trades down into the optimal trade entry and here it does wick through a little bit here but your stop is going to be at the low so as your risk

rules.rule: 2017 targets: the old high is the first objective, then target 1, target 2 and the symmetrical price swing.
rules.quote: our old high is our first profit objective and it's been hit so far next up side would be target one target two and symmetrical price ring respectively

rules.rule: Shorts should come from premium and target discount, measured against the 50% equilibrium of the dealing range.
rules.quote: everything above that 50 level is premium everything below is discount so if we're looking for a short setup we want to see it in premium and we want to see our targets down in discount

rules.rule: First objective after an MSS entry is the 50% equilibrium of the range.
rules.quote: first objective would be 50 percent of the range

rules.rule: Project from the intermediate-term high down to the swing low. The -1.5 standard deviation is the primary target (other lectures also project -1.0 to -2.5).
rules.quote: the negative 1.5 standard deviation is your primary projection target

rules.rule: Intraday full-position target goes at a significant liquidity pool, for example above morning swing highs for longs.
rules.quote: full position profit targets for intraday index futures trades should be anchored to significant buy-side liquidity pools resting above morning swing highs

rules.rule: Once price breaks and displaces in your favour, trail the short stop down above the lower intermediate highs (the swing hierarchy used as a trail).
rules.quote: as soon as price breaks lower and displaces in favor of the position, trail the stop-loss down aggressively above lower intermediate highs

rules.rule: A second position may be added when a new MSS forms in the same direction and price retraces into the newly formed FVG.
rules.quote: after an initial long position is established from an FVG retracement, a second position may be placed when price forms another bullish market structure shift and retraces into the newly formed Fair Value Gap

rules.rule: Swing-scale management: partials at the first and second weekly objectives, then trail the runner behind daily swing lows.
rules.quote: Scale out 30% at the first weekly objective, 30% at the second, and hold the remaining 40% with a trailing stop behind daily swing lows until the macro target is reached.

rules.rule: Do not move the stop up under an inversion FVG until structure has actually broken (a break above short-term highs).
rules.quote: if you're long and you rolled your stop loss just below the inversion fair value gap: Never, never, never do that until it breaks structure and leaving it

rules.rule: If price trades through an old swing level or FVG without displacement breaking a short-term swing, there is no setup.
rules.quote: if price trades through an old swing level or Fair Value Gap and fails to produce displacement breaking a short-term swing low/high, no trade setup exists

rules.rule: No displacement means no trade. Do not anticipate the turn.
rules.quote: if there is no displacement, there is no trade. Do not try to anticipate the turn without displacement

rules.rule: A wick break inside a conflicting buy-side/sell-side imbalance is not an MSS.
rules.quote: This is not a market structure shift because it's a wick inside of a buy-side imbalance sell-side inefficiency.

rules.rule: An engulfing candle alone is not an MSS. Per the dossier summary, displacement means an energetic move through a key swing that leaves an unfilled FVG.
rules.quote: an engulfing candle is not a shift in market structure.

rules.rule: Displacement-leg quality: for a short, the FVG must sit above the 50% level of the displacement leg. Below 50% invalidates the short.
rules.quote: for a bearish displacement leg to qualify for a short entry setup, the resulting Fair Value Gap must be located above the 50% equilibrium level of that displacement leg's high-to-low range

rules.rule: Structure is read on a three-timeframe stack. Short-term trades use 4h for bias, 1h for management and 15m for entry timing. Day trades use 1h, 15m and 5m.
rules.quote: for short-term trades you'll be using the 4-hour chart for your trade premise or your directional bias and then on the one-hour chart that would be your trade management or mid-level time frame and then your 15-minute chart would be utilized for your timing for entry

rules.rule: 2025 shift: not a static top-down read. Cycle continuously through the continuum (15m, 5m, 1m), revisiting each on its candle close.
rules.quote: that means I'm constantly cycling through all those time frames it's not top- down analysis it's cycling through continuously

rules.rule: Stated in the 2022 mentorship to work in both forex and index trading.
rules.quote: it works in forex it works in index trading

rules.rule: 2017 claim that the 3-bar swing/daily-bias method is asset-agnostic.
rules.quote: this works in stocks it works in futures it works in bonds it works in just about anything they can trade

rules.rule: 2020: entries belong inside the killzones: London open, New York open, London close and Asia.
rules.quote: we always go back to our key premise of trading within kill zones okay so you want to be doing your entries and your kill zone times London open New York open London close or Asia

rules.rule: 2017 'Trading the Key Swing Points': the key swing points in this lesson are session-time swing points (Asia, London, NY highs and lows). They matter when they coincide with higher-timeframe price levels.
rules.quote: you want to be using higher timeframe price levels and when these specific key swing points or time of day overlap with higher timeframe levels you can anticipate what would be otherwise expected on the higher time frame

rules.rule: 2017 windows (NY time): London 02:00-04:00, New York 07:00-10:00.
rules.quote: London is basically two o'clock to four o'clock in the morning that's the sweet spot or the best time to anticipate a higher load of form and the New York is going to be seven o'clock in the morning to ten o'clock in the morning

rules.rule: A break of a short-term low late on a Friday is not trusted. Day of week and time of day must be weighed before trusting any intraday break of structure.
rules.quote: Price breaks this short-term low—there's your intraday break in market structure. But it's Friday; it's not likely to continue. You have to understand what day of the week and what time of day it is.

rules.rule: 2022 mentorship: do not trade the noon to 1pm New York lunch hour.
rules.quote: noon to 1:00 in the afternoon New York time that is a no trade time period

rules.rule: Sep 2025: for forex and DXY he does not look at anything after 12:00 ET (relevant to the GBPUSD CISD trade).

daily_bias.summary: Grade the odds of an up-close or down-close day from higher-timeframe flow and a mechanical daily swing sequence, aim at the previous day's high/low ("to it and through it", about 10-20 pips beyond), buy at or below / sell at or above the day's open, and drop the daily bias in favour of local liquidity or an intraday counter-trend scalp when the picture is unclear or event risk dominates.
daily_bias.needs_clock: Split answer. The core daily-candle logic needs no clock, only a consistent daily bar. That covers up-close/down-close classification, the 3-bar daily swing high/low state machine, the day-4 raid of candle 3's high, the day-5 PDH/PDL run, outside-day detection, the 3-day range, and the 10-20 pip overshoot. It could run on 24/7 synthetic indices if you pick an arbitrary day boundary (for example 00:00 UTC), scale the overshoot by ATR instead of pips, and accept that "key support/resistance" must come from price-derived levels. The open-price rule (buy at or below the day's open, sell at or above) needs only a defined day-open anchor, so a synthetic's own daily open works, but it loses the specific midnight-New-York meaning. Everything session-based needs a real clock and is not meaningful on 24/7 synthetics. That covers London setting the low or high of day, London Close 10:00-12:00 NY, the 11:00 NY draw-out, the Mon-Wed-only rule, the Tue/Wed weekly extreme, the 1:30 PM and 3-4 PM windows, the 9:30 opening range, and the 9:45/10:00 news filter. The event-week bias-avoidance rule needs an economic calendar and cannot be done from price alone.
daily_bias.how_to_code: Mechanical, price-only core on completed daily bars D[t] with O,H,L,C. (1) Classify each day: up-close if C>O, down-close if C<O. Outside day if H[t]>H[t-1] and L[t]<L[t-1]. Bullish outside-down-close if outside, C<O, C near L, H>prior H (false break), and the HTF context is bullish. That gives a long bias for the next day. (2) Bullish 5-candle state machine, using 3-bar fractals (swing high if H[i] is above both neighbours): (a) price trades through (H > value of) the last confirmed daily swing high, so state=ALERT; (b) wait for a 3-bar swing low whose low is above the prior swing low (higher low only), and note candle 3 as the bar after the swing-low bar; (c) day 4 opens below candle 3's high and its high exceeds candle 3's high, so state=ARMED; (d) from day 5 on, expect high[t]>high[t-1], with a sweep of about 10-20 pips or a fraction of ATR beyond the PDH. The target is the PDH plus that overshoot. (e) Terminate when a new daily swing high forms or price hits a key level (use a prior HTF swing or an unmitigated daily/weekly FVG). Bearish is the exact mirror: break a swing low, form a lower swing high, day 4 trades below candle 3's low, then run the PDL each day. (3) Open-price rule: with a long bias, allow entries only when price <= day_open (short: >= day_open). In 2020 form day_open is the 00:00 New York open. Cap at Mon-Wed and expire around 11:00 NY. For a price-only version use the daily open. (4) HTF flow filter: weekly draw = nearest unraided old high/low or unfilled weekly/daily FVG, and require the daily idea to agree. Invalidate a day if both PDH and PDL are tagged before your entry, or if a bearish-bias day takes the PDL before the PDH. (5) Order-flow check: in bullish flow no candle body should close through the last down-close candle that supported price (the mirror applies for bearish flow). (6) Counter-trend tape variant: on 1m, a sell-side sweep (close back above the swept low) followed by price entering a bullish FVG against the daily bias gives a long. Put the stop under the FVG/OB low and target the nearest internal buy-side pool, not the HTF draw. Take partials there and trail the rest. Subjective parts a programmer must approximate: which swing high counts as "of importance", what counts as "key support/resistance", "bullish market overall" for the outside-day rule, how far past the PDH/PDL is enough, whether a day is a consolidation or "seek and destroy" day, picking the weekly draw (old low vs high vs imbalance), event-week avoidance, and the FVG/OB choice in tape reading.
daily_bias.changes_over_time: 1) Daily bias mandatory versus unrealistic. In 2017 (uE-aaP16nOw, 1Wmh8829mZs, vJvcZGGeTZU) the daily bias is a rigid, rule-based daily-candle sequence. The Core Content Month 08 re-upload (dated 20221002, -cXnnHjy9s0) says: "If you don't have higher timeframe directional bias from the daily chart, you have no business taking day trades." But 2022-06-22 (koN1ge8bewI) says "everyday bias is unrealistic" and moves to a weekly-expansion read. The 2024 streams (LpdFdIckXqo, joqM_Z96vtM, aaKO-eu-tQ4) say bias is only a probability, to be avoided in FOMC/NFP weeks, with "trade the liquidity that's available". The 2026 zyKAPNk_prA gives an opening-range procedure for when there is no initial bias. The Core Content uploads are probably older mentorship material re-uploaded in 2022. That is my inference, not stated in the dossiers, so dating by upload date can mislead. 2) Open-price rule. In 2017 (Sb9m_dxr4bI) it is fractal: buy at or below the monthly, weekly or daily open. The Sunday open is extended to Friday for the weekly (Yqio1Ja0lIQ). By 2020 (RLDLuYaZYI4) the daily open is midnight New York, drawn out to about 11:00. In 2021 (BZ4HVsArJBE) it is used only Mon-Wed and ignored Thu/Fri. The 2017 midnight line first appears in G8OEsUAoIWE. 3) Outside day. In 2017 an outside day with a down close in a bullish market is a buy setup (vJvcZGGeTZU). In 2022 (hzoMJQlEv5M) an outside day that falls about 1 handle short of an old daily low means a consolidation day, to be faded at 3-4 PM toward the 50% midpoint. These are different contexts, but they pull in different directions. 4) Counter-trend. The 2017 daily-bias material treats trading with the daily bias as the rule. By 2022 (k26euOG6zAk, gLK4Qm6jte8) he trades against it intraday, with the HTF draw as a best case only. 5) Internal inconsistencies: uE-aaP16nOw calls the swing a "three bars" pattern (18:13) but at 20:02 describes "two lower highs on either side". The 1Wmh8829mZs bullish rule needs a higher swing low, yet a lbAQNxRPXMs daily chart is described as a swing low forming after trading below an old low. 6) Source fidelity. The 2017 dossiers hold raw auto-caption text (e.g. "load" for low, "rated" for raided), so they are high fidelity. rules.rule: The daily-bias step has one job: estimate the odds that today closes up or closes down.
rules.quote: what we're trying to do is ascertain the likelihood of it being a up close or a down close day

rules.rule: Not every day is tradeable. Do not force a trade every day.
rules.quote: do not try to force your live account into a condition where it must trade every single day day trading is not every day trading

rules.rule: No-bias branch: when there is no bias, stop trying to predict and trade the liquidity that is actually available.
rules.quote: so you can trade without a bias you can trade the liquidity that's available

rules.rule: Monthly chart gives the macro institutional bias.
rules.quote: the purpose of using a monthly chart is that it provides a macro institutional bias so we can see what large institutions are doing

rules.rule: Daily setups have the best odds when the monthly and weekly both agree with the daily idea.
rules.quote: the highest probabilities and trading the daily chart is when both the monthly and weekly support the trade idea that you would be using or hunting on daily

rules.rule: Order-flow axiom: in a bullish flow, down-close candles and down moves are where smart money buys. In a bearish flow, up-close candles and rallies are where it sells.
rules.quote: Smart money buys in down markets, and they sell in up markets. That is the fundamental understanding you must have.

rules.rule: 2022 method: do not predict each day. Read the weekly chart for the likely weekly expansion (old high/low or an imbalance above/below price) and let the days inherit it.
rules.quote: i'm not trying to get a daily bias every single day i'm trying to determine the likely weekly expansion and again what is that i utilize a weekly chart and i studied that

rules.rule: 2024 definition: bias is a probability statement about where the largest movement is likely, not a certainty.
rules.quote: How can you grind out an income without a bias? What is bias? That's where you think the largest probability of movement is going to be

rules.rule: 2024 intraday form: the opening gap is the initial bias and the frame for the session (index futures).
rules.quote: Remember the opening Gap is the initial bias Caleb the framework for the day.

rules.rule: Bullish draw: the previous day's high or an old high is buy-side liquidity (buy stops), and price is drawn up to it. Bearish is the mirror at the previous day's low.
rules.quote: it's the previous day's high or an old high that's gonna be in the form of buy-side liquidity or buy stops so the market will draw up to that level

rules.rule: Bullish daily sequence step 1: price trades through a daily swing high (3-bar fractal), so go on bullish alert and wait for a daily swing low to form.
rules.quote: and if price trades through the swing high you are now on bullish alert you wait for the swing low the form

rules.rule: Step 2: the new daily swing low must be a higher low. It must not take out the previous recent swing low.
rules.quote: key point here is this swing low should not take out a previous recent swing low

rules.rule: Bearish mirror: price trades below a swing low, then wait for a retracement to form a swing high (overbought), then target a run on the low of candle 3.
rules.quote: we want to see price trade below a swing low once that occurs then we start waiting for a swing high to form why are we doing that because we're waiting for a retracement it's gonna go to an overbought condition

rules.rule: Outside-day setup: in a bullish market, an outside day that false-breaks the previous high and closes down near its low is a buy setup.
rules.quote: an outside day with a down close that's typically bullish reason why it creates a false break above the previous day's high and then close it on the low if we're in a bullish market overall and that occurs generally sets up a really good buy scenario

rules.rule: Reference range: the highest high and lowest low of the last three days, with today counted.
rules.quote: we're always gonna be looking back the last three days okay that's your there's your range okay you're gonna be looking back at the highest high and the lowest low in the last three days

rules.rule: Counter-trend variant: a day that looks bullish intraday can be counter-trend to the higher timeframe. This is a deliberate against-HTF intraday trade.
rules.quote: in a day that's likely to be bullish it's counter trend to a higher time frame

rules.rule: Day 4 trigger: after the swing low confirms (candle 3), the next day opens below candle 3's high and is expected to run through it.
rules.quote: the third candle that makes the swing low that high you want to see the next candle open below that candle is high and then anticipate the market to run through this candle is high

rules.rule: Once day 4 trades through candle 3's high, day 5 is expected to run the previous day's high (PDH raid).
rules.quote: we want to see the high be traded through one day number four okay once day number four does that we know that day number five we can be looking for a run on previous day's high liquidity

rules.rule: A full down-close day inside a bullish scenario is the signal to start following: the market is primed for an OTE long and runs on previous highs.
rules.quote: whenever you see a full day's down close that's like a big red neon sign say start following me especially if you're in a bullish scenario that markets primed to have an optimal trade entry long and start running out previous day's highs

rules.rule: Bearish daily execution: the day opens, makes a small Judas/Power-of-3 tail, then sells to a down close reaching for the previous day's low.
rules.quote: every single trading day opens creates a small little tail power three Judas swing sell it down close reach for the previous day's low

rules.rule: 2022 limit-order form: the daily candle must have fully closed down (a forming candle is not valid) with higher-timeframe flow seeking PD arrays above. Up-close and sell side is the mirror.
rules.quote: The daily should post a bearish candle. The daily chart must close the candle with a down close, and it is not valid while the daily chart candle is trading and or forming.

rules.rule: Counter-trend tape-reading trigger: sell-side liquidity has been taken and price has traded into a fair value gap, so go long against the daily bias.
rules.quote: on the basis of the sell stops or sell side liquidity being taken we've already traded into a fair value gap around that 4 000 level

rules.rule: No-bias trigger (2026): let the first 30 minutes of the opening range form, wait for the first FVG, and let the market consume the 9:45/10:00 news before committing.
rules.quote: submitting to the first half an hour of the opening range, looking for first fair value gap, looking for the market to consume 9:45 or 10:00 news

rules.rule: Open-price rule: when daily bias is bullish, buy at or below the daily open. When bearish, sell at or above it.
rules.quote: if we're bullish relative to the daily timeframe we are looking to be buying at or below the daily opening price and if we're bearish on the daily we're gonna be focusing on selling short at or above the daily opening price

rules.rule: 2020 version of the open-price rule: the reference open is the midnight New York open. Buy at, near or below it when bullish.
rules.quote: If you study daily ranges when the market's bullish and study where that opening price is at midnight: you want to be buying at or very near the opening price or below it.

rules.rule: Swing-trade form: place a buy limit at the close of the completed down-close daily candle. The next day's open dips below it, giving a deep discount fill.
rules.quote: When we use a buy limit entry at the close, what we're doing is the very next day or the next candle when it opens up, we're expecting price movement to move below that down candle's close

rules.rule: Intraday confirmation: if London forms a low in agreement with a bullish daily, wait for the retracement lower into the New York open and buy the continuation.
rules.quote: if London agrees with the daily chart being bullish that means we should be seeing a low form in London we would anticipate a retracement lower into New York open

rules.rule: Counter-trend/tape-reading stop: sit just under the defended low. Price trading back into it means the idea is wrong and you accept the loss.
rules.quote: now i have six contracts long and i'll move my stop up just a little bit underneath that low right there it should not trade back down into that if it does i'm wrong and that's fine

rules.rule: No-bias long: the original stop goes below the structural low, even if wider than preferred.
rules.quote: The original stop has to be below that low right there. So, buying it here, stop loss down there.

rules.rule: Bullish target is the previous day's high. Bearish target is the previous day's low.
rules.quote: if we're bullish we're gonna be focusing on the previous day's high for momentum and more bearish when we focus on the previous day's low for momentum

rules.rule: Expect each day to run the previous day's low and go through it, not stop at it.
rules.quote: each day we're focusing on the previous day's low and that's where it's going to be aiming for to it and through it

rules.rule: Overshoot size for forex: price usually reaches about 10 to 20 pips beyond the previous high or low.
rules.quote: I teach that price generally will reach about 10 to 20 pips above a previous high or low

rules.rule: Counter-trend trades do not need the ultimate higher-timeframe draw. Bank profit at internal liquidity.
rules.quote: but price does not need to reach the ultimate draw on liquidity for an intraday trade setup to be valid and profitable

rules.rule: Bias lifecycle: keep expecting the PDH raid each day until a new daily swing high forms or price reaches key support/resistance. Then the sequence is over.
rules.quote: we're looking for previous day's highs to be rated each day until a swing high when a daily forms or price reaches a key support or resistance level

rules.rule: Once in profit, move the stop to breakeven and manage the trade toward the PDH.
rules.quote: move my stop loss to a point of no loss it's above my entry point so now I have an opportunity to sit in this trade and hopefully manage it to the point where it takes out previous day's high

rules.rule: Exit before the named objective rather than demanding perfection.
rules.quote: I always want to exit before my target so if I'm calling this as an objective I'm going to be exiting before that

rules.rule: Weekly cap: once the weekly pip objective is made in one day, stop trading for the week.
rules.quote: if I can get my entire weekly objective which is 50 to 75 pips per week if I can get that done in one day then I won't do any more trading after that regardless of what day of the week it is

rules.rule: Counter-trend trade: take partials at the next draw on liquidity (buy-side pool) and trail the runners.
rules.quote: buyside liquidity is the next draw on liquidity i'll take four of the contracts off

rules.rule: If price tags both sides of the previous day's candle, the directional edge is gone: indecision or a coming reversal.
rules.quote: very rarely do you see both sides of the previous day's candle tagged or traded through if it does it's usually indecisiveness or it's going to be a reversal soon

rules.rule: Bearish bias needs the buy-side/old-high run first. If the previous day's low is taken first and price then rallies, the short is cancelled.
rules.quote: if price takes out the previous day's low or sell-side liquidity first and then rallies, the price action is not bearish and cancels a short setup

rules.rule: Weekly-bias version: in a bullish week, if price trades below the low set by Wednesday's New York open, cancel the trade and sit out the day.
rules.quote: if we go lower than the low formed on Wednesdays New York open you have to nix the trade and go to the sidelines on the day

rules.rule: Order-flow check: in a bullish move down-close candles must hold as support. In a bearish move up-close candles must not be breached. A violation means the flow has changed.
rules.quote: if the move has been bullish down closed candles should not be violated down closed candles should not be violated they're going to act as support bearish market moves up close candles should not be breached and broken through

rules.rule: Mid-range of a consolidation is 50/50. Do not look for continuation setups there.
rules.quote: when price is trading near the middle of an established consolidation range, the directional probability drops to 50/50; traders should not seek continuation setups in this zone

rules.rule: When the daily is consolidated around equilibrium the bias is hard to read. Demand more intraday information before acting.
rules.quote: we've Consolidated around equilibrium now when you have this condition it can make it very difficult to get a true reading on bias

rules.rule: Do not pre-commit to a specific daily bias before the market trades. He says this usually ends up wrong.
rules.quote: everyday bias is unrealistic if i go in looking for a specific predetermined daily bias before the market starts trading invariably i'm going to have it incorrect

rules.rule: In event-risk weeks (FOMC/NFP), do not force a daily bias. Know the execution plan instead.
rules.quote: you don't even need to know bias you just need to know how you're going to execute.

rules.rule: Not every week or day follows the macro bias. Retracement weeks exist, so the higher-timeframe bias is not a guarantee.
rules.quote: it's not that every week is gonna be bullish or bearish not every week will move in the macro directional bias however there will be some weeks that move violently in agreement with the macro monthly bias

rules.rule: The swing/PDH-PDL logic is claimed to be market-agnostic: stocks, futures, bonds and anything tradeable.
rules.quote: this works in stocks it works in futures it works in bonds it works in just about anything they can trade

rules.rule: Read the DXY daily as the benchmark, then mirror it onto foreign currencies. EURUSD aims at the previous day's low when the dollar aims at the previous day's high.
rules.quote: what does that translate for foreign currency in terms of daily bias it's gonna be a mirror image so if we go to the euro dollar

rules.rule: Delivery is top-down: weekly, then daily, then 1h/15m/5m.
rules.quote: delivery top down that means from the weekly down into the daily chart down into the one-hour 15-minute five-minute chart

rules.rule: With a bullish daily, London usually prints the low of the day. With a bearish daily it prints the high of the day.
rules.quote: the London session typically creates the low of the day when the market is primarily bullish and the high of the day when bearish

rules.rule: Counter-trend afternoon model: from 1:30 PM NY, if the day is expected higher, expect a retracement into discount first.
rules.quote: in the afternoon session starting at 1:30 PM, the algorithm seeks liquidity; if the day is expected to expand higher, it will seek discount pricing first via a retracement

rules.rule: The day's reference open is midnight New York. Draw it forward on the 15m chart to about 11:00 NY.
rules.quote: The opening price is the most important: the opening price at midnight New York time. Draw that out in time on your 15-minute chart usually out to around 11 o'clock in the morning New York time.

rules.rule: Use the open-price rule on Monday to Wednesday only. Ignore the open on Thursday and Friday.
rules.quote: we're focusing primarily on buying below the opening price in bullish weeks on monday tuesday and wednesday bearish weeks we're looking to sell short on monday tuesday and wednesday above the opening price on thursdays and fridays we're not factoring that in

rules.rule: On an up-close day the London Close window (10:00 to noon NY) is typically when the day's high forms.
rules.quote: it's an up close day the London close is going to be typically when the high of the day is formed between 10 o'clock and noon

rules.rule: Weekly-bias timing: in a bullish week the weekly low forms before Wednesday's New York open, with best odds from Tuesday's London to Wednesday's NY open.
rules.quote: the weekly low to form before Wednesday's New York open or would be otherwise 7:00 a.m. New York time the odds further increase between Tuesday and Wednesday focusing on Tuesday's London to Wednesday's New York open

premium_discount.summary: Frame a dealing range (swing high to swing low that swept liquidity), split it at 50% equilibrium, only buy bullish PD arrays in discount and sell bearish PD arrays in premium after a sweep plus displacement, target equilibrium first (the opposite discount or premium array or liquidity pool next), and in a consolidation fade the false breakout back to the midpoint instead of holding for the far end.
premium_discount.needs_clock: Mostly no. The core is price geometry (swing-defined or rolling-lookback dealing range, 50% line, premium or discount location of an FVG or order block, sweep plus displacement plus structure shift, equilibrium or opposite-array target, pyramiding side-of-equilibrium rule) and can run on 24/7 synthetic indices using price delivery alone, with 20/40/60-bar lookbacks standing in for his 20/40/60-day IPDA ranges. Clock-bound variants that need replacing or dropping on synthetics: premium/discount versus the 8:30 NY open or midnight open (iZLXnNiZm_s, Sqw2bww93Zo), the 3:00-4:00 PM consolidation-day false-breakout window (hzoMJQlEv5M), the Model 13 windows 7-10 AM forex and 8:30-11 AM index (kNlySn81dmo), the Asian-range day-trade filter (5Z_3NbclMSY), and the 2026 first-hour (9:30-10:30), first-30-minute and 7:00-8:30 news-day dealing ranges (6DuByzKLDsc, C7CwjBOtHwM, hIusATccCcM). On synthetics substitute rolling windows (or the daily bar open) for those session anchors.
premium_discount.how_to_code: 1) Dealing range (price only): confirm swing highs and lows with an N-bar fractal (N=3 to 5). Range = [L,H] where H is the latest confirmed swing high that swept a prior swing high or equal highs (buy-side liquidity) and L is the latest confirmed swing low that swept a prior swing low or equal lows (sell-side liquidity), per his 2020 definition. Fallback or alternative: rolling highest high and lowest low over a 20, 40 or 60 bar lookback on a higher timeframe (his IPDA data range). EQ = (H+L)/2. Premium = price above EQ, discount = below. Optional gradient levels: quadrants at L+0.25R and L+0.75R, octants at multiples of 0.125, OTE band 0.62 to 0.79 retrace from the swing extreme. 2) Range life: recompute on every new confirmed swing; treat a candle-body close beyond H or L as the end of the range (this comes from the dossier summary of s-iqN0h2Fgg, not a quote) and treat a trade through EQ against bias and back as a reset (w2zTfhjScDg, 2026). 3) PD arrays: FVG (bullish if candle3.low > candle1.high, bearish mirror; CE = gap midpoint), order block (last opposite-colour candle before a displacement leg that breaks structure; mean threshold = body midpoint), breaker (failed order block after structure break), mitigation block, rejection block (swing-extreme candle body or wick), liquidity void (run of one-sided candles or stacked gaps). Tag each array premium or discount by its midpoint versus EQ; for the 2022 FVG filter, compare against the 50% of the displacement leg's own high-low (QkokVv0owSE). 4) Directional entry (2022 model): require HTF bias (subjective, see below); sweep of a range extreme or equal highs/lows; displacement (body above k x ATR) with a market structure shift (close beyond the last opposing swing); an FVG on that leg located in premium for shorts or discount for longs; place a limit order at the FVG edge or just inside; stop 1 to 2 ticks beyond the FVG's candle-1 extreme (2022) or exactly at it (Model 13), or beyond the sweep extreme; TP1 = EQ of the range, with 60 to 80% off for day trades; runner to the opposing liquidity pool or the nearest opposing-half array (discount array at or under EQ for shorts); optionally a gradient version where the target is the next quadrant level. 5) Consolidation fade (g7jchu4g31c, hzoMJQlEv5M, RgpxhuVp5Xg): detect a consolidation as M bars whose range stays under k x ATR or a stack of inside bars between boundary swings Lc and Hc; EQc = (Lc+Hc)/2. Wait for a false break of Hc or Lc that sweeps equal highs/lows and closes back inside, in the direction opposite the break but only if HTF bias agrees for the long side; then require a lower-timeframe swing break with an FVG and enter on the retrace into the FVG; stop beyond the sweep extreme; target EQc only (do not hold for the far boundary); no new entries while price is within a small band around EQc (his 'no man's land' 50/50 zone; the band width, for example plus or minus 10% of range, is my number, not his). 6) Management: allow adds only while price is still on the entry side of EQ (shorts: price above EQ; longs: at or below EQ); partial at EQ; optionally an Event Horizon exit at the midpoint between the current pool and the next liquidity pool (25% of remainder). 7) Invalidation: short FVG on the wrong side of 50%; bearish bias but sell-side liquidity taken first; break of the array's CE plus candle low; a rally that fails to reach the CE of a rejection block means weakness. Subjective parts: which swing counts as the dealing range (he admits most cannot pick it), higher-timeframe bias, what counts as displacement or a structure shift, which array to prefer when several overlap (matrix ordering is inconsistent between lessons), grading with octants and quadrants, and whether the day is a consolidation day.
premium_discount.changes_over_time: EVOLUTION. 2017-2019: equilibrium as a magnet and symmetry anchor on the total highest-high to lowest-low range (_hVCTzVH8iw 2018), a short taken right at an Asian-range equilibrium (M27EOgtHhis 2017), and a silent 2019 intraday video (lcsDZW_hxwc, no spoken rules; its 'buy in discount, take profit at the opposing extreme' text is dossier description only). 2020: the Interbank Dealing Range is the swing that swept buy-side and sell-side liquidity, with the 50% Fibonacci as the premium line (_9QfSbpZTZA); purge-and-revert shorts. 2022 Mentorship (Jan-Jun): practical rules (FVG must be above 50% of the displacement leg, discount FVG longs, targets at EQ or in discount, consolidation-day fade to the midpoint). 2022 Core Content (Aug-Oct): Month 1 definitions, Month 5-7 PD array matrix hierarchy, weekly/monthly nesting and 20/40/60-day lookbacks, Month 9 consolidation rule (work one side, take only the move back to EQ). 2023-2024: stops behind three PD arrays (PejS-nZTQlE), pyramiding allowed only on the correct side of EQ (oheyS8MUqno, YIxurbDNrWM, SObhjCvXCNk, joqM_Z96vtM), consequent encroachment versus equilibrium vocabulary (ZkLc4-adodg). 2025-2026: PD array matrix 'skeleton' with halves, mean threshold and consequent encroachment (043OW8trIJE), quadrants, octants and gradient levels on wicks and gaps, 'unrealized dealing range', and Event Horizon (midpoint of two liquidity pools, 25% partial). The unit of premium/discount shrinks from the whole swing to a single FVG, wick or order block. CONFLICTS. (a) Target: take only the move to EQ and do not hold for the opposite end (g7jchu4g31c, hzoMJQlEv5M closing 4 of 6 contracts at the midpoint, Q6GFu8-Z4rY) versus price being delivered from one end of the dealing range to the other (s-iqN0h2Fgg), the 2019 description of exiting at the range extreme, the 2020 terminal target at the opposite swing, and his 06 Sep 2022 remark that you need not trade to the draw on liquidity. (b) Stop: 1 to 2 ticks beyond the FVG candle (CnTXwAuDi9Y 2022) versus 'not one tick above it' (kNlySn81dmo 2024) versus behind three PD arrays (2023) versus 1 to 2 ticks above the imbalance midpoint (L6DHi1iXRW0 2025). (c) Strictness: 'only buys at a discount and only sells at a premium' (s-iqN0h2Fgg) versus 'best buys come at equilibrium and below' (qC0LogyIk2I); also exceptions for trending days (shallow pullbacks, PBzd2u4AgbE), trapped-sentiment days (xGn4UxJiz9M) and 'premium relative to the short-term dealing range' (8z6My18WZqA), so a nested smaller range can label the same price differently. (d) Matrix order: pwO-E-OOH5k and Y1oxwc354oo list mitigation block first and old high last; soY9zX3gt2U lists old high first and mitigation block last; s-iqN0h2Fgg gives a different cascade (old swing highs, rejection block, order block, FVG/void, breaker). The premium list ends with 'Old High / Historic Low' and the discount list with 'Old Low / Historic High'. (e) Dealing range definition: total high-low (2018), swing that swept both sides (2020), point of origin to intermediate-term high (g--tikwaupk 00:17:02), 20/40/60-day lookback (2022, 2024), unrealized range from a first high and an old daily high (2026); 6DuByzKLDsc (Mar 2026) says the opening range is 30 minutes and the first-hour dealing range is 60 minutes, while C7CwjBOtHwM (Aug 2026) says the first 30 minutes is the dealing range and the opening range. (f) Equilibrium versus consequent encroachment: ZkLc4-adodg says a gap midpoint is not equilibrium; 043OW8trIJE (Oct 2025) says 'Equilibrium or halfway mean threshold'. RELIABILITY. The 'Algorithmic Rules' sections of s-iqN0h2Fgg, YuefjnUKQdM, qC0LogyIk2I and SiVmoeyOWZE (never buy in premium, range invalid on a body close beyond 100% or 0%, 62/70.5/79 deep discount) are dossier summaries, not quotes; only their quoted lines are cited here.
