rules.rule: Split the dealing range at 50%. The 50% line is equilibrium, above it is premium (sell zone), below it is discount (buy zone). Buy in discount, sell in premium.
rules.quote: The 50 percent level is equilibrium. Above 50 percent is premium; below 50 percent is discount. Smart money only buys at a discount and only sells at a premium.

rules.rule: Match the PD array to the half of the range: in discount look for bullish PD arrays, in premium look for bearish PD arrays.
rules.quote: In a discount market we would be looking for a bullish PD array. When price is in a premium market we look for a bearish PD array.

rules.rule: Same definition in the 2022 Mentorship wording: above the equilibrium level is premium, below it is discount.
rules.quote: where equilibrium is anything above that level would be considered premium anything below it discount

rules.rule: Equilibrium is the midpoint of the range. Anything below it is a discount market.
rules.quote: What is equilibrium? Equilibrium is the midway point of a price range. When the market goes below equilibrium, anything below equilibrium is now a discount market.

rules.rule: Longs are best at or below equilibrium, and only when the higher-timeframe basis is bullish. Discount plus bullish HTF equals high probability.
rules.quote: The best buys come at equilibrium and below it. Anything below equilibrium or the 50 level is viewed as a discount. When a market is at discount and its higher timeframe basis is bullish, discount prices are high-probability buying opportunities.

rules.rule: Shorts are best taken from premium. Price going from equilibrium into premium is what gives the highest-probability short.
rules.quote: When we are above equilibrium, we are at a premium. The reason why we look for price to go from equilibrium to premium is because that offers the highest probability for getting short.

rules.rule: Price cycles discount to fair value to premium and back. Locate fair value (equilibrium) first, then you know which side to be on.
rules.quote: The market moves back and forth: from discount to fair value, to premium, back to fair value, back to discount. Once you know where fair valuation is, you know exactly what side of the market to be on.

rules.rule: Array memory: if discount arrays recently gave support, expect the premium arrays above price to be the next draw.
rules.quote: If discount arrays have provided support for price, probabilities increase that the premium arrays will be sought after above the market price.

rules.rule: Mirror of the above: if premium arrays recently gave resistance, expect the discount arrays below price to be the next draw.
rules.quote: If premium arrays have provided resistance for price, probabilities increase the discount arrays will be sought below the market price.

rules.rule: Inside a consolidation work one side only, the side of the daily or 4-hour order flow. If that flow is bullish, buy any short-term low that is violated below the equilibrium.
rules.quote: Inside of the range or the consolidation, when the daily or 4-hour order flow is bullish... any short-term low that's violated below the equilibrium, we're going to look to go long on that.

rules.rule: 2018: anchor the range to the total range, the highest high and the lowest low, not a truncated swing.
rules.quote: I'm teaching you something entirely different and amplifying why it's important to use the total range: the highest high and the lowest low.

rules.rule: 2019: a dealing range is simply two clearly defined price points (a major high and a major low).
rules.quote: A dealing range is anywhere between two price points that are very clearly defined.

rules.rule: 2020: the dealing range is the swing that has run buy-side liquidity above AND sell-side liquidity below (his next sentence: a swing that has done both is your dealing range). Equilibrium is the exact midpoint of that swing.
rules.quote: What that is is the Interbank Dealing Range high and low. What it specifically draws attention to is the most recent run on liquidity above the marketplace, which is buy side liquidity, and below the marketplace, which is sell side liquidity

rules.rule: How to measure for a long: anchor low to high on an impulsive expansion. Do not draw high to low on a bearish swing to locate a discount level.
rules.quote: do not draw the Fibonacci retracement from a high to a low on a bearish swing to locate a discount level; you must anchor from low to high on an impulsive expansion move

rules.rule: Range source: the algorithm looks back 20, 40, 60 days of institutional data (IPDA data ranges) and PD arrays are either on the chart or being reached for.
rules.quote: PD arrays: they're either in the chart or they're in the process of being reached for. The algorithm looks back 20, 40, 60 days of institutional data.

rules.rule: Premium PD array matrix, in the order the lesson lists it (the lesson overview reads it as nearest-to-farthest above price): mitigation block, bearish breaker, liquidity void, FVG, bearish order block, rejection block, old high.
rules.quote: Premium PD Array Matrix hierarchy: Mitigation Block, Bearish Breaker, Liquidity Void, Fair Value Gap, Bearish Order Block, Rejection Block, Old High / Historic Low.

rules.rule: Discount PD array matrix, same order: mitigation block, bullish breaker, liquidity void, FVG, bullish order block, rejection block, old low.
rules.quote: Discount PD Array Matrix hierarchy: Mitigation Block, Bullish Breaker, Liquidity Void, Fair Value Gap, Bullish Order Block, Rejection Block, Old Low / Historic High.

rules.rule: Use the matrix as a ranked scan: start at current price and go outward, nearest unmitigated array first.
rules.quote: The algorithm scans outward from current market price through these arrays in strict sequential order.

rules.rule: 2025: the PD array matrix is a structural skeleton, a sequence of arrays price moves between, not a set of random levels.
rules.quote: This structure. This is the skeleton behind the PD Array matrix.

rules.rule: 2025: equilibrium is the halfway mean threshold of a PD array. Price should reach the consequent encroachment (50%) or up to the high of the array.
rules.quote: Equilibrium or halfway mean threshold. You want to see consequent encroachment or up to the high of the PD array.

rules.rule: 2024: terminology split. The 50% of a gap is consequent encroachment, not equilibrium. Equilibrium is the midpoint of a range that has been delivered up and down.
rules.quote: Here is your consequent encroachment that's the midpoint okay that's not equilibrium... why is it consequent encroachment and not equilibrium? Because equilibrium is a range that has been delivered up and down

rules.rule: 2026: not any range will do. The dealing range must be framed with the correct high and low.
rules.quote: dealing range, okay? Any old range is is not what we're looking for... you have to frame the high and low correctly

rules.rule: 2026: an unrealized dealing range can be projected from a first high and an old daily high, before price reaches the far end.
rules.quote: this is an unrealized dealing range. But we can calculate that with the first high here and an old daily high could draw too. It doesn't matter if it gets up there.

rules.rule: 2026: he says nobody else grades an unrealized dealing range and most cannot pick the right one, i.e. range selection is discretionary.
rules.quote: You don't see anybody grading an unrealized dealing range. They don't even know how to pick the right one.

rules.rule: 2026: grade the swing with octant and quadrant levels. A PD array that forms at a gradient level is perceived as high probability and validated.
rules.quote: If we put our octants and quadrant levels on there, just grading that price swing, that's how we determine where PD arrays should form and should they form at that gradient level or looked at level.

rules.rule: Short trigger in premium: a stop run (sweep) above an old high while price is above equilibrium (his example is the 98.00 big figure on USDJPY).
rules.quote: We went short here based on a stop run above an old high, right at the 98 big figure level, because we are at a premium above equilibrium. That is institutional edge.

rules.rule: Long trigger in discount: price goes below equilibrium, sweeps sell stops, then trades higher. Needs bullish higher-timeframe order flow.
rules.quote: Markets will not sustain discount prices when higher timeframe order flow is bullish. It goes below equilibrium to a discount level, sweeps sell stops, and then aggressively trades higher.

rules.rule: Do not enter just because price reached a level. Wait for displacement and a market structure shift as the algorithm's confirmation.
rules.quote: wait for the algorithm to communicate a shift through displacement and Market Structure Shift

rules.rule: Consolidation trigger: fade the breakout of the range high (or low) by doing what smart money does, selling the breakout above a previous high.
rules.quote: Smart money is going to be selling that breakout... we're looking for the consolidation breakout above a previous high and when that happens we're doing the same thing by mimicking smart money.

rules.rule: Consolidation-day short: buy stops swept above relative equal highs, then a 1-minute swing-low break that leaves an FVG, then sell on the retrace into that FVG.
rules.quote: when price sweeps buy stops above relative equal highs between 3:00 PM and 4:00 PM on a consolidation day, wait for a 1-minute swing low breakdown with a Fair Value Gap, then enter short when price trades back up into that FVG

rules.rule: Long entry: retrace into a 15-minute FVG that sits in discount (below 50% equilibrium) of the current dealing range.
rules.quote: enter long when price retraces into a 15-minute Fair Value Gap that is located within a Discount (below 50% equilibrium) of the current Dealing Range

rules.rule: Short entry filter: after a bearish displacement leg, the resulting FVG must sit above the 50% level of that leg's high-to-low range (a premium FVG).
rules.quote: for a bearish displacement leg to qualify for a short entry setup, the resulting Fair Value Gap must be located above the 50% equilibrium level of that displacement leg's high-to-low range

rules.rule: Do not sell in a discount. Sell only at the half or higher, because the half or higher is premium.
rules.quote: equilibrium we need to get to a premium we don't want to sell in a discount... a half or higher that's a premium

rules.rule: Swing version of a long: buy daily (and 4-hour) bullish discount arrays, listed as mitigation block, breaker, void, FVG, order block, rejection block, old low or high.
rules.quote: You're going to buy all daily bullish discount arrays: that is a bullish mitigation block, bullish breaker, liquidity void, fair value gap, bullish order block, rejection block, and or an old low or high.

rules.rule: Nesting rule: when the daily is in a correction, sell daily bearish premium arrays only at or nested inside weekly premium arrays.
rules.quote: When the monthly is bearish, the weekly is bearish, and the daily is bullish, that means there's a correction underway on the daily chart. You're going to sell daily bearish premium arrays at or nested in weekly premium arrays.

rules.rule: Day-trade version: buy under the Asian range low (plus 5 pips for spread) at 1-2 standard deviations, coupled with a discount PD array.
rules.quote: I like buying under the Asian Range plus 5 pips for the spread... look for one or two standard deviations in the Asian Range coupled with a discount PD array.

rules.rule: 2022 stop for an aggressive short: 1 to 2 ticks above the high of the candle that formed the top of the FVG.
rules.quote: for an aggressive short stop loss, place the stop 1 to 2 ticks above the high of the candle that formed the top of the Fair Value Gap

rules.rule: Long stop: just below the swing low that was formed when the sell-side liquidity was taken.
rules.quote: place the protective Stop Loss just below the Swing Low that was formed when taking out the sell-side liquidity

rules.rule: Consolidation-day short stop: above the newly formed swing high that swept the liquidity.
rules.quote: stop loss placed above the newly formed swing high that swept the liquidity

rules.rule: 2024 Model 13 stop: exactly at the high of the FVG's candle, with no padding. Conflicts with the 1-2 tick buffer taught in 2022.
rules.quote: stop loss is placed at the high of the candle that forms the high of the Fair Value Gap used for the setup... that's the stop loss okay not one tick above it not a full handle above it

rules.rule: 2025 midpoint-based stop: for a bearish setup the stop sits one or two ticks above the midpoint of the 1-minute imbalance.
rules.quote: If I'm bearish, I want to see it stay below the midpoint of that one minute imbalance or sell side efficiency... stop loss would be anywhere in here or one tick or two above the midpoint.

rules.rule: Take the equilibrium of the range. A short is wanted in premium and its targets are down in discount.
rules.quote: get your equilibrium price point... everything above that 50 level is premium everything below is discount so if we're looking for a short setup we want to see it in premium and we want to see our targets down in discount

rules.rule: First objective is 50% of the range, equilibrium (EURUSD London trade, 2022).
rules.quote: first objective would be 50 percent of the range... equilibrium

rules.rule: From premium or discount price first looks to rebalance to the equilibrium of the last recent range. Equilibrium is the default first target.
rules.quote: When markets are at a premium or at a discount, they're always going to initially look to rebalance, that means the equilibrium price point between the last recent range.

rules.rule: Buying a real deep discount and merely getting back to equilibrium produces many trades; do not exit before equilibrium.
rules.quote: If you buy at a real deep discount and just get back to equilibrium, you'll find a lot of trades like that.

rules.rule: On consolidation days the target is the 50% midpoint of the daily range, which price gravitates back to.
rules.quote: in the middle there's your midpoint and it's going to want to gravitate back to the 50 percent midpoint of the daily range

rules.rule: Consolidation rule: take the move back to equilibrium and do not hold for the opposite end of the range.
rules.quote: We're looking for price to return back to equilibrium. We do not anticipate or always hold for the opposite end of the consolidation

rules.rule: Market Efficiency Paradigm: when short, the target must lie below equilibrium (in discount).
rules.quote: When we're going short, the Market Efficiency Paradigm is suggesting that you as the trader and my student were looking for something below equilibrium to target, because that's what the algorithm is going to do.

rules.rule: Identify the discount target before selling from a premium PD array.
rules.quote: Keying off all potential sell scenarios when we sell short from a premium PD array requires identifying the discount target beforehand.

rules.rule: Model 13 profit-taking hierarchy: opposing PD arrays, specifically the discount PD array at or nearest under equilibrium of the dealing range, then under previous session low, then under previous day low.
rules.quote: Profit Taking Logic: We are looking to take profits at opposing PD Arrays... Any Discount PD Array at or the closest under Equilibrium of the dealing range. Under Previous Session Lows. Under Previous Day Low.

rules.rule: 2025 gradient version: after a reaction at consequent encroachment the next target is the lower quadrant level.
rules.quote: So if it's going to be bearish and it's reacting off the consequent encroachment level, where could it trade down to? The next level, which is the lower quadrant level.

rules.rule: Scale-out rule: take 60-80% off at the equilibrium of the 60-minute range you are trading inside.
rules.quote: At the equilibrium of the price range you are trading inside of on a 60-minute chart, take or have taken 60 to 80 percent off... you have to take profits on these rules.

rules.rule: Take partial profits once price moves into premium, above the 50% halfway point of the retracement swing.
rules.quote: take partial profits when price moves into premium above the 50% halfway point of the retracement swing

rules.rule: Pyramid shorts only while price stays above equilibrium. Once price is below the midpoint, stop adding.
rules.quote: you can add to your position as long as you are above equilibrium; once price drops below the midpoint of the range you cannot pyramid anymore

rules.rule: Mirror for longs: add only at or below equilibrium. In premium do not add.
rules.quote: This order block returned back to equilibrium... because we're now in a premium we don't want to add anything... you only want to be adding to long positions when price is at or below equilibrium.

rules.rule: 2026 variant: Event Horizon is the midpoint between two liquidity pools; bank about 25% of the remainder there and let the runner go.
rules.quote: Take about 25% of the remaining portion off when you're at event horizon... and then I would let the runner reach for the rest.

rules.rule: A short setup is invalid if its FVG is below 50% of the displacement leg.
rules.quote: if the FVG is below 50%, the short setup is invalidated

rules.rule: Skip selling daily premium arrays when the daily just made a lower low and rejected, which makes a bullish breaker.
rules.quote: You're going to avoid selling daily premium arrays if the daily has just posted a lower low and rejected — this is going to be seen as a bullish breaker.

rules.rule: Array failure: a break below consequent encroachment and below the individual candle low signals weakness.
rules.quote: Below consequent encroachment and goes below this individual candlestick low... that tells you weakness.

rules.rule: No-trade zone: in the middle of an established consolidation range direction is 50/50, so do not seek continuation setups there.
rules.quote: when price is trading near the middle of an established consolidation range, the directional probability drops to 50/50; traders should not seek continuation setups in this zone

rules.rule: 2025: price in the middle of the range is no-man's land, 50/50, be very careful.
rules.quote: We're basically in no man's land. So now it becomes a 50/50 higher or lower. So you have to be very very careful when you're trading forex now because we're right back in the middle of the range and it could literally go either direction

rules.rule: Bias filter: in a bearish bias price must run buy-side liquidity first. If it takes the previous day's low first and then rallies, the short setup is cancelled.
rules.quote: if price takes out the previous day's low or sell-side liquidity first and then rallies, the price action is not bearish and cancels a short setup

rules.rule: Down-close candles in premium (above equilibrium of the dealing range) are not valid bullish order blocks. Validity of a PD array depends on its half of the range.
rules.quote: You do not look at these down close candles as an order block... they are not a bullish order block ICT why? It's relative to the dealing range

rules.rule: A rally that cannot reach the halfway point (consequent encroachment) of a rejection block shows extreme weakness and price goes the other direction.
rules.quote: Can't even get to halfway point. If you can't even meet me halfway, why bother, bro? It's exceedingly weak. It's going to go the other direction.

rules.rule: 2026: the range resets. When bearish, if price trades below the midpoint and then back to equilibrium, that retrace is a reset and the range must be re-drawn.
rules.quote: How's that a premium? Because the range resets... when we're bearish, if price goes below the midpoint, which is equilibrium, if we trade back to equilibrium, that's a reset.

rules.rule: 2025 half rule on an inversion FVG: price should hold one half of the rectangle; wicks into the other half are tolerated but a body there breaks it (the transcript wording is garbled).
rules.quote: You want to stay in the lower half of that rectangle. It can wick in the upper half, but it cannot leave a body outside of the upper half of it to the upside in other words.

rules.rule: Caveat: on a trending day pullbacks are shallow, so waiting for a deep discount retrace gets you left behind. Enter FVGs that form in flight.
rules.quote: On a trending day, the pullbacks are not deep. If you sit there waiting for a deep discount retracement, the market is just going to leave you behind. You enter on the Fair Value Gaps that form in flight.

rules.rule: Caveat: when retail sentiment is already trapped on one side, price may not retrace to discount or premium first.
rules.quote: no need for it to drop down because the sentiment has been to the downside... retail was already trapped short

rules.rule: Read monthly, weekly, daily and 4-hour the same way through the PD array matrix. Best when all four align.
rules.quote: What you're doing is you're going to be looking at the monthly, the weekly, the daily, and the four hour the same way as I'm outlining here... this is the PD array Matrix.

rules.rule: Monthly and weekly arrays set the macro draws that pull daily and intraday delivery.
rules.quote: On higher timeframe charts, monthly and weekly arrays dictate the macro draws that pull daily and intraday order flow.

rules.rule: Frame the trade on a lower timeframe PD array that sits inside the higher timeframe PD array.
rules.quote: Lower timeframe PD array is going to be used on a timeframe lesser than the higher timeframe PD array to frame the actual trade execution.

rules.rule: Day-level premium and discount can also be taken from the 8:30 NY open: below the opening price is discount, above it is premium.
rules.quote: 8 30 open in New York local time that's the beginning of the trading day for equities... anything below that opening price is discount anything above that is premium

rules.rule: On consolidation days wait for the 3:00 to 4:00 PM NY window for the false breakout outside the daily range, then fade back to the midpoint.
rules.quote: on consolidation days, wait until the 3:00 PM to 4:00 PM window for the algorithm to engineer a false breakout outside the daily range to seek liquidity before returning to the midpoint

rules.rule: Model 13 windows: 7:00-10:00 EST for forex and 8:30-11:00 EST for index futures, watching 5-minute down to 1-minute after a liquidity raid.
rules.quote: We use Time Of Day - 7am to 10am EST for Forex and 8:30am to 11am EST for Index Futures. Monitoring 5 down to 1 minute charts after a Liquidity Raid occurs

rules.rule: March 2026: the opening range is the first 30 minutes; the first hour 9:30 to 10:30 is the first hour's dealing range.
rules.quote: The first 30 minutes is opening range... we're going to go back to 10:30, which is your first hour's dealing range.

rules.rule: April 2026: the 9:30 to 10:30 first hour's dealing range can be traded inside without going beyond it.
rules.quote: Between 9:30 and 10:30, that first hour's dealing range. That's an entire universe. You can do so much with that. You can trade inside of it and never trade beyond it.

rules.rule: August 2026: he calls the 9:30-10:00 first 30 minutes both the dealing range and the opening range, at odds with the March 2026 definition.
rules.quote: The first 30 minutes is just like a dealing range concept, like 9:30 to 10:00 Eastern time in the morning. That's the opening range for regular trading hours. That that's our first 30 minutes. That's the dealing range. That is the opening range.

rules.rule: 2026 news-day range: the highest high and lowest low from 7:00 AM to the 8:30 release defines the pre-release dealing range.
rules.quote: highest high and lowest low of the range prior to 8:30 release. So, 7:00 in the morning starts the time. Go through up to the point of 8:30, which is here.

draw_on_liquidity.summary: ICT's draw on liquidity is the next pool of resting stops (old, equal or smooth highs/lows, range extremes, open float, ATH) or unrebalanced inefficiency (FVG, daily volume imbalance, opening gap) that price is being pulled to. Bias and targets come from it. Trade only when the path to it is a low-resistance run, enter after the opposite pool is swept and displacement appears, target the pool (often just ahead of it), and stand aside when no draw is known or it has been fulfilled.
draw_on_liquidity.needs_clock: The core concept needs no clock. Pools and inefficiencies are defined by price geometry alone: swing highs/lows, equal levels, FVG/volume imbalance, N-bar range extremes, and the running ATH. He says price is fractal and not tied to a real time element (YcAfcpUCbDw 08:47), and the HTF/LTF hierarchy can be rebuilt by aggregating bars. The 20/40/60-bar IPDA windows, the 3-month open float (about 60 daily bars) and the 20-day Charter lookback port fine as bar counts. A 'daily' bar needs only an arbitrary day boundary on a 24/7 feed (e.g. 00:00 UTC). Clock-dependent parts do not port and should be dropped or replaced: London 2-5am and NY 7-10am killzones, the 8:30-11:00 NY window, 3pm spool, 3:15-3:45 macros, lunch macro 11:30-13:30, Friday time limits, the 9:30 opening range gap, NDOG/NWOG, CME 4:14/4:15 settlement, and the IPDA true day (midnight to 3pm NY). Caveat: his stated mechanism is real resting stop orders, fund stops and open interest. Synthetic indices have no such orders, so whether pools attract price there is an empirical question. Implement it as a price-only pattern and test out-of-sample.
draw_on_liquidity.how_to_code:
MECHANICAL PARTS:
1) Swing points: use a 3-candle fractal, and run it on several aggregated timeframes. In 2017 he defined a swing high as a high with two lower highs on either side.
2) Pool registry: each unpurged swing high is BSL at its high and each unpurged swing low is SSL at its low. Add prior-day and prior-week high/low, and the range extremes of the last 20/40/60 daily bars. Add the ~60-bar open-float high/low, and the all-history maximum as the ATH pool. A pool is taken when any bar trades beyond it. Treat a wick through as the sweep, and a body close beyond as a breakout (his CE/body-respect logic).
3) Relative equal highs/lows: two or more swing points whose levels differ by less than a tolerance. 'Smooth' means no bar between them pokes above the level. He gives no numeric tolerance, so use k x ATR or a fraction of the leg and tune it.
4) Inefficiency pools: an FVG is candle1 high < candle3 low (mirror for bearish). A volume imbalance is a gap between consecutive bodies with overlapping wicks. A void is a run of FVGs. The daily volume imbalance is the same detection on D1. Store low, high and CE (50%). It stays open until price trades into it, and he wants bodies to respect CE while wicks may pass.
5) LRLR / HRLR score: count unmitigated opposing arrays (order blocks, breakers, FVGs against the direction, recent swing points) between price and the target pool. 0-1 means low resistance and 3 or more means high resistance. Confirm with behaviour: displacement candles with bodies of roughly 1-1.5 x ATR, FVGs left open, few bars inside one gap, and shallow pullbacks.
6) State machine: IDLE, then DRAW_SET (pool plus direction), then optionally SWEEP of the opposite pool, then DISPLACEMENT (an impulse leaving an FVG and breaking a short-term swing in the draw direction). Then ENTRY, a limit at the FVG edge/CE or the order block, only after displacement. Then MANAGE, then DRAW_FULFILLED when price trades through the pool or within a few ticks of it.
 - Stop: beyond the swing that swept the pool, or 1-2 ticks beyond candle 1 of the entry FVG.
 - Target: the pool level, or a few ticks inside it (he front-runs it). Take partials at a nearer pool or the midpoint between the pool and the old high/low, which the 2026 dossiers call 'event horizon'. Trail the stop to breakeven/CE after displacement.
 - Cancel if: no displacement; the opposite pool is taken first against the bias; the regime is HRLR; or the draw is already fulfilled.
7) ATH mode: if price is at the running maximum, the pool is the ATH plus any relative equal highs. Direction is continuation. Targets are 25% of the prior range beyond the break (2024) or standard-deviation extensions (2026). Take shorts only after displacement/MSS (April 2026 shows ATH-sweep Turtle Soup shorts).
8) Bias options, all codeable but a subset of what he says: the 2017 daily swing sequence (swing high broken, higher swing low forms, day-4 trades through candle 3 high, so day 5 targets the previous day's high), the position of price in the 20/40/60-bar range (premium/discount), and the weekly candle direction.
SUBJECTIVE PARTS (unspecified numerically): what counts as 'obvious' or 'clean'; the equal-level tolerance; which timeframe's pool is the dominant draw when several compete; how much resistance makes it HRLR; displacement quality ('willingness to escape'); wick versus body; 'narrative'; and how far in front of the pool to exit. The only hard numbers are the 10-20 pip (up to 30) sweep depth on forex intraday, which must be volatility/timeframe-scaled elsewhere; the 20/40/60-day and 3-month windows; and the ATH 25% projection.
draw_on_liquidity.changes_over_time:
1) Source vocabulary: 2017-2018 teaching is forex-based. The draw is the previous day's high or low, picked from the daily swing sequence (5-candle rule). The sweep goes 10-20 pips, up to 30, beyond it, and a 3-day or 5-7 day lookback sets the range. 'Equal highs' is called a double top that he likes to see targeted, and the YcAfcpUCbDw (2017-12) 'double-top sweep' adds the rolling 12-month, 3-month, 30-day and prior-week levels as pools. The LRLR/HRLR labels appear in 2018-2019 dossiers (_hVCTzVH8iw, ZiNpaXftqPE, 54yWnOON0zQ), but their 'verbatim' lines are thin or paraphrased.
2) Upload date is not teaching date: the 'Core Content' months (22XkhpJR5eA, npL3ZXJ5zOU, Gnw54f9v6SA, vqtA1S9JH34, y0lVKWLsZeM, O69iFqP1j7o) were uploaded Aug-Oct 2022, and in 2026 he says the swing-trader material is from his 2016-2017 core content (KEqzv2yOAf0 04:23). Several of these 2022 dossiers read as templated, with generic paraphrased 'verbatim' lines. I used them only for definitions that are corroborated elsewhere.
3) Lookback windows are inconsistent: 3 days (2017), 5-7 days, 3 months or about 60 days (open float, 2022), 20/40/60 days (IPDA, 2022), 20-40 days (Jan 2023), a single 20-day dealing range (Charter Model 11, 2024). Code several windows and let the data choose.
4) 20-day highs: in 2022 (vqtA1S9JH34 00:07:40) 20-day highs/lows are resting fund liquidity that algorithms harvest. In 2025 (5N4QHrY6DRc 11:37) he says his Turtle Soup does not use a 20-day high and is a 1-minute stop-hunt that needs a narrative. Yet Charter Model 11 (2024) is built on a 20-day range.
5) Equal highs/lows play two roles: a target the run is drawn to (LRLR) and the level where a sweep reverses (Turtle Soup). He resolves it as: the pool is the draw, and once it is taken the draw is fulfilled and price rebalances (O69iFqP1j7o 00:25:46, LMi_mO3AP08 51:20). He does not give a rule for telling a sweep-and-reverse from a run-and-continue in advance. Displacement and the HTF bias are the only discriminators.
6) Reach versus front-run versus exit early: 2017 'exit before my target', 2022 'don't insist on the draw', 2026 limit orders just ahead of the pool. In 2022 he also says the HTF draw is a magnet that price keeps working toward, and one Core Content line (mQA8jCem9d0 00:38:30) says it 'will relentlessly draw toward that level until reached'. Treating the draw as certain to be reached contradicts the 'need not reach it' lines.
7) Sweep depth: a fixed 10-20 pips (up to 30) in 2017 and in the 2022 re-upload, explicitly not valid for intraday charts or HTF levels (Sb9m_dxr4bI 12:06). 2024-2026 give no pip number. He talks about 'smooth versus jagged' levels and range expansion after the sweep instead.
8) HRLR handling changed: 2019 stand down or cut size (54yWnOON0zQ), 2022 Core Content avoid, Oct 2024 reduce risk or scale in partials and keep a runner (DzJpkxI057g, 9HUAUF_h2tI), 2026 smaller size and take the first partial (tp0qkiWCctw, O217xQsEUgI) rather than skipping. Layered NDOG/NWOG levels are named as a cause of HRLR (NMCy1H2_Wr8, 2024). The same Aug 2024 lecture (ZkLc4-adodg 56:29) says NDOG/NWOG are 'the larger draw' that is the more influential.
9) ATH: Dec 2024 gives a 25% projection and 'avoid picking a top'. Sep 2025 says do not short ATH and ignore TGIF retracements at ATH. April 2026 shows ATH-sweep Turtle Soup and MMSM shorts on MNQ after displacement (BOZTN4VzzeA, 6VaEdP4TYe8), and the 2026-04-11 weekend review still calls top-picking advanced. The 20260420/20260514 dossiers (r-ztz7kReYc, wprXVW1pW9Y) add standard-deviation projections, but only in their overviews, not in quotes.
10) Markets: forex-centric through 2022, index-futures-centric from 2023. By Oct 2025 he dismisses unliquid forex as high-resistance.
11) New draw types accrete over time: the daily volume imbalance and opening gaps (NDOG/NWOG/ORG) appear from 2023-2024, and 'event horizon' (midpoint between a pool and an old high/low) in 2026. None are in the 2017 or 2022 formulations.
12) Dossier quality: several quotes carry transcription noise (for example 'rated' for raided, and 'cell side' for sell side), kept verbatim. For KHxQjsITOLo, a silent video, the only 'Verbatim Quote' cells are on-screen annotations, so those parts are labelled as SHOWN, not STATED.
draw_on_liquidity.markets: The trade count is a parse of the dossiers' 'Trades taken or shown' tables, because he shows no standalone draw-on-liquidity trades. Of 559 parseable trade rows, 164 name a liquidity pool as the Target. These are equal highs/lows, a draw on liquidity, a liquidity pool, a daily volume imbalance or an ATH. If previous-day/old-high/low and any buy-side/sell-side targets count, the number is 342. Only 22 of 741 table rows use the words draw on liquidity, daily volume imbalance, ATH or LRLR in the row itself. By year, the 164 split 2017: 13, 2020: 3, 2021: 7, 2022: 11, 2023: 22, 2024: 20, 2025: 36, 2026: 52. By market, the 164 split NQ/MNQ 105, ES 21, GBPUSD 18, EURUSD 9, USDCAD 3, AUDUSD 2, DXY 2, CL 2, NZDUSD 1, USDCHF 1. The 342 broad set adds more EURUSD, GBPUSD, USDCAD and USDCHF; it is the only set that includes USDJPY and GBPCHF, and its 3 'FOREX PAIR' rows are unnamed. Daily-volume-imbalance targets appear in about 8 NQ trades from 2023 to 2026: KHxQjsITOLo, 7pW4-84U1RE, b4DOrfGau8w, 28M9ouiKmSY, mQsT-xux5Xk, AmTpyveQsbg, kzeFqGK9gCQ and ojy5ApHhEu4. Two trades are labeled LRLR (svYZKOrWPRo, 3YfetuXVhOE), plus one AAPL row (rcO8). About 5 trades run long into ATH, and 2 to 3 are ATH-sweep reversal shorts (Apr 2026). Besides index futures (NQ 2022-2026, ES 2022-2023), he uses it on forex majors and DXY (2017-2022: GBPUSD, EURUSD, USDCAD, AUDUSD, USDCHF, USDJPY monthly), crude oil CL, bonds ZB and BTC (2017/2020), and says it works on stocks. Dates such as 20230101 and 20250101 in filenames are placeholders. For example, pn1OgwxlK4U references the NQU2025 September contract.

rules.rule: 2023: if you cannot name the next draw on liquidity, stop trading for the session and keep what you made. Trading with no known draw is guessing.
rules.quote: So if I don't know where the next draw on liquidity is, how the hell do you think you're going to know it? That's the time when you stop pushing buttons and walk away with what you took from the market!

rules.rule: 2020 version of the same filter: only trade toward where liquidity (previous day high/low) will clearly be reached; if it is not clear, stay out.
rules.quote: you want to stick with where the liquidity is gonna be reaching relative to the previous day's high or low and if it's not really clear just simply stay out

rules.rule: 2024: set the higher-timeframe draw (15m, 1h or Daily) before looking for any 1-minute execution setup.
rules.quote: you must identify where the market wants to go before looking for any 1-minute execution setup.

rules.rule: 2017 definition: bullish bias means price is drawn up to the previous day's high or an old high, which are buy stops (buy-side liquidity). Bearish is the mirror, toward the previous day's low or an old low.
rules.quote: when we look for where the markets going to reach for in terms of bullishness it's the previous day's high or an old high that's gonna be in the form of buy-side liquidity or buy stops so the market will draw up to that level

rules.rule: 2020: the draw is a direction or magnet. Price does not have to travel all the way to the level for the idea to be right.
rules.quote: it's not important or even required that price trades from this level here all the way up to that level and higher it just needs to draw towards it that's the reason why I call a draw and liquidity

rules.rule: 2017 mechanical daily bias, bullish case: swing high broken, higher swing low forms, Day 4 trades through the candle-3 high, then Day 5 runs the previous day's high. Bearish is the mirror.
rules.quote: we're watching once the daily swing low forms we want to see the high be traded through one day number four okay once day number four does that we know that day number five we can be looking for a run on previous day's high liquidity

rules.rule: 2017: the previous day's high stays the daily draw each day until a new daily swing high forms or price reaches a key support/resistance level. 'Rated' is the dossier's spelling of 'raided'. The bearish mirror uses the previous day's low.
rules.quote: we're looking for previous day's highs to be rated each day until a swing high when a daily forms or price reaches a key support or resistance level

rules.rule: Core Content (re-uploaded 2022): start with the monthly and weekly charts to get the dominant draw, then work down.
rules.quote: Apply everything from a monthly and weekly perspective first. That gives you the dominant draw on liquidity that smart money is engineering.

rules.rule: 2022 IPDA lookback: each day, locate price against the highest high and lowest low of the last 20, 40 and 60 days to see which old high/low is the draw.
rules.quote: Every day you sit down at your daily charts: where are we at with respect to the lowest low and highest high in the last 20 days, the last 40 days, and the last 60 days?

rules.rule: 2024 Charter Model 11: take the 20-day dealing range, pick the next old high or old low in the direction of the weekly bias, and target external range liquidity.
rules.quote: Inside this Dealing Range we look for the next draw on liquidity. Where is Price likely to trade to next, below which Old Low, above which Old High? We look for a PD Array in the direction of the Weekly Range Bias. We target External Range Liquidity.

rules.rule: 2022 sequencing filter: a bearish bias must run buy-side liquidity (or an old high) first. If sell-side is taken first and price then rallies, it is not bearish.
rules.quote: in a bearish market bias, price must run buy-side liquidity or an old high/rebalance level first before running sell-side liquidity

rules.rule: 2026: continuation runs toward buy-side liquidity in a market that has already shown it is bullish are the easy, preferred draws. Counter-trend reversals are harder.
rules.quote: They're always easier when you're looking for continuation expansion runs to target buy side once it's already been proving it's bullish

rules.rule: Definition of the pools: buy stops (BSL) rest above old highs and sell stops (SSL) rest below old lows. Core Content re-upload, 2022.
rules.quote: What is liquidity? Liquidity refers to where orders are resting in the marketplace. There are high levels of liquidity resting above old highs in the form of buy stops, and liquidity below old lows in the form of sell stops.

rules.rule: External range liquidity (ERL) is the BSL above the current range high and the SSL below the range low. Runs on liquidity pair institutional orders with these pending orders.
rules.quote: External range liquidity: the current trading range will have buy-side liquidity above the range high, and sell-side liquidity below the range low. Runs on liquidity seek to pair orders with pending order liquidity.

rules.rule: 2023 binary draw: price is always being drawn to either liquidity above/below the market (pools) or an inefficiency (FVG/volume imbalance).
rules.quote: Because they don't know where the Market's likely to be drawn to whether it be liquidity above or below the marketplace or an inefficiency.

rules.rule: Clean equal or relatively equal highs are expected to be driven through and then rejected (Turtle Soup/double-top sweep). Lows are the mirror. Said 2017-12 on the daily chart.
rules.quote: double-top sweeps that means when we see price action creating very clean equal highs or relatively equal highs we're expecting that phenomenon to take place for a price would drive above those equal highs reject and trade lower

rules.rule: Tolerance for 'equal': a high only slightly below the prior high counts as equal highs. Retail reads it as a double top and puts buy stops just above. He gives no numeric tolerance.
rules.quote: today's intraday high is just slightly lower than yesterday's high and I always look at that as equal highs and retail traders or less informed traders will will view that as a double top and usually there's going to be buy stops resting just above that

rules.rule: Smooth (clean) highs/lows are the ones price seeks, though not necessarily the same day. Jagged areas are not clean pools.
rules.quote: Smooth edges, smooth lows: it will always always find a way to seek that liquidity, maybe not on the same trading day but it will always look for it.

rules.rule: Open float, as defined in the Month 05 re-upload: frame about 3 months (about 60 trading days) of daily data. Its highest high and lowest low mark the open-float liquidity.
rules.quote: Basically you're looking at three months of data, and by doing that, what it'll do is give you a range to look for the highest high and the lowest low on the daily chart.

rules.rule: Framing the open float is the stated easiest way to know where the liquidity is.
rules.quote: You have to have all these things in mind, looking for where the liquidity is, and the easiest way to do it is by framing the open float.

rules.rule: Open float is the pool of unresolved orders: sell stops (for new shorts and for exiting longs) below lows, and buy stops above highs.
rules.quote: There are open interest in the form of sell stops for entry orders and sell stops for collapsing long positions, and there are buy stops to get long.

rules.rule: LRLR definition, Core Content 2022: price moves rapidly and cleanly toward an obvious pool with no heavy opposing order blocks in the way.
rules.quote: A Low Resistance Liquidity Run is characterized by price moving rapidly and cleanly toward an obvious liquidity pool without heavy opposing order blocks.

rules.rule: 2024 LRLR definition: price is allowed to run freely to an obvious draw on liquidity. High-resistance runs are hard to trade.
rules.quote: what is a low resistance liquidity run? It's when price is allowed to freely run to an obvious draw on liquidity.

rules.rule: 2026 observable LRLR signature: price escapes quickly and leaves small inefficiencies behind. Many candles inside one inefficiency means it is not low resistance.
rules.quote: When you start seeing prices show a willingness to escape and really run and leave little inefficiencies, that right there, that's low resistance liquidity run.

rules.rule: Daily volume imbalance as the draw: a yellow band (19,932.75 to 19,945.75) drawn above price on NQ is the magnet for an intraday expansion. This is a SHOWN chart annotation from a silent video, not speech.
rules.quote: Chart Annotation: Yellow shaded band "19,932.75 to 19,945.75" representing the Daily Volume Imbalance

rules.rule: 2026: the daily volume imbalance is stated in advance as the place price should trade up into. He then aims for it.
rules.quote: This dipped down in here. This is that daily volume imbalance I said we would likely trade up into

rules.rule: All-time highs: a market at ATH tends to keep printing new ATHs, so the draw is continuation.
rules.quote: When a market is trading at All Time Highs, it is more likely that it will continue to post higher All Time Highs.

rules.rule: 2025: an ATH is a stop pool, because traders who short it have their stops above. This is why he avoids shorting it.
rules.quote: there's a lot of people that want to be short because they want to try to short all-time highs. And if they are up here, they're really ramping down and putting stop losses here

rules.rule: ATH as terminal buy-side benchmark, Feb 2024 (MNQ long into 18,121.50). The quote is the chart annotation (SHOWN), not speech.
rules.quote: Chart Annotation: "All Time High - 18121.50" marked in red horizontal line across the top of the chart.

rules.rule: Core Content 2022: let the stop run happen. Entry is better once price has traded 10-20 pips beyond the old low or high, not at the exact level.
rules.quote: It's better to wait for the market to trade under that low, and once it trades under there 10–20 pips, that's a really good ideal entry point.

rules.rule: 2017 forex rule of thumb: the sweep goes about 10-20 pips beyond the previous high or low.
rules.quote: I teach that price generally will reach about 10 to 20 pips above a previous high or low

rules.rule: 2017: the 10-30 pip sweep depth applies to the low-timeframe, pip-scaled case. Higher-timeframe levels need a larger overshoot expectation, so sweep depth must be scaled.
rules.quote: obviously we can't use a 10 to 20 or 30 pip sweep idea when we deal with intraday charts looking for movements beyond the old highs and lows

rules.rule: 2026 quality of the run: after taking the lows price must accelerate with range expansion, not just fish below the old lows.
rules.quote: You never want to see it just like fishing below the old lows. You want to see it try like accelerate with range expansion.

rules.rule: 2022 Mentorship: a sweep alone is not a trigger. Without displacement there is no trade.
rules.quote: if there is no displacement, there is no trade. Do not try to anticipate the turn without displacement

rules.rule: Charter Model 9, 2024: enter at an internal-range array (order block, FVG or void) and let it expand to external range liquidity. That path is the low resistance liquidity run.
rules.quote: Most of the time you're going to find that internal range liquidity entries will run to external range liquidity. That means you're going to see order blocks, fair value gaps, or voids be your entry and it'll expand outside of the present short-term dealing range to external range liquidity. And that is your low resistance liquidity run.

rules.rule: 2022 consolidation-day example: buy stops above relative equal highs are swept, a 1m swing low breaks with an FVG, and he shorts the retrace into that FVG.
rules.quote: when price sweeps buy stops above relative equal highs between 3:00 PM and 4:00 PM on a consolidation day, wait for a 1-minute swing low breakdown with a Fair Value Gap, then enter short when price trades back up into that FVG

rules.rule: 2023: after a stop hunt, take the FVG that lines up and be patient.
rules.quote: And then whenever you get a fair value Gap something that lines up after a stop hunt then go in and do what you're looking for that's not complicated but you have to have patience.

rules.rule: Short after a buy-stop sweep: stop above the new swing high that swept the liquidity.
rules.quote: stop loss placed above the newly formed swing high that swept the liquidity

rules.rule: 2022 aggressive stop for an FVG entry: 1-2 ticks beyond candle 1, the candle forming the far side of the gap.
rules.quote: for an aggressive short stop loss, place the stop 1 to 2 ticks above the high of the candle that formed the top of the Fair Value Gap

rules.rule: Stop sits just beyond the low/high that must hold. If price trades back through it, the idea is wrong and is accepted as wrong. This is a tape-reading example, not a fixed pip rule.
rules.quote: now i have six contracts long and i'll move my stop up just a little bit underneath that low right there it should not trade back down into that if it does i'm wrong and that's fine

rules.rule: Entering from discount, first profit is at the opposing liquidity or a key premium PD array.
rules.quote: Entering in that discount range, taking first profit would have to be at opposing liquidity or a key premium PD array.

rules.rule: 2022: the working draw can be a nearer pool. The farther pool (the buy stops above the day's high) is optional.
rules.quote: treating with the idea that it could run up here and take out the buy stops above the high of the day it doesn't need to do that to be profitable so my draw on liquidity is here

rules.rule: 2026: front-run the pool. Put limit exits just ahead of the relative equal lows rather than demanding the sweep.
rules.quote: I think that that was a reasonable level to trade down into. Now, because I want to get out before it gets down there, I had limit orders just ahead of that level right there

rules.rule: 2026 Silver Bullet: the first FVG after 10:00 aims for a relative equal low, or any smooth (non-jagged) level.
rules.quote: give it till 10:00 and if nothing's obvious then simply submit yourself to the 10:00 hour silver bullet which is the first fair value gap aiming for a relative equal low or where it's not made jagged, anything smooth

rules.rule: ATH target, Dec 2024: with no overhead history, project one quarter of the previous range beyond the break as the likely stop-point.
rules.quote: One quarter of the previous range broken out, that's where I think markets can trade to when we're trading with all-time highs

rules.rule: ATH target, 2026: scale heavy partials into standard-deviation extensions. The -1 to -2.5 SD range appears only in the dossier overview, not in this quote.
rules.quote: taking heavy partials into these standard deviation extensions.

rules.rule: 2022: do not insist on reaching the draw. Take the planned exit (limit) before it.
rules.quote: I did not need to trade to the draw on liquidity. This is a crucial point, folks: don't insist that your target or your draw on liquidity is the be-all end-all objective and you have to hold for that. That is foolish.

rules.rule: 2022: the HTF draw is a magnet, but an intraday trade is valid and profitable without price reaching the ultimate draw.
rules.quote: price does not need to reach the ultimate draw on liquidity for an intraday trade setup to be valid and profitable

rules.rule: Scale at the next pool: when the next buy-side pool is reached he takes 4 of 6 contracts off.
rules.quote: buyside liquidity is the next draw on liquidity i'll take four of the contracts off

rules.rule: 2017: exit before a known target. Demanding the perfect fill at the target is a mistake.
rules.quote: I always want to exit before my target so if I'm calling this as an objective I'm going to be exiting before that okay it's much high probability

rules.rule: Aug 2024 NQ trade toward the daily volume imbalance: stop moved from 19,862.75 to 19,881.00 (locking +660 USD) during the expansion. SHOWN annotation, not speech.
rules.quote: Stop migration: Initial stop at 19,862.75 moved to 19,881.00 (+660.00 USD locked) during mid-expansion

rules.rule: Same trade: sell 4 of 6 contracts at 19,929.25 as price enters the lower edge of the daily volume imbalance and leave 2 runners. SHOWN annotation, not speech.
rules.quote: Execution Marker: "Sell 4 @ 19,929.25" right inside the lower boundary of the Daily Volume Imbalance

rules.rule: 2026: once the move clears the candle high, trail the stop to the low of the daily volume imbalance so it cannot turn into a loss.
rules.quote: immediate rebalance on this wick. So, let's see if we get any kind of discount sensitivity off of that to the upside, clear this candlestick's high. If it does, then I'm going to run the stop loss right to the low of the daily volume imbalance.

rules.rule: Core Content: at the macro-range boundary the low-resistance run is finished, so take profits.
rules.quote: you must take your profits. The low resistance run is complete.

rules.rule: Once the draw is fully satisfied at the extreme, expect a reversal. Do not chase the same direction.
rules.quote: Prepare for the reversal once the draw on liquidity is fully satisfied at macro extremes.

rules.rule: 2024: displacement back down after the pool is taken confirms the draw is fulfilled, and the market shifts into rebalance mode.
rules.quote: confirming that the draw on liquidity is fulfilled and market shifts into rebalance mode.

rules.rule: Bias invalidation: if sell-side is taken first and price then rallies, a bearish short setup is cancelled.
rules.quote: if price takes out the previous day's low or sell-side liquidity first and then rallies, the price action is not bearish and cancels a short setup

rules.rule: HRLR: when price must fight through several swing points and order blocks, delivery is choppy and prone to reverse before the target, so skip it or cut size.
rules.quote: In a High Resistance Liquidity Run, price has to fight through multiple previous swing points, order blocks, and levels. It creates a choppy, difficult delivery that is prone to reversing before reaching your target.

rules.rule: 2017: an old high/low that has already reversed price before is a reaction level, not a level to expect a run through.
rules.quote: when the hourly or 60-minute chart trades to an obvious old high or old low that has shown a clear willingness to reverse price before in the past

rules.rule: 2026: urgency check on a daily volume imbalance. If price rushes straight back to fill it, that is less bullish.
rules.quote: I don't want to see it come back immediately for that volume imbalance. I I don't want to see that because if it's in a hurry to get back to that inefficiency, that's kind of a little less bullish.

rules.rule: ATH rule, Sep 2025: do not try to pick the top. Keep taking continuation buy signals until they stop working.
rules.quote: it's very important to never really try to expect or pick the top in a market that's trading at alltime highs because it can just keep going and you have no idea where it's going to go.

rules.rule: Fractal: the same draw/sweep behaviour is expected on lower and higher timeframes, with no real-time element required (2017-12 HTF concepts).
rules.quote: price is fractal that means the things that we would see and expect to see unfold in the lower timeframes just not tied to any real time element we would still expect the same phenomenon to occur on higher timeframe charts

rules.rule: 2024: internal range to external range and back, on every timeframe.
rules.quote: Internal range to external range. External range to internal range. Every time frame, I don't care what time frame

rules.rule: 2017: the liquidity-draw logic is asset-agnostic (stocks, futures, bonds, forex).
rules.quote: this works in stocks it works in futures it works in bonds it works in just about anything they can trade

rules.rule: ATH logic applies to forex and futures, as stated in the 2025 'Trading All Time Market Highs' dossier. The sentence sits in that dossier's markets table, not its rules table.
rules.quote: What I'm talking about tonight is applicable to Forex and futures and any other asset class trading at all-time highs

rules.rule: Oct 2025 shift: he dismisses forex that is not liquid and loose, calling it high resistance rather than low resistance runs. His focus is index futures (NQ/ES).
rules.quote: because it's not highly liquid. It's not loose. It's high resistance, not low resistance liquidity runs

rules.rule: 2017 forex scalps: the New York killzone (7-9am NY) is where the swing toward the draw is expected.
rules.quote: this is the New York ICT kill zone okay where we target the swing that usually it comes in around between 7 o'clock in the morning and nine o'clock in the morning New York time

rules.rule: 2024: each session makes a range (London 2-5am NY) whose high and low become reference points and liquidity targets for the later sessions.
rules.quote: These are the reference points that that session created its range the highest high inside of London between 2 o'clock in the morning here and 5:00 a.m.

rules.rule: 2022: at 3pm NY the algorithm starts to spool price toward the draw on liquidity.
rules.quote: and then at three o'clock the algorithms will start to spool price in the direction of the draw on liquidity

rules.rule: 2026: the last hour targets smooth relative equal highs. The jagged area is not the target.
rules.quote: We're targeting relative equal highs for the last hour trading. Notice this is smooth compared to the jaggedness down here

rules.rule: 2026: time limits the draw. A distant pool is unlikely to be reached late on Friday.
rules.quote: Don't expect these relative equal highs to be taken before the draw on liquidity because it's Friday. It only has a little bit of time.

ipda.summary: IPDA data ranges: each day on the daily chart, mark the highest high and lowest low of the last 20, 40 and 60 trading days (60 is roughly his 3-month quarterly-shift window), read whether price sits in premium or discount of that range, and expect the interbank algorithm to deliver price to un-purged old highs/lows and imbalances inside it, which gives the daily bias and draw on liquidity before any lower-timeframe entry.
ipda.needs_clock: The core model does not need a clock. It is the rolling highest high and lowest low of the last 20, 40 and 60 completed daily candles, the 50% midpoint (premium vs discount), and un-purged old highs/lows and imbalances inside that window. That is pure price delivery, so it could run on 24/7 synthetic indices if you define a 'day' as a fixed 24-hour bar. Two caveats. First, on synthetics 20/40/60 daily bars are calendar days, with no weekend gaps as in FX trading days. Second, he defines the IPDA true day as starting 00:00 New York time (_2nUKLAD9ig) and says in 2025 that the algorithm refers only to time and OHLC (vgG9JAKwng4), so the bar boundary should be fixed and consistent. Clock-dependent add-ons that would not port: the Month 09 routine (midnight NY open, CBDR/Asian range, London kill zone), the Model 5 Monday/Friday filter, seasonal tendencies (April/May, July/August), calendar-quarter shifts, and the DXY, yield and COT filters, which are not price-only.
ipda.how_to_code: 1) Build completed daily candles with a fixed bucket (00:00 NY for FX, any fixed 24h bucket for synthetics). 2) For N in {20, 40, 60}: HH_N = max high and LL_N = min low of the last N completed daily bars (the IPDA dossiers do not say whether today's bar counts, so make it a parameter), EQ_N = (HH_N + LL_N) / 2. 3) Location: price above EQ_N is premium (look for bearish arrays, draw = LL_N or old lows), below is discount (bullish arrays, draw = HH_N or old highs); the YV4fEF4d2wA and ze8jAMdmBqc quotes combine these. Prefer agreement across 20/40/60. 4) Draw on liquidity: list swing highs/lows inside each window that price has not traded through since they formed (the 'un-purged' test), plus unfilled FVGs and volume imbalances. The nearest un-purged level in the bias direction is the objective, and external range liquidity is the window extreme. 5) Run vs sweep at the extremes: a sweep is a new N-day high/low whose bar closes back inside the prior range (the false-break fade in vqtA1S9JH34), and a run is a close beyond it. He gives no numeric closes-back-within rule, so this is a parameter. 6) Quarterly shift (optional): about 60 to 90 trading days between swings, anchored to a daily market structure shift near a 60-day extreme (n7SPAK_tpN8: anchor the line to an MSS, do not force calendar dates). 7) Execution layer: a lower-timeframe (4h/1h/15m) PD array (order block, FVG, 62% OTE) inside the daily-range discount or premium, in the direction of weekly bias. Stop beyond the swing: he gives 15 pips (Model 5), 20 pips (shown Model 7 and Model 11 trades) or 25 pips (Model 3). Target is the opposite window extreme or external range liquidity, with 10/20/30 pip grades beyond a new low (Model 7). Manage by cutting stop risk 25% at 25% of the objective, 50% at 50%, and break-even only at 75%. Subjective parts: which window (20, 40 or 60) governs, whether today's bar counts, what makes a pool un-purged, PD-array quality and selection, weekly bias, MSS anchoring for the quarterly shift, and any invalidation. No dossier gives a numeric invalidation level for the ranges.
ipda.changes_over_time: 1) Lookback length changed over time. 2017: key levels are the rolling 12-month high/low, last 3 months, last 30 days and last week (YcAfcpUCbDw), plus a 3-day range for scalping (uE-aaP16nOw) and a 5 to 7 day contraction check (uxsmSMsuleY). Sept 2020 (_9QfSbpZTZA): he uses the term IPDA for the algorithm and defines the dealing range as the swing that ran liquidity on both sides, with no 20/40/60. 2022 Core Content (Month 05, uploaded Sept 2022; chart dates in the dossiers are 2015-2017, so upload date is not recording date): the formal 20/40/60 daily lookback (LRKtiysz4nA, YV4fEF4d2wA) and the 3-month 'open float' (about 60 days; vqtA1S9JH34, BkmZgjuYREU). Jan 2023 (QKvjPltjsqU): only 20 to 40 days. 2023-24 Charter: Models 1 and 11 use the 20-day range only; Models 3, 4, 5 and 7 use 20/40/60; in Model 4 (H05w52zQGdQ) he says the 20 has an asterisk because it is the 20/40/60 set, and in Model 7 (G4lhid5dh0I) he says to use all the potential data ranges out to 60 trading days. 2) Mechanism changed. 2022 (LRKtiysz4nA 00:30:46, vqtA1S9JH34) says the algorithm targets the stops traders place beyond the 20/40/60 extremes, and the 20-day breakout (Larry Williams, Turtle) is fade material. 2025 (vgG9JAKwng4 26:31) says the algorithm does not see your stop or contracts traded and refers only to time and OHLC. That conflicts with the stops story. The Month 12 dossier (eIdnsgq-G7A) paraphrases it as aligning with Jan/Apr/Jul/Oct, but that is not a verbatim quote. 4) Stops are not tied to the ranges and differ by model (15, 20, 25 pips). The 7 counted trades come from Charter and Month 09 dossier tables where the 20/40/60 range sets bias or target: Model 1 vCvRrINpknI, Model 3 ze8jAMdmBqc, Model 4 H05w52zQGdQ, Model 7 _7oZZ2bhEGU and G4lhid5dh0I, Model 11 pblXxWhnRz4, and Month 09 cqf8nH54bb8. rules.rule: Daily routine: every day on the daily chart, place price against the highest high and lowest low of the last 20, 40 and 60 days.
rules.quote: Every day you sit down at your daily charts: where are we at with respect to the lowest low and highest high in the last 20 days, the last 40 days, and the last 60 days?

rules.rule: Purpose: the data ranges tell you the draw on liquidity before you look for an intraday setup.
rules.quote: Trade with more insights using the IPDA data ranges and you will never wonder what the draw on liquidity is.

rules.rule: Quarterly shift: accumulation and distribution phases repeat every 3 to 4 months (the 60-day window is the same scale as this cycle).
rules.quote: There's a quarterly shift that takes place every three or four months, and you can see that these smart money accumulation and distribution phases repeat.

rules.rule: Quarterly shift stated as every 90 to 120 days and tied to calendar quarter starts (variant).
rules.quote: Look for an interbank quarterly shift every 90 to 120 days. Institutional algorithms rebalance portfolios at the start of each calendar quarter.

rules.rule: Window definition: roughly three months of daily data (about 60 trading days); mark its highest high and lowest low (this is the 60-day range).
rules.quote: Basically you're looking at three months of data, and by doing that, what it'll do is give you a range to look for the highest high and the lowest low on the daily chart.

rules.rule: The algorithm references 20, 40 and 60 days back; PD arrays are either already on the chart or being reached for.
rules.quote: PD arrays: they're either in the chart or they're in the process of being reached for. The algorithm looks back 20, 40, 60 days of institutional data.

rules.rule: Inside the rolling window, flag liquidity pools (old highs/lows) that have not yet been purged.
rules.quote: What we do is we think in terms of the rolling lookback cycles to identify where liquidity pools have been left un-purged.

rules.rule: Inside the lookback dealing range, find the next draw: which old low below or old high above price is likely to trade next.
rules.quote: Inside this Dealing Range we look for the next draw on liquidity. Where is Price likely to trade to next, below which Old Low, above which Old High?

rules.rule: Quarterly-shift anchor: start the vertical line at a prior market structure shift, not a calendar date.
rules.quote: Once you do that, what you're doing is you're anchoring your vertical line to a previous market structure shift.

rules.rule: Why the extremes matter (2022 framing): stops sit below lows and above highs of the 20/40/60 ranges and the algorithm targets them.
rules.quote: The AI cannot think for a human, but because human nature says that we will as traders put our sell stop below a low and our buy stop above an old high, the algorithm targets those levels.

rules.rule: Interbank objective one: reprice to liquidity - run the lows, take the stops, then expand.
rules.quote: The interbank algorithm exists to reprice to liquidity. It engineers a run below the lows, captures the retail stops, and then explodes higher.

rules.rule: The two interbank price delivery objectives: inefficiency/fair value (imbalances) and liquidity.
rules.quote: The algorithm is seeking inefficiency and fair value, and it's seeking liquidity. Period

rules.rule: 2020 definition of dealing range: the swing that ran buy side and sell side liquidity (no fixed day count given).
rules.quote: Once you have arrived at a particular swing that has done both, that is your dealing range.

rules.rule: Equilibrium: price above the 50% midpoint of the range is premium.
rules.quote: Anytime we get above the midpoint of a particular range, the algorithm sees that as a premium

rules.rule: Price in discount of the range seeks bullish PD arrays; price in premium seeks bearish PD arrays.
rules.quote: In a discount market we would be looking for a bullish PD array. When price is in a premium market we look for a bearish PD array.

rules.rule: Swing bias is checked against the 20/40/60-day lookback; when bullish, look for discount arrays (quote starts mid-sentence in the dossier).
rules.quote: or 60-day look back inside of the data range and when this bias is bullish we look for discount arrays

rules.rule: Choose PD arrays in the direction of the weekly range bias and target external range liquidity.
rules.quote: We look for a PD Array in the direction of the Weekly Range Bias. We target External Range Liquidity.

rules.rule: Intermarket filter: if DXY shows distribution, expect euro strength and hunt discount arrays.
rules.quote: If we see that we're expecting bullishness on the part of the euro dollar because the dollar index was showing distribution, we hunt discount arrays.

rules.rule: False break of a 20-day/3-month extreme: price runs beyond the high/low into resting stops, then reverses (fade).
rules.quote: What makes these false breaks higher and lower so lucrative is the fact that we understand that large traders, in the form of a fund trader, have their buy stops above.

rules.rule: SMT trigger: DXY higher high with the paired market making a lower high marks a sell program (distribution).
rules.quote: The dollar making a higher high while the underlying, in this case the dollar yen, makes a lower high: that would be a sell program showing heavy distribution.

rules.rule: Model 4 position trade: look for early-week manipulation converging with price moving opposite to the expected long-term roadmap.
rules.quote: look for a convergence of both manipulation and price opposite to expected long-term road map

rules.rule: Day-trade version: if bullish, wait for a Judas move below the midnight New York open by a standard deviation of Asian range or CBDR.
rules.quote: if I'm bullish I want to see a move down below that opening price to some measure of standard deviations of the Asian range or Central Bank Dealers Range

rules.rule: Long day trades only after the daily has broken a swing high in the recent run (Model 1, with price in discount of the 20-day range).
rules.quote: buying only when the daily has taken out a swing high in the last recent price run

rules.rule: Frame execution with a lower-timeframe PD array nested inside the higher-timeframe PD array.
rules.quote: Lower timeframe PD array is going to be used on a timeframe lesser than the higher timeframe PD array to frame the actual trade execution.

rules.rule: Model 1 entry: optimal trade entry at the 62% level refined inside the order block.
rules.quote: optimal trade entry pattern and keying off of the 62% level notice I refined it inside the order block

rules.rule: Order block entry reference is its 50% mean threshold.
rules.quote: That's the mean threshold or midway point (50%) of the bullish order block. Algorithms calibrate sensitive accumulation around that exact level.

rules.rule: Model 3 swing: initial stop kept within 25 pips.
rules.quote: 25 pip stop loss it gives you a huge upward R multiple for profit

rules.rule: Model 5: stop 15 pips beyond the swing high; re-enter if stopped on a valid entry.
rules.quote: we will place our stop loss Above This High plus 15 Pips we will re-enter if stopped out on a solid entry

rules.rule: Model 11 risk sizing: 1% of equity divided by stop cost, always round lots down.
rules.quote: $100 divided by $2.00 = 50 micro lots per trade or 1% of the Account Equity. Always round down.

rules.rule: Identify the opposite-side (discount) target before taking the premium PD-array entry.
rules.quote: Keying off all potential sell scenarios when we sell short from a premium PD array requires identifying the discount target beforehand.

rules.rule: Day-trade target is external range liquidity (old range extreme) in the weekly bias direction.
rules.quote: we want to be looking at the external range liquidity

rules.rule: Model 7: objective graded 10, 20, 30 pips beyond each new low (his shown trade ends 30 pips below the 60-day low).
rules.quote: every time we create a new low we do 10 20 30 pip grades below it to get our objective targets

rules.rule: Position trade: aim for the middle bulk of the quarterly-shift move, not the exact top or bottom.
rules.quote: We are trying to get in sync with that quarterly shift to get the meat in between, in other words the biggest portion of the move.

rules.rule: Graduated stop: at 25% of the objective cut stop risk 25%, at 50% cut 50%, break-even only at 75%.
rules.quote: when we are in profit 25% of our expected objective stop loss can be reduced by 25%

rules.rule: Stop goes to break-even only at 75% of the expected profit objective.
rules.quote: when position is at 75% of the expected profit objective stop must be at break even at that point

rules.rule: Position trade: trail stop behind intermediate swing lows on the daily chart.
rules.quote: Trailing stops: as price continues to expand, you lock in profit by trailing stops behind intermediate swing lows on the daily chart.

rules.rule: Take partials at intermediate PD arrays, re-enter or pyramid on daily retracements.
rules.quote: Scaling out: when price achieves intermediate-term PD arrays, you take partials and look to re-enter or pyramid on subsequent daily retracements.

rules.rule: Expect these moves to take time; study how long delivery takes from a data-range setup.
rules.quote: I'm really trying to draw your attention to something that I want you to focus on and study: how long it takes for these things to come to fruition using IPDA data ranges.

rules.rule: Do not trade against the daily order flow (general rule; no numeric invalidation level is given for the ranges).
rules.quote: never fight the order flow on the daily chart Banks and largest institutions will dictate where price goes

rules.rule: Lower intermediate-term highs mean sell-side liquidity is still the draw, so a long bias is not confirmed (inferred; the dossier warns not to buy into it).
rules.quote: If intermediate-term highs keep creating lower intermediate-term highs, it confirms the algorithm is reaching down for sell-side liquidity.

rules.rule: Use all of the 20/40/60 trading-day data ranges, out to 60 days, on any market (Model 7 universal plan).
rules.quote: the last 60 Trading days for the lookback data range because it's a universal trade plan we use all of those potential data ranges

rules.rule: Model 7 is universal across asset classes.
rules.quote: price action model number seven again this is Universal trading so it's applicable to every asset class

rules.rule: He flags the 20 with an asterisk because the lookback is the 20/40/60 set of data ranges, not a single 20.
rules.quote: lowest low in the past 20 and the 20 has got a little asterisk there because again it's 20 40 60 IPDA data range

rules.rule: 2023 variant on ES daily: look back 20 to 40 days only.
rules.quote: Remember, I'm looking back 20 to 40 days

rules.rule: 2017 precursor: last week, last 30 days and last three months high/low as key levels (no 20/40/60 yet).
rules.quote: monthly high and low we're gonna look at the last three months high and low and we're look at just the last 30 days or whatever the previous month is it's highest high and its lowest low

rules.rule: IPDA true day starts at midnight New York time and ends 3:00 PM New York time (he still calls it a 24-hour interbank day, which is inconsistent).
rules.quote: Every day at 12:00 AM midnight New York time begins the IPDA true day this is the beginning of the 24-hour interbank trading day. Every day at 3:00 PM New York time ends the IPDA true day 24-hour interbank trading day.

rules.rule: 2025: the algorithm refers back only to time and open/high/low/close.
rules.quote: the only thing it refers back to is number one time and then it works on the Open high low and close

rules.rule: Model 5 day-trade filter (its Stage 1 uses the IPDA ranges): skip Mondays and Fridays, trade Tuesday to Thursday.
rules.quote: on this trade plan I'm filtering out Mondays and I'm filtering out Fridays so it allows us to give us an opportunity for trading on Tuesday Wednesday and or Thursday

power_of_3.summary: Power of 3 / AMD: every period (month, week, day, session) opens at a reference price, the market first runs the opposite way past that open to grab stops (manipulation or Judas swing), then expands the other way (distribution). In a bullish bias he buys at or below the open, and in a bearish bias he sells at or above it.
power_of_3.needs_clock: Partly. His practical anchors are clock-based: the midnight New York open (00:00 ET), the 08:30 open, the Sunday 18:00 weekly open, the monthly open, the Judas window 00:00-05:00, and the London and NY killzones. The core logic is price-only and fractal (dIT4HTFYGGo 01:35): the period's open, a sweep the opposite way, then expansion past the open. The period boundaries (e.g. rolling N-bar or fixed-length windows) can be synthetic bar boundaries instead of NY time, so it could run on 24/7 synthetic indices using only OHLC. Two caveats. First, the session-timing rules (London makes the low or high, 11:00 cutoff, Mon-Wed only) would be lost. Second, in 2025 (Z0VYZoaTIKE 00:54) he explicitly refuses to endorse crypto or synthetic markets, and his stated rationale is real stop and liquidity pools. Any edge on synthetics must be tested empirically and cannot be assumed from his teaching.
power_of_3.how_to_code:
Mechanical core:
1. Choose a period P (day, week or month; for synthetics, a fixed N-bar window) and its open O = open of the first bar of P. Midnight NY is the daily anchor. The weekly anchor is the Sunday 18:00 open in 2017 (Yqio1Ja0lIQ), but he also says to ignore Sunday candles for daily-chart anchoring (nBschaCBNLU).
2. Bias (partly subjective): bullish means manipulation must go below O and entry is at or below O. Bearish means the mirror image above O. Objective proxies: HTF swing direction, previous-period high/low as the draw, and monthly/weekly/daily agreement. COT and SMT are not price-only.
3. Accumulation (contraction filter): compare the last 5-7 candle BODIES (ignoring wicks). Flag when the latest body, or the Asian/CBDR range, is small relative to the others, or when an inside-body day appears (the threshold for "small" is subjective). The 2022 videos add an ADR/CBDR < 60 pips filter, but only as a non-quoted dossier summary.
4. Manipulation: inside the window (00:00-05:00 NY, or 08:30-11:00 NY for the second PO3) record the extreme against bias. Require extreme < O - k (bullish) with k = about 20-30 pips, or 1-2 standard deviations of the Asian range/CBDR (about 33 pips), or a 10-20 pip sweep beyond the Asian range or equal highs/lows. k is not fixed and changes by year.
5. Trigger: price reclaims O, or an MSS / displacement leg appears after the extreme. His 2017 entry is a limit at or below O or at the 62-79% OTE of the leg. By 2022 he uses an OB or FVG inside the manipulation leg.
6. Stop: beyond the manipulation extreme, plus a buffer of 3-10 pips. For swings, use 150 pips (2017) or 50 pips (2024), or a 5-day ADR from the open.
7. Targets and management: previous day high/low, the Asian range opposite side, the ADR high, and 20 pips beyond the old high or low. Take 80% off at the ADR high before 10:00, or 50-80% at +100 pips, then move the stop to breakeven. Do not wait for a return to O.
8. Invalid or skip: weekly bullish case, price trades below the Wednesday-NY-open low or back to the open after Wednesday. Skip Thursday and Friday open referencing, skip heavy markets with no rally, and skip one-way shot days where no Judas forms. Subjective parts: HTF bias, what counts as "small" range, which liquidity pool is the draw, and whether manipulation is complete.
power_of_3.changes_over_time:
2017 (dIT4HTFYGGo, Sb9m_dxr4bI, M27EOgtHhis): Power of 3 is the OHLC bar model applied to any timeframe, with fixed pip heuristics (about 30-pip Judas rally, 10-pip sweep, 20-pip overshoot). The monthly, weekly and daily opens are the references. Entries are simply at or below the open. 2017 midnight-open work (xJMbva8SjzE, G8OEsUAoIWE) sets the window as midnight to 05:00 NY with the line drawn to 11:00.

2020 (RLDLuYaZYI4 and others): same logic, framed as OLHC/daily bias. These dossiers are summary-style, so many "rules" are paraphrase, not verbatim.

2021 (BZ4HVsArJBE, GVx-yJkehtA): the open is used only Monday to Wednesday, and Thursday/Friday is distribution, with Monday often left to others and Tuesday the action day.

2022: adds the 08:30 open (Sqw2bww93Zo; IEa1N0rTtbc 96:46 "last ditch for power 3 is 8 30") and a NY-session fractal PO3 (kmVXVJE08eQ). Judas size becomes standard-deviation based (about 33 pips; cqf8nH54bb8). Entries move to OB/FVG arrays (OVfn/oMtf) instead of simply "at or below the open", and partial rules appear (80% at ADR before 10:00).

2024 (s1gCDuzcukU): weekly stop shrinks from 150 pips (2017) to 50 pips, with the weekly entry on Tuesday/Wednesday under the 4:00 open.
