2025 (Z0VYZoaTIKE, pM8oWrcIJqU, ib9sa6ldwA4): the midnight open is replaced or extended by the Midnight Opening Range (00:00-00:30 ET) with standard-deviation projections, applied to NQ and forex. He explicitly rejects crypto and synthetics.

2026 (KHkUPAsdyfk, NPU4gsM9jqA, C7CwjBOtHwM): midnight open as a "fulcrum", return to the open not required, TGIF settlement below Friday's midnight open, the 9:30 RTH open as a magnet, all on NQ.

Conflicts to flag:
(a) Crypto: 2017 (G8OEsUAoIWE) he says he does not trade it but students claim it works. The Dec 2020 Bitcoin dossier (lp9cfZrqwjA, summary-style) says crypto uses the same algorithm. In 2025 (Z0VYZoaTIKE) he will never cosign crypto or synthetic markets.
(b) Weekly open: 2017 uses the Sunday open (Yqio1Ja0lIQ) but also says to ignore Sunday candles when anchoring a daily-chart OTE (nBschaCBNLU).
(c) Monday: 2017 Yqio1Ja0lIQ sits out Monday, 2021 leaves Monday to others and trades Tuesday, 2026 (rtIcbG6twrI) says avoid Monday because it is the manipulation/accumulation part of the week except NFP Monday. These are consistent, but they differ from OSOK 2022 (LBlK6JB0QS0), which expects the weekly high on Monday or Tuesday in London.
(d) Weekly timing: 2017 says weekly low by Wednesday NY open, 2020 says 70% Tuesday high for a bearish week.
(e) Contraction measured on candle bodies only (uxsmSMsuleY), while the 2022 Hoo_wTMgdcY dossier describes an inside bar as the contraction.
(f) Some dossiers (LifG37ky-Rg, RLDLuYaZYI4, Z0VYZoaTIKE, _9QfSbpZTZA, mQA8jCem9d0) are summary-style with few verbatim quotes. The auto-caption dossiers (dIT4, Sb9m, uxsm, xJMb, Yqio) are the most reliable for exact wording.
power_of_3.markets: Mostly EURUSD, GBPUSD, USDCAD and AUDUSD, plus DXY for daily bias (2017 to 2021). From 2022 he moves to E-mini S&P (ES) and Nasdaq (NQ) futures, with some FX majors. Trade-count basis: 23 trades whose dossier rows are tied to open-anchored Power of 3, Judas swing, weekly or monthly open, or a midnight-range entry. They span about 20 dossiers. Of those, 4 are in the 8 starting videos (Sb9m_dxr4bI x2 and uxsmSMsuleY x2). Two more starting-video trades are open-related but under other model names (M27EOgtHhis GBPUSD short, KHkUPAsdyfk NQ short). The other starting videos (dIT4HTFYGGo, LifG37ky-Rg, RLDLuYaZYI4, Z0VYZoaTIKE) show no trades, only diagrams or charts. The count is approximate because the dossier trade tables are auto-summarised. He says it works on forex and futures and, in 2017, on "just about everything that trades electronically overnight". In 2025 he says it works in every asset class except crypto, and he will not endorse crypto or synthetic markets.

rules.rule: Expect a large expansion after small ranges. He measures candle bodies only (wicks ignored) over the last 5-7 daily bars. A small open-to-close body is the cue to anticipate Power of 3.
rules.quote: big ranges come after small ranges form and we ignore the Wicks we're focusing only on the bodies of the candles

rules.rule: When the open-to-close relationship shrinks, anticipate an expansion and think Power of 3 (open, small counter move, close near the extreme).
rules.quote: focus only on the open and close relationship when that gets small what's about to happen is you're going to see an expansion and this is when anticipating power three

rules.rule: Lookback for contraction or expansion on the daily chart is 5-7 days.
rules.quote: if it's a daily chart I want to see what's happened in the last 5 to seven days okay I look back about 5 to seven days for range contraction and expansion

rules.rule: Intraday contraction: a very narrow Asian range (19:00-00:00 NY) raises the odds of a trending day, with a sweep of one side first.
rules.quote: if we have a very narrow consolidation there that sets up a huge possibility of the algorithm going into a trending model

rules.rule: Trade the daily open only when the higher timeframes agree. Monthly and weekly set the bias and the daily is the hunting timeframe.
rules.quote: the highest probabilities and trading the daily chart is when both the monthly and weekly support the trade idea that you would be using or hunting on daily

rules.rule: The daily bias question is whether today closes up or down relative to the open.
rules.quote: what we're trying to do is ascertain the likelihood of it being a up close or a down close day

rules.rule: Bullish bias: look to buy at or below the period's opening price.
rules.quote: on a daily range that opening price if we're bullish we want to be buying at that opening price or below it ideally

rules.rule: Bearish bias: expect manipulation above the open that engineers long liquidity.
rules.quote: when we're bearish we would be anticipating manipulation and what form of manipulation will we expect to see engineering long liquidity

rules.rule: Monthly-open version of the same rule: bearish monthly means sell at or above the monthly open.
rules.quote: if we have come to the conclusion that the monthly chart or perspective on the monthly is bearish then we are focusing our analysis on selling short at or above the monthly opening price

rules.rule: Why the open matters: institutions key off monthly and weekly opens, so he copies them.
rules.quote: large institutions use algorithmic systems that key off of monthly and weekly opening prices since there are massive amounts of volume in these entities actions we would do well to imitate or mimic their actions and directional bias

rules.rule: The bullish manipulation leg runs below the open to create short-side liquidity, which smart money then buys.
rules.quote: why would we want to be buying below the opening price we're more bullish because the market makers are going to be looking to engineer short liquidity

rules.rule: The drop below the open also stops out early longs (neutralizing long liquidity).
rules.quote: neutralizing long liquidity that means there's individuals it's probably already long or just recently bought near the opening price in the drop down below the opening price will upset their long position in other words it'll just run their stop

rules.rule: Clean highs and double tops hold buy stops, and the market probes them (bearish manipulation targets).
rules.quote: it would view that as a stiff resistance price point and those levels are too clean the market will in fact want to go through their probe it for buy stops

rules.rule: Bullish Judas anatomy at midnight: pop above the Asian high, drop below the midnight open, then below the Asian low.
rules.quote: the element of a bullish Judas swing is a pop above the Asian range high then a drop below the opening price at midnight and then below the asian range low when that occurs that's the actual Judas swing

rules.rule: Model stated in one line (2022): on bullish days price opens, manipulates below the NY midnight open to make the low of the day, then distributes higher.
rules.quote: on bullish days, expect the market to open, manipulate price below the New York midnight opening price to create the low of the day, and then distribute higher

rules.rule: Bearish mirror (2026): open, go above the midnight open, then drop and go lower for the day. The midnight open acts as the fulcrum.
rules.quote: if we were bearish, normal ICT power three concept would be open, go above the open at midnight and then drop lower and go lower for the day.

rules.rule: Size of the daily Judas rally above the open is about 30 pips (2017 daily FX), after which price drops and sets the low of the day.
rules.quote: here's the power of three the opening price small door rally up not usually about 30 pips or so and then it drops down creates the low of the day and comes off the low there it is

rules.rule: Bearish confirmation: price trades above the midnight open, rejects, and trades at least 25-30 pips lower in London. That supports a continuation or bearish New York session.
rules.quote: we want to see price move above the opening price at midnight New York time if that occurs and price rejects that goes lower and trades 25 to 30 pips lower at least minimum for the London session

rules.rule: Manipulation completes with a sweep about 10 pips beyond equal lows (or highs). Stops trip, smart money buys, then expansion follows.
rules.quote: reaches down below the consolidation into an area of liquidity which is 10 pips below equal lows there sell stocks are triggered where smart money would be buying

rules.rule: Weekly version: the new week drops below the weekly open (Judas) to shake out longs and lure shorts.
rules.quote: the new week we would expect to see the opening price that drop down which is a Judas swing this engineered move is to knock individuals are already out long

rules.rule: Climax reversal: a trap at the extreme right before the reversal (summary-style dossier).
rules.quote: A climax reversal pattern meaning that the retail crowd gets sucked in at the absolute high, right before the algorithm pulls the rug.

rules.rule: Daily entry: buy at or very near the midnight NY open, or below it, when bullish.
rules.quote: If you study daily ranges when the market's bullish and study where that opening price is at midnight: you want to be buying at or very near the opening price or below it.

rules.rule: Buy the Judas drop below the open and do not chase price above it.
rules.quote: You want to be buying on the Judas swing down or below the opening price and don't chase price

rules.rule: Bullish ideas need price below the midnight open.
rules.quote: when you're looking for bullish ideas you want to see price trading below the opening price at midnight new york time

rules.rule: 2017 weekly swing entry: buy 30 pips below the Sunday open.
rules.quote: buy 30 pips below the opening price on Sunday and use a hundred and 50 pips stop

rules.rule: 2024 Model 2 weekly entry: buy under the 4:00 open on Tuesday or Wednesday and hold into Thursday's NY open (the dossier transcribes 4:00 as 400).
rules.quote: buy under 400 opening price on Tuesday or Wednesday using 50 pip stop loss holding for Thursday's New York open

rules.rule: 2017 weekly swing stop: 150 pips (swing traders, not short-term).
rules.quote: use a hundred and 50 pips stop this is for swing traders not short-term traders and let that go and see if you don't get 150 to 300 pips

rules.rule: HTF-integration stop (2022): one 5-day ADR measured from the open (about 60-100 pips).
rules.quote: take whatever the average daily range is, subtract it from the opening price

rules.rule: Distribution target: expansion about 20 pips beyond the old high, after a sweep of about 10 pips beyond equal lows.
rules.quote: we have an expansion move or reins expansion up into a move of running 20 pips above the old high and your distribution cycle goes into the marketplace

rules.rule: Daily draw: the previous day's low (bearish) or high (bullish), to it and through it.
rules.quote: each day we're focusing on the previous day's low and that's where it's going to be aiming for to it and through it

rules.rule: On higher timeframes the overshoot beyond old highs and lows must be larger than 10-30 pips.
rules.quote: when we were using longer term timeframe levels we had to have a greater expectation of terms of the magnitude or range of how far it will move past those price points

rules.rule: The destination (liquidity) matters more than the entry.
rules.quote: the entry is not the most important thing knowing where the price is most likely trying to go to is what's most significant

rules.rule: 2025 midnight-range version: standard-deviation projections of the midnight range or first displacement give targets.
rules.quote: we can also get very, very precise elements to how the algorithm will rebook and redeliver to premium and discount.

rules.rule: After the manipulation low is set, expansion is fast with little pullback (summary-style dossier).
rules.quote: once the manipulation low is set, the expansion move happens rapidly with minimal pullback.

rules.rule: Take partials: day traders bank about 80% and short-term traders at least half, once the move reaches a 100-pip interval.
rules.quote: as a day trader you certainly want to be banking 80% of your position and if you're a short-term trader you want to be at least half your position out because the weekly can change gears midweek

rules.rule: After the first 100-pip partial, move the stop to breakeven.
rules.quote: if it allows you to make a hundred pips when you take your first partial off and put your stop at breakeven you're in a beautiful position

rules.rule: 2022: if the ADR high is reached before 10:00 AM NY, take 80% off.
rules.quote: If ADR high is reached prior to 10 AM, take 80% off of your position.

rules.rule: 2026: do not hold for a return to the open (a failed return is the norm). Target the relative equal highs instead.
rules.quote: don't hold with the expectation that we're going to go all the way back up to the opening price. It's not necessary.

rules.rule: Weekly: if price trades below the low formed by Wednesday's NY open, cancel the trade and stand aside for the day.
rules.quote: if we go lower than the low formed on Wednesdays New York open you have to nix the trade and go to the sidelines on the day

rules.rule: Weekly bullish case: after Wednesday, price must not return to the weekly open.
rules.quote: Wednesday is the line in the sand if it trades above the opening price when we're bullish we do not permit it to come back down to the opening price

rules.rule: Late in the week the open is no longer a reference (Thursday and Friday).
rules.quote: we're not going to reference the opening price on thursday because we're so late in the week

rules.rule: Both sides of the prior day's range traded through means indecision or an upcoming reversal. The bias is not clean.
rules.quote: very rarely do you see both sides of the previous day's candle tagged or traded through if it does it's usually indecisiveness or it's going to be a reversal soon

rules.rule: Do not force the Judas swing in a heavy market that will not rally.
rules.quote: sometimes the markets are just simply too heavy and they're not going to rally

rules.rule: Some days have no Judas dip (a one-way shot off a higher-timeframe level).
rules.quote: in this particular day it doesn't do that and the reason why it's because it's moving off of a higher time frame daily level

rules.rule: Fractal: the concept applies to any charted time interval.
rules.quote: everything I'm going to suggest to you here is applicable to every time measurement okay I know is every time interval if it can be charted this same phenomenon or concept can be applied to it

rules.rule: 2025: works in forex and futures, with the exception of crypto. In the same passage he says he will not cosign crypto or synthetic markets.
rules.quote: It works obviously in Forex and it works in Futures, it works in every asset class with the exception of crypto.

rules.rule: 2017 Judas-swing markets: EURUSD, GBPUSD, AUDUSD, USDJPY (and USDCAD).
rules.quote: euro dollar Cable Aussie dollar dollar yen there's four markets if you just watch those it'll give you a wide array of potential scenarios where this type of thing forms

rules.rule: Monthly open gives the macro bias.
rules.quote: the purpose of using a monthly chart is that it provides a macro institutional bias so we can see what large institutions are doing

rules.rule: Daily open: buy at or below it when bullish on the daily.
rules.quote: if we're bullish relative to the daily timeframe we are looking to be buying at or below the daily opening price

rules.rule: 2017: he said it works in other assets that trade electronically overnight, including indices. Crypto was students' claim only.
rules.quote: I don't trade Bitcoin or cryptocurrencies but I have students of mine that swear by this working in that asset as well

rules.rule: Judas window: from the midnight NY open to 05:00 NY.
rules.quote: you start hunting the Judas swing at midnight New York time okay so this is a New York opening price and it ends at 5:00 a.m. New York time

rules.rule: Anchor is the midnight NY open, drawn forward to about 11:00 NY.
rules.quote: The opening price is the most important: the opening price at midnight New York time. Draw that out in time on your 15-minute chart usually out to around 11 o'clock in the morning New York time.

rules.rule: London usually makes the low of day when bullish and the high of day when bearish.
rules.quote: the London session typically creates the low of the day when the market is primarily bullish and the high of the day when bearish

rules.rule: 2022: Power of 3 recurs fractally inside the NY session (08:30-11:00).
rules.quote: the new york session is the 8 30 to 11 time period new york local time so i'm looking for this framework to offer power 3 which is a fractal element of accumulation manipulation and distribution

rules.rule: Use the midnight open for the whole day and the 08:30 open for the morning session.
rules.quote: if you're looking at the entire daily range you're going to use the opening price at midnight but if you're going to be looking at the morning session you want to be using the 8 30 opening price

rules.rule: Weekly: the open applies Monday to Wednesday.
rules.quote: we're focusing primarily on buying below the opening price in bullish weeks on monday tuesday and wednesday bearish weeks we're looking to sell short on monday tuesday and wednesday above the opening price

rules.rule: Weekly low: expected between the Sunday open and Wednesday's NY open.
rules.quote: what we're looking for is the weekly low to form between Sunday's opening and Wednesday there high odds or the weekly low to form before Wednesday's New York open

rules.rule: 2020 weekly PO3: in a bearish week the high of week forms Tuesday (else Wednesday), with 70% stated.
rules.quote: I teach that when we're bearish, there's a 70% likelihood that the high of the week will form on Tuesday. If it doesn't form on Tuesday, it will occur on Wednesday

rules.rule: 2025 variant: the midnight opening range is 00:00-00:30 ET.
rules.quote: At 12:30 so that way it'll give us the midnight opening range, so that's your range

killzones.summary: A time-of-day filter on New York clock time: Asia builds a 19:00-00:00 range, London (02:00-05:00, older 01:00-05:00) usually prints the day's high or low, 05:00-07:00 is dead, NY (07:00-09:00 or 07:00-10:00) continues or reverses London, and London Close (10:00-12:00) gives a small retracement or continuation; ICT entries (mostly OTE) are only taken inside these windows.
killzones.needs_clock: Yes, hard dependency. The model is the clock: every rule is a New York wall-clock window (DST-aware, he says to chart in NY local time), plus anchors at 19:00, 00:00 and 08:20. It cannot be run on 24/7 synthetic indices using only price delivery. Synthetics have no sessions, no London/NY liquidity hand-offs and no midnight NY open, and he never says the effect exists without those institutions. Only the price-structure pieces carry over without a clock: consolidation range, sweep of its high/low, displacement, MSS, then OTE retracement to the opposite side. To test them, define an arbitrary repeating pseudo-day (e.g. fixed UTC bars per cycle) and treat 'Asian range', 'London' and 'NY' as hypotheses to measure, not as something his teaching supports.
killzones.how_to_code:
1) Time layer (objective): convert bars to America/New_York with DST. Label each bar with a session: ASIAN_RANGE [19:00,00:00) (alt 20:00); JUDAS window [00:00,05:00); LONDON_KZ [02:00,05:00) (param: start 01:00 or 02:00; sweet spot to 04:00); LONDON_LUNCH [05:00,07:00) no new entries; NY_KZ [07:00,09:00) or [07:00,10:00); NY_SESSION [08:30,11:00); LONDON_CLOSE_KZ [10:00,12:00) on 5m only; day ends 15:00 (14:00 often caps the extreme). Index variant: AM [08:30,11:00), PM [13:30,16:00), avoid 12:00-13:00. Make every boundary a parameter, because his definitions drift.
2) Daily anchors (objective): midnight_open = open of the 00:00 bar; asian_hi/lo/mid = max high / min low / midpoint over [19:00,00:00); width in pips. Optional filters: width <= 20 pips = prime, > 40 = skip London; CBDR (14:00-20:00 NY per one Month 08 caption) > 50 skip. Do not mix with the 2024 Model 5 note 'Asian range 20 pip or more'.
3) London KZ signal: inside [02:00,05:00), bullish if price trades below asian_lo (and below midnight_open) by a threshold (about 10-20 pips; Judas about 30 pips), then displaces back up and breaks the last lower high (MSS). Impulse leg = sweep low to the break high, anchored on candle bodies. Place a limit at 62-79% (70.5 centre). Stop beyond the sweep extreme (+5 pips, or 50% of 5-day ADR from the Asian low in the Month 08 model). Targets: asian_hi/mid, previous day high or equal highs +10-20 pips, then SD projections; take 50-80% at T1 and move the stop to breakeven +1 pip. Mirror for bearish.
4) NY KZ signal: require London to have printed the extreme in the daily-bias direction (London low on bull days). After 07:00 measure the retracement against that move; the setup is valid only once a retracement of at least 20 pips exists, entered at 62% of the London leg, stop beyond the London extreme, target the day's extreme / previous day high or low. Cancel if no 20-pip retracement by 09:00 (2017) or an order unfilled by 11:30 (2022).
5) London Close: 5m only, 10:00-12:00; if the day already printed a high/low earlier, fade the retracement off it with a 5m OTE for 10-20 pips, or take a continuation entry; flatten by 12:00.
6) Invalidation filters: bar in 05:00-07:00; Z-day / seek-and-destroy (classify by low net displacement with repeated stop runs); the day after a 14:00 FOMC; Asian range or CBDR above limits; Mon-Wed only for 'buy below midnight open'.
Subjective parts: daily bias (draw on liquidity), what counts as an 'obvious' old high/low, whether the Asian range 'matters' that day, Z-day versus seek-and-destroy, which swing anchors the OTE, and which window version (01:00 vs 02:00; 09:00 vs 10:00) to use.
killzones.changes_over_time:
1) London start: 01:00-05:00 in Oct-Nov 2017 (M27EOgtHhis 18:31, UpyS34voILk 02:57) and in the Month 08 re-upload (_2nUKLAD9ig 00:03:11, chart dated Apr 2017). From Dec 2017 it is 02:00-05:00 (G8OEsUAoIWE 01:41, PrbvJ5Gzh4Q 11:21, GVx-yJkehtA 13:49, Q6GFu8-Z4rY 08:25, 7rbV8aWkcqY 10:15, and 2025 WGGDbeRpo4w / 7cYwwE1GoV8 'London Open Killzone 2:00-5:00 AM ET'), with 02:00-04:00 as the sweet spot (uE-aaP16nOw 32:09).
2) NY window drifts: 07:00-09:00 (plNN9n7nrxc 01:00, lbAQNxRPXMs 06:06, UuMaC9n8Uy4 01:36), then 07:00-10:00 (uE-aaP16nOw 32:09, _2nUKLAD9ig 00:04:05, GVx-yJkehtA 13:49, 7rbV8aWkcqY 05:35). From May 2020 he separates it from a wider 08:30-11:00 'NY session' (ifFDif82Bmg 01:26 'it's not the ict new york kill zone', PrbvJ5Gzh4Q 11:21, GVx-yJkehtA 13:49). In June 2022 index trading uses AM 08:30-11:00 and PM 13:30-16:00 (2XhDi5GoNUI 03:37 / 06:20). A 2025 note gives a 07:00-07:30 opening range for the NY KZ (Zm9Q0NDRxoY 22:20).
3) London Close: window stable at 10:00-12:00 (3OEUIkkcmLE, _2nUKLAD9ig 00:04:34, BZ4HVsArJBE 07:51), but the role changes. 2017: a retracement off the high/low on a 5m OTE, or the day's high/low forms there (3OEUIkkcmLE 02:56 / 04:10), or a continuation (04:38). Jun 2022 narrows it to 'london closed profit taking' 10:00-11:00 (koN1ge8bewI 18:30). Oct 2022 makes it a reversal on large-range days with a 'second swipe' (KrGTimL3YRQ 32:20) and says a trending day is capped by 14:00 (JKzEhfwV1dY 00:11:32). Also used as a time-based exit (AcKelqKMkr8 18:45).
4) Asian: Dec 2017 teaches Asian-open OTE scalps of 15-20 pips (ley5HZs4bUM) while saying he dislikes trading Asia (07:48). The same month the Asian range is only a reference box (JA0mLNJeytY). In 2020 'Asia' is still listed as a killzone (xGFCIUFxsbw 33:23); by the 2022 Core Content it is only a range. He also says the Asian range is not important on some days (c5pKck9PwsQ 55:40, 2018 summary dossier).
5) Asian range size and hours: 19:00-00:00 in JA0mLNJeytY, _2nUKLAD9ig and the Friday Asian Range lessons; 20:00-00:00 in several 2018-2022 summary dossiers (5Z_3NbclMSY, zanmou0ic5U, fmC14ZvCS3o), which are not verbatim. Size: 20 pips or less is wanted and over 40 is skipped (5Z_3NbclMSY 07:32, stK2gNqhLaM 09:30), but the Jan 2024 Model 5 dossier quotes 'Asian range 20 pip or more' (2fgXDt3T3XE 09:25), a conflicting direction left unresolved.
6) Role of London: 2017 says it has the highest probability of printing the day's high or low (G8OEsUAoIWE 03:43), but a 2025 review says the London kill zone was 'lethargic' and NY made the Judas swing (tNL_BtccMfA 06:15). The Asian-range breakdown must happen after 06:00 European open (s1gCDuzcukU 48:56, 2024).
7) Added later: day-of-week filters (Tue/Wed prime in -cXnnHjy9s0; midnight-open buys only Mon-Wed in BZ4HVsArJBE 07:13; Mondays left to others in GVx-yJkehtA 12:30), sideline filters (FOMC, CBDR over 50, Asian range over 40), and a 2022 shift to FVG/order-block limit entries ('place orders in the kill zone and walk away', eai0nHhAC8w 48:38) versus the 2017 'walk if no 20-pip retracement by 09:00' (UuMaC9n8Uy4 01:36). Entry method also changes from 62-79% OTE (2017) to a fixed 62% with a 5-pip stop (PrbvJ5Gzh4Q 2021) to Silver Bullet / FVG entries (7cYwwE1GoV8, 2025).
8) Source quality: only the 2017 tables read like transcripts. The Month 08 / Core Content dossiers (_2nUKLAD9ig, -cXnnHjy9s0, JKzEhfwV1dY, 5Z_3NbclMSY, stK2gNqhLaM, KrGTimL3YRQ) and the 2018-2020 summary dossiers have cleaned or paraphrased 'verbatim' text, and several 2018-2020 summaries give different clock times (e.g. 11:00 London Close, 08:30-11:00 NY window) that I did not use as quotes.
killzones.markets: The 15 trades are those in the eight starter videos: London KZ 2 (EURUSD), NY KZ 3 (AUDUSD, EURUSD, USDCAD), Asian KZ 4 (USDJPY, NZDUSD, AUDJPY, GBPCHF), London Close 2 (AUDUSD, USDJPY), Asian Range 3 (AUDUSD), UuMaC9n8Uy4 1 (GBPUSD); uE-aaP16nOw and _2nUKLAD9ig show none. A rough count of other dossiers adds about 22 killzone-labelled OTE or Judas examples in 2017 (lbAQNxRPXMs, xJMbva8SjzE, UpyS34voILk, nBschaCBNLU, M27EOgtHhis, x39H7GJggoc, the 20171027 USDJPY, USDCHF, AUDUSD, USDCAD and gold set and others) and about 20 more in 2021-2025 where the killzone is only the time filter. Every one is a hindsight chart example and nearly all are wins, with no loss statistics. Markets: FX majors (EURUSD, GBPUSD, AUDUSD, USDCAD, USDJPY, USDCHF), Asian crosses (AUDJPY, GBPCHF, NZDUSD), gold (2017 examples). He says it also works on DAX/FTSE/ES/YM/NQ, commodities and bonds. From 2022 he applies it to ES/NQ with different windows (AM 08:30-11:00, PM 13:30-16:00 NY). Timeframes: 15m main, 5m for London Close, 1m allowed later, 1h/daily for context.

rules.rule: Chart clock must be New York local time; every window on this card is NY time (cleaned-text dossier from the 2016/17-era Month 08 lesson, re-uploaded 2022).
rules.quote: If you're ever questioning what I'm referring to in terms of the beginning and endings you have to have a New York time clock

rules.rule: Asian Range box = 19:00 to 00:00 New York (5 hours). Some later summaries use 20:00; this is the verbatim version.
rules.quote: 7:00 PM Eastern Standard Time in New York time begins the Asian range. Every day at midnight Eastern Standard Time New York ends the Asian range.

rules.rule: Asian killzone = Asian open to midnight NY only (he ignores the rest of Asia). In the same video he says he uses a two hour window after the Asian open for scalps, and that Asia mostly consolidates.
rules.quote: it will consolidate until midnight New York time now the Asian trading session actually extends beyond the midnight hour of New York time but I focus specifically in the realm of the Asian open to midnight

rules.rule: Trading day anchor: IPDA true day runs 00:00 to 15:00 NY; the midnight NY open price is the day's reference.
rules.quote: Every day at 12:00 AM midnight New York time begins the IPDA true day this is the beginning of the 24-hour interbank trading day. Every day at 3:00 PM New York time ends the IPDA true day 24-hour interbank trading day.

rules.rule: London killzone = 02:00 to 05:00 NY (his main definition from Dec 2017 onward).
rules.quote: the ideal ICT London kill zone for your learning is going to be 2 a.m. to 5 a.m. and it's relative to New York time

rules.rule: Earlier/wider London killzone = 01:00 to 05:00 NY (Oct-Nov 2017 and the Month 08 re-upload).
rules.quote: my kill zones encompassing the entire normalized kill zone which encompasses one o'clock in the morning New York time to 5:00 a.m. New York time that's my London kill zone and it's all reference to New York time

rules.rule: Sweet spot inside the windows: London 02:00-04:00 for the day's low/high; NY 07:00-10:00.
rules.quote: London is basically two o'clock to four o'clock in the morning that's the sweet spot or the best time to anticipate a higher load of form and the New York is going to be seven o'clock in the morning to ten o'clock in the morning

rules.rule: London lunch = 05:00 to 07:00 NY: quiet, minor retracements, no entries; wait for the NY open.
rules.quote: five o'clock in the morning New York time to seven o'clock in the morning New York time which is classically like a London lunch the period where it can go quiet it can have minor little retracements but I don't like to see any type of entry between 5 o'clock and 7 o'clock in the morning New York time because it can tend to wait for the New York open

rules.rule: New York open killzone = 07:00 to 09:00 NY in the Dec 2017 killzone series.
rules.quote: key times to monitor are 7:00 a.m. to 9:00 a.m. New York time this is what I refer to as the classic ICT New York open kill zone

rules.rule: New York killzone widened to 07:00-10:00 NY in the Month 08 lesson (also stated Nov 2017, Jul 2021, Feb 2022).
rules.quote: Every day at 7:00 AM Eastern Standard Time New York begins the New York Kill Zone. Every day at 10:00 AM Eastern Standard Time New York ends the New York Kill Zone.

rules.rule: By 2021 he separates the NY killzone (07:00-10:00) from the NY session window (08:30-11:00); London 02:00-05:00.
rules.quote: london kill zone is two o'clock in the morning to five a.m new york is seven a.m to ten a.m and if you want to use the new york session time not the new york kill zone the new york session time is 8 30 in the morning till 11 a.m new york time

rules.rule: 08:20 NY (CME open) is an intraday turning point; the Month 08 chart shows a reaction low there.
rules.quote: 8:20 AM New York time this is the CME open. Look at this line draw straight up with your imagination and goes right to that little short term low and price rallies away from that that is not randomness.

rules.rule: London Close killzone = 10:00 to 12:00 NY; small scalps of 10-20 pips.
rules.quote: the London close frequently sets up an optimal trade entry pattern that can offer 10 to 20 pips for a scalp the key times to monitor are 10 a.m. to noon New York time this is the ICT London close kill zone

rules.rule: London killzone: EURUSD and GBPUSD; 15-minute charts.
rules.quote: the euro dollar and the British Pound pairs are ideal for this time of day

rules.rule: NY killzone: majors paired with the dollar; 15-minute charts.
rules.quote: the majors that are coupled with the dollar index or the dollar that to me is the ideal pair for this time of day

rules.rule: Asian session: AUD, NZD and JPY pairs (AUDUSD, NZDUSD, USDJPY) because they are active then.
rules.quote: the Australian dollar the New Zealand dollar Japanese yen pairs are ideal for this time of day they're active their markets are open at that time

rules.rule: Four markets to watch for the Asian range / Judas pattern: EURUSD, GBPUSD, AUDUSD, USDJPY (USDCAD also shown).
rules.quote: euro dollar Cable Aussie dollar dollar yen there's four markets if you just watch those it'll give you a wide array of potential scenarios where this type of thing forms

rules.rule: London Close must be read on the 5-minute chart; higher timeframes hide the detail.
rules.quote: whenever we're studying the London close you have to be looking at it from a 5-minute anything higher than that you're not going to get the detail you need

rules.rule: He says the London-open behaviour applies to any market that trades electronically overnight (indices, commodities, bonds; crypto only per students).
rules.quote: this same phenomenon occurs in other assets now I don't trade Bitcoin or cryptocurrencies but I have students of mine that swear by this working in that asset as well it works in commodities it works in bonds it works in just about everything that trades electronically overnight

rules.rule: Personal caveat: he stays away from exotic crosses and so dislikes trading Asia.
rules.quote: like we can do a pound Swiss those types of to me that's an exotic I don't trade them I tend to stay away from them and that's the other reason why I don't like to trade the asian session

rules.rule: Index futures (2022 mentorship final episode): AM session 08:30-11:00 and PM session 13:30-16:00 NY are the 'killzones' (the PM window is quoted; the AM window is in the same dossier row).
rules.quote: 1:30 PM to 4:00 PM New York Local Time

rules.rule: Why use killzones: a setup must have a time it forms; this removes the fear of missing moves.
rules.quote: this is why I use kill zones this time element of the trading day I know what I'm looking for I know my setup and if I know what time it should occur I know when what days of the week it should form and I know it should be either a bullish model or bearish model I'm not anxious about missing a move

rules.rule: Entries are taken only at killzone times: London open, New York open, London close or Asia.
rules.quote: we always go back to our key premise of trading within kill zones okay so you want to be doing your entries and your kill zone times London open New York open London close or Asia

rules.rule: Day-of-week filter (Month 08, cleaned-text dossier): Tuesday and Wednesday are the prime days.
rules.quote: The day of the week is paramount in understanding about day trading because Tuesday and Wednesday form the high or low of the week predominantly.

rules.rule: A very narrow Asian range (7pm-midnight) raises the chance of a trending day with London expansion.
rules.quote: if we have a very narrow consolidated range between 7:00 p.m. and midnight or what would be deemed as the Asian range so if we have a very narrow consolidation there that sets up a huge possibility of the algorithm going into a trending model

rules.rule: Month 08 quantification of 'narrow': Asian range of 20 pips or less before London (cleaned-text dossier).
rules.quote: We're going to demand that the Asian Range is in a 20 pip range or less ahead of Frankfurt and London

rules.rule: Asian-session crosses (AUDJPY, GBPAUD, GBPCHF etc.) can give 20-50 pips, but only a couple of times a week.
rules.quote: you can trade these crosses at this time of day and many times you can catch anywhere between 20 and 50 pips not every single day but a couple times a week

rules.rule: London's extreme follows the daily bias: bullish daily means London posts the low; bearish daily means London posts the high.
rules.quote: the London session typically creates the low of the day when the market is primarily bullish and the high of the day when bearish when the market is poised to trade higher on a daily timeframe we can focus on the London session to post a low of the trading day if the daily is poised to trade lower we can focus on the London session to post the high of the trading day

rules.rule: NY continuation: if London agrees with the daily bias (e.g. makes a low on a bullish day), expect a NY retracement then a continuation OTE.
rules.quote: if London agrees with the daily chart being bullish that means we should be seeing a low form in London we would anticipate a retracement lower into New York open and in agreement with that daily bias so we would anticipate a New York low to post a continuation setup or optimal trade entry buy

rules.rule: Bearish London confirmation: price goes above the midnight open, rejects, and falls 25-30 pips; that supports a NY continuation short.
rules.quote: to confirm them on the session being bearish we want to see price move above the opening price at midnight New York time if that occurs and price rejects that goes lower and trades 25 to 30 pips lower at least minimum for the London session that would indicate at least the expectation that New York sessions should present a continuation idea or bearishness

rules.rule: London Close role 1: on an up-close day it typically forms the day's high between 10:00 and noon (mirror for down days).
rules.quote: if we're bullish and the daily close is going to be high relative to its opening in other words it's an up close day the London close is going to be typically when the high of the day is formed between 10 o'clock and noon

rules.rule: London Close role 2: it can instead be a continuation point that runs into the NY afternoon.
rules.quote: the London close can create continuation points for swings that trade well into New York afternoon hours that means if we're bullish overall in the day instead of creating the high of the day in bullish markets or bullish days many times the London close can actually create a continuation pattern

rules.rule: Asian range is measured as highest high to lowest low between 19:00 and 00:00 NY; its high and low are the liquidity London targets.
rules.quote: the height of the range is the highest high between 7:00 p.m. to midnight in New York time to the lowest low between 7:00 p.m. and midnight New York time the width of the range is obviously the duration of 7:00 p.m. to midnight New York time

rules.rule: Draw the midnight NY open price forward to about 11:00; it divides the Judas move from the real move.
rules.quote: whatever the opening price is exactly at midnight New York time I draw that out to around 11 o'clock in the morning

rules.rule: The market runs the stops above or below the Asian range, then goes the other way for the rest of the day.
rules.quote: the market will seek the liquidity above or below this range with a premise that it's going to put them in the wrong side and then it'll go the other way for the remainder of the trading day

rules.rule: Judas swing window is midnight to 05:00 NY; the day's high or low forms inside it.
rules.quote: you start hunting the Judas swing at midnight New York time okay so this is a New York opening price and it ends at 5:00 a.m. New York time and that's basically the entire five hour window that would be utilized for anticipating this price move

rules.rule: Draw on liquidity for a bullish session is the previous day's high or an old high (buy stops).
rules.quote: when we look for where the markets going to reach for in terms of bullishness it's the previous day's high or an old high that's gonna be in the form of buy-side liquidity or buy stops so the market will draw up to that level

rules.rule: London stop run: equal highs swept by about 10 pips give the London high of day.
rules.quote: notice also that we have equal highs in here okay about 10 pips above this short-term high that gives us the high of the day at the same time we would reasonably expect to see London open create the high of the day

rules.rule: Typical Judas size: roughly 30 pips against the day's direction from the open before the real move.
rules.quote: here's the power of three the opening price small door rally up not usually about 30 pips or so and then it drops down creates the low of the day and comes off the low there it is

rules.rule: Bullish Judas trigger: pop above the Asian high, then a drop below the midnight open and below the Asian low.
rules.quote: what we're looking for is the element of a bullish Judas swing is a pop above the Asian range high then a drop below the opening price at midnight and then below the asian range low when that occurs that's the actual Judas swing

rules.rule: Bearish Judas trigger from a tight Asian range: drop first, then a run above the Asian high and above the midnight open.
rules.quote: asian range small tight consolidation we want to see it drop down trip traders in right away then run on the other side of the asian range high that movement above the opening price above the asian range high that is the Judas swing

rules.rule: NY continuation trigger: the setup forms after 07:00 as a retracement against the London move.
rules.quote: typically the setup will form after 7:00 a.m. New York time you're going to be waiting for a price retracement lower

rules.rule: London Close trigger: retracement off the day's high (bull day) or low (bear day), entered on a 5-minute OTE; very short term.
rules.quote: the price action seen at London close typically sees a retracement off the high of the day on bullish days and off the low on the day that is seen bearish there's typically a 5-minute optimal trade entry setup in these conditions but they're very important to remember this they're very very short-term in nature

rules.rule: Entry inside a killzone is the OTE retracement: 62%, 70.5% (sweet spot) and 79% of the impulse leg.
rules.quote: optimal trade entry right in here 62% trace on level 70 point 5 and 79% ok they're my specific levels

rules.rule: NY scalp entry: limit at the 62% retracement after 07:00, expecting a retest of the day's high or previous day's high.
rules.quote: if it does form enter on the 62 percent retracement fib as it drops lower expect price to retest the high of the day or the previous day's high and then look for targets one two and symmetrical price swing on the FIB

rules.rule: Asian-range model (Month 08, cleaned-text dossier): buy 5 pips under the Asian low to allow for spread.
rules.quote: I like buying under the Asian Range plus 5 pips for the spread

rules.rule: Same model: entry zone is 1 to 2 standard deviations of the Asian range, and it must sit in a discount PD array.
rules.quote: look for one or two standard deviations in the Asian Range coupled with a discount PD array

rules.rule: Bullish breakout-and-retest: extend the Asian high/low forward; buy when price returns to the Asian high.
rules.quote: periods when price is bullish we can extend the age and range high and low into the future when price returns back to the Asian range high we can anticipate institutional buying

rules.rule: Bearish Judas entry: short after price runs above the Asian high and clears the buy stops.
rules.quote: running above the asian range high clearing out their stops which would be a buy stop

rules.rule: Stop goes at the swing extreme of the OTE leg (the high for shorts); first scale is the old low, then targets 1 and 2.
rules.quote: here's our setup going to New York ICT Killzone here's your entry optimal trade entry your risk is the high and your first scaling is the old low then you have target one which is hit here and ultimately target two for a nice little handsome Swissy trade

rules.rule: Asian-range model: stop distance is 50% of the 5-day ADR measured from the Asian low (or high). Cleaned-text dossier.
rules.quote: take 50 pips minus the Asian range low, whatever that price is, that's what your stop loss has to be.

rules.rule: Mechanical 2021 OTE drill in the London/NY killzones: stop 5 pips beyond the old high/low the fib was drawn from.
rules.quote: your stop has to be five pips above the old high that you pulled your fib from so in other words dragging your fib from here to here wherever 62% retracement level is that's your entry price

rules.rule: London open OTE expectancy: 25-50 pips, aimed at the day's high/low.
rules.quote: the London open frequently sets up an optimal trade entry pattern that can offer 25 to 50 pips for a scalp

rules.rule: NY open OTE expectancy: 20-30 pips.
rules.quote: the majors that are coupled with the dollar index or the dollar that to me is the ideal pair for this time of day the New York open frequently sets up an optimal trade entry pattern that can offer 20 to 30 pips as a scalp

rules.rule: Asian open OTE expectancy: 15-20 pips.
rules.quote: the Asian open can sometimes set up an optimal trade entry pattern that can offer 15 to 20 pips for a scalp

rules.rule: London Close expectancy: 10-20 pips; more than 20 is rare.
rules.quote: typically going to be very small short-term 10 15 maybe even 20 pips if you get anything more than 20 pips it's going to be a rarity

rules.rule: Over-run allowance: price usually reaches 10-20 pips beyond a previous high or low, so size targets past the pool.
rules.quote: I teach that price generally will reach about 10 to 20 pips above a previous high or low

rules.rule: Month 08 rule (cleaned-text dossier): at the first objective take 50-80% off and move the stop to breakeven plus 1 pip.
rules.quote: Once price moves in your favor and hits your first objective, you must take off 50% to 80% of your position and move your stop to breakeven plus one pip to eliminate risk.

rules.rule: Asian-range model: take 60-80% off at the 50% equilibrium of the 60-minute range (cleaned-text dossier).
rules.quote: At the equilibrium of the price range you are trading inside of on a 60-minute chart, take or have taken 60 to 80 percent off

rules.rule: 2022: if the order has not filled by 11:30 NY, cancel it; do not leave it good-till-cancelled.
rules.quote: Now, what happens if it doesn't fill you by 11:30? Pull the order. It's it. Don't put it you know, good till cancel. Just pull it because you want to be entering on the day that it creates this

rules.rule: 2022: the killzone is when you decide the entry and place the order; the fill itself may come later.
rules.quote: Kill zones are when you determine your entry, and you place your orders, and you walk away. You don't need to have your entry filled inside that kill zone window. Your order idea and your order placement need to be considered at that time.

rules.rule: No new trades 05:00-07:00 NY (London lunch). Cleaned-text dossier; same rule in G8OEsUAoIWE 09:40.
rules.quote: Be mindful that between 5:00 AM and 7:00 AM New York time is London lunch. We don't take new trades in that window; the market goes into consolidation or retracement.

rules.rule: NY scalp is void if no retracement of at least 20 pips has formed by 09:00 NY.
rules.quote: ideally you wanna be selecting retracements of at least 20 pips are lower if no retracement of 20 pips forms by 9:00 a.m. walk that means cut they don't try to take any trades

rules.rule: Unfavourable day types: Z day (quiet up-and-down consolidation) and seek-and-destroy day (choppy until the last part of the day).
rules.quote: the times you're going to be unfruitful using this information is when we have a Z day where it goes up and down in quiet consolidation or a seek and destroy day which is a really wild choppy up-and-down day where it doesn't really go anywhere until the last portion of the day and then it runs out the stops

rules.rule: Skip the London open after an FOMC release (usually 14:00 NY the day before). Cleaned-text dossier.
rules.quote: Avoid trading London open after FOMC events that create whipsaw

rules.rule: Skip London when the Central Bank Dealers Range (the 14:00-20:00 NY range per another Month 08 caption) is over 50 pips. Cleaned-text dossier.
rules.quote: If the Central Bank Dealers Range is greater than 50 pips, I'm already knowing firsthand I'm possibly going to pass on a London

rules.rule: Asian range over 40 pips: no normal London setup (delayed-protraction profile only, else sidelines). Cleaned-text dossier.
rules.quote: If the Asian Range is greater than 40 pips, I'm going to consider the delayed protraction profile

macros.summary: Algorithmic macros: fixed 20-minute New York clock windows (10 minutes before to 10 minutes after an hour, e.g. 9:50-10:10, 10:50-11:10, 1:50-2:10, 2:50-3:10, plus the Market-On-Close 3:45/3:50-4:00 and pre-market 6:50/7:50/8:50 windows) in which ICT says the price algorithm 'spools' and runs price to the nearest liquidity pool or inefficiency; he takes an FVG / inversion-FVG / immediate-rebalance entry inside the window, stops beyond the gap or its 50%, and targets the nearest liquidity (for the lunch macro, the first swing high after 10:00).
macros.needs_clock: Yes, by definition. Every window is a New York wall-clock interval (minute-of-hour :50 to :10 of named hours), and its anchors are also clock-based (9:30 open, 10:00 opening-range close, 4:14 PM settlement, 8:30 news). On 24/7 synthetic indices there are no sessions or institutional clock, so only a generic hourly phase test (price delivery inside minute :50-:10 of each hour, using the feed's own timestamps) can run; the named windows (9:50, 10:50, 1:50, 2:50, MOC) cannot be mapped, and the 10:00 target rule, opening range gap and settlement logic have no equivalent. What is price-only: displacement/spool detection, FVG/IFVG/immediate-rebalance entries, CE-based stops, nearest-liquidity targets. Treat the macro as an optional time gate to be tested out of sample; on random-walk synthetics do not expect the macro itself to add edge.
macros.how_to_code:
1. Clock gate: convert candle times to America/New_York (DST-aware). Windows = [H:50, (H+1):10] for configured H. Dossier-supported set: 6:50, 7:50, 8:50 (news-driven), 9:50, 10:50, 11:50, 12:50, 1:50, 2:50; closing windows 3:15-3:45 (30 min), 3:45-4:00 (MOC, 2024-25) and 3:50-4:00 (settlement or 2026 MOC); other-session ones (London 2:50 AM, Asian 9:50 PM, 5:50 AM). Make the list configurable and split each window into first half (:50-:00) and second half (:00-:10). Allow a post-window grace (MOC can run to 4:14).
2. Context (mostly subjective, parameterize): session or daily bias; draw on liquidity = nearest unswept swing high/low, relative equal highs/lows, PDH/PDL; for the lunch macro, the first swing high/low after the 10:00 line (fractal swing on 1m); RTH opening range gap (prior 4:14 PM close to 9:30 open) with CE, quadrants and octants; optional standard deviation projections. Lunch macro precondition: morning move one-directional with no minor opposite swing taken.
3. Trigger inside the window: displacement = candle(s) with body greater than k times ATR(1m) or a 3-candle FVG forming in the direction of the draw; 'speed and magnitude' = body expansion over the last N candles. Half-split: if nothing spooled in the first half, arm for the second half. Window start candle can arm the MOC (3:50) case.
4. Entry: limit/market on retrace into the displacement FVG; immediate rebalance = the candle right after the FVG-creating candle trades into the gap and closes back out; IOFED = partial fill of an FVG; IFVG = a gap traded through by a candle body close and retested from the other side. Optionally also allow entries up to about 10 minutes before the window start (his 2026 statement).
5. Stop: beyond the gap edge or beyond the CE (50%) of the relevant gap (higher gap if two gaps stacked, 'Two Gap Rule'); or key candle open/high plus 1-2 ticks; for BISI longs require bodies in the upper half, exit on body close below CE.
6. Target: nearest opposing liquidity (first swing high after 10:00, relative equals, PDH/PDL, opening gap CE or octant level, session smooth highs/lows). Partial at first internal pool, runner to the main pool.
7. Management: trail to break-even-plus-costs after displacement, then behind successive 1m swing lows/highs or under/over the displacement candle open; never widen a stop; flat by window end, or by about 4:14 for MOC (his rule varies, so make it a parameter).
8. Invalidation filters: 8:30 NFP/FOMC release minutes; no displacement in the window; bodies close through CE; parabolic days (no retracement to the 10:00 area); reject windows not in the configured list.
Subjective and not codable without choices: the bias, which liquidity pool counts as the draw, how much movement counts as spooling, 'smooth' highs, 'low-hanging fruit', whether a given day's macro is 'working', wick versus body tolerance on CE.
macros.changes_over_time:
1. Window list grows and drifts. 2022: only precursors ('at three o'clock the algorithms will start to spool', CL94EnGqB4Q; '8:30 spooling', CnTXwAuDi9Y; a 3:30-3:45 'Market On Close algorithm', wOzyoZD7b7M). 2023 mentorship (Jun-Jul): one macro, 9:50-10:10, handing off to the 10:00-11:00 Silver Bullet. 2023-11: lunch hour 11:50-12:10 (ES). 2024-01: 10:50-11:10, 2:50-3:10, MOC 3:45-4:00 and the general rule 'every hour :50 to :10' (livestreams 23-24 Jan). 2024-06/08/09/10: 12:50-1:10 lunch macro, 12:30 PM lunch macro (on-screen text only), 1:50-2:10, 3:15-3:45 (30 minutes, not 20), 3:50-4:00 settlement, 11:50-12:30 'NY lunch macro'. 2025: pre-market 6:50-7:10 and London 2:50-3:10 AM; 7:50-8:10 (Oct); 10:50 re-framed as the start of the lunch run toward the first post-10:00 high. 2026: 5:50 AM, Asian 9:50 PM, 12:50, 3:50 MOC; lunch macro described as 11:30-1:30 with 11:50-12:10 inside it, and 11:30 as the latest start when delayed.
2. 'Lunch macro' means different things: 10:50-11:10 start (4hkZEQiB02U, BdmULCuem5Q), 11:50-12:10 (qW0_Mxfp_Z4, zq4hz_XiTRE), 12:30, 12:50-1:10 (CRE7Pmch5G0, 5ycp9oGKPms), or the whole 11:30-1:30 span (MxaJD1WIzos, zq4hz_XiTRE).
3. MOC length: 3:30-3:45 (2022), 3:45-4:00 with nested settlement macro 3:50-4:00 (2024 krdRxohMI3g; 2025 hc9SDgW93gc), then 3:50-4:00 as the MOC itself and can continue to 4:14 (2026 PP1-i0ti_tQ). 
4. Window length: nearly all sources say 20 minutes, but 6ZFkXGo_Wjo (Apr 2025) is dossier-summarized as 'sensitive 30-minute window... stop listening to people that tell you there's a 20-minute after the open' (ambiguous, probably about the opening range) and 3:15-3:45 is 30 minutes.
5. Role of the window: 2023 = rebalance/reprice into the opening range gap before the Silver Bullet (fXVJnBVizYY, Sf_uYZBWTrA); 2024 = place FVG/IFVG trades and trail inside it, exit into liquidity before it ends (dossier-inferred rules for ylzrm3dZGWw, rn32EntwGCs); 2025 = adds immediate rebalance, 10:00 low-hanging-fruit target and IOFED; 2026 = octant/quadrant time-and-price grid, 'no volume needed', and explicitly not limited to the window ('you don't have to take trades only in macro time', 4SJlJdIANCo). The 2026-09-28 trade entered at 10:55 and was held to about 12:15, contradicting the 2024 'close before the window ends' reading, and PP1-i0ti_tQ says the MOC move can run past 4:00.
6. Management differs by day: pyramid 12 to 18 lots inside the macro (Fv3gNx9ta0I), pyramid 20 to 25 (9HUAUF_h2tI), versus de-risking down to one runner in a high-resistance run (dWyXLze4c4k).
7. Source reliability: the silent-video dossiers (ylzrm3dZGWw, rn32EntwGCs, qW0_Mxfp_Z4, EwYBWf0fJxM, Fv3gNx9ta0I, odS7IIktqOY, 9HUAUF_h2tI, _Ts5bpglOdU) have no spoken words; their 'Verbatim Quote' cells are bracketed descriptions or chart text, not ICT's words, so none are used. Some cells in fXVJnBVizYY look paraphrased. Several timestamps look unreliable (e.g. hc9SDgW93gc stop quote at 01:06 in a 33 minute video).
8. A 6:50-7:10 macro is only supported by one garbled quote in which he says critics think it 'supposedly never exists'; 5:50 and 9:04 pre-market macros each have one source.
macros.markets: About 26 distinct trades tied to a named macro window across about 30 dossiers (the same trade shown in several videos is counted once; Aug 30 2024 appears in odS7IIktqOY, HM2M9a4OEFQ and krdRxohMI3g; the 2026-09-28 trade in KhnKA8Uu0n8 and UVVmS0de0g0; 4hkZEQiB02U is counted with BdmULCuem5Q). Of the 8 starting videos: Sf_uYZBWTrA (ES short, 9:50), ylzrm3dZGWw (NQ long, 10:50), xGn4UxJiz9M (NQ long, MOC), rn32EntwGCs (NQ short, 2:50), hc9SDgW93gc (NQ 10-lot short, MOC), 4hkZEQiB02U (NQ long, lunch macro, review), UVVmS0de0g0 (NQ long, 10:50, review) show a trade each; fXVJnBVizYY is theory only. Markets: NQ about 22 (also MNQ paper shorts, 2 executions in sPKglrJAVFY, not counted), ES 3 (Sf_uYZBWTrA, qW0_Mxfp_Z4, 7zlblhLGraA), GBPUSD 1 (demo, London 2:50 AM macro). Windows with trades: 7:50, 8:50 (PPI), 9:50 (AM and Asian 9:50 PM), 10:50, 11:50-12:30 lunch, 12:30/12:50, 1:50, 2:50, MOC. Execution chart is almost always 1m (15s refinement, 5m context). Every macro trade shown is a win (winners-only selection), so no hit rate can be derived.

rules.rule: Definition (first codified in the 2023 mentorship): a macro is a short list of directives the algorithm runs in a fixed clock window to seek liquidity or inefficiencies. It is a time filter, not a pattern.
rules.quote: A macro is a short list of directives that the algorithm will run. It's like a small little list of orders that it has to do to then seek where liquidity and or if inefficiencies are.

rules.rule: What the macro does: during the window price will spool, meaning move and run for liquidity (2:50-3:10 example from the 2024 PM session review).
rules.quote: 2:50 to 3:10 macro, and it's just a time when the market will spool and run for liquidity.

rules.rule: A macro is about price movement (spooling), not about buying or selling volume. Volume or order flow is irrelevant to detecting it, so a price-only detector is consistent with his statement (2026).
rules.quote: It's simply when the price will spool. That means movement. And you do not need a lot of volume to make price move. You just need one contract

rules.rule: 2026 stance: the Market-On-Close macro alone is enough to build a career on; he calls these small surgical strikes.
rules.quote: I mentioned market on close macro, you can do your entire career with just market on close macro

rules.rule: General schedule (Jan 2024): real macros run from 10 minutes before the top of every hour to 10 minutes after. The 3:00-4:00 PM hour holds four macros (2:50-3:10, 3:15-3:45, MOC 3:45 or 3:50 to 4:00).
rules.quote: Mentioned times of macros and and such and I mentioned how the real macros are 10 minutes to the top of the hour every hour to 10 minutes after there are four macros in the last hour trading between 3:00 and 4:00 Eastern Standard Time.

rules.rule: Same schedule restated the day before: every macro is :50 to :10 around the hour, except the odd one in the last hour.
rules.quote: There are four specific macros in that 1 hour time frame. Every single macro apart from that one is only 10 minutes till the top of the hour to 10 minutes after the hour.

rules.rule: 2026 explanation of the window shape: the last 10 minutes of one hour plus the first 10 minutes of the next (10:50-11:10 example).
rules.quote: trading down into the macro 1050 1110. It's the last 10 minutes of the hour and the first 10 minutes of the new hour

rules.rule: Pre-market 6:50-7:10 AM ET macro exists in his chart set (Jan 2025 lecture). The quote text is a garbled transcript with an editor bracket, and he adds that it 'supposedly never exists', so he is answering critics.
rules.quote: trading up into the 650 to 610 a.m. [7:10 a.m.] Eastern time macro that supposedly never exists

rules.rule: Pre-market 7:50-8:10 AM ET is 'my macro time'; price traded into a quadrant level and reversed on the tick (Oct 2025).
rules.quote: we come back right back down in during the macro 750 Eastern time to 8:10 that's my macro time.

rules.rule: 9:50-10:10 AM morning macro: it hunts volume imbalances and fair value gaps, then price displaces away (Oct 2024 review).
rules.quote: 9:50 to 10:10 macro and then price displaces trades the sell side back down.

rules.rule: A macro low or high can form at the very end of the window (the 10:10 candle was the low of the 9:50-10:10 macro, 2026).
rules.quote: it's occurring during 9:50 to 10:10 macro. What's the lowest candle here? 10:10.

rules.rule: Lunch macro of 11:30-1:30 contains the 11:50-12:10 macro, where the algorithm starts work and 'spooling' should show a willingness to take opposing liquidity (2026).
rules.quote: Here's your buy side during the 11:50 a.m. to 12:10 macro. That's when the algorithm will start to do its work. It'll start spooling.

rules.rule: 12:50-1:10 PM macro starts the afternoon run (April 2026 review).
rules.quote: The run starts here at 12:50. That's the 12:50 1:10 macro time. It starts dropping off.

rules.rule: 1:50-2:10 PM macro delivered a low (Sept 2024 review of the Aug 30 PM trade).
rules.quote: 1:50 and 2:10 macro, look at that beautiful delivery right there, boom, right at the low.

rules.rule: 2024 close schedule: Market-On-Close macro 3:45-4:00 and a nested Settlement macro 3:50-4:00 (last 10 minutes).
rules.quote: Market on close macro which is 3:45 to 4:00, and then we have the settlement macro which is the last 10 minutes which is 3:50 to 4:00, and there's your macros for the people that want to know what they are.

rules.rule: 2025 lecture: MOC macro is 3:45-4:00 PM.
rules.quote: At 3:45 to 4:00 that's our macro, Market on Close macro

rules.rule: 2026 lecture changes the MOC start to 3:50 PM (10-minute script window).
rules.quote: So the market on close macro, it begins at 3:50 Eastern time. Okay? So 3:50 p.m. New York local time starts that.

rules.rule: 2026: what happens in the MOC macro can continue past 4:00 (he says 3:14 but means the 4:14 PM settlement), so the window end is not a hard exit.
rules.quote: Now, many times whatever takes place at the macro of 350 to 4:00, it can continue beyond that to 3:14.

rules.rule: Lunch-macro prerequisite: a one-directional morning move that never took a minor swing high/low sets up a retracement back into that range. Bias for the macro run is the retracement/rebalance direction.
rules.quote: notice that no short-term high was taken in any of this drop when that occurs you're setting yourself up to see a retracement going back in that range.

rules.rule: 2023 9:50 repricing macro: after a Judas swing away from the opening range gap, expect the algorithm to reprice back into the gap (to its 50%).
rules.quote: I'm going to anticipate the algorithm repricing back down into the opening range gap

rules.rule: MOC counter-case: when retail sentiment is already trapped on one side, the algorithm needs no retracement before it runs the other way.
rules.quote: no need for it to drop down because the sentiment has been to the downside

rules.rule: Macro logic: price has already taken liquidity and rebalanced inefficiency; then it starts its run for the opposing liquidity. The setup is taken liquidity plus filled gap, then run to the opposite pool.
rules.quote: so two functions of delivery of price have been met: seeking liquidity and inefficiency. It has balanced this out here, and then it starts its run for the opposing side of liquidity.

rules.rule: Mark 10:00 AM as a time filter; the first swing high (or low) printed after 10:00 becomes the lunch-macro low-hanging-fruit objective.
rules.quote: your time filter is 10:00 a.m. so at 10:00 in the morning put a vertical line on that

rules.rule: 2026: the daily or session extreme comes from agreement between a standard-deviation projection and a pool of liquidity (his example was the RTH opening range gap -2.0 deviation lined up with a prior daily low).
rules.quote: The only thing we're going to be doing is we're going to get an agreement with standard deviation and a pool of liquidity. That's what daily highs and lows work off of.

rules.rule: Final-hour macros: aim at smooth relative equal highs (or lows), because stops sit there.
rules.quote: We're targeting relative equal highs for the last hour trading. Notice this is smooth compared to the jaggedness down here

rules.rule: 2026 time-and-price grid: horizontal levels are octants/quadrants of the dealing range, and the vertical axis is the macro start time. A PD array should form at each octant or quadrant level.
rules.quote: Every single time we get to an octant or a quadrant level, you're looking for a PDA to form.

rules.rule: Once the clock enters the macro, price must start to spool in the direction of the narrative; if it does, you have your cue (Jan 2025).
rules.quote: Then we are in macro time now so price should start spoiling what direction: lower.

rules.rule: Half-split rule (2026): if no spooling shows in the first half of the window, expect the last 10 minutes to spool and run, and be positioned. Subjective: the amount that counts as spooling is not defined.
rules.quote: the last 10 minutes of that macro, it's going to spool. It's going to run. And I want to be in there

rules.rule: The candle that opens the macro is the activation point (3:50 MOC); the move is time-driven, not supply/demand, Wyckoff or footprint driven.
rules.quote: And on this very candle that starts the 350 macro, the algorithm starts running. What is it using? Is it using supply and demand? Is it using Wyckoff? Is it using level two footprint? volume profile? No.

rules.rule: Confirmation of real macro delivery: displacement with speed and magnitude, meaning elongating large-bodied candles in the run direction.
rules.quote: Want to see speed and magnitude, that means the candles should start elongating, becoming large black stretched-out candles. We want to see black limousines taking it downtown.

rules.rule: Immediate rebalance entry: an expansion candle leaves a BISI/SIBI, the next candle dips straight into it and closes back out, and he buys it at market inside the 10:50 macro (Feb 2025).
rules.quote: this is a New York launch macro trade and cover all the details as we go I'm going along here also on an immediate rebalance so you can see how that came down closed in and I'm annotating the buy balance sell efficiency.

rules.rule: IOFED entry: re-enter a partial fair value gap fill during macro time and expect immediate expansion to the limit target.
rules.quote: That's institutional order flow entry drill, which is an entry into a partial fair value gap and we should see expansion to the downside and hit that limit order.

rules.rule: Inversion fair value gap entry inside the 10:50-11:10 macro after repeated taps into buy-side liquidity (Oct 2025 example).
rules.quote: inversion fair gap macro 1050 1110 trading at the closing prices third stage of smart money shorting at all-time high and one more tap into that buy side and it careens lower

rules.rule: 2026: entries may come just before the window; the macro is a sweet indication, not a strict entry gate.
rules.quote: you can short it just ahead of the macro. You don't have to take trades only in macro time.

rules.rule: 2026: a trade outside the exact window is fine if it is in sync with the macro that started the run.
rules.quote: this is not Oh, you're trading outside of the macro time. No, you're trading in sync with the macro that started this run

rules.rule: 9:50 repricing short with two stacked gaps (2023 Two Gap Rule): stop just above the 50% (CE) of the higher gap.
rules.quote: I'm finding half of that or 50% of it, consequent encroachment, and I place my stop loss just above that

rules.rule: Long on a BISI in the 10:50 macro: price must stay in the upper half of the imbalance, otherwise he trails the stop up or is wrong; the stop sits below the low of the rebalancing displacement candle.
rules.quote: I want to see price stay in the upper half of that blue shaded area I'm bringing the stop loss up because if it goes down there I'm [wrong].

rules.rule: Inversion FVG long (London macro): hold above the 50%; the stop sits in the lower half of the inversion gap.
rules.quote: I want to see it stay above the consequent encroachment or midpoint of that, and notice my stop loss is in the lower half of that inversion fair value gap in orange.

rules.rule: Volume-imbalance short in the lunch macro (June 2024): stop just above the open of the key candle.
rules.quote: in fact I'm going to take that stop and place it just above the opening on that

rules.rule: MOC short (2026): stop one to two ticks beyond the candle extreme.
rules.quote: candlestick's high plus a tick or two. That's a really good place to put a stop loss.

rules.rule: Lunch / 10:50 macro objective is the first high that forms after 10:00 AM.
rules.quote: we're inside of the 1050 1110 macro and that is the high I'm aiming for

rules.rule: Codified low-hanging-fruit objective of the lunch macro: first swing high after the 10:00 AM line.
rules.quote: that's the lunch macro that's exactly the low-hanging fruit objective for the lunch macro.

rules.rule: MOC short: price should rip through the displacement gap and trade straight to the minor sellside pool.
rules.quote: just rip through it and trade down to that minor sellside liquidity pool.

rules.rule: 3:15-3:45 / final-hour: find the smooth highs or lows; the run stops at the smooth edge.
rules.quote: Notice the time it's happening at 3:30. It's algorithmic. Sweet spot between 3:15 and 3:45's macro. Find where it's smooth. And notice where it stopped going. It stopped going lower. Left smooth edges on the upside.

rules.rule: Trail the stop to cover commissions (no loss), then take the trade off at the target (MOC long, Jan 2024).
rules.quote: trading and that would cover commissions and no loss would be incurred we get above 52 I'll take it off

rules.rule: Place the stop at the structure and do not widen it; target the nearest short-term low with a gap or volume imbalance (MOC lecture).
rules.quote: Now I'm going to place my stop loss there. Notice I do not move that stop higher. And I'm going to target that little short-term low there with a fair value gap, volume imbalance included.

rules.rule: Once the trail stop is set, stick to it; do not move it back out (2026).
rules.quote: while the transaction's open you don't see me moving my stop loss up once I adjust it. It's just a good practice once you commit to a lower trail stop loss to stick to it.

rules.rule: Take a partial, lock the stop in structure, then walk away from the chart (Jan 2025).
rules.quote: One partial has been taken again, so now I'm in a position where I don't care if it stops me out, but if it continues that's all the better, and I have to walk away from the charts at this time.

rules.rule: Clean MOC delivery should not return to touch the imbalance on the next candle; a candle that comes back to retest it weakens the macro read.
rules.quote: in the perfect world it should not come back on the next candle to even come back and touch it

rules.rule: On parabolic trend days the lunch macro retracement to the 10 AM level may never happen, so do not wait for or force it.
rules.quote: Notice there's no lunchtime macro. No retracement back to here's 10 a.m. Find a low

rules.rule: Skip news-driver releases (NFP, FOMC): manual intervention overrides the algorithm, so macro logic is suspended into the 8:30 release.
rules.quote: it's like FOMC, a manual intervention where they literally override normal flow. You're encouraged not to try to trade it going into the release.

rules.rule: Only his listed times count as macros; invented times such as 10:40 are not macros.
rules.quote: don't call it a macro. Call it something else cuz macros are not like that.

rules.rule: The macro works on Forex too (London 2:50-3:10 AM, GBPUSD, demo trade on the 1-minute chart).
rules.quote: We're presently inside of the 2:50 AM 3:10 AM macro, and yes it works on Forex. So I'm going to be buying here inside of a reclaimed BISI fair value gap.

rules.rule: He prefers the Nasdaq index future for macro trading because it moves better than Forex (Oct 2025).
rules.quote: it doesn't have high probability one direction over the other. So, that's why I stick with the NASDAQ. And it's really moving better than Forex anyway

retail_traps.summary: Textbook patterns (bracketed-range breakouts, bull/bear flags, 3-touch trendlines, head and shoulders, double tops/bottoms, oscillator divergence) are stop pools: when higher-timeframe premium/discount and order flow point the other way, wait for the retail breakout to sweep the stops and then trade the opposite way toward the liquidity on the other side.
retail_traps.needs_clock: No for the core rules. Nothing in the pattern-fade quotes depends on time of day or a session. It needs only: equal-high/low and range-boundary detection, a sweep-and-close-back test, a higher-timeframe premium/discount bias and an opposing liquidity target. On 24/7 synthetic indices the higher timeframe must be built from fixed N-bar aggregation or a rolling swing range instead of calendar days. Clock items exist but are optional overlays: London Judas swing after midnight (XwYYWBttWro 13:57) and, in a sibling consolidation-day model (hzoMJQlEv5M), a 3-4 PM false breakout. Two caveats: his daily and weekly levels come from calendar candles, and on synthetic feeds there are no real resting retail stops, so the thesis becomes an empirical pattern that needs out-of-sample testing.
retail_traps.how_to_code: Common skeleton (price only). 1) Higher-timeframe bias: resample bars into an HTF series (N-bar aggregation on synthetics). Take the latest HTF dealing range (swing high and low), set equilibrium at 50%, label premium above and discount below, and optionally mark the nearest unmitigated HTF order block or FVG. Pattern direction that agrees with the HTF read is skipped. 2) Detect the retail pattern on the lower timeframe and compute its stop pool. Bracketed range: N bars inside a band under k times ATR with two or more touches each side; pools sit just above the high body and below the low body (pv2 says body, not wick). Double top/bottom: two fractal highs/lows within a tolerance (subjective, e.g. 0.1 to 0.25 ATR); pool just beyond. Flag: displacement leg (impulse of k ATR or more), then 5 to 20 bars drifting against it with a shallow retrace; pool beyond the flag boundary. Three-touch trendline: line through three fractal lows or highs with tolerance; mark the fractal between touch two and three. Head and shoulders: LS/head/RS fractals with a neckline through the two troughs; pool beyond the neckline; target is the head extreme. Divergence phantom: price higher high with an oscillator (e.g. RSI) lower high; pool above the high. 3) Trigger: price pierces the pool boundary, then closes back inside, or breaks structure the other way, within m bars. 4) Entry: after the displacement, enter on the retrace into the order block / FVG formed by the reversal (dossier-derived: 0.7697 15m OB; he also says buy the stops below the neckline). 5) Target: the opposite pool (range high, equal highs, head extreme, or retail stops), plus either 10 to 20 pips beyond (2017 fixed rule) or a measured move equal to the range depth (owq30). 6) Stop: no quote exists for this model. gq2Q2y4ch9k's trade table says below the manipulation low, and the sibling model hzoMJQlEv5M says above the swing high that swept liquidity; code beyond the sweep extreme and flag it as inferred. 7) Invalidation: HTF or intermarket (DXY/SMT) confirms the pattern direction, or price accepts beyond the sweep (closes beyond and holds) instead of returning. Subjective parts: tolerance for equal, line fitting, what counts as a flag or head and shoulders, mature versus immature trend, what makes an HTF order block valid, sweep depth, and when to treat a double top as a target (2017) versus fade it after the sweep (2022).
retail_traps.changes_over_time: 1) Dating: Month 02-04 core videos were uploaded Aug-Sep 2022 but dossiers place them in 2016 (case studies use 2015-2016 dates), forex only, built on daily order blocks, breakers and premium/discount. 2) 2017 style differs: he trades OTE longs in the NY window toward a double top and says "double tops I don't believe in I like to see them targeted" (lbAQNxRPXMs 06:59), so the pattern is a draw, not a fade; he coins Candyland for equal lows (uiszrzGyUqU 10/27/17) and scorns shorting bearish divergence (pcw_ty0hqoo 01:34). 3) Sweep depth conflict: fixed 10-20 pips beyond the level (lbAQNxRPXMs 04:26; dIT4HTFYGGo 19:04 says 10 pips below equal lows and 20 above) versus range-depth measured moves (owq30ATPU5s 00:13:48, 48-pip example). 4) He uses a measured-move projection as his own target tool (owq30) while calling the retail flag measured move the trap (cRbPS3uxkj4). 5) cRbPS3uxkj4 says the false flag applies in mature trends or HTF distribution; the dossier summary says flags can work in immature trends but gives no quote. 6) 2018-2021: the same idea is retold for Bitcoin trendlines (RjFRTOKGviU), EURUSD in the Instagram Logic video (Ic1rqvbk99c 04:15) and IPDA framing; the rule is always sweep the pool then reverse. 7) 2023: Candyland becomes priming levels that respect resistance before news (DVxC7UAHzwk), and the Dec 2023 NQ fake bear flag (gq2Q2y4ch9k) has no HTF order block context in its dossier; its Rules table is only IMPLIED descriptions with no spoken quote, so nothing from it was used as a quote. 8) 2024: fRS8m-wShIo uses a fake double bottom absorbed into an inversion FVG as supporting evidence for a 30s NQ short rather than as the trade. 9) Dossier quality: the 2022 core dossiers are summarised with spliced quotes (timestamps like [01:26]-[01:38], [03:00]-[03:06]), so some quotes here are contiguous sub-parts of those cells; no stop quote exists for this model; the dossier rules sections (e.g. entry on the retest of the 15m order block, enter long after a sweep and return inside the range) are summaries, not his words."
retail_traps.markets: Count of 9 = 1 formal trade-table entry (gq2Q2y4ch9k, 2023-12-15 NQ 1m fake bear flag, long from the false-breakdown low into buy-side liquidity, win) + 8 worked case-study walk-throughs in the 2022-uploaded 2016-era core videos: USDJPY (pv2-R-STviA, 1 multi-stage accumulation), AUDUSD false bull flag and false bear flag (cRbPS3uxkj4, 2), GBPUSD trendline traps Dec 2015 and May 2016 (o8NfSK-pUlE, 2), GBPUSD head-and-shoulders and inverted H&S (w8lbrvZXUVY, 3 incl. the 1.5502 Oct 18 order block). owq30ATPU5s, Xae0VrbkyFk and XwYYWBttWro show no trades. Adjacent uses, not counted: lbAQNxRPXMs (2017, two OTE longs into a double top / equal highs, both wins), fRS8m-wShIo (2024-05-24 NQ 30s short with a fake double bottom absorbed into an inversion FVG). Markets: FX majors (USDJPY, AUDUSD, GBPUSD, EURUSD, USDCAD), Bitcoin (RjFRTOKGviU, 2018), ES (DVxC7UAHzwk, 2023 Candyland), NQ (2023-2024). Timeframes: patterns on 15m/1H against daily/4H arrays in 2016-era; 1m and 30s on NQ in 2023-24.

rules.rule: Flag patterns are suspect when they form in a mature trend or at a higher-timeframe distribution level (false bull flag in premium). Retail sees continuation; he expects a reversal. The dossier summary adds that flags can still work early in an immature trend, but that is not a quote.
rules.quote: In a mature bull trend or in higher timeframe distribution levels, price will print a false bull flag. Retail traders see this as a classic continuation buy pattern, but it many times results in a reversal.

rules.rule: Use the trap trade only when a textbook pattern is on the chart AND the higher-timeframe premise points the opposite way to what the pattern implies.
rules.quote: What I'm actually going to tell you is how you can capitalize on these patterns when they appear in charts and our higher timeframe premise indicates the opposite direction is unfolding.

rules.rule: Bias comes from a top-down read of the higher timeframe as premium or discount, not from the pattern. Pattern direction that agrees with premium/discount is not faded.
rules.quote: There's going to be times when we break our market down from a top-down perspective by defining the market in terms of discount or premium

rules.rule: Look for the pattern because retail looks for it, then fade it in the direction justified by higher-timeframe institutional order flow (daily/4H order block, breaker).
