rules.quote: You look for the pattern because retail will look for the pattern, but you're going to fade that pattern based on what you see on the higher timeframes. We look for institutional order flow to justify why this should be bearish.

rules.rule: Principle behind the trendline trap: price ignores diagonal lines and only reacts to where liquidity rests. A trendline is never the reason for a trade.
rules.quote: Price has no awareness of your trend line. Price doesn't respect what you have on your charts. Price only respects where the actual liquidity is in the marketplace.

rules.rule: General mechanism: obvious support/resistance (and the patterns drawn on it) lets orders pile up. Once enough are trapped, price cleans out those stops and then runs the true direction.
rules.quote: Market makers allow orders to build up around obvious support and resistance levels. Once enough orders are trapped, the algorithm expands, cleans out those stops, and runs in the true direction.

rules.rule: Bracketed range: breakout traders put buy stops above the range high and sell stops below the range low. Those two pools are the setup. The dossier adds that he anchors them to candle bodies, not extreme wicks.
rules.quote: Neophyte traders or breakout traders will bracket the trading range in price with orders

rules.rule: Equal highs or a double top hold buy stops just above them (the mirror holds for double bottoms and sell stops). The pool is the target, not resistance.
rules.quote: You know there's going to be buy stops above this high, especially above an equal high or double top.

rules.rule: Textbook double top: retail shorts with a protective buy stop just above the highs, expecting the low to hold as support. That stop is the pool.
rules.quote: Retail says 'let's get short and put a protective buy stop above these highs.' And they're looking for the market to trade down into this low because support bounced.

rules.rule: False flag setup: a quick rally into a consolidation that looks like a bull flag, inside an area of heavy higher-timeframe distribution, is not treated as bullish.
rules.quote: When we get into areas of heavy distribution like this and we see a quick rally up in a consolidation which would look like a bull flag, we don't see that as a bullish scenario.

rules.rule: Candyland: obvious equal lows (or double/triple bottom) on the daily chart are sell-side liquidity ripe to be taken, then paired with an optimal trade entry. Same word is used for equal highs in 2023.
rules.quote: if you look at the daily chart it had a really obvious equal lows I teach that as candyland it's just ripe for the taking sell side liquidity

rules.rule: Divergence phantom: price makes a higher high while the oscillator makes a lower high. Retail shorts it, which stacks buy stops above the high.
rules.quote: Price makes a higher high like this, and the indicator makes a lower high. Retail gets excited to short, but it's a phantom divergence.

rules.rule: False breakout trigger (bullish regime): price is sent below the range low to run the sell stops. The sweep is the trigger, not a breakdown signal.
rules.quote: Market makers will typically send price below the range to neutralize the sell stops.

rules.rule: Once the range low breaks, the resting sell stops supply the counterparty orders smart money buys; the long is paired with them.
rules.quote: When the market breaks below the consolidation, those sell stops are used to pair long orders.

rules.rule: False flag trigger: he waits for the flag to make a false move and then break the other way (a close back through the flag plus a break of structure is the usual coded form). Bear flag mirrors this.
rules.quote: What we're doing is looking for it to create a false move and break lower.

rules.rule: Head and shoulders in a bullish higher-timeframe regime: the neckline break is a turtle-soup long that takes out the equal/clean lows, not a new selling leg. The inverted pattern in a bearish regime is the mirror (breakout above the neckline is a buy-stop raid).
rules.quote: When that neckline is broken, I don't see that pullback as a resuming lower or a new selling scenario. I see that as a Turtle Soup Long that took out two previous lows where clean lows were there

rules.rule: Trendline trap trigger: on the third touch of an ascending trendline, watch the swing high formed between touch two and touch three (mirror for descending trendlines).
rules.quote: When that third touch of that uptrend line is seen in price action, many times I get dialed in expecting the high that forms between the low at the second time it hits the trend line and the third time it hits the trend line

rules.rule: Cross-market filter for FX false breakouts: an upside breakout in a foreign currency that the dollar index does not confirm is a false breakout (retail candyland).
rules.quote: When you see what would otherwise look like strength and breakouts on the upside in foreign currencies, always double-check them with the dollar index. If you don't see that, then you know that the false breakout on the upside in foreign currencies

rules.rule: Trendline trap entry: aim at the high between touch two and three, using a bearish order block or a turtle soup there, with the daily/4H array opposing the trendline.
rules.quote: that high in between, I aim in that high for a bear order block or a turtle soup.

rules.rule: Head and shoulders fade entry: buy the sell stops under the equal lows or neckline in a bullish regime. The same sentence names the target, the head, which is why it is also listed under target in the rule summary.
rules.quote: I'll buy the sell stops below those equal lows or where the neckline is, and then I'll look for the head or highest peak to be violated.

rules.rule: False flag entry: after the flag fails to the downside and the structure breaks, the short is taken. The dossier summary (not a quote) places the short on the retest of the new 15m bearish order block (0.7697 AUDUSD example).
rules.quote: and we're able to see what everyone else with a retail-minded perspective would see in terms of continuation on the upside, but when we see it break down, we know we can sell it short.

rules.rule: False breakout target: after the sell-stop sweep, price expands to the liquidity above the old high to scale out the longs.
rules.quote: So naturally, they're going to expand price up to the liquidity above the old high to scale out their long positions.

rules.rule: Smart money exits where buyers are, so the buy stops and breakout buyers above the highs are the objective (mirror for shorts below lows).
rules.quote: They have to get out in a place where there's willing participants to buy. Buyers are always above the highs, either in the form of a buying breakout or buy stops on short positions.

rules.rule: Divergence phantom: the retail stops (above the high that shows divergence) are the target.
rules.quote: We can reverse engineer that thought: see where retail traders think divergence means a reversal, and use their stops as targets.

rules.rule: Measured move: project the prior price swing (the consolidation or double-bottom/top range) to get the target for the run.
rules.quote: In the marketplace there is a pretty recurring phenomenon that takes place about measured moves. This price swing here projected up gives us the target.

rules.rule: How far the stop run goes is set by the size of the range inside the double bottom or consolidation (48-pip example).
rules.quote: It's moving that far based on the movement inside of the double bottom or inside the consolidation before the double top is run.

rules.rule: 2017 version of the overshoot: price usually runs about 10 to 20 pips beyond a previous high or low, a fixed-distance rule.
rules.quote: I teach that price generally will reach about 10 to 20 pips above a previous high or low

rules.rule: When the double top is the objective, take the exit a little early at the institutional level just under it instead of waiting for the exact pool. This is his 2017 GBPUSD scalp that targeted a double top.
rules.quote: I like to get out a little early hence 131 80 it's institutional level I know I'll get a really good exit on that and there it was

rules.rule: Do not fade when the intermarket picture confirms the move (dollar index makes the lower low while the foreign currency makes the higher high): reversals are low probability. This is his reversal-pattern rule applied to this model, not a retail-trap quote.
rules.quote: When the dollar index makes a lower low and foreign currencies make a higher high, this confirms current price action and the underlying trend is likely to continue. The idea of stalking reversal patterns in this condition is not highly probable

rules.rule: 2016-era core lesson: pattern on a lower timeframe (1H or 15m in the dossier case studies) read against a daily order block. A 1H head and shoulders is bought because the daily bullish order block should send price higher.
rules.quote: retail traders are going to see that as a selling scenario. We do not expect that, because on the daily chart we're expecting the bullish order block to send prices higher.

rules.rule: Applied outside FX: on Bitcoin (Dec 2018) a retail diagonal support line is expected to be rolled through toward buy-side imbalance after a bearish breaker.
rules.quote: Retail traders are going to see this as a supposed diagonal support line or quote-unquote bullish trendline. It's a fallacy. Bitcoin will roll through this and aggressively make a move to the buy-side imbalance.

rules.rule: Only time statement tied to the stop-run idea in the assigned set: the London Judas swing runs stops after midnight. It is a session overlay, not a requirement of the pattern-fade rules.
rules.quote: After midnight, there is a manipulation that takes place in the form of a Judas Swing in London. What is it doing? It's making the high or low of the day by running stops, setting up the real move into New York.

macro_qualifiers.summary: Higher-timeframe fundamental and intermarket filters (interest-rate differentials, 10-year yields vs the Dollar Index, COT commercial ranges, open interest vs its seasonal average, seasonal curves, relative-strength divergence, commodity carrying-charge/premium spreads) that set direction for position and swing trades, which are then executed from HTF PD arrays.
macro_qualifiers.needs_clock: No intraday clock. Nothing here depends on time of day or sessions. The inputs are calendar and higher-timeframe: month-of-year / day-of-year for seasonals and low-magnitude months (March, June, August; May-October for stocks; July-August scale-back), weekly COT data, daily/weekly open interest, and a roughly 3-month quarterly-shift horizon. Most of the layer cannot run on 24/7 synthetic indices using price delivery alone. COT, open interest, central-bank rate differentials, 10-year yields, carrying-charge/calendar spreads and commodity seasonals all need external real-market data, and synthetic indices have no commercials, no contract months, no interest rates and no real seasonality. Only two pieces are price-only: (1) the 'two of four asset classes trending' check, which could be recast as 'N of the correlated indices are trending', and (2) the relative-strength/SMT divergence test (reference makes a new extreme, the other instrument fails to confirm). Caveat: independently generated synthetic streams have no real economic correlation, so any divergence signal would have to be validated empirically and has no ICT rationale there.
macro_qualifiers.how_to_code:
This is a directional-bias layer that gates a separate entry model; the dossiers give no stop or target of its own. Entries use HTF order blocks, FVGs, OTE and discount/premium arrays on D/W/M. Suggested detection:
1) Data feeds: weekly CFTC commercial net position (long minus short); daily open interest; ZB/ZN/ZF and DXY price series; policy rates per currency; 15/20/40-year day-of-year seasonal curves per symbol; nearby and deferred contract prices.
2) COT index: for lookbacks L = 6, 12, 24 and 48 months compute idx = (net - min_L)/(max_L - min_L). The 2022/2024 version is bullish above 0.5 (12-month midpoint) and bearish below. A 'macro extreme' is a new 24- or 48-month max/min, which overrides shorter programs. A 'cyclical' buy program is the net short contracting toward the top of its 12-month range even while below zero. The older 2017 version just used the sign of net versus zero. For USD-base pairs invert the futures signal (6C bearish means USDCAD bullish). Gate the signal on a prior liquidity raid of the HTF swing.
3) Open interest: oi_change = OI / OI[n bars ago] - 1 and oi_gap = OI - mean(OI at the same calendar week over the prior N years). Bullish: price inside an HTF support / discount array and oi_change <= -10% to -15% (or oi_gap clearly negative) while consolidating. Bearish: price at an HTF resistance / premium array and OI rising above its seasonal average while consolidating. Use daily/weekly only.
4) Seasonal: build the average return curve per calendar window and require the 15-year and 40-year curves to agree. Valid only if the weekly trend of the last two years agrees. Failed-seasonal flag: price makes lower lows inside a bullish seasonal window (and the mirror) means a strong opposite bias. Calendar filters: cut size in Jul-Aug, avoid new stock campaigns in Mar/Jun/Aug, treat May-Oct as low magnitude.
5) Rates: diff = rate[base] - rate[quote]; the high-yield currency is the long side only after price retraces into an HTF discount array. Direction version: falling ZB/ZN (rising yields) gives DXY long / foreign short, the reverse for rallying bonds. Triad / SMT: compare swing highs and lows of ZB, ZN, ZF in the window where DXY is at its order block; flag when at least one maturity fails to confirm another's new extreme, and also when DXY makes a new extreme that ZN fails to confirm.
6) Relative strength: for reference R (DXY) and asset A, flag accumulation when R prints a higher high and A fails to print a lower low (the dossier states the mirror for distribution). Rank a universe by the count of non-confirmations and keep only the top 3-5 leaders. For stocks use higher-low-versus-Dow plus a bullish seasonal window.
7) Aggregate: score = signed sum of the qualifiers; require qualifiers from at least 2 of 3 tiers and at least 2 of 4 asset classes trending. Then run the entry model only in the allowed direction.
Management comes from the Month 05/Charter material: risk at most 1%, trail behind daily swing lows, scale out at intermediate PD arrays, stop-reduction ladder (25/50/75% of the objective), about a 3-month horizon.
Subjective parts: what counts as an 'extreme' (he gives no percentile), what is 'key' HTF support/resistance, whether the 10-15% OI drop is over days, weeks or the whole consolidation, what counts as 'trending' or 'alignment' between the 10-year note and DXY, how to read the seasonal composite images, how to weigh 15- versus 40-year curves, and whether a triad failure needs one or two maturities (dossier summary says one).
macro_qualifiers.changes_over_time:
COT benchmark changes over time and is inconsistent. In the 2017-12-22 video (aWgYCfvnlqM) and the 2021 Market Maker series (Vh0NtdPPj1M, 'commercials being above the zero line') the zero line is the bullish/bearish divider. But uxsmSMsuleY (2017-12-17, five days earlier) already monitors 12-month commercial extremes. In the 2022 Core Content (Hoo_wTMgdcY, 9H4iaaQXV5Y) he explicitly says not to read it against the zero line: use the 12-month range halved at 50%, plus 6-month, 2-year and 4-year ranges, and even net-short-below-zero can hold tradable buy programs. In Jan 2024 (E0sA_SWIxKM 32:51) he still halves the commercial extreme to find equilibrium.
Open interest is used two ways: (a) a 10-15% drop at support (Hoo_wTMgdcY) and (b) actual OI versus the multi-year seasonal average (qRYkTWePXF0). It is also used just to pick which contract month to follow at rollover (YMt87VQRpNM 2020, ZpSwaiwGgt0 2023), which is unrelated to bias.
Rate differential (level of rates, w6VlX-rsTUs, Vh0NtdPPj1M) versus rate direction (bond futures / yields falling or rising, MJwWUd_FM-k, 6oQVb0zVxMM, N8_8tEw2_44) are different tools. The triad is 30/10/5-year in 6oQVb0zVxMM but 10-year vs 30-year (plus Bunds) in MJwWUd_FM-k.
Seasonals: in 2021-2022 they are a roadmap that must be qualified by weekly trend, never a trigger (BiRjR_kqBC0, 6Sp-pr3yCkc, Vb6ueaPqut0 warns against entering on a calendar date alone). In 2024 he ties swing/position trades directly to spring (April-May) strength and bearish GBP months, and in 2026 he states seasonal windows more flatly ('we are definitely in our seasonal tendency for lower prices', 20260901-djabvhihIM8; late-August lower prices, 20260824-grcLMbjs-zs). 2026 also adds the failed-seasonal rule (xbtW_0ipuos).
Later teaching de-emphasises these qualifiers. COT is nearly absent from 2023+ commentary apart from the Jan 2024 Charter Model 3. In 2026 (rXgEMIJ1fQg, Rwao8f6oD0Q) he lists commitment of traders and seasonal tendency among the tools that cause analysis paralysis when a student tries to use everything ('If you're not following a model. You're gambling'). The 2023 reviews mostly use seasonals and 10-year yields as risk-sizing and calendar caution (August).
He later pairs COT with a liquidity run. In aWgYCfvnlqM (2017) he says he did not understand institutional order flow when first using COT.
Dossier-quality caveats: the 2022 Month 04/05/10/11 dossiers are summaries. Many 'Verbatim' cells are paraphrases without quote marks (for example the carrying-charge, Month 11 mega-trade and silver/cattle rows), so only quote-marked text was used. Their trade rows are generic, with no price levels. The Williams %R, contrarian-headline and NR3/NR7 volatility filters in the Hoo_wTMgdcY 8-hallmark list sit beside these qualifiers but are separate tools.
macro_qualifiers.markets: Currency futures and spot FX: 6C/USDCAD, 6E/EURUSD, 6B/GBPUSD, 6J/USDJPY, 6A/AUDUSD, NZDUSD, CHF, EURGBP, and the Dollar Index (DXY) as the master anchor. Rates: 30-year bond (ZB), 10-year note (ZN) and yield (TNX), 5-year note (ZF). Commodity futures: soybeans, corn, wheat, cattle, lean hogs, cotton, crude, copper, silver, gold, cocoa. Equities: Dow, ES, NQ and Dow-30 stocks. Trade count: 23 trade-table rows across 21 videos. Only 5 are in the eight starting videos (9H4iaaQXV5Y 2 generic rows, qRYkTWePXF0 1 EURO 2010 long, Vh0NtdPPj1M 2 for USDJPY and GBPUSD longs). 18 more come from related videos (ygtvWKyOzHQ 2, gs3KMgz84yc 1, WsolkBzpDOQ 1, R2NjnYozhdw 2, rlTl8QKpqCU 2, rcO8-nb3S0Q 4, At43V93rnDQ 1, CxwFON8MLB0 1, u5S6Zt1ZIpA 1, 2CWIbdP1kZw 1, H05w52zQGdQ 1, E0sA_SWIxKM 1). Six of the 23 are generic rows with no price levels (9H4iaaQXV5Y x2, gs3KMgz84yc, At43V93rnDQ, CxwFON8MLB0, u5S6Zt1ZIpA). aWgYCfvnlqM, O2Sio7opKxo, BiRjR_kqBC0, w6VlX-rsTUs and 4i_hnoEk6lw show no trade ticket; w6VlX-rsTUs is only the AUDUSD 1,200-pip case study. Most trades are historical case studies, not live tickets. In every row the entry itself comes from an HTF order block or discount/premium array, so the macro layer adds no entry of its own.

rules.rule: Macro, rate-differential, intermarket and seasonal work is his 'big picture' tier; COT/top-down/sentiment is the 'intermediate' tier. He wants at least two of the three tiers (big picture, intermediate, short-term) in agreement before risking capital. These are qualifiers, not triggers.
rules.quote: We break our trading into three perspectives: the big picture perspective, the intermediate-term perspective, and the short-term perspective. You need to have at least two of them in agreement

rules.rule: Qualify a swing trade by requiring at least two of the four asset classes (stocks, commodities, currencies, interest rates) to be trending. In the same lecture (08:26) he groups them: one of commodities/stocks and one of currencies/rates must be trending.
rules.quote: We want at least to have at least half of the four or two of them showing a profile where there's trending environments underway.

rules.rule: A seasonal tendency is a roadmap of past performance, never a guarantee or a stand-alone signal.
rules.quote: Seasonal tendencies are merely a proverbial roadmap of past performance, and they are not to be viewed as a guarantee.

rules.rule: Interest-rate differential: rank central-bank rates, take the currency with the high rate (example: AUD) and couple it against the low-rate currency to choose the pair. The high yielder is the long side, the low yielder the funding side.
rules.quote: You're going to determine the forex pair coupling based on those two respective countries. For an example we're going to assume that the Australian dollar is our selection for our high interest rate.

rules.rule: Order of analysis (2021): the interest-rate differential comes first (which rate is higher, i.e. a positive differential), then he checks commercial positions on the COT report. Majors only.
rules.quote: the precursor the interest rate differential which interest rate is higher than the other one

rules.rule: Read daily 30-year bond / 10-year note futures as the rates barometer. Bond futures rallying means yields falling (bearish for the currency). Bond futures dropping means yields rising, funds buy the dollar, so DXY up and foreign currencies down. He uses this for a 3-6 month outlook.
rules.quote: As the bond market rallies, that's a lowering of interest rates. And when it drops down in the futures market for the bond market, that is an increase in interest rates

rules.rule: Compare the 10-year note move with the Dollar Index direction and look for alignment between them.
rules.quote: Should that be occurring with a bullish or bearish move in the dollar index? You look for alignment between the two.

rules.rule: Explosive, trending currency trades are expected when the 10-year note seasonal tendency is active.
rules.quote: When the 10-year treasury notes seasonal tendency is in effect, that's when you see currency trades that are explosive and trending.

rules.rule: Multi-market confirmation for position trades: stocks, interest rates, commodities and currencies should all support the outlook.
rules.quote: All four of them together (the stock market, interest rates, commodities, and currencies) should be confirming your general outlook on the marketplace.

rules.rule: 2017 COT rule: commercial net position above the zero line is bullish; at or below zero is neutral to bearish. Commercials are the large hedgers.
rules.quote: by having that anything above the line would be deemed bullish and anything below it or at it would be neutral to bearish

rules.rule: Futures-vs-spot inversion: 6C (CAD futures) bearish means USDCAD bullish, and vice versa. He wants a significant commercial net long (or heavy net short) in the futures to justify the trade in the spot pair.
rules.quote: so what i like to look for is a significant net long position to justify my long entry and or a heavy net short position to justified my short position

rules.rule: 2022 COT rule: take the last 12 months of commercial net positions, split the range in half, and define bullish or bearish against that midpoint instead of the zero line. Above midpoint meaning bullish is inferred from the same lecture; the quote does not spell out direction.
rules.quote: whatever that range is, we divide that in half and then we define that in terms of being bullish or bearish.

rules.rule: Judge commercial hedging by where the net position sits inside its 12-month and 6-month range (also 2-year and 4-year ranges for macro extremes), not by the raw zero line.
rules.quote: When we look at commercial hedging we're not looking just at whether they're above or below the net sum zero line

rules.rule: Open interest is read as the gap between actual OI and its multi-year seasonal-average line, not as a raw number.
rules.quote: what I do is I look at the difference between open interest actual number and the seasonal average by getting a better feel or intensity about what the commercials are doing.

rules.rule: Seasonal curves (15-year and 40-year composites) give calendar windows. Example: a March-April low, then a spring high. Foreign-currency futures seasonal highs line up with Dollar Index seasonal lows.
rules.quote: Between March and April there's usually a seasonal low that forms, and then it rallies up to making a spring high.

rules.rule: A seasonal is only qualified if the weekly price direction of the last two years agrees. The dossier adds that he warns against buying a seasonal low while weekly order flow is aggressively lower.
rules.quote: Look at these last two years: what was the underlying price direction on the weekly chart? Was it bullish or bearish? That's what qualifies the seasonal tendency.

rules.rule: Relative strength is a divergence against DXY, not RSI. DXY makes higher highs but the commodity or currency fails to make a lower low, so it is being accumulated and is bullish. The dossier states the mirror: DXY lower lows and the asset fails to make a higher high means distribution.
rules.quote: If the Dollar Index is making higher highs, and the commodity fails to make a lower low

rules.rule: Currency selection: if the dollar is expected higher, use the cross (e.g. EURGBP) to find the weakest currency and pair weakest against strongest.
rules.quote: if the Dollar is expected to go higher, we look for which currency is the weakest relative to its cross. You pair the weakest against the strongest and that's where the explosive moves happen.

rules.rule: Stock relative-strength filter: in a bullish seasonal window pick stocks making a higher low while the Dow makes a lower low. This comes after filter one, that the market as a whole is poised to rally.
rules.quote: Filter number two: during bullish months we want to be selecting higher low stocks

rules.rule: Confluence recipe for equities: fundamental basis, seasonal window, relative strength with index SMT divergence, and the stock unwilling to go lower.
rules.quote: you're looking at relative strength ideas supporting with the SMT divergence between the indices, and that stock is showing an unwillingness to go lower, you have every portion of a winning recipe.

rules.rule: Intraday variant: when NQ refuses to make the lower low that ES makes, trade the relative-strength leader (NQ) rather than the laggard.
rules.quote: Nasdaq is the relative strength leader. When it refuses to go lower, you don't buy the weak sister; you buy the leader that's tearing higher.

rules.rule: COT commercial positioning only becomes significant after a liquidity run. Price must have raided stops first, then the commercial net position is noteworthy.
rules.quote: there has to be some measure of liquidity ran out which we see here then a net short position by the commercials would be significant or noteworthy

rules.rule: A rate advantage alone is not enough. The setup is the higher-yielding currency retracing into HTF support or an old low while the rate advantage exists (AUDUSD 0.7150 example, 1,200+ pips).
rules.quote: When you couple that 7150 level, which is a higher-timeframe support level or an old low, and you also notice that the market has that rate advantage, that's where the explosive moves come from.

rules.rule: Open interest at HTF support: if OI declines while price consolidates there, commercials are covering shorts, which is bullish accumulation.
rules.quote: In times where price is trading at key support levels on a higher timeframe basis, open interest will decline

rules.rule: Open interest at HTF resistance: if OI rises while price consolidates there, commercials are adding short hedges, which is bearish.
rules.quote: In times where price is trading at a key resistance level on a high timeframe basis, open interest will rise while price is consolidating.

rules.rule: Commodity premium (inverted) market: nearby contract above the next month, shown as a nearby-minus-deferred spread above zero, means commercials need immediate supply. Combine it with price dropping into a daily or weekly discount array (Cotton example). Per the dossier's markets table he warns against buying carrying-charge (contango) markets.
rules.quote: If the price of today's nearby contract is higher than that of the next month out in the future

rules.rule: Open-interest trigger: an OI drop of 10-15% or more at support signals commercial short covering. These are the only numeric thresholds he gives.
rules.quote: If open interest declines 10% or 15% or more, that's indicative of commercial short covering. If there is a reduction of open interest, that shows their willingness to not want to offer liquidity or expect lower prices.

rules.rule: Intermarket divergence trigger: the Dollar Index makes a lower low that the 10-year note does not confirm, which qualifies a quarterly-shift trade idea.
rules.quote: For the dollar Index to have a lower low here, it's contrary to what the 10-year note is doing, creating an intermarket divergence.

rules.rule: Interest-rate triad: compare 30-, 10- and 5-year futures while DXY sits at an order block. A divergence (a failure swing in one maturity) is the green light to refine the idea. The dossier's rule list says only one of the three needs to fail, but that detail is not in this quote.
rules.quote: if you can see the interest rate divergence or interest rate triad by looking at those 30, 10, and 5-year

rules.rule: When price reaches a focus point (order block, liquidity pool, void, FVG), consult the rate triad and the Dollar Index to confirm smart money is behind the idea.
rules.quote: When price action trades to a focus point like an order block, a liquidity pool, a liquidity void, or fair value gap, you refer to the interest rate triad and the dollar index.

rules.rule: Seasonals do not time the entry. The macro qualifier only sets the roadmap, and the entry comes from the HTF PD array or structure.
rules.quote: Seasonal tendencies give you the roadmap. They don't give you the exact minute to enter, but they tell you what the wind is doing behind your sails.

rules.rule: Seasonal or macro trades are executed from an HTF order block (previous down candle is a bullish OB, up candle for bearish; old resistance turns support).
rules.quote: Off of a previous down candle which is a bullish order block

rules.rule: Model 4 position trade (2024) on a bearish seasonal: sell at the open of the monthly bearish order block (GBPUSD example, short from 1.3150).
rules.quote: bearish order Block in this case we're actually going to use the open to sell

rules.rule: Position trades risk no more than 1% of the account, big in time held but not in allocation. The macro lectures give no numeric stop. The dossier summary places stops beyond HTF PD arrays or swing extremes.
rules.quote: How much money should you be risking? No more than 1%

rules.rule: Alternative risk definition for wide multi-month commodity stops: buy call options so the premium paid is the total risk.
rules.quote: If you don't want the exposure required for futures margin, you could have done call options. Whatever you paid for the option was your total risk, while you participated in a multi-dollar move.

rules.rule: Target is the opposing liquidity or HTF PD array. For a short, old lows are the discount PD array target, and longs mirror this with old highs.
rules.quote: using the same liquidity based Concepts looking at Old lows as our discount PD array

rules.rule: Aim for the middle of the quarterly shift (dossier says about 60-80% of the move) rather than the exact top or bottom.
rules.quote: We are trying to get in sync with that quarterly shift to get the meat in between, in other words the biggest portion of the move.

rules.rule: Time horizon for macro-qualified position trades is about three months (one quarterly shift).
rules.quote: As I mentioned in this mentorship, my time horizon is about three months. I think it's pretty much as realistic as you're going to get for position trading.

rules.rule: Trail the stop behind intermediate daily swing lows as price expands.
rules.quote: Trailing stops: as price continues to expand, you lock in profit by trailing stops behind intermediate swing lows on the daily chart.

rules.rule: Take partials at intermediate-term PD arrays and re-enter or pyramid on daily retracements.
rules.quote: Scaling out: when price achieves intermediate-term PD arrays, you take partials and look to re-enter or pyramid on subsequent daily retracements.

rules.rule: 2024 Charter Model 4 graduated stop reduction: stop reduced 25% at 25% of the expected objective, 50% at 50%, and break-even only at 75%.
rules.quote: when we are in profit 25% of our expected objective stop loss can be reduced by 25%

rules.rule: Failed seasonal: if price cannot rise during its seasonal buy window, expect lower prices and avoid buying (crude oil example, 2026).
rules.quote: if you can't see the price run higher when it should be seasonally going higher, it's very strong indication that we're likely to keep going lower unless some kind of news event or war intervenes.

rules.rule: A COT net position crossing the zero line is only a transition from long to short, not a directional reversal. Do not flip bias on a zero-line cross.
rules.quote: notice also that just because they swung below the zero line like they did here that is in no way indicative of a directional change

rules.rule: Do not buy an asset in distribution (consecutive lower lows with no accumulation divergence against the dollar). Cocoa is the example.
rules.quote: this would never meet the criteria as a buy while the dollar was acting as it was.

rules.rule: Multi-year COT extremes (2-year or 4-year) override any short-term commercial hedging program and signal a long-term trend reversal.
rules.quote: by having those extremes we will discount any short-term hedging program.

rules.rule: Risk-off macro regime (2017): do not blindly buy foreign currencies expecting normal expansions. The dossier's plan filter also cuts risk from 1% to 0.5% in risk-off.
rules.quote: When there's waning interest in risk, you cannot be blindly buying foreign currencies expecting normal expansions to take place.

rules.rule: Open-interest and COT qualifiers are for position and swing trades on higher timeframes (weekly/daily), never for day trades.
rules.quote: These open interest ideas are not day trades, they're really position and swing trades because it works on the higher timeframe basis.

rules.rule: For rate differentials stay with the major currencies and their central banks, not exotics.
rules.quote: for instance the israeli interest rate we're not interested in the polish interest rate in the czech interest rate or the hungarian interest rate

rules.rule: COT plus liquidity/order-flow works across currency futures, stock indices, bonds and commodity futures.
rules.quote: when you blend these two things together you get really amazing results and it's not limited just currencies it's in stock indices and it's in bonds and it's in commodity futures

rules.rule: Calendar-of-year filter for stocks (Dow seasonal): March, June and August are low-probability months. This is a month-of-year filter, not an intraday clock.
rules.quote: We have months where we know that there's going to be far less likely to have an opportunity with high probabilities, and those are March, June, August

rules.rule: May-to-October is the 'low magnitude' period for stocks: cut leverage and option activity. Opposite windows are Feb-May and Oct-Dec (bullish).
rules.quote: If you're going to be trading, do a lot less leverage, if you're going to be trading options do a lot less activity, don't be so aggressive during these periods of the year.

rules.rule: 2024 position-trading rule: scale back size in July and August for the seasonal volume drop. In 2023 he said the same about August.
rules.quote: around July and August scale back how much you try to trade

rules.rule: Treasury-note seasonal halves: bearish in the first half of the year, bullish in the second, which feeds DXY and currency bias by calendar half.
rules.quote: There's two primary or dominant cycles in the seasonal for treasury notes, and it's bearish for the first half of the year and then bullish for the second part of the year.

market_conditions.summary: A regime filter, not an entry model: before trading, classify the tape as low resistance (clean runway to a liquidity pool, trade it) or high resistance, Seek & Destroy, Z day, trapped order flow, decoupled indices or a news dead zone (stand aside or shrink size and scalp). The 2026 videos add that he now trades HRLR and Seek & Destroy days actively rather than only avoiding them.
market_conditions.needs_clock: Partly. The regime classifiers use price delivery only and could run on a 24/7 synthetic index over a rolling window: obstacles between price and the nearest liquidity pool, candle overlap, displacement and gap-fill behaviour (LRLR vs HRLR), and alternating two-sided sweeps that fail to hold (Seek & Destroy, trapped order flow). These parts are clock-bound and do not port: the economic calendar (NFP, CPI, FOMC 2:00/2:30 PM, Jackson Hole day one), 'after the 9:30 open expect HRLR', the noon-1 PM no-trade hour, the 10:00 AM 'obvious run' check, the 2 PM Seek & Destroy resolution, the 2 PM-8 PM Central Bank Dealers Range filter, the 4:14 PM settlement/opening-gap anchors, and 'the day after a large-range day' (a daily bar boundary; use a rolling window instead). Decoupled-market detection needs a second correlated index (ES/NQ/YM), so it cannot run on a single synthetic index. A Z day (low-volatility quiet range) can be approximated by volatility percentile alone.
market_conditions.how_to_code:
Build one regime classifier that runs before every entry model and outputs a state plus a size multiplier.

1. Liquidity map. Mark swing highs and lows (3-candle fractals), relative equal highs/lows (within a tolerance), prior day/session highs and lows, and opening-gap levels (NWOG, NDOG, RTH opening range gap).

2. Resistance score (LRLR vs HRLR). From current price to the nearest target pool in the trade direction, count the opposing unmitigated arrays in the path: order blocks, FVGs/inversion FVGs, breakers, Balanced Price Ranges and layered NDOG/NWOG levels. Add a tape score: overlap ratio of the last N candle ranges, number of candles spent inside one FVG (a high count means HRLR), depth of retracements after a displacement leg, and whether FVGs after displacement stay partly open. LRLR = zero or one obstacle, a clean equal-high/low target, displacement candles (body above k times ATR) that leave open FVGs, retracement under about 50 percent of the leg, and little time spent near the entry. HRLR = two or more obstacles (the dossiers' 'three unmitigated blocks' and '3+ NDOG/NWOG' thresholds are summary text, not his quotes), choppy overlap, deep pullbacks, and slow progress.

3. Seek & Destroy and trapped order flow. In a rolling window, detect at least two alternating sweeps of the window's high and low in which price closes back inside the range both times and no displacement leg holds beyond either side. An expanding high/low sequence (higher highs and lower lows, the 'megaphone') strengthens the flag. In the 2024 teaching, block entries while it is flagged. Clear the flag after a displacement close beyond the range that holds, or after the final stop-run; in 2017 and 2021 that came late in the day, and in 2021 it came with the 2:00 PM manipulation.

4. Z day. Range or realized-volatility percentile below a threshold, with few sweeps. Standing aside is his rule.

5. Decoupled. With two or three correlated indices, flag when one makes a new swing extreme the others do not confirm (SMT-style), or when net direction over the window disagrees (for example NQ up, ES flat, YM down). It needs a second feed.

6. Calendar and clock gates, where a session clock exists. Block or shrink on NFP, CPI and FOMC (before 2:30 PM) days, Jackson Hole day one, the day after a large-range day, and the noon to 1 PM hour (2022 rule only). Expect HRLR after the 9:30 open, and check for a clear run by 10:00 AM.

7. Output states and sizing. LRLR: full size, full target at the external pool. HRLR: roughly 30 percent size (he went from his standard ten contracts to three), first partial at the first nearby liquidity, trail the stop under the FVG midpoint or inversion FVG, and re-enter after a wick stop-hunt. Seek & Destroy, trapped, Z day, decoupled and news dead zone: flat (2017-2025 teaching), with an optional 2026 mode that fades the sweeps with small size and a trailing stop. The HRLR to LRLR transition is the cue to re-enable full-size entries.

Subjective parts a programmer must parameterise: what counts as a significant obstacle (an HTF array matters, a 1-minute gap may not); 'clean' equal highs; 'enough' displacement; how long to wait before declaring a transition; when a day is S&D versus ordinary HRLR chop (he warns against confusing them); and whether the 2026 trade-the-S&D mode is wanted at all.
market_conditions.changes_over_time:
Teaching changed in these ways:

1. Seek & Destroy: step aside, then trade it. 2017 (3OEUIkkcmLE): a Seek & Destroy day, like a Z day, is a day his patterns are unfruitful. 2020 (7PwoZyn7Wh4, Powell speech on EURUSD): sit on your hands, it 'grinds you down'. 2021 (BZ4HVsArJBE): on an FOMC day he calls it seek destroy, takes short-term highs and lows all day, and then trades the 2:00 PM low sweep long. 2022 (P5pyzmgZA1s): do not trade projected ranges on NFP/Seek & Destroy days. Sep 2024 (Qg3O1GkJDeQ, NDwNIqUkASc): step aside once two-sided stop runs start. Aug 2026 (SUcRywSry5U, MD1Ts09dkYs): he trades the 'seek and destroy model' on Jackson Hole day one, long and short, with trailing stops, and says he is 'buying the sell stops'. He also says breakout trading is the thing to avoid, and (17:11) watch price rather than force trades. So 'stand aside' became 'fade the sweeps, do not trade breakouts, size small'.

2. HRLR: stand down, then scalp it. The 2019 and 2022 dossiers (54yWnOON0zQ, 22XkhpJR5eA) frame HRLR as 'reduce size or stand down' and 'stand down or demand strict +1R'. Oct 2024 (3YfetuXVhOE): trading HRLR means chop and stop-outs, 'wait for LRLR'. But Oct 2024 to Aug 2026 (9HUAUF_h2tI, dWyXLze4c4k, tp0qkiWCctw, e6XwTK4hVqI, C7CwjBOtHwM, O217xQsEUgI) he trades NQ live in HRLR with small size, early partials, a pulled-away target and pyramiding. He says to reduce risk, not that no trade exists.

3. Lunch hour. 2022 (N29ZJ-o31xs) is an absolute no-trade hour from noon to 1 PM. 2024-2025 trades the 11:50-12:30 'NY lunch macro' in HRLR (9HUAUF_h2tI, dWyXLze4c4k).

4. News days. Trapped-order-flow (2019) and 2023 dossiers say stand aside on NFP, and 2025 has a declared 'CPI No Trade' day. On the other hand, 2026-09-03 (xpH0wDANtmM) analyses NFP Thursday as HRLR and calls it a 'profitable session' with a bearish-below-octant read. FOMC: 2021 trades the 2:00 PM sweep; 2024 says the real move is the 2:30 PM press conference.

5. Terms and scope. 'Z day' appears only once (2017). 'Trapped order flow' appears only in the 2019 video, with one cross-reference from 20180108-AcKelqKMkr8, a dossier dated earlier than the video it cites. 'Decoupled' appears in 2023 (ES/NQ/YM), Oct 2024 (ES vs NQ, with SMT) and Apr 2026 (neutral, 'don't touch it'; Friday). LRLR/HRLR started as a forex and higher-timeframe liquidity-run concept (2019-2022: equal highs/lows, multi-day moves) and became an intraday NQ tape-reading regime (2023 Greyhound bus vs hot knife; 2024 'expect HRLR after 9:30').

Data caveats. Many older and 2024 dossiers look LLM-summarised: the 2019, 2020 and Month-1/Month-7 2022 'quotes' read as polished paraphrase, the 2024 Mentorship quotes are fragmentary caption snippets, and their trade tables (for example '+25-40 handles') look templated. Several rules appear only in dossier summaries, not in quotes, so they are not on this card as quoted rules: cut leverage in half when decoupled (xUWonBnfYOk overview), 'three unmitigated order blocks' as the HRLR threshold, and the 70 percent gap-to-CE rule. Treat them as hints. Where a quote on this card is a contiguous piece of a longer dossier cell that contains '...', only the clean piece is quoted (for example the 2026 S&D 'megaphone' is in the same MD1Ts09dkYs 08:36 cell but not in the quoted span).
market_conditions.markets: NQ (E-mini Nasdaq-100) is the main market, in nearly every 2024-2026 video (HRLR, LRLR, Seek & Destroy and decoupled work). ES and YM appear for tape reading and decoupling (2022, 2023, 2024) and for the 2022 post-large-range-day abstention. In forex the older videos use EURUSD (trapped order flow after NFP 2019, Seek & Destroy on Powell's speech 2020) and GBPUSD (LRLR 2019 and 2022, FOMC Seek & Destroy 2021). The 2022 bond lesson uses ZB (30-year bond) for consolidation days, and the 2022 stocks lesson uses AAPL for an LRLR. In Oct 2025 he calls forex 'high resistance' and says he is not interested in it.

rules.rule: Purpose of the whole filter: classify the tape before any entry model, because the pain he wants you to avoid is being in the market in the wrong conditions.
rules.quote: One of the main focuses of my channel here is to help you avoid pain, and pain in its pure sense in trading is losing money when you shouldn't have been in the market.

rules.rule: Day-profile filter (2017): a Z day (quiet up-and-down consolidation) or a Seek & Destroy day (wild choppy up-and-down, going nowhere until the last part of the day, then running the stops) is a day his time-based patterns do not work.
rules.quote: the times you're going to be unfruitful using this information is when we have a Z day where it goes up and down in quiet consolidation or a seek and destroy day which is a really wild choppy up-and-down day where it doesn't really go anywhere until the last portion of the day and then it runs out the stops

rules.rule: Non-farm payroll day is a day he likes to refrain from engaging in, because of the uncertainty and the whipsaw that follows (the lesson is built on EURUSD after the Feb 1 2019 NFP).
rules.quote: Last week we had the Non-Farm Payroll, and typically that's a day that I like to refrain from engaging in. But I'm going to give you some things that added to the uncertainty about that particular day.

rules.rule: The morning session after a large-range expansion day is a consolidation day that chops up and down; treat it as a no-trade or low-odds day.
rules.quote: Trading the day after the large range day: they do things and they fall victim to this in this consolidation day where it's just chopping up and down.

rules.rule: HRLR is the condition when price is inside a larger consolidation (range-bound); do not expect clean fast delivery from it.
rules.quote: range-bound and potentially high-resistance liquidity run conditions. Now, again, why am I saying it's like that? Because we're inside of a larger consolidation

rules.rule: When correlated index futures (ES, NQ, Dow) are not moving together the session is decoupled and he calls it problematic for trading.
rules.quote: Decoupled all day and make very problematic conditions for trading.

rules.rule: Calendar cue (2026): Jackson Hole day one is the highest-likelihood Seek & Destroy day, though it can still form on day two.
rules.quote: Day one of Jackson Hole Symposium is the highest likelihood of a seek and destroy day. It doesn't mean it if it doesn't form on day one that it can't do it on day two.

rules.rule: Higher-timeframe first: the monthly and weekly give the dominant draw on liquidity, which is the pool a low resistance run travels toward.
rules.quote: Apply everything from a monthly and weekly perspective first. That gives you the dominant draw on liquidity that smart money is engineering.

rules.rule: Bias test for a low resistance run: if you are bearish there must be no reason for price to go higher and no reason for it to pause; if you can argue the other side, it is not the clean condition.
rules.quote: If you're bearish, it should be next to impossible for you to see any reason for it to go higher. No justification for it to go higher, no justification for it to pause. And when you trade in those conditions, that is a low-resistance liquidity run.

rules.rule: When price sits inside overlapping prior-day structure or the previous opening range gap and nothing argues for a side, keep no bias and do not touch it.
rules.quote: All of this market structure this way right here, all of this tells me don't touch it.

rules.rule: LRLR definition: clean highs or lows ahead with no significant obstacle between price and the resting stops, so price accelerates into them.
rules.quote: A Low Resistance Liquidity Run is when the market has clean highs or clean lows with no significant obstacles in between. The market can accelerate with speed and efficiency right into those resting stops.

rules.rule: HRLR definition: price must fight through multiple previous swing points, order blocks and levels on the way to the target, giving choppy delivery that may reverse before the target.
rules.quote: In a High Resistance Liquidity Run, price has to fight through multiple previous swing points, order blocks, and levels. It creates a choppy, difficult delivery that is prone to reversing before reaching your target.

rules.rule: A New Week Opening Gap high sitting in the path is a typical HRLR obstacle.
rules.quote: Week opening gap high, characteristic of what high resistance liquidity run looks like.

rules.rule: Stacked old new-day and new-week opening gap levels in the path cause an HRLR.
rules.quote: these layered new day opening gap and new week opening gap levels, that's what causes high resistance liquidity runs.

rules.rule: Resistance depends on the direction relative to a Balanced Price Range: running to a BPR is low resistance, running through it is not.
rules.quote: It's not a low resistance liquidity run to trade through a balanced price range it is a low resistance run to trade to a balanced price range when you're above it we're trading down.

rules.rule: Trapped order flow: price clears the stops on both sides (sweeps one side, then breaks the other aggressively) so that both buyers and sellers are knocked out and no direction is established.
rules.quote: Anyone that was short was knocked out. Anyone that sold short here was knocked out as well. And it broke down aggressively, clearing both sides. That is trapped order flow.

rules.rule: Seek & Destroy profile on an event day: alternating runs up and down that clear stops on each side, an expanding (megaphone) range, rather than a single directional run.
rules.quote: seek and destroy likely. So, it's going to go up, down, up, to clear stops, down to clear stops

rules.rule: Decoupled indices as seen on the tape: one average much stronger, one much weaker, one in between, all doing their own thing.
rules.quote: The Dow was relatively stronger higher, and then Nasdaq was exceedingly weak compared to that, and where we're at in the ES—everything is doing its own thing!

rules.rule: Decoupled (2026 example): NQ makes a rally or high that ES and the Dow do not confirm, so he declines to chase it.
rules.quote: ES, Dow have not followed suit with this rally up on NQ

rules.rule: Do not mislabel ordinary high-resistance chop as Seek & Destroy; they are different diagnoses (HRLR is difficult delivery between opposing levels, S&D is a two-sided stop hunt).
rules.quote: That is not seek and destroy that is not the Chop is real in high resistance.

rules.rule: The all-clear: the market moves from high resistance to low resistance conditions, which is when efficient one-way delivery appears and the filter lets you trade.
rules.quote: Transitioning from high resistance to low resistance liquidity runs—that is where very efficient, symmetrical price movement occurs.

rules.rule: Live confirmation of an LRLR: price shows a willingness to escape and leaves only small inefficiencies instead of printing many candles inside one gap.
rules.quote: When you start seeing prices show a willingness to escape and really run and leave little inefficiencies, that right there, that's low resistance liquidity run.

rules.rule: Post-entry check for the clean condition: price should leave the entry area quickly and rarely move toward the stop; if it hangs around the entry it is not an LRLR.
rules.quote: When that execution is done, it spends very little time around where I entered and rarely ever moves towards my stop.

rules.rule: Stand-aside trigger (HRLR/chop): after taking out a low, if price cannot hold below the wick and snaps back, that failure is the clue that the environment is low probability.
rules.quote: when it fails to hold, that's your clue that this is low probability.

rules.rule: Stand-aside trigger (early Seek & Destroy warning): the market is starting to expand both ways; he names the day a Seek & Destroy day where everyone gets hurt.
rules.quote: Market which could eventually trade to a Seek and Destroy day where everyone gets hurt.

rules.rule: Displacement urgency check inside an HRLR trade: price should show long stretched-out candles through the level; if it is slow, the trade is not working.
rules.quote: I don't like how long it's taking in here. It needs to start showing really long stretched out down close candles. Get below here and rip through that level and reach down into here.

rules.rule: If trading inside HRLR/layered-gap conditions, wait for the first fair value gap to form and rest the limit order in it.
rules.quote: Wait for that first fair value gap to form and have your limit order sitting in that fair value gap

rules.rule: First presented FVG after displacement is the reference: if bearish it should send price lower; if price blows through it, it becomes an inversion FVG to trade the other way.
rules.quote: That means if it's bearish, it should send price lower. If it blows through, then it becomes a bullish inversion fair value gap.

rules.rule: In a working HRLR trade he adds contracts on the next fair value gap and raises the stop under its midpoint (pyramiding).
rules.quote: gap again, I'll add two more contracts. Okay, we're using the stop up now just below the midpoint of this.

rules.rule: 2026 change: on a Seek & Destroy day he does not step aside or chase the breakout; he fades the stop-run, buying the sell stops that breakout shorts have placed.
rules.quote: you're sell short on a breakout. I'm buying the sell stops.

rules.rule: HRLR stop: just beyond the defending swing low wick, then rolled under the next low once price proves itself.
rules.quote: defense is this swing low, which is why I have my stop loss just below this wick. Okay? Once it does that, then I'm going to roll the stop just below that low right there.

rules.rule: Trail the stop under the inversion fair value gap once candle bodies have spent time inside it and held.
rules.quote: Bring the stop up again. Now the stop here is below the inversion fair value, guy, because we've spent a lot of time with the bodies in there

rules.rule: HRLR target: take the first partial at the first nearby liquidity and treat it as paying yourself, even if the rest is stopped out.
rules.quote: It's running right up into first partial. And at that point, you know, it doesn't make a difference if it comes all the way back down to stop me out

rules.rule: LRLR target: internal-range entries (order block, FVG, void) run out to external range liquidity beyond the short-term dealing range.
rules.quote: That means you're going to see order blocks, fair value gaps, or voids be your entry and it'll expand outside of the present short-term dealing range to external range liquidity. And that is your low resistance liquidity run.

rules.rule: HRLR scalp expectation: with 30 to 40 handles of range available a scalper hopes for 10 to 15 handles on NQ (about 300 dollars per mini); small targets, not runners. 'He' is a hypothetical student.
rules.quote: he might be able to ferret out, you know, 10 or 15 handles and if it turns on him stops him out and you know, he's doing about 300 bucks per mini contract.

rules.rule: Scale size down in HRLR: he used three contracts instead of his standard ten because unrealized swings are harder to manage with size.
rules.quote: It's much more to manage when it's like this when you're trading with size. Whereas this is only three contracts. It's not even that big of a deal.

rules.rule: When price lingers in the gap without expanding, cut the position to a minimum runner and trail the stop aggressively to the nearest short-term high.
rules.quote: in the event that it should pop up and get the stop loss it's not taking two contracts it's just taking one okay and lower to stop down aggressively to that little short-term High

rules.rule: Move the target out of the way in choppy tape so you manage by whether candles still respect the inversion FVG instead of target fixation.
rules.quote: so to remove that I just move the target completely out of the way I'm managing more specifically about does it still want to respect that inversion fair value Gap

rules.rule: Use a partial stop-loss order on part of the size for tug-of-war retracements, rather than all-or-nothing on the stop.
rules.quote: tug-of-wars that take place, just put a stop-loss in on partial. I had seven contracts net long. I put two contracts on a stop right here. So, if it goes below there, it's going to sell two of the seven I had as a partial

rules.rule: After the stop is hit on a wick high and price then washes out, he re-enters immediately; stop hunts in HRLR are expected.
rules.quote: So, here's that execution being stopped out right at the high of that wick right where my stop is and then washed out. And there I am going right back in.

rules.rule: Once the payday is secured, never move the stop back (2026 Seek & Destroy trade).
rules.quote: never never never want to pull the stop back. I've secured a payday

rules.rule: Core stand-aside rule: when odds are low, standing on the sidelines is the best trade.
rules.quote: When the odds are low, the best trade you can make is to stand on the sidelines.

rules.rule: When Seek & Destroy takes over the tape, step aside (2024 teaching).
rules.quote: but when Seek and Destroy takes over, step aside.

rules.rule: Recognising a stop-hunting condition and not participating is the discipline being taught.
rules.quote: Recognizing the stop hunting condition and choosing not to participate is true discipline.

rules.rule: Do not force trades in low-probability tape; being flat is an active position.
rules.quote: You don't force trades in these environments; being on the sidelines is an active, profitable position.

rules.rule: When price is erratic around a level without clear displacement, leave it alone.
rules.quote: When it's doing this, you just got to leave it alone, folks. Just leave it alone

rules.rule: Do not force a breakout or a trending model inside HRLR; it is especially problematic for newer traders.
rules.quote: it can be problematic for traders that are brand new. If you're trying to force a breakout, if you're forcing some kind of a trending model

rules.rule: In HRLR where price struggles and overlaps, cut risk (and take profits quickly) rather than stand pat.
rules.quote: Recognizing high resistance liquidity runs: when price struggles and overlaps, reduce risk.

rules.rule: Decoupled indices on a Friday with an unfilled gap: do not trade against the divergence or against the gap; stay out.
rules.quote: Not on a Friday. Not against the divergence that's been created, not against the gap that hasn't been really traded into deep enough.

rules.rule: News-day no-trade: if the liquidity run he wanted around the release did not happen (e.g. no sellside taken first), declare a no-trade session.
rules.quote: Would have rather seen it use CPI to drop down, take some sellside, and then do these size runs here up into that blue fair value gap that I mentioned on daily chart last night.

rules.rule: Forex London filter: if the Central Bank Dealers Range (2 PM to 8 PM NY) is wider than 50 pips he passes on London.
rules.quote: If the Central Bank Dealers Range is greater than 50 pips, I'm already knowing firsthand I'm possibly going to pass on a London

rules.rule: Classify the regime on the 15-minute chart: LRLR or HRLR.
rules.quote: Taking you into the 15-minute chart are we in low resistance liquidity run conditions or are we in high resistance liquidity.

rules.rule: Tight, not-loose forex price action is high resistance, not low resistance, and he says he is not interested in trading it (same video recommends NQ futures or the US100 CFD).
rules.quote: because it's not highly liquid. It's not loose. It's high resistance, not low resistance liquidity runs

rules.rule: After the 9:30 AM New York open expect high-resistance conditions on index futures.
rules.quote: After the 9:30 opening bell just expect it to be high resistance liquidity

rules.rule: Obvious directional run expected around 10:00 AM on an event day; a fuzzy morning with no run is problematic (pre-NFP Seek & Destroy example).
rules.quote: talking about this in X live I mentioned how this is problematic and we'd want to see an obvious run at 10 o'clock

rules.rule: Noon to 1 PM New York is a no-trade hour (2022 mentorship).
rules.quote: lunch hour noon to one don't trade it okay do not trade it it can do a lot of weird things in that hour or simply do nothing and go sideways

rules.rule: FOMC: the 2:00 PM rate release and the 2:30 PM press conference are separate stages and the real move comes with the press conference (2024).
rules.quote: how it usually behaves is the real move comes with the press conference.

rules.rule: Seek & Destroy day resolves in the afternoon (2021 FOMC day): short-term highs and lows are taken all day, then the 2:00 PM manipulation takes the low of the day and price goes higher.
rules.quote: this is seek destroy okay seek destroy is a market profile where it's literally taking out short-term highs and lows all day long then finally at two o'clock in the afternoon when the manipulation enters the marketplace it takes out the low of the day

targets_sd.summary: Plan the exits before the entry: project the entry swing outward as a measured move (2017: first scaling at the swing extreme, then -0.27, -0.62, -1.0 = "symmetrical price swing"; 2020+: 0.5/1/1.5/2 SD of that swing; 2022+: SD of session ranges), snap exits just ahead of 00/20/50/80 price levels and overlapping fib clusters, and prefer a nearby liquidity pool ("low-hanging fruit") over the full draw.
targets_sd.needs_clock: Partly. Price-only pieces (no clock): the swing-based projections (zero level at the swing extreme, then +0.27/0.5/0.62/1.0/1.5/2.0 times the swing range, "symmetrical swing" = 1.0), the fulcrum measured move, the 10-15 pip confluence-cluster test, the 00/20/50/80 round-number grid and rounding exits just ahead of it, 10-20 pip overshoot beyond a pool, and "low-hanging fruit" defined as the nearest unmitigated old high/low or relative equal highs/lows. These could run on 24/7 synthetic indices using only price delivery, with the caveat that the round-number premise (institutions place orders on 00/50/20/80) is unlikely to hold on algorithmic synthetics, so treat the grid as a hypothesis to test, not as given. Clock-dependent pieces: CBDR (14:00 to 20:00 NY) and Asian range SD, the 14:00 cap, the 08:30 to 11:00 and 07:00 to 09:00 windows, the midnight 00:00 to 00:30 opening range, RTH opening-range-gap SD, the first swing high after 10:00, and Friday-close to Monday-open gap midpoint. On 24/7 synthetics these would need substituted rolling or fixed bar-count windows, which is not something he teaches.
targets_sd.how_to_code:
Two anchor families share one geometry, plus a liquidity layer.

A) Swing projection (2017 to 2026, price only). 1) Find an impulse leg after a break of a short-term extreme, measured body-to-body (lowest open/close to highest open/close): range R = |body_high - body_low|, P0 = the leg extreme in the trade direction (long: highest body; short: lowest body). 2) Levels beyond P0 in the trade direction: P0 + k*R. 2017 labels: -0.27, -0.62, -1.0 (-1.0 = "symmetrical price swing" = 200% extension of the leg). 2020 labels: 0.5 SD, 1 SD, 1.5 SD, 2 SD (2 SD = the "-300% extension" of 2017). Check against v6ATva5DF0I trades table: low 106.224, old high 106.462, R = 23.8 pips, -0.5 SD = 106.581, -1.0 SD = 106.700, which matches P0 + k*R exactly. 127.2/161.8/200 in summary-style dossiers are the same levels as -0.27/-0.62/-1.0. 3) First scaling is P0 itself (old high/low), not Target 1. Skip the trade if (P0 - entry) < 2 x risk (2017 test), if the first scaling is under about 15 pips or 10 points or 5-10 handles, or if the swing cannot give 3 partials plus a runner (E9F 45:20). 4) Entry is a limit at the 62% retracement (70.5 and 79 are alternatives), stop at the opposite leg extreme (0 pips in 2017, 5 pips in 2023, more in 2020 examples).
B) Fulcrum measured move. For a leg L to H, after price retraces and then trades through L (the fulcrum break), project L - k*(H-L), k = 1, 1.5, 2, 2.5 (2023, 2026). Gate on the break; do not pre-place before it.
C) Round-number grid. For each instrument define the figure (100 pips, or 100 handles) and mark .00, .20, .50, .80 (the 2024 Model 7 lecture adds 40 and 60; 2020 uses 5 and 10 levels). For each projected level, find the nearest grid level on the near side and move the exit just ahead of it (round down for longs, up for shorts; a few pips or ticks for the spread). Confluence score = number of distinct projections (from different swings, or fib plus grid) inside a 10-15 pip window (under 5 is best); reject isolated levels (score 1). Beyond a figure or previous high/low, allow a 10-20 pip overshoot as a far target.
D) Liquidity layer (low-hanging fruit). Target list = nearest unmitigated opposing old high/low, previous day high/low, first relative equal highs/lows to the left, gap consequent encroachment (50% of the gap), first swing high after 10:00. Place the exit a few ticks before the pool, even if the projection reaches further.
E) Session-range SD (clock). CBDR = body high/low of 14:00 to 20:00 NY; usable only if width is 40 pips or less (ideal 20 to 30). Levels = high + n*width and low - n*width, n = 1 to 4; expect London extreme at 1 to 2 SD, up to 3 on some days, 4 on news days. Same construction for the Asian range (20 pips or less), Float (half-range unit), midnight 00:00 to 00:30 range (0.5, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0) and the RTH opening-range-gap (-2.0, with a pool of liquidity).
F) Management state machine. Partial 1 at P0 (or the -0.5 level if P0 is under 15 pips): 2017 swing 50% off, day trade 75 to 80% off. Stop to about the midpoint of the range at first scaling (2020), break-even at Target 1 (2017) or plus 2 to 3 pips at the second scaling (2020), or graduated 25/50/75% (2024). Partials at T2 and T3; close the day trade at 2 SD keeping 20% (2020) or flatten fully on the third take-profit (2024). Score a hit as filled when price is within 3 to 5 pips (FX tolerance he states in 2024).
Subjective parts: choosing which swing and which two pivots count as the fulcrum; which pools count as the low-hanging fruit; judging confluence and "convergence" with a higher-timeframe array; whether to hold the runner; how far ahead of a level to exit. These need fixed parameters in code (for example cluster window = 10 pips or 0.1 ATR, front-run buffer = spread plus 2 ticks) and should be tested rather than assumed.
targets_sd.changes_over_time:
Source reliability. Dossiers for JdHABKIEU1I, J_7v2i3ogwk, GFdWahZUNOw, zanmou0ic5U, g8bhZReDK-Q, sfRO5LrTgTA (and J2C9vd4-awI, FZ6QIWBu688) are polished model-written summaries; their "quotes" cannot be cross-checked. zanmou0ic5U's rules are third-person ("ICT will look to fill four pivots"), and its "rule of four" and float-range unit are paraphrase. The transcript-style dossiers (Cg0-CFJOJvg, nNEt9QTCTtk, nBschaCBNLU, the 2017 OTE clips, the 2020 OTE Pattern Recognition series, KEqzv2yOAf0, 2022 to 2026 reviews) are more trustworthy.

Era 1, 2017: first scaling at the swing extreme, Target 1 = -0.27, Target 2 = -0.62, symmetrical price swing = -1.0 (= 200 extension; later "-300% extension" appears for swing trades), exits chosen at institutional levels (00, 20, 50, 80) with a 10-20 pip overshoot beyond big figures and previous highs/lows; reward judged as at least 2x risk on the first scaling (Cg0 17:09). Summary dossiers instead say 127.2/161.8/200 and call 127.2 "symmetrical" (FZ6QIWBu688), with a 50/30/20 split (J_7v2i3ogwk); the percent figures are the same levels as -0.27/-0.62/-1.0, but "symmetrical" is misused there and the split has no verbatim support.
Era 2, 2020: the same geometry is renamed standard deviations (0.5, 1, 1.5, 2 SD of the OTE swing), first scalp at the old high or the -0.5 level (15 pips minimum), round down to 5 or 10 levels, collapse at 2 SD, 80% off and 20% on, four scaling stages required. Risk to reward is downplayed ("forget risk to reward", one to one is fine), and he says the fib "has absolutely nothing to do" with why price goes there; liquidity does.
Era 3, 2022: Core Content months 8 and 9 move SD to session ranges (CBDR 14:00 to 20:00, Asian range, Float), 1 to 4 SD, CBDR must be 40 pips or less, ideally 20 to 30; 2022 Mentorship episodes use -1.0 and -1.5 SD of the swing and he cautions (y8cKMOHMVb0, yFpHbBnsK_c) not to insist on the draw, with "low-hanging fruit" as a five-point or +10-handle first partial.
Era 4, 2023 to 2024: fulcrum measured move and Larry Williams' Target Shooter lineage (GFdWahZUNOw); SD grid -1, -1.5, -2, -2.5 on the fib (summary and chart annotations); Charter models claim 3 to 5 pip precision and 15-minute consistency.
Era 5, 2025 to 2026: "low-hanging fruit" becomes a named discipline (tenet 5, czSUBVHD9u8): gap midpoint, first swing high after 10:00, first relative equal highs/lows to the left, just above equal lows; SD plus pool-of-liquidity agreement (-2.0 of the RTH opening range gap, -2.5, event horizon); isolated levels declared useless; 70% claim that a half gap trades in the first 30 minutes (5ycp9oGKPms). The word "fulcrum" is used loosely: the low that must break (GFdWahZUNOw), the swing high (KEqzv2yOAf0), and the midnight open (KHkUPAsdyfk); he says the swing-trader's model is from his 2016-17 core content.

Direct conflicts. Stop: exactly at the extreme (2017) vs 5 pips (4f1vjQMlV50) vs high plus 15 pips (NB7Bku099tU) vs one tick (Q0Xa-Vqy5vo) vs 10 to 30 pip stops in the 2020 examples. Break-even: at Target 1 (2017) vs midpoint at first scaling then entry plus 2 to 3 pips at the second (2020) vs graduated 25/50/75 and break-even only at 75% (2024). Partials: swing 50% or day trade 75 to 80% (9CCrlTIrkxw) vs 80/20 (ZbkEvNpm-_k) vs at most two partials then everything off on the third target (CTS27DsveNs) vs 50/30/20 (summary only). Bodies vs wicks: bodies for anchors (2017, 2020, CBDR 2022), but he says he sometimes includes wicks for projections (uiszrzGyUqU 04:02), the 2023 swing-low study says to anchor to the lowest price, and breakers use the full range. Exit placement: aim 10 to 20 pips beyond a pool or big figure, but also front-run it or the nearest institutional level; low-hanging fruit explicitly stops short of the draw. Precision claims drift from "to the pip" (2017) to "3 to 5 pips is precision" (2024).
targets_sd.markets: Forex: EURUSD, GBPUSD, USDCAD, AUDUSD, USDJPY, USDCHF, EURAUD, AUDJPY, EURJPY (he says he dislikes yen pairs), spot gold (2017 to 2020, 2022 to 2024 Charter). Futures: ES (2020, 2022, 2023, 2026), NQ and MNQ (2021 to 2026), crude oil CL, 30-year bond ZB and Mexican peso 6M (2020). He states it works on all pairs, markets and asset classes (9CCrlTIrkxw 00:46) and prefers ES over NQ for clean price action (KEqzv2yOAf0 06:22). Timeframes: 1h to 5m swing and scalp OTE examples (2017), 5m (2020 series), 15m for session-range SD (2022, 2024), 1m and 15s for execution (2024 to 2026). Trade count of about 85 is approximate: a keyword scan of the Target column in the Trades tables of about 60 dossiers gave 76 rows, plus about 10 more found by hand in differently formatted dossiers (2022 to 2026 NQ/ES SD trades), minus a few false hits; some tutorial reviews repeat one live trade. Of the eight start videos only nNEt9QTCTtk (2 trades), zanmou0ic5U, g8bhZReDK-Q, sfRO5LrTgTA and KEqzv2yOAf0 (1 each) have a trades table; JdHABKIEU1I, J_7v2i3ogwk and GFdWahZUNOw have only teaching or one live delivery (ES 4098.50) with no trade table. About 40 of the rows are 2017 or 2020 forex and futures OTE examples.

rules.rule: Use the projection grid to plan profit-taking (exits), not to find entries; the fib is only a measuring tool for targets.
rules.quote: Fibonacci is just a measuring tool I use and I use it for like targeting I don't use so much for entry

rules.rule: The objective is a draw on liquidity; price only has to draw toward it, it does not have to reach it.
rules.quote: it's not important or even required that price trades from this level here all the way up to that level and higher it just needs to draw towards it that's the reason why I call a draw and liquidity

rules.rule: The fib projection does not cause the move; the resting liquidity (previous day high/low etc.) is the reason, so direction/target comes from liquidity and the fib only frames it.
rules.quote: it's not the magic of the fib the fib has absolutely nothing to do with the reasons why prices going down there the reason why it's going down there is there's a liquidity resting below this low

rules.rule: Price grid: institutional levels are the 00 (big figure), 20, 50 (mid figure) and 80 levels; these are the exit/reaction levels (summary-style dossier, polished wording).
rules.quote: Algorithms do not trade random numbers; they trade institutional price levels: 00, 20, 50, and 80.

rules.rule: Institutions use round numbers; price trades around the 00 big figure, the 50 mid figure and the 20/80 levels next to them (e.g. 12750 mid figure, then 12780 as the next institutional level).
rules.quote: it's 20s 80s because they go beyond the big figure zero zero levels above or below it dependent on if you're bearish or bullish and the mid figure okay like 12750 that's a mid figure level then we have 127 80 which is the next institutional price level

rules.rule: Anchor the swing for the projection body-to-body: lowest open/close to highest open/close of the impulse leg that broke a short-term high.
rules.quote: all we're doing is looking for a hard time frame level a short term high to be broken measure to swing or impulse leg up referencing the body to body lowest body portion that could either be a open or close to the highest open or close in the swing high that's where you anchor your reference points

rules.rule: Use candle bodies (bulk of volume), not wicks, because wicks differ between brokers.
rules.quote: it's the reason why I teach you to use the bulk of the volume with the bodies of the candle and not the wicks the wicks are always going to be slightly off relative to your brokers

rules.rule: 2017 fib calibration: zero level = first profit/scaling at the swing extreme, then negative 0.62, negative 0.27 and negative 1 (= symmetrical price swing) as the extension targets.
rules.quote: and we have our target levels which is zero negative zero point six two negative zero two seven and then negative one for a symmetrical price swing

rules.rule: Put the fib on the parent swing and mark Target 1, Target 2 and the symmetrical price swing as the objectives for that swing.
rules.quote: put it on target 1 and I'm going to put it on target 2 up here and I'm gonna put one more at symmetrical price swing so these will be our objectives relative to this price swing

rules.rule: Confluence = several fib extensions (from different swings) landing within 10-15 pips of each other (under 10 better, under 5 best); more than 15 pips apart is not a confluence.
rules.quote: how far away would I be willing to allow price to move about 10 to 15 pips depending upon the type of market structure there is but anything more than 15 pips I'm not really willing to let that be deemed a confluence if it can be less than 10 pips it's even better in this instance we have 1928 1924 so we're less than 5 pips

rules.rule: 2023 standard-deviation projection = a measured move of the high-to-low (or low-to-high) swing, with the swing extreme acting as the fulcrum point (borrowed from Larry Williams' Target Shooter).
rules.quote: Once standard deviation basically a measured move using this high down to that low, this low being a fulcrum point

rules.rule: Anchor the SD grid on a proper swing low: a low with a higher low on each side (summary-style dossier).
rules.quote: We have a low, higher low to the left of it, higher low to the right of it

rules.rule: Session-range variant: one standard deviation = the Central Bank Dealers Range height added above its high and subtracted below its low.
rules.quote: That measurement of price range in terms of pips can be reproduced or replicated if you will in the form of a standard deviation: one standard deviation above and below would be the same range added to the high of the Central Bank dealer's range and subtracted from the low.

rules.rule: The size of the Judas-swing (protraction) away from the CBDR becomes the multiplier for the next leg, so the grid is filled in units of that range.
rules.quote: How much of a standard deviation did we see? Because that becomes the known range to work with and it becomes our multiplier as well.

rules.rule: Float-range variant: use half of the float range as the repeating unit to project (paraphrase-style dossier).
rules.quote: you just keep projecting half of the float total range as a new number to fill.

rules.rule: The measured-move projection only becomes live after price breaks the fulcrum low; the swing alone does not guarantee delivery.
rules.quote: Just because I'm measuring a high to a low like that doesn't mean it's going to definitely go to that level. It first has to break below that low, and that's the fulcrum point. So whatever move it has done from that low to high, it's like a measured move idea.

rules.rule: 2016-17 swing-trader's model: after the fulcrum, if price trades lower the same measured move projects down from there.
rules.quote: So, this is a fulcrum point. So, everything that from this low up to this high here, if price goes lower, it should swing basically this measured move up should project that same thing down here.

rules.rule: Sequence on the way out: price reaching the old high/low (zero level) is the first scaling event; Target 1 is beyond it.
rules.quote: at that high or just below it that's where my first profit is that's your first scaling that's not your first target first target is here

rules.rule: Host-model entry used with these targets: limit at the 62% retracement of the swing, expect a retest of the day/previous-day high, then work targets 1, 2 and the symmetrical swing.
rules.quote: if it does form enter on the 62 percent retracement fib as it drops lower expect price to retest the high of the day or the previous day's high and then look for targets one two and symmetrical price swing on the FIB

rules.rule: 2020: prefers the 62% level as the entry so the order fills and covers the dealer spread; deeper 70.5/79% risks missing the trade (the 'low-hanging fruit approach' applied to entry).
