rules.quote: always using a 62 percent trace malevolent as your entry and try to use 2 70.5 level or the 79% tracin level but as I mentioned in previous recordings in this series you're likely to miss the trade and/or the dealer spread may not be covered for your entry to fill so again we're using the low-hanging fruit approach

rules.rule: 2017 stop sits exactly at the swing extreme with no pip buffer.
rules.quote: stop will be exactly at this low not 10 pips for 5 to put pips below that it's gonna be right at that low

rules.rule: 2023-24 Charter variant: stop 5 pips beyond the swing extreme.
rules.quote: stop loss below this low minus five Pips or five Pips below slowest low in the swing

rules.rule: Reward check: distance from entry to the first scaling must be about twice the risk (risk-to-reward is judged on the first scaling, not the final target).
rules.quote: whatever my risk is from here to here I want two times that from my entry to first profit

rules.rule: Symmetrical price swing = a 200 extension of the swing, i.e. the same leg repeated beyond the swing extreme (-1.0 on his fib).
rules.quote: gives us a symmetrical price swing if we do 2 of them that takes us up to here I guess it's a projection high of 76 79

rules.rule: Summary-style dossier: 162 extension as a good level, 200 extension as the runner objective (same geometry as -0.62 and -1.0).
rules.quote: The 162 would be a nice level, and ultimately our higher level profit objective is a 200 extension. That's your runner target.

rules.rule: Scale the exits to the pair's average daily range instead of assuming 100 pips (summary-style dossier).
rules.quote: It's not always 100 pips. I classify the average daily range for the Euro and the British Pound USD, and we scale out accordingly.

rules.rule: Exit choices: be conservative at the 20 level before the fib confluence, or take 25/30 round levels, or hold for the far cluster; exits are chosen from the institutional levels around the confluence.
rules.quote: here's your choices you can be conservative and get out at the 20 institutional level right before all those confluences agreed you can get out 1 1925 you can get out 1 1930 round number or you can hold for 1 1935 because their 5 levels 0 levels and obviously the 1 1920s institutional level

rules.rule: Prefer the exit nearest an institutional level; here he would take the 20 level.
rules.quote: the closer I can get to an institutional level the better truth be told 1 1920 would be my level

rules.rule: 2020 first scalp: at the -0.5 level, but only if it gives at least 15 pips.
rules.quote: using the fib levels point 50 or 0.5 negative 0.5 rather this is an area where you take first profit if it allows you if it allows you 15 pips or more okay so there's your rules you want to take 15 pips at first scalp exit at the negative 0.5 level

rules.rule: 2020 ladder in standard-deviation units of the OTE swing: old high (1:1), 0.5 SD, 1 SD, 1.5 SD and 2 SD, where he kills the trade.
rules.quote: at the old high we have a 1 to 1 right away at the old high at plus 15 pips at 1/2 a standard deviation it's up 29 pips 43 pips at 1 standard deviation 1 and a half standard deviations takes us to plus 56 pips and ultimately at 2 standard deviations where we would kill the trade at 70 pips

rules.rule: Round the projected target down to the nearest 10 level instead of demanding the exact fib number.
rules.quote: 6 5 1 0 is the nearest 10 level without getting up to that level so what we're doing is we're rounding down to the next 10 level okay

rules.rule: Target ladder: a swing that sets up at a mid figure (50) aims for the 80 level first.
rules.quote: if you ever see a swing that sets up at a mid figure anticipate it reaching up to the twenty seven eighty level as an objective

rules.rule: If the 80 level trades through, expect the big figure plus a 10-20 pip sweep above it.
rules.quote: and always always anticipate some measure of 10 to 20 pips above that big figure

rules.rule: Liquidity-pool overshoot: price generally reaches about 10-20 pips beyond a previous high or low.
rules.quote: I teach that price generally will reach about 10 to 20 pips above a previous high or low

rules.rule: CBDR-based SD expectations: sell-day highs usually stop at no more than 2 SD above the range (often 1 SD); buy-day lows reach at least 2 SD below.
rules.quote: Ideally sell days create the high of a day no more than two standard deviations above the Central Bank dealers range, many times just one standard deviation. Ideal buy days will create the low of the day no less than two standard deviations below the Central Bank dealers range.

rules.rule: Rule of four: expect roughly four SD projections to fill, with one more possible (paraphrase-style dossier).
rules.quote: four is just a general rule of thumb, it can always go one more level.

rules.rule: 2022: anchor the fib from the intermediate-term high to the swing low; -1.5 SD is the primary projection target.
rules.quote: the negative 1.5 standard deviation is your primary projection target

rules.rule: 2023: a -1.0 SD projection called the daily low to the tick (summary-style dossier).
rules.quote: down to a standard deviation of negative one (-1.0), and that is the daily low to the tick! That's what gives us the precision.

rules.rule: 2026: -2.5 SD drawn low-to-high with negative values, valued when it converges with another level.
rules.quote: So it's 2.5. Make sure it's negative on your fib and you're drawing it from low to high.

rules.rule: 2026: the daily high/low forms where a standard-deviation level agrees with a pool of liquidity (or a key inefficiency/FVG).
rules.quote: The only thing we're going to be doing is we're going to get an agreement with standard deviation and a pool of liquidity. That's what daily highs and lows work off of. And if it's not that, it's trading down to a key inefficiency or my fair value gaps

rules.rule: 2024 Model 7: grade targets 10, 20 and 30 pips beyond every new swing low.
rules.quote: every time we create a new low we do 10 20 30 pip grades below it to get our objective targets

rules.rule: Minimum size of a worthwhile target: 10 points (40 ticks) on index futures, 15 pips in forex.
rules.quote: the minimum trade framework should be 10 points or 40 ticks for index futures or indices the minimum trade framework should be 15 Pips for Forex pairs

rules.rule: Low-hanging fruit objective = the nearest obvious low/high or inefficiency, e.g. just getting to that old low.
rules.quote: What would be a low hanging fruit objective? Just getting to that low. Or as I mentioned in the analysis and commentary, this would be a low hanging fruit objective if it could just get down to that.

rules.rule: Low-hanging fruit is placed just above the relative equal lows (front-running the pool), even though the full move could go through.
rules.quote: So, even though it was likely to lead into this, I used a low-hanging fruit objective to get in, which would be just above the relative equal lows.

rules.rule: Target selection at the open: look left for the first pool of relative equal highs/lows.
rules.quote: Because this is the first one you come to at opening bell at 9:30 open, start looking to the left. Where is the first relative equal highs? They pop off right here.

rules.rule: Gap variant: the 50% midpoint of the Friday-close to Monday-open gap is the easiest low-hanging fruit objective.
rules.quote: the easiest low hanging fruit objective would be half of that Gap that was formed from previous week's closing price on Friday and the Monday open opening price of this present week

rules.rule: Lunch-macro variant (clock-based): the first swing high after 10:00 is the low-hanging fruit.
rules.quote: that's the lunch macro that's exactly the low-hanging fruit objective for the lunch macro.

rules.rule: 2017 use of the phrase: 20-25 pips per setup, two per week, 50 pips a week is low-hanging fruit for a developing trader.
rules.quote: focusing on 20-25 pips per setup in an aiming for two good ones per week I think 50 pips is a really low hanging fruit reachable achievable and certainly realistic in the scope of a developing trader

rules.rule: 2017: at Target 1 (fib) move the stop to break-even with no partial; at Target 2 take a portion off and move the stop to just below the first-scaling (old-high) level.
rules.quote: if it trades up to target one on your fib that would be in this case 130 169 at that moment then you can move your stop-loss to break-even and take no partial and then try to reach for target 2 and at that point take a portion of the trade off and then move to stop-loss just below 130 154

rules.rule: 2020: once the first scaling pays 15+ pips, cut the stop to about the midpoint of the swing range.
rules.quote: if you can get first scaling where it's 15 pips or more you want to start reducing your risk on your stop to about midpoint of the range that you identified here

rules.rule: 2020: collapse the day trade at 2 SD; if price action favours more, take 80% off and leave 20% on.
rules.quote: the rules for this model is you collapse at two standard deviations but if you have a criteria in price action that lends well to a likely outcome of reaching for a higher target then at this point here you absolutely have to have 80% off and then leave 20% on

rules.rule: Beyond 2 SD only a small leftover portion is kept.
rules.quote: if you think you're going to go higher than that leave a leader in oh it's a small portion of your original position to see if you can capture anything

rules.rule: 2017 partial size: swing trade 50% off at the first objective; day trade 75-80% off.
rules.quote: for a swing trade you can take off like 50% leave the remaining 50% on whereas a day trade if it goes to your first objective you want to think about 75 to 80% off and leave a small portion on because it's a day trade

rules.rule: Front-run the projected cluster: exit a little ahead of the overlapping fibs (spread buffer) and always leave a little on.
rules.quote: I want to be out before that I want to be out at 26 95 I want to be just a little bit ahead of all those overlapping fibs because I want to make sure I get my price so I'll always leave a little bit on

rules.rule: 2026: rest limit orders just ahead of the target level (the sell-side pool) rather than at it.
rules.quote: Now, because I want to get out before it gets down there, I had limit orders just ahead of that level right there

rules.rule: Do not insist on the full draw on liquidity; bank the nearer objective (22.25 handles on ES instead of holding for the draw).
rules.quote: And I did not need to trade to the draw on liquidity. This is a crucial point, folks: don't insist that your target or your draw on liquidity is the be-all end-all objective and you have to hold for that. That is foolish.

rules.rule: 2024 Charter stop reduction: cut the stop by 25% when 25% of the expected objective is in profit (and 50% at 50%).
rules.quote: when we are in profit 25% of our expected objective stop-loss can be reduced by 25%

rules.rule: 2024 Charter: stop goes to break-even only at 75% of the expected profit objective (contrasts with 2017 break-even at Target 1).
rules.quote: when position is at 75% of the expected profit objective stop must be at break even at that point

rules.rule: 2024 Model 10: at most two partials; the third take-profit closes everything.
rules.quote: in your rules you want to say that two partials on the third take profit all your position comes off it's as simple as that

rules.rule: 2026: heavy partials into the standard-deviation extensions.
rules.quote: taking heavy partials into these standard deviation extensions.

rules.rule: Skip the trade if the entry is already past the level where the first scalping profit-taking level sits.
rules.quote: what would be their absolute latest time you can use for an entry it's where your first scalping profit-taking level is it's got to be at or below that otherwise you can't take the trade okay so there's your trade filter

rules.rule: Skip the setup if the swing is too small to allow three partials plus a runner (four scaling stages).
rules.quote: in my case I like to look for a leverage that allows me to take three partials and then give me something to let run that means I can get four stages of scaling out of that position not all positions will allow me to do that and here's the thing if it doesn't let me do that I don't take that trade

rules.rule: CBDR-based SD projections are not used when the range is wider than 40 pips.
rules.quote: We move to the sidelines and we do not look to trade with the Central Bank dealers range in our repertoire when the range is greater than 40 pips.

rules.rule: Example of a 58-pip CBDR day: too large, so the projections are not usable that day.
rules.quote: The next one in our example here the range is 58 pips. Now this is too large. Our rules state that we want to have 40 pips or less, ideally 20 to 30 pips. So this particular trading day we have to allow the market to do whatever it wants to do

rules.rule: Do not force the SD grid every day; it needs a 20-30 pip CBDR.
rules.quote: where this will get you in trouble is you're going to try to apply the standard deviations every single day and you're going to forget about the importance of having a range between 20 and 30 pips for the Central Bank dealers range.

rules.rule: An isolated SD level is useless; it needs a convergence with other levels (HTF array, pool).
rules.quote: Not interested at that level because it's by itself. It's isolated. Isolated levels are useless. There has to be a convergence of several things that I teach in terms of smart money concepts that makes the level viable

rules.rule: Claims the swing/OTE projection method works on all pairs, markets and asset classes (2017 examples are 1h to 5m forex).
rules.quote: I'm going to be using this currency pair this works on all currency pairs all markets all asset classes as well

rules.rule: 2020: carried over from forex to ES index futures (handles instead of pips).
rules.quote: one of the central tenets that this pattern is it's not limited to 4x so I'm going to show you how you can use it in the futures market this is an index futures and it's the delivery contract of June 2020 of the S P e-mini futures

rules.rule: 2026: prefers ES over NQ for clean price action and key levels.
rules.quote: More professionals trade S&P than the Nasdaq, simply because it's much more cleaner in terms of its price action

rules.rule: Forex tolerance: an SD target counts as hit if delivered within 3-5 pips.
rules.quote: remember standard deviations are within 3 to five Pips that's considered precision in Forex

rules.rule: CBDR window is 14:00-20:00 New York time; ideal width under 40 pips, preferably 20-30.
rules.quote: The time period that frames the Central Bank dealers range is 2:00 PM to 8:00 PM New York time. The ideal range is less than 40 pips, preferably the range should be no more than 20 to 30 pips in total range high to low.

rules.rule: 14:00 New York usually caps the high/low of a trending day, so CBDR SD targets are expected before then.
rules.quote: Even in a really long winded trending day, 2:00 PM usually caps the high or low of the day if we continue through London Close Kill Zone

rules.rule: 2020 OTE series window for the swing-based SD ladder: 08:30-11:00 New York.
rules.quote: focusing primarily for moves within the 8:30 a.m. to 11:00 a.m. New York session

rules.rule: 2017 scalp window for the Target 1/2/symmetrical ladder: 07:00-09:00 New York.
rules.quote: wait until 7:00 a.m. New York time to stock your long entry between 7:00 a.m. and 9:00 a.m. New York time

rules.rule: 2025: midnight opening range (00:00-00:30) is the base for 0.5/-1 SD projections.
rules.quote: If you look at the opening range, this is the lowest low in that range between 12:00 and 12:30 and here's the highest high of the range

partials.summary: Pay yourself in stages: sell part of the position at the first opposing liquidity pool (old high/low, previous-day extreme, opposing FVG or its CE, 50% equilibrium, event horizon, a standard-deviation level), make the rest safe with a structure-based stop, and let a small runner reach the terminus. It is a management overlay on other entry models, not an entry model.
partials.needs_clock: The partial logic itself is clockless. It uses only price structure: opposing swing extremes, FVG/volume-imbalance edges and their 50% (CE), the 50% equilibrium of the dealing range, the midpoint between two pools (event horizon), standard-deviation or Fibonacci projections, and the stop trail. All of that could run on a 24/7 synthetic index using only price delivery. He also uses it in the quiet Asian session (7M56e9O06Ko), so it is not tied to a killzone. Only four things touch the clock: (1) the rule 'if ADR high is reached prior to 10 AM take 80% off' (OVfn-gDk2dE), which can be approximated by 'daily-range target reached within the first N bars of the session' or dropped; (2) news-day variants (NFP/CPI/PPI/Fed speech 10:00: heavier partials, delayed stop tightening); (3) the 2020 forex drills, which only take the entry inside 08:30-11:00 NY (that clock belongs to the entry model, not to the partial ladder); (4) the 'high resistance'/holiday-volume regime notes, which are about participation. Dropping these loses only the news and ADR-timing variants.
partials.how_to_code:
Treat it as a position-management state machine layered on any entry model. Inputs: entry E, initial stop S, R=|E-S|, direction, position size N (contracts or lots).

1. Build the pool ladder in the trade direction beyond E, nearest first. Candidates: (a) the most recent opposing swing extreme or previous-day/session extreme (the 'old high/low', 'zero level' of the OTE fib); (b) the near edge or CE of an opposing FVG / volume imbalance / NWOG-NDOG; (c) the 50% equilibrium of the active dealing range (for a long, only partial on the premium side of it); (d) event horizon = midpoint between pool 1 and the next larger pool; (e) standard-deviation projections of the dealing range (-0.5, -1, -1.5, -2, -2.5) or fib -0.27/-0.62/-1.0 and 162%/200% extensions; (f) ADR fractions for forex. Pool 1 is the nearest candidate. In the 2017 teaching it had to pay at least 2R (Cg0-CFJOJvg 17:09). In 2020 it had to be worth at least 15 pips and the setup had to allow 3 partials plus a runner (E9F_aT9f038). In the modern futures videos there is no minimum, only the pool.
2. Place resting limit orders at or a tick or two ahead of each pool (OYNpIeu9czw). Do not wait for a close beyond it.
3. When pool 1 fills, sell fraction f1. It is a parameter, and his own values vary: 0.5 for swing and 0.75-0.8 for day trades in 2017; 0.5-0.8 in the 2022 Month 8 lessons; 0.6-0.8 at the 60m equilibrium; 0.8 at ADR before 10:00; a third to a half of the contracts in the 2023 to 2026 futures trades (5 of 15, 3 of 9, 1 of 3, half for a 'double tap'); about 0.25 of the remainder at event horizon. Then move the stop to cover costs or breakeven (older teaching: breakeven or +1 pip), or to a structural level instead: behind the newest swing, the far side or CE of the latest FVG, or under the wick low. Never loosen a stop once it is moved.
4. On each further pool, sell f2, f3 and re-trail the stop. Model 10 rule: after two partials, everything comes off at the third objective. Older day-trade rule: collapse at 2 SD and leave about 20% only if price action favours more (80/20). Keep a runner (one contract, 10-20%) for the terminus, such as the 200% extension or the HTF pool.
5. 'Running down equity' trigger: if a new extreme in your favour prints and no partial has been taken yet, take one.
6. Defensive partial: instead of one stop for everything, put a stop order on a fraction (for example 2 of 7 contracts) at the nearest defensive structure, and keep the rest on the wider stop. When the market is sluggish or the pool above/below is unpurged, shrink to a one-contract runner and trail to the nearest micro swing.
7. Exits and exceptions: a single contract cannot be partialed (manage by stop only). A pure scalper takes one exit at the first pool. A 'full pull' with no partials is allowed when he expects heavy displacement.

Objective parts: swing/FVG/CE/equilibrium/SD levels, limit orders at them, stop trailing rules, fixed fractions in a given era, the 75% breakeven rule (NB7Bku099tU), and the ADR-before-10:00 rule. Subjective parts: which pool counts as the 'first' pool; the size of f1 (he varies it with environment, news, sluggishness and unpurged pools); choosing the 'defensive PD arrays' to trail behind; how event-horizon anchors are chosen (old low to next pool is ballparked); when to skip partials; when to shrink to a single runner; reading 'bodies respecting the upper/lower half' as the exit cue. For backtests, fix a ladder (for example 50% at pool 1 plus stop to BE, 30% at pool 2, 20% runner trailed behind structure) and test the variants as separate parameter sets.
partials.changes_over_time:
The core idea never changes: pay yourself at liquidity and do not demand the terminus. The mechanics change a lot.

1. First-partial size and unit. 2017: percentages by style, with 50% or more for swing/short-term and 75-80% for a day trade (Yqio1Ja0lIQ 32:58, 9CCrlTIrkxw 26:35). The Vol 7 dossier (J_7v2i3ogwk) shows a 50/30/20 ladder at old low / 162% / 200%, but that table is dossier summary and the verbatim quotes only give the 162% and 200% runner target. 2020: a pip-based ladder (15 pips minimum at -0.5, then -1 SD rounded to a 10 level), 3 partials plus a runner or skip the trade, and 80% off / 20% on beyond 2 SD (E9F_aT9f038, ZbkEvNpm-_k). 2022 core content: 50% at +3R in the Month 02 account-growth example (pctqB3UD6dk), 50-80% at the first objective (-cXnnHjy9s0), 60-80% at the 60m equilibrium (5Z_3NbclMSY), 80% at ADR before 10:00 (OVfn-gDk2dE), 30/30/40 for the weekly swing (VL4YLTRerHY). 2024 Charter models: scalping Model 12 sells 8 of 10 at 20 pips; Model 10 sells everything at the third objective after two partials (a conflict with the older 'always leave a runner'). 2023 to 2026 futures: contract counts (5 of 15, 3 of 9, one of three) and, in 2026, about 25% of the remainder at event horizon and 'half off at the easy pool' for the double tap.

2. Stop after the first partial. 2017: breakeven (Yqio1Ja0lIQ 36:04), or +1 pip (7WM8qdkanIY 25:06 'move my stop down to +1'). One 2017 dossier (UuMaC9n8Uy4 17:15) has him move the stop to breakeven at target 1 with 'no partial' and take a portion only at target 2. 2020: stop to the midpoint after a first scaling of 15+ pips, then 2-3 pips beyond entry after the second (E9F_aT9f038). Oct 2022: breakeven +1 pip. 2023 to 2025: warnings against rushing to breakeven or 'jamming' the stop (VLis0LcbUaQ summary, WGGDbeRpo4w 39:29 'I'm not in a rush to jam my stop'), and the 25/50/75 rule from 2024 (NB7Bku099tU: breakeven only at 75% of the objective). Dec 2023 swing video rZFisy9AILQ ('Leaving Stop Unchanged After 3 Partials') says to leave the original stop alone after three partials. Its rules are tagged IMPLIED and its 'Verbatim Quote' cells are paraphrases, not real quotes, so that rule cannot be quoted. The 2017 swing quote (9CCrlTIrkxw 12:23) says something similar. 2025 to 2026: stops go behind specific PD arrays (FVG CE or far edge, wick low, gap low) and, once committed, are never retracted (tByaPnk3fc4). The first-partial-then-breakeven rule of 2017 to 2022 therefore conflicts with the 2023 to 2025 'do not rush' material.

3. Are partials mandatory? 2017 to 2023: yes ('never exit 100% at T1', 'you always pay yourself'; Dec 2023 'hoping and praying' remark in A97shZGPE2I 01:04:30). The exceptions come later: hit-and-run scalping takes no partials (aaKO-eu-tQ4, May 2024); a 'full pull' with no partials when he expects heavy displacement (r3E1WQcx2-c, Jan 2025); a single contract cannot be partialed (rtIcbG6twrI, Jul 2026). In 2026 he rebuts critics who call partials 'for scared traders' (O217xQsEUgI), as he did in 2020 (RP6rVMJP4hA 06:01).

4. Vocabulary and framing. 2017 to 2020: fib targets (-0.27, -0.62, -1.0 symmetrical, 162%/200%), standard deviations, pips and the Average Daily Range. 2022 to 2023: equilibrium, CE, NWOG, Ma Deuce quadrants, R-multiples and % account growth. 2025: 'costs and risk covered', walk away after a partial. 2026 adds new names: Event Horizon, double tap, running down equity, free look ('it pays me $837 to see if I can hold'), defensive partial by a partial stop order, and 'premium-side only' partials.

5. Source-quality cautions. Some dossiers (rZFisy9AILQ and parts of J_7v2i3ogwk, pctqB3UD6dk and the 2022 Month 02 set) mix real quotes with generated analysis. Only the verbatim lines are used above. The pcw_ty0hqoo timestamp '01:72' is printed that way in the dossier.
partials.markets: Forex: EURUSD, GBPUSD, AUDUSD, USDJPY, USDCAD, USDCHF, GBPJPY (2017 to 2020 OTE lessons, 2022 core content, 2024 Charter models; AUDUSD 1h for the 2017 swing example, 5m for the 2020 OTE drills). Crude oil CL (30 May 2020, ZbkEvNpm-_k). Gold appears only as a conceptual OTE illustration. Index futures: ES (2022 to 2023) and above all NQ/MNQ (live executions from Dec 2023 to Oct 2026, mostly on the 1m chart, including the Asian-session NQ trade in 7M56e9O06Ko). Note on trades_shown: 134 is a keyword count, not his own tally. It is the number of rows in the 'Trades taken or shown' tables (662 rows across 627 dossiers with such a table) whose text mentions partial, scaled, scale-out, scaling, runner, banked, 'took N off' or 'contracts off'. These rows sit in 129 dossiers. About 60 of the 134 are dated 2026. Many rows are brief summaries, so treat it as approximate.

rules.rule: Always pay yourself: whenever the market offers a chance to take something off, scaling out is mandatory, not optional (2020 OTE lesson).
rules.quote: as a general rule of thumb you always pay yourself

rules.rule: Law of Partials: a partial gets you paid and takes risk off the table.
rules.quote: getting paid. Okay? Partials, when you take on partial profit, in history, you take the risk off the table

rules.rule: Reject 'all or nothing'; take partials and pay yourself on the way to the bigger objective.
rules.quote: Take partials. Don't listen to people who tell you it's all or nothing. I've learned to pay myself on the way to the higher-end profit objective.

rules.rule: Rationale (Diminishing Risk): after a partial the remaining position is easy to hold psychologically.
rules.quote: The concept applied to this by taking partials is diminishing risk. It's so much easier to hold on to a trade psychologically and emotionally

rules.rule: Regime filter: when the Dollar Index is range-bound he dials expectations back to scalp-size objectives, so profits are taken early.
rules.quote: It's not really making any ground higher or lower. So our prognostication is dialed back because we're not looking for big trending moves

rules.rule: News-driven days: set an extreme final target but bank partials along the way because unrealized profit can vanish.
rules.quote: but being mindful that you got to take partials along the way because NFP can take it quickly away from you if it's unrealized profit

rules.rule: 2017 OTE: first scaling sits at the old high (or just below it); this is distinct from the first full target further out.
rules.quote: at that high or just below it that's where my first profit is that's your first scaling that's not your first target first target is here

rules.rule: First partial order pre-placed above the previous day's high (timestamp printed as 01:72 in the dossier).
rules.quote: I have my orders set to take two off above the previous day's high

rules.rule: Futures: first partial (5 of 15 contracts) at the first algorithmic swing projection target.
rules.quote: That swing projection target is my first target, I'll take five contracts out

rules.rule: Partial at the 50% equilibrium of the dealing range.
rules.quote: It's 50/50, so I'm going to take three contracts off of it right here

rules.rule: Month 8 day trading: 60-80% off at the 50% equilibrium of the 60-minute range being traded.
rules.quote: At the equilibrium of the price range you are trading inside of on a 60-minute chart, take or have taken 60 to 80 percent off

rules.rule: Ma Deuce: first partial at consequent encroachment (50%) of the gap, second at the lower 25% quadrant, remainder at the next discount array.
rules.quote: first partial would be here at consequent encroachment and you let it run some more to get down to the lower quadrant

rules.rule: 2026 Event Horizon = halfway point between a nearby pool and the old high / larger pool; used as a partial anchor.
rules.quote: We're inside that fair value gap we're going to see event horizon, which is again the halfway point between the 1-hour minor buy side liquidity pool and then the old high here.

rules.rule: Take one contract off when price reaches the event horizon between an old low and the next target.
rules.quote: this is an old low down to there. Okay? So, if it gets in this vicinity here, I'll take one off cuz that's event horizon.

rules.rule: Long: do not take the partial below the 50% mark; take it on the premium side.
rules.quote: I just don't want to take a partial below halfway. So, everything here is germane. I'm taking a partial in in the premium side of the low where I longed from

rules.rule: Double tap: two profit zones, an easy near pool (center mass) and a far runner target (head shot).
rules.quote: Double tap is simply one to the head, one to the chest. So this would be a head shot up here and this is center mass or torso.

rules.rule: If a key pool (relative equal highs/lows) is still unpurged against the trade, take heavier partials early.
rules.quote: initially I took more off in the beginning of the trade because I wasn't comfortable holding the the risk that was on the trade because I was put off by not seeing these relative equal highs taken.

rules.rule: 2017 forex: each time the move has traded about a 100-pip interval, something must come off.
rules.quote: anytime your moves ever traded a hundred pip intervals you have to take something off learn to do that

rules.rule: Running down equity: on a new extreme (new low for a short) with no partial yet, pay yourself rather than wait for the terminus.
rules.quote: Anytime it creates a new low and you haven't taken a partial yet it's actually a good idea to to pay yourself

rules.rule: Partial the moment the first structural low breaks and costs are recovered.
rules.quote: I'm going to take off five there because we broke a low and costs are recovered

rules.rule: Execute the partial as a resting limit order at or just ahead of the key liquidity level, not at market.
rules.quote: scale out of a short position by taking partial profits with a limit order at or just ahead of the identified key liquidity level

rules.rule: After first profit put the stop where it cannot take you out below (above, for shorts) entry.
rules.quote: there's nothing better than taking first profit and putting your stop in a position where it doesn't take you out below your entry or in case if you're shorting above your entry

rules.rule: 2017: first partial then stop to breakeven.
rules.quote: if it allows you to make a hundred pips when you take your first partial off and put your stop at breakeven you're in a beautiful position

rules.rule: Month 8: at first objective take 50-80% and move stop to breakeven plus one pip.
rules.quote: Once price moves in your favor and hits your first objective, you must take off 50% to 80% of your position and move your stop to breakeven plus one pip to eliminate risk.

rules.rule: 2020: after a second scaling the stop must sit 2-3 pips beyond entry in profit.
rules.quote: if you ever get a second scaling you have to be above your entry point at least 2 or 3 pips and just let it go

rules.rule: 2024 Charter variant: stop only goes to breakeven at 75% of the expected objective (do not rush it); conflicts with the earlier breakeven-after-first-partial.
rules.quote: when position is at 75% of the expected profit objective stop must be at break even at that point

rules.rule: 2017 minimum: the first scaling must pay at least 2x the risk.
rules.quote: whatever my risk is from here to here I want two times that from my entry to first profit

rules.rule: 2020 forex: first scale-out at the -0.5 fib level provided it is worth 15 pips or more.
rules.quote: this is an area where you take first profit if it allows you if it allows you 15 pips or more okay so there's your rules you want to take 15 pips at first scalp exit at the negative 0.5 level

rules.rule: Size at first objective: about 80% off for a day trader, at least half for short-term/swing.
rules.quote: as a day trader you certainly want to be banking 80% of your position and if you're a short-term trader you want to be at least half your position out because the weekly can change gears midweek

rules.rule: Swing 50% off / 50% on; day trade 75-80% off with a small portion left.
rules.quote: for a swing trade you can take off like 50% leave the remaining 50% on whereas a day trade if it goes to your first objective you want to think about 75 to 80% off

rules.rule: Month 02 example: first profit objective at 3:1 reward to risk with half the position (the dossier summary says 50% at +3R).
rules.quote: If we take our two percent position and we look for a first profit objective of three to one reward to risk

rules.rule: Weekly swing split: 30% / 30% / 40% runner trailed behind daily swing lows.
rules.quote: Scale out 30% at the first weekly objective, 30% at the second, and hold the remaining 40% with a trailing stop behind daily swing lows until the macro target is reached.

rules.rule: 2026 double tap: half the position off at the easiest (nearest) pool, rest for the head-shot target.
rules.quote: So this is the easiest one. So half the position comes off there

rules.rule: 2026 Event Horizon: about 25% of the remaining position off there, runner reaches for the rest.
rules.quote: Take about 25% of the remaining portion off when you're at event horizon

rules.rule: Runner objective: 162% extension as a nice level, 200% extension as the runner target.
rules.quote: The 162 would be a nice level, and ultimately our higher level profit objective is a 200 extension. That's your runner target.

rules.rule: 2020 model: 80% off and 20% left as runner when price action favors reaching beyond the 2 SD exit.
rules.quote: if you have a criteria in price action that lends well to a likely outcome of reaching for a higher target then at this point here you absolutely have to have 80% off and then leave 20% on

rules.rule: Day-trade hard exit at 2 standard deviations (a small leader may stay on).
rules.quote: the rules for this model says we have to bail on the day trade at 2 standard deviations

rules.rule: Model 10 (2024): at most two partials; at the third take-profit everything comes off.
rules.quote: in your rules you want to say that two partials on the third take profit all your position comes off it's as simple as that

rules.rule: Model 12 scalping (2024): 8 of 10 off at the 20-pip first profit, leave 2.
rules.quote: you could take eight of those minis off at 20 Pips whenever you get first profit in the scalping model leave two on

rules.rule: Trail: as price keeps taking out highs, step the stop up behind structure.
rules.quote: your favor and it keeps taking highs out and you're long, you step your stop up behind structure

rules.rule: Once the first partial is paid, getting stopped on the rest no longer matters.
rules.quote: It's running right up into first partial. And at that point, you know, it doesn't make a difference if it comes all the way back down to stop me out

rules.rule: Defensive partial: put a stop order on only part of the position (2 of 7) so a retracement sells a partial instead of all or nothing.
rules.quote: I had seven contracts net long. I put two contracts on a stop right here. So, if it goes below there, it's going to sell two of the seven I had as a partial

rules.rule: Stop sits just beyond the defensive swing low wick, then rolls beneath the next low.
rules.quote: defense is this swing low, which is why I have my stop loss just below this wick. Okay? Once it does that, then I'm going to roll the stop just below that low right there.

rules.rule: Trail only behind verified PD arrays (wick CE, gap low, imbalance base); price trading below them breaks the runner's premise.
rules.quote: So I can actually bring my stop up and lock in a little bit more juice out of this lemon because if it's going to retrace, it shouldn't find its way below this wick's consequent encouragement.

rules.rule: After a partial, lower (short) or raise (long) the stop to the far side of the newest FVG.
rules.quote: And there's a partial again. and I lowered the stop right above the high of that fair value gap because if it's now going to trade back to it, it's going to go higher.

rules.rule: Take two off, roll the stop under the wick low, then strangle the last contract with the stop.
rules.quote: I'm going to take two off there. And I'm going to roll the stop underneath that wick low. Cuz if it goes there, I don't want to be a part of it anymore

rules.rule: Sluggish market: shrink to a minimum runner and drag the stop down aggressively to the nearest micro high.
rules.quote: in the event that it should pop up and get the stop loss it's not taking two contracts it's just taking one okay and lower to stop down aggressively to that little short-term High

rules.rule: Free look: the banked partial pays for staying in the remainder toward event horizon and the target.
rules.quote: It pays me $837 to see if I can hold on to it long enough to ride this bull

rules.rule: After partials are banked, accept that the runner can be stopped out.
rules.quote: You're in a position now where if it goes to your target it's wonderful, and if it doesn't you've already locked in your gains

rules.rule: 2017 swing: during consolidation do not trail the stop; take partials and only trail after the run leaves the consolidation.
rules.quote: leave your stop down here okay do not trail your stop-loss you want to be taking partials okay

rules.rule: Never retract a trailed stop once it is committed.
rules.quote: As soon as you commit to a stop loss that's adjusted that way, stick with that.

rules.rule: 2020 pre-trade filter: if the trade cannot be scaled in 4 stages (3 partials plus a runner), skip it.
rules.quote: not all positions will allow me to do that and here's the thing if it doesn't let me do that I don't take that trade

rules.rule: Exception: a hit-and-run scalper takes no partials and exits at the first logical liquidity.
rules.quote: if you are going to be hard and fast and you want to be a surgical hit and run type scalper you don't take any partials you just take the first logical level of liquidity

rules.rule: Exception: a single contract cannot be partialed, so it is managed by the stop only.
rules.quote: Since I'm only using one contract, it's got to be managed through the stop loss. There's no ability for me to do partials because I only have a single contract.

rules.rule: Exception: no partials when expecting a full sell-side pull from heavy order flow.
rules.quote: I'm not going to do any partials so it's going to be a full pull to sell side liquidity if I can get it

rules.rule: Scaling is calibrated to the Average Daily Range of EURUSD and GBPUSD (2017).
rules.quote: It's not always 100 pips. I classify the average daily range for the Euro and the British Pound USD, and we scale out accordingly.

rules.rule: 2026: trades NQ only and says what he teaches applies to other markets.
rules.quote: looking at the NASDAQ again. Keeping things simple. Not a long list of markets to look at. Everything I'm teaching here is applicable to everything else.

rules.rule: If the ADR high is reached before 10:00 AM New York, take 80% off.
rules.quote: If ADR high is reached prior to 10 AM, take 80% off of your position.

rules.rule: During the 10:00 Fed speech, delay lowering the stop (do not strangle the runner).
rules.quote: Until we get below this with a body, I don't want to lower the stop loss down to the low of that inversion fair value gap yet cuz it could just real quick cuz the Fed's talking right now.

rules.rule: Works in the quiet Asian session as well; it only means slower delivery.
rules.quote: Usually Asia is just simply very subdued. Doesn't mean you can't find something to feed you.

pyramiding.summary: Once the first position is in profit, add size into each fresh FVG, order block or volume imbalance that forms in the trade direction after displacement, and raise the stop each time so the whole stack's costs and risk are covered. Take every tranche off into the liquidity pool. He never adds to a loser.
pyramiding.needs_clock: No. The rule is price-only: a winning position, a fresh FVG, OB or volume imbalance after displacement, a premium/discount location against the dealing range, and a stop that covers costs. It could run on 24/7 synthetic indices using only price delivery. The clock appears only as a setting for his demos (1:50-2:10 PM, 09:50-10:10, 08:50-09:10 macros, London 04:30-05:10, pre-market ahead of 9:30). The 2025-26 octant, quadrant and opening-gap anchors (NDOG/NWOG/RTH opening range gap) need a session clock, but a swing-defined dealing range replaces them. On synthetics, 'costs covered' means spread, not the $10 per contract round turn he quotes.
pyramiding.how_to_code:
The trade count is approximate: it counts each dossier whose trade table or chart note shows size added to a winner. About 57 dossiers qualify, from 2022-02 to 2026-09, usually one trade each with 1-4 adds. Adds per trade run from 1 to 4 and total size from 3 to 25 contracts. The eight start videos are EIwGNs9A430, vuBRMFhFZAY, ojy5ApHhEu4, twgtbikJtL0, 3FGFEuaDSOc, SObhjCvXCNk, Fv3gNx9ta0I and whBgkHxUSQQ. Seven of them have a trade row. whBgkHxUSQQ teaches pre-market pyramiding but has no trade table.

It is a management overlay on a position opened by another model, not a standalone entry.

1. Preconditions. Track an open position with direction d (short = -1) and a list of fills. Require the first structural break in d: close beyond the prior swing low (shorts) or high (longs), or a displacement candle with body > k*ATR(14). The 'we broke a low and costs are recovered' step belongs here. Subjective: k, and the swing fractal size.
2. Fresh PD array created after the initial entry, in the trade direction. Bearish FVG: low[i-2] > high[i]. Bullish FVG: high[i-2] < low[i]. Volume imbalance: adjacent bodies with non-overlapping bodies but overlapping wicks. Order block (shorts): the last up-close candle, or the run of consecutive up-close candles, before a down leg that breaks a swing low. Reclaimed FVG: a gap price has already traded through both ways but is still respected. Add arrays only while formed after the entry. Subjective: displacement strength, and which of several gaps is 'first presented'.
3. Add trigger. Price retraces into the array: touch of the near edge or CE (50%) of the FVG, or the open or mean threshold of the OB. Candle bodies must not close beyond the far edge (the order block's open for shorts). Wicks through are tolerated.
4. Location gate (Charter era, 2024): a dealing range from the swing leg being traded. Allow short adds only if price >= midpoint, long adds only if price <= midpoint. Block adds once price crosses it. Intraday silent videos do not state this gate, so make it a toggle. Subjective: which range counts.
5. Risk gate before sending the add: set the stop S so that the stack's net PnL at S, including costs, is >= 0. Equivalently S = blended entry + d*(cost per unit), and the add price must still be on the correct side of S. If the stop would sit on the wrong side of price, skip the add. Strict variant (ojy5ApHhEu4): first trail to cover the existing stack's risk, then add. Loose variant (k26euOG6zAk, ypkWB8EpO5s): add first, then raise the stop to just beyond the new OB/FVG, which is only risk-reduced.
6. Sizing. 2022 rule: size[add] <= size[initial], decreasing. 2024 trades add equal or larger tranches (6 then +9, 5 then +10). Make add size a parameter. Cap total risk: aggregate worst-case loss <= initial risk, or <= 1% for position trades. Observed adds per trade: 1 to 4.
7. Stop trail. After each add: for shorts, stop = high of the newest bearish OB or FVG (his own annotation: 'Stop Loss Is FVG High'). Do not move the stop below an array until a body trades through it. Do not choke the stop tight on news.
8. Exits. Partial of a third to two thirds at the first internal pool (relative equal lows/highs, prior session extreme). The rest runs to the external pool or is stopped. Close all tranches together at the terminal pool.
9. Invalidation: no add when the position is not in profit, when the new array was already violated by a body close, when price has crossed equilibrium, or inside a range without displacement.

Subjective parts: displacement threshold, the dealing range, whether an OB is 'valid' (compound OBs), which FVG is first presented, and the add size. Objective parts: FVG/volume-imbalance geometry, equilibrium test, and stop and cost arithmetic.
pyramiding.changes_over_time:
1. Size shape. In 2022 he says biggest first, then smaller, and never more contracts on later entries than the initial (QKc_i90chVg 35:41, EpGQnhjXBq8 49:38, tpPtItWqmlg 32:20). Several 2024 executions add equal or larger tranches: ES 6 then +9 (ypkWB8EpO5s), 5 then +10 (My9wQ8_UtZk), NQ 6 then +4 +4 (2QD_2AG7Syo). The 2022 'smaller adds' rule is not kept in later videos. Those silent videos carry no spoken rule.
2. Stop ordering. ojy5ApHhEu4 (2023-01) says never add until the previous risk is neutralized by trailing the stop. In k26euOG6zAk (2022-05-11), j0Z2EbuJXGU (2022-05-16) and ypkWB8EpO5s (2024-08-27) the stop is raised on or after the add and still sits beyond the entry, so risk is only reduced. Only AxNoqk5Vx8o (2024-09) and Fv3gNx9ta0I (breakeven first, then adds) show the stop at cost or better. 'Costs & Risk Covered' appears in 2024-09 (as a chart annotation) and 'costs are recovered' in 2024-01 (spoken). vuBRMFhFZAY (2023-01) is described as warning against trailing stops too early.
3. Location gate. In the 2024 Charter lessons (SObhjCvXCNk Jan 10, oheyS8MUqno Jan 31, YIxurbDNrWM Feb 8) and the 2024-04-30 stream (joqM_Z96vtM), adds are allowed only on the premium side for shorts and the discount side for longs. 2022-23 videos state no such gate. Fv3gNx9ta0I adds at 19,132 and 19,113 while price is falling through the NDOG low into the discount half, which conflicts with the gate if 'discount' is judged on the dealing range from that day's high.
4. Risk cap. The 1% aggregate cap appears only in position-trade lessons (SObhjCvXCNk, okN5p701T7Y, crPpMwgwa7k). Intraday videos use the stop-to-cover-risk idea instead.
5. Stance on pyramiding. 2022-09-07 (SO3SJFNRim8) forbids it in the one-contract income plan. 2025-01-01 (6wt3xy34bNk) cautions against pyramiding and going crazy, yet the 2024-2026 silent videos show it constantly, up to 25 NQ contracts.
6. Consolidations. whBgkHxUSQQ (2023-12-11) says beginners avoid consolidations, but advanced traders pyramid deep inside a pre-market consolidation ahead of 9:30.
7. Array vocabulary over time: 2022 FVG/OB after MSS; 2023 inversion FVG, rejection block, wick CE; 2024 reclaimed FVG, breakaway gap, volume imbalance; 2025 BISI/SIBI, first-presented FVG; 2026 quadrant/octant, 'chain of custody'.
8. Source quality. Many 2023-2026 'Rules He States' cells for this model are the dossier writer's description of silent videos (evidence tag SHOWN or IMPLIED). Some are not in quote marks (twgtbikJtL0, ojy5ApHhEu4, 3FGFEuaDSOc, EIwGNs9A430 transcript summaries). Treat those as likely paraphrase. The strongest spoken quotes are 2022 (tpPtItWqmlg, EpGQnhjXBq8, QKc_i90chVg, k26euOG6zAk), 2024-01 Charter (SObhjCvXCNk, oheyS8MUqno, YIxurbDNrWM, VODMCdDnMs8), 2025-02 (ApRUZj_bDTs) and 2026 (O217xQsEUgI, 7zlblhLGraA). The dated Core Content lessons (crPpMwgwa7k, okN5p701T7Y, vb_Yc-gCBfU) are dated by upload, which may be later than recording.
9. Pre-2022 dossiers have no pyramiding rules. The only hits are a single 'Add-on' trade label (20171219-9CCrlTIrkxw) and a chart note (20201207-PBzd2u4AgbE)."
pyramiding.markets: NQ and MNQ futures are the main market, about two thirds of the trades, on 5s, 15s, 30s and 1m charts. ES is next (1m and 15s, for example 2022-05 and 2024-05/08). EURUSD and GBPUSD appear in the Charter position-trade walkthroughs (Model 4 short adds at 1.1410 and 1.1340 on 4h and daily charts; Models 6 and 7). Core Content Month 05 describes daily-chart position pyramiding on FX and commodities.

rules.rule: Pyramid only a position that is already winning, using fair value gaps that form after the first entry. The stack's stops are trailed so initial capital at risk shrinks while the gains compound.
rules.quote: Pyramiding into fair value gaps allows the operator to compound gains while reducing initial capital at risk as stops are systematically trailed.

rules.rule: Adds should serve a higher-timeframe draw on liquidity. Do not take one-minute entries without knowing the higher-timeframe pool price is reaching for. The 2024 'no bias' scalps are a looser variant (see variants).
rules.quote: Do not look for entries on a one-minute chart without knowing exactly what higher timeframe pool price is reaching for.

rules.rule: Prerequisite: an initial position already exists, taken from an FVG retracement after a market structure shift. A second position is allowed when a new structure shift forms and price retraces into the newly formed FVG.
rules.quote: after an initial long position is established from an FVG retracement, a second position may be placed when price forms another bullish market structure shift and retraces into the newly formed Fair Value Gap

rules.rule: Location gate from the Charter position-trade lessons: shorts may only be pyramided at or above the dealing-range midpoint (premium). Longs are the mirror image, in discount.
rules.quote: at the midpoint or higher when price is in a premium and you can only pyramid in a premium

rules.rule: The reason the run continues: resting stops beyond obvious swing points are the draw, so the stack is built while price is being delivered toward them.
rules.quote: Institutional algorithms seek out resting retail sell stops clustered below conspicuous swing lows and double bottoms during pre-market liquidity purges.

rules.rule: Add only on the return into a newly created premium FVG (for shorts) after confirmed displacement. Existing stops are trailed to protect capital at the same time.
rules.quote: Pyramiding short contracts only on return to premium Fair Value Gaps after confirmed downward displacement; stops on existing positions trailed to protect capital.

rules.rule: A bearish FVG that price has already traded back through (a reclaimed FVG), where price is accelerating toward a structural low, is a valid add point.
rules.quote: I'll add more there because that's just too good to pass up: reclaim bearish fair value gap for those who are wondering, should be breaking this low accelerating pretty hard

rules.rule: Each run of consecutive up-close candles (for shorts) that gets broken lower is a new bearish order block. Smart money is adding at that candle's open, so the pyramid adds there each time.
rules.quote: consecutive of closed candles is your bearish order block and changes the delivery at that candle's open. accumulates more shorts by smart money breaks lower again

rules.rule: Entry for the add is a limit or touch at a tiny volume imbalance or micro FVG that price pulls back into during displacement. Example: 7 contracts short, then 3 more.
rules.quote: that little small little Gap right there with the volume of balance as price went up into it there that's where I added again so I went short seven contracts added three more contracts

rules.rule: Entry for the add is inside the fair value gap, at the mean threshold of a reclaimed order block. When that gap is an inversion FVG he treats it as dynamic support.
rules.quote: That entire range is the order block, and I'm adding into it here inside the fair value gap that is already identified as an inversion fair value gap.

rules.rule: Add on the order block when there is no follow-through against the position. Example: 4 contracts long, then 2 more on the bullish OB for six.
rules.quote: that lack of follow-through kind of like bolsters i'm gonna do two more here trading on to the order block

rules.rule: Core risk rule: do not add until the existing stack's risk has been neutralized by trailing the stop.
rules.quote: When pyramiding, never add size until the previous position's risk has been neutralized by trailing the stop.

rules.rule: The annotation he writes on the chart when he adds 6 to 12 contracts and immediately lifts the stop to the add price (19,708.25). The stop is raised to cover commissions and risk across all contracts.
rules.quote: Costs & Risk Covered

rules.rule: After the add, tuck the stop just under the new low or structure. If price trades back into it, the setup is wrong and he accepts the stop.
rules.quote: now i have six contracts long and i'll move my stop up just a little bit underneath that low right there it should not trade back down into that if it does i'm wrong and that's fine

rules.rule: After adding into a new FVG, raise the stop to just below that gap's midpoint. This is the 2026 version of the trail-to-cover-risk step.
rules.quote: gap again, I'll add two more contracts. Okay, we're using the stop up now just below the midpoint of this.

rules.rule: Trail behind rejection blocks and closed candles, not tight to price. He accepts being stopped out of the runners.
rules.quote: Take this stop and roll it down to the rejection block right there on this closed candle

rules.rule: The whole stack exits at a significant liquidity pool, for example buy-side above morning highs or sell-side below lows.
rules.quote: full position profit targets for intraday index futures trades should be anchored to significant buy-side liquidity pools resting above morning swing highs

rules.rule: When the final higher-timeframe objective is tagged, close all remaining tranches. Do not hold for extra.
rules.quote: when that final objective is tagged, take the entirety of the position off; don't get greedy looking for extra crumbs

rules.rule: Partials are placed at liquidity pools on a time-based chart, not from DOM or level-2 data.
rules.quote: Everything that I've outlined here is shown to you on a time-based chart. My partials are based on liquidity.

rules.rule: Risk budget: for position trades, total risk across all tranches must stay at or below 1%. The first entry therefore risks less than 1%.
rules.quote: you don't want to exceed 1% that means if you have intentions of potentially adding to the position then you have to use less than 1% on your first entry

rules.rule: Size shape in 2022: biggest position first, then smaller adds (for example 5, 3, 2). A growing ladder (1, 2, 4, 8) is called reckless.
rules.quote: buying one then buying two then buying four then buying eight that is reckless and i've done that and i've roasted accounts doing it so don't do that

rules.rule: Adds are never larger than the initial entry (2022 teaching).
rules.quote: never adding more contracts on later entries than on the initial entry

rules.rule: Take part of the stack off on the first structural low break, to recover costs and make the trade risk-free. Leave the rest open for the breakaway.
rules.quote: I'm going to take off five there because we broke a low and costs are recovered; I want to see this one stay open because that'll be breakaway

rules.rule: Once partials are banked, the remaining runners are free. If they are stopped out, that is fine.
rules.quote: You're in a position now where if it goes to your target it's wonderful, and if it doesn't you've already locked in your gains

rules.rule: In 2026, the first partial is taken into the nearest pool because it pays the trader whatever happens next.
rules.quote: It's running right up into first partial. And at that point, you know, it doesn't make a difference if it comes all the way back down to stop me out

rules.rule: No more adds once price is back past the dealing-range midpoint. For shorts that means below it; for longs, above it. An add in the wrong half is vetoed.
rules.quote: you can add to your position as long as you are above equilibrium; once price drops below the midpoint of the range you cannot pyramid anymore

rules.rule: Mirror for longs: only add to longs at or below equilibrium. Down-close candles in premium are not valid bullish order blocks.
rules.quote: you only want to be adding to long positions when price is at or below equilibrium.

rules.rule: Do not trade inside a consolidation until displacement shows the algorithm's hand. Pyramiding deep in a pre-market consolidation is the advanced exception.
rules.quote: Why I teach folks to not try to trade during consolidations you want to see the market show a displacement

rules.rule: Do not pyramid when the plan is a fixed-size income model (one contract per trade, no scaling).
rules.quote: We're not pyramiding, we're not trying to increase as we make more money. All this is is an income approach.

rules.rule: Late-era caution against compulsive expansion, in favour of a few surgical trades.
rules.quote: You're not trying to expand and pyramid and go crazy, just going in there and taking out surgical strikes that make sense, winning and moving to the sidelines and being content.

rules.rule: Intraday execution is on the 5-second to 1-minute chart. He says algorithmic delivery is as precise at 5s as on higher timeframes.
rules.quote: I'm looking at this little area right there on a 5-second chart that's supposed to be just noise; that's funny

rules.rule: Executions, risk controls and adds are watched on the 15-second chart (2025).
rules.quote: As I mentioned, every time I talk about executions, I'm looking at a 15-second chart, folks.

rules.rule: Position-trade version on the daily chart: take partials at intermediate PD arrays, then re-enter or pyramid on the next daily retracement.
rules.quote: Scaling out: when price achieves intermediate-term PD arrays, you take partials and look to re-enter or pyramid on subsequent daily retracements.

rules.rule: Daily-chart stop-order version: after a big run, bank partials and re-enter at the opening price of subsequent down candles.
rules.quote: if price moves away and gives hundreds of pips, you take partial profits and look to re-enter at the opening price on subsequent down candles.

rules.rule: The only spoken time reference is accumulating and pyramiding in a deep pre-market consolidation ahead of the 9:30 open. This describes where he does it, not a gate on the rule.
rules.quote: Get an opportunity to Pyramid anything else in so that's what you run the risk of the deeper you can trade inside of that consolidation ahead of 9:30

rules.rule: A silent 2024 example adds 6 contracts inside the 1:50pm-2:10pm PM macro window (12 to 18 contracts). The window is chart-annotated, not a stated requirement.
rules.quote: 1:50pm - 2:10pm Macro

stops_trailing.summary: Put the hard stop behind the PD arrays that justify the trade (below the order-block mean threshold or candle low, a tick or two past the FVG candle), never widen it, then only ratchet it toward profit: a 25-50-75 percent-of-target ladder in the 2022 and Jan 2024 teaching, cover-cost/break-even after the first partial, and from 2025-26 candle-by-candle structural trails behind new swing lows, FVG/wick consequent encroachment and inversion FVGs.
stops_trailing.needs_clock: No for the core logic. The mean-threshold or candle-extreme stop, the percent-of-target ladder, the 1R de-risk, never widening or retracting, the closing-basis structural trails and the near-target lock all depend only on entry, stop, target and bar prices, so they can run on 24/7 synthetic indices using price delivery alone. Clock-bound extras can be dropped or replaced by bar-count or volatility gates: the 9:31-10:00 first-presented-FVG CE anchor (Sbu7tn8r03w 15:30), no tightening within about 1 minute of the 9:30 bell and cover-cost a few minutes before it (Jxl5UJk_ylc), raising the stop before the 10:00 Fed speech (iSWZOe3aUFE), the lunch-hour stop-run worry (2XhDi5GoNUI 07:13), and the Tuesday-Thursday day filters of the Charter FX models (entry filters, not stop rules).
stops_trailing.how_to_code: State: direction d, entry E, initial stop S0, risk R=|E-S0|, expected objective T (first liquidity target), progress p=(price-E)*d/((T-E)*d). Invariant: stop never moves away from price, so for longs S=max(S_old,S_new), for shorts S=min(S_old,S_new); reject any request that would widen. 1) Initial stop: anchor behind the framing array. For a bullish OB use the candle low or the mean threshold MT=(open+close)/2, i.e. body midpoint (the dossiers also say 50 percent of the range, so the OB-range-midpoint variant is a valid alternative); for an FVG entry use candle-1 extreme; for IFVG or wick entries use the CE (50 percent) boundary. Add a buffer of 0, 1 tick or 1-2 ticks (era dependent), or 5/15/25/50 pips in the FX Charter models. Cap risk (1 percent equity; 4 ES points in the 2022 model) and skip the trade if no valid array fits under the cap. 2) Thesis stop: wicks may probe MT, but a body close beyond MT, or breach of all three supporting arrays, means exit. 3) Percent ladder (Jan 2024): when p>=0.25 set stop distance to 0.75R, when p>=0.50 to 0.50R, when p>=0.75 set S=E (optionally E plus costs). The 2022 Ep41 version has only the 50 percent trim and 75 percent break-even steps. 4) De-risk alternatives: at +1R or after the first partial at the first liquidity pool, set S=E plus commissions (cover costs); older rule: BE plus 1 pip after 50-80 percent is banked. 5) Structural trail, the 2025-26 version: when a bar closes beyond the prior short-term swing extreme (closing basis) or a displacement leg prints, set S to just beyond the new swing low/high, or the CE or edge of the newest FVG, wick CE or IFVG, only if that level sits behind the arrays still supporting the trade. Do not trail while the market is consolidating (2017). 6) Near-target lock: once the last intermediate swing breaks and price is within about 80-90 percent of T, force S>=E. 7) Optional tiered stops: a stop on a fraction of the contracts works as a defensive partial. Subjective parts: which level counts as the expected objective T; whether 'reduced by 25/50 percent' is of the original or the current risk; closing basis versus wick; swing and intermediate-high definitions; which arrays count as the 'three'; the aggressive-versus-patient trail choice (rules conflict); the volatility override; psychological exits.
stops_trailing.changes_over_time: Chronology (dossier dates are upload dates; the 2022 'Core Content' and 'Mentorship' uploads are probably older material): 2017 teaches break-even or breakeven+1 after the first partial or Target 1 (UuMaC9n8Uy4, Yqio1Ja0lIQ, s9bg8JF7rm8) but also says do not trail during consolidation (9CCrlTIrkxw). 2020 (E9F_aT9f038) has no percent ladder: after a 15+ pip first scale the stop goes to the range midpoint, and after the second scale it sits 2-3 pips above entry. 2022 adds mean-threshold stops (tpPtItWqmlg, tnxvmHq8xEg 2023), 1R mitigation (vWDElb65YHg) and the first 50/75 percent ladder (2XhDi5GoNUI). Jan 2024 Charter Models 2, 4 and 5 give the full 25-50-75 ladder (KQdsa7S1LoQ, H05w52zQGdQ, NB7Bku099tU). I found no percent-ladder statement after Jan 2024. In 2025-26 the dossiers show candle-by-candle structural trails (FVG CE, wick CE, IFVG, swing lows) and cover-costs, and in Aug 2026 the explicit never-retract rule (tByaPnk3fc4 43:39 and 42:43 'cardinal sin', SUcRywSry5U 32:18, HFWqQelvrJw 26:56). Conflicts: (a) break-even timing: ladder says only at 75 percent and 'you're not rushing to get Break Even' (NB7Bku099tU 11:23), but Model 8 in the same month says move to break-even right after the first partial (fHp3JkxFFjU 28:30) and 2025-26 does cover-cost after the first partial or expansion. (b) Patient versus aggressive trailing: do not trail tight immediately (CnTXwAuDi9Y 42:47, 2022-05-11) and do not jam (WGGDbeRpo4w, 2025), versus trail aggressively one week later (OYNpIeu9czw 07:41) and in volatility (muL9EoMpYTM, 28M9ouiKmSY where a trailed stop turned a loss into a scratch), versus 'keep the stop where it is, don't choke the trade' in volatility (jz0RbL1oVK8 08:05). A closing-basis trigger reconciles most of it. (c) Swing trades: rZFisy9AILQ (Dec 2023, leave the stop unchanged after three partials) and VLis0LcbUaQ (Apr 2023, avoid the premature-breakeven trap) teach not trailing, but their dossier rows are IMPLIED or summaries with no verbatim quote, so no part cites them. (d) Initial-stop buffer: exactly at the candle extreme with no padding (kNlySn81dmo) versus 1-2 ticks (CnTXwAuDi9Y, PP1-i0ti_tQ), 1 tick (F8s_vfK9HaM 10:15), or fixed pips (5/15/25/50). (e) The 2XhDi5GoNUI 46:17 wording 'trimmed down to 25 percent' at 50 percent is ambiguous against the Charter 'reduced by 50 percent'. (f) 'Never widen' is explicit only as 'do not force higher risk' (SO3SJFNRim8, 2022) and the 2026 never-retract rule; the 'gamblers widen stops' point in vWDElb65YHg is dossier paraphrase, not a verbatim quote. Some dossier quote cells look cleaned or paraphrased (semicolons, bracketed words), so treat precise wording cautiously.
stops_trailing.markets: Management overlay, not a standalone entry model, so the count is trade-table rows whose stop/result cell mentions a trailed, rolled, break-even or cover-cost stop: 121 rows across roughly 115 videos (keyword count, approximate). By market: NQ/MNQ about 90 rows (almost all 2024-2026, 1-minute), ES/MES about 10 (2022-2023), EURUSD about 5, plus GBPUSD, AUDUSD and USDCAD in 2017-2020 and the Jan 2024 Charter FX models (15m/hourly). Only four trades are shown with the full percent ladder: Model 2 EURUSD short (KQdsa7S1LoQ, +160 pips), the ESU22 PM long on 5m (2XhDi5GoNUI, stop trimmed at 50 percent and break-even at 75 percent), a Model 5 Cable short schematic (NB7Bku099tU) and a Model 4 EURUSD position short (H05w52zQGdQ, +240 pips). Daily-chart FX and commodity position trades use swing-low trails (okN5p701T7Y, VL4YLTRerHY).

rules.rule: Every order carries a real stop in the market at the moment of entry; mental stops are banned. All trailing rules below presuppose that stop exists.
rules.quote: You have to have proper risk management. Don't overlever and stop losses have to be used. You cannot use a mental stop.

rules.rule: The stop is anchored behind the PD arrays that justify the trade (order block, FVG, wick CE, IFVG). If three of them are breached the premise is dead.
rules.quote: My stops will always be behind three PD arrays. Because if three PD arrays fail, the next thing is my ass

rules.rule: Refine the entry array (step down timeframes) until a structurally valid stop fits inside the fixed risk cap (4 ES points in the 2022 model). If none fits, skip the trade; never widen the stop to fit.
rules.quote: If no fair value gap allows for a four-point stop loss, we do nothing. We do not force higher risk just to take a trade.

rules.rule: Order-block entry: initial stop goes below the mean threshold (50 percent of the OB candle) or below the candle low.
rules.quote: the stop loss must be placed below the mean threshold

rules.rule: A stop sitting beyond the order-block mean threshold is already calibrated; tolerate wicks into the 50 percent level and do not tighten or pull the stop because of a wick.
rules.quote: stops have already been calibrated, do not panic on wicks.

rules.rule: 2022 FVG model: stop 1 to 2 ticks beyond the extreme of the candle that formed the FVG edge (mirror for longs).
rules.quote: for an aggressive short stop loss, place the stop 1 to 2 ticks above the high of the candle that formed the top of the Fair Value Gap

rules.rule: Charter Model 13 (2022 YouTube model, taught Feb 2024): stop sits exactly at the FVG candle extreme with no padding. Conflicts with the 1-2 tick buffer taught elsewhere.
rules.quote: that's the stop loss okay not one tick above it not a full handle above it

rules.rule: 2026 NQ: stop at the candle (or wick) extreme plus one or two ticks.
rules.quote: candlestick's high plus a tick or two. That's a really good place to put a stop loss.

rules.rule: Inversion FVG entry (2026): the initial stop starts at the IFVG consequent-encroachment boundary.
rules.quote: it's basically consequent encroachment is the top of that inversion fair value gap. So the stop loss has to start and open up on a trade just right at that

rules.rule: Charter Model 5 (FX day trade): stop = swing extreme plus a fixed 15-pip buffer; re-entry allowed if stopped on a valid setup.
rules.quote: we will place our stop loss Above This High plus 15 Pips we will re-enter if stopped out on a solid entry

rules.rule: Charter Model 2 (weekly FX): fixed 25-pip stop, 50 pips for the alternative (delayed) entry.
rules.quote: you're going to use a 25 pip stop loss it'll be a 50 pip stop loss if you use the alternative entry

rules.rule: Charter Model 1 (FX): stop 5 pips beyond the swing extreme.
rules.quote: stop loss below this low minus five Pips or five Pips below slowest low in the swing

rules.rule: In high volatility the structural initial stop may be wider than a student expects; do not force ultra-tight stops.
rules.quote: It's a little wider than you're probably used to because you want really really small stop losses and they're kind of hard to pull off right now with the level of volatility

rules.rule: Risk counts as mitigated once price has moved about one standard deviation (about 1R) from entry; only after that is the stop locked in or trailed.
rules.quote: Once price moves one standard deviation from what our risk is, that initial risk is already mitigated.

rules.rule: Structural trail trigger: advance the stop only after a candle closes beyond the prior short-term high (closing basis), then park it just beyond the new low.
rules.quote: if it can take out this high here on a closing basis, then I'll roll the stop up to just below here. I like to see it really make a strong showing above this minor short-term high

rules.rule: Trail only after displacement through the reference low and a candle close; the new stop goes behind that candle's extreme.
rules.quote: Once it displaces below that low here and it closes, you can move the stop down behind this candlestick's high. I'm teaching stop management.

rules.rule: Do not move the stop until price has traded back through the quadrant level and made the new low; then move it just beyond the swing high. Never before.
rules.quote: once this trades below this quadrant level again in that low, I'll move the stop loss to just above this swing high, but not before

rules.rule: 2017 swing teaching: during a consolidation leave the stop alone; only start trailing once price leaves the consolidation.
rules.quote: now we have a consolidation when price leaves the consolidation then and only then do we consider looking to lower our protective stop-loss

rules.rule: The percentage ladder is measured as the fraction of the entry-to-expected-target range travelled; at 75 percent the stop goes to break-even.
rules.quote: now when price moves to 75 percent of the expected targeted range and it means from your entry to here if it moves 75 of that then the stop goes to break even

rules.rule: Name of the universal ladder (Charter Model 2, Jan 2024): 25-50-75 trailing stop-loss protocol.
rules.quote: my stop loss protocol management the trailing stop-loss is 25 50 75

rules.rule: Step 1: at 25 percent of the expected profit objective, cut the stop distance by 25 percent.
rules.quote: when we are in profit 25% of our expected objective stop-loss can be reduced by 25%

rules.rule: Step 2: at 50 percent of the expected profit objective, cut the stop distance by 50 percent.
rules.quote: when we are in profit 50% of our expected objective stop-loss can be reduced by 50%

rules.rule: Step 3: break-even only once 75 percent of the expected profit objective is reached.
rules.quote: when position is at 75% of the expected profit objective stop must be at break even at that point

rules.rule: 2022 Mentorship Ep41 version of the ladder: at 50 percent of the target range the stop is trimmed (dossier row reads 'trimmed down to 25 percent', ambiguous), not jammed to break-even.
rules.quote: your stop loss can be reduced or trimmed down to 25 percent

rules.rule: Once the 1R mitigation point is reached, lock in the stop or trail it to break-even.
rules.quote: Now at this point, you lock in your stop loss or trail it to breakeven.

rules.rule: 2017 version: take the first partial, then stop to break-even (no percent ladder).
rules.quote: if it allows you to make a hundred pips when you take your first partial off and put your stop at breakeven you're in a beautiful position

rules.rule: 2017 swing trading: do not trail, take partials, leave the stop in the original place.
rules.quote: leave your stop down here okay do not trail your stop-loss you want to be taking partials okay

rules.rule: 2020 OTE series: after a first scale-out of 15+ pips, reduce the stop to about the midpoint of the identified range.
rules.quote: if you can get first scaling where it's 15 pips or more you want to start reducing your risk on your stop to about midpoint of the range that you identified here

rules.rule: Do not tighten the stop immediately after price moves into profit; give the trade room.
rules.quote: do not trail the stop loss tight immediately upon price moving into profit

rules.rule: Opposite emphasis one week later: after displacement in favour of the position, trail aggressively behind lower intermediate highs.
rules.quote: as soon as price breaks lower and displaces in favor of the position, trail the stop-loss down aggressively above lower intermediate highs

rules.rule: After the partial fills, roll the stop to cover costs (break-even plus commissions).
rules.quote: once it takes this low out and it partials me out with profit then my stop will roll down to cover costs

rules.rule: FVG trail: after a partial, lower the stop to just beyond the high of the newly formed FVG; a return to it kills the delivery.
rules.quote: And there's a partial again. and I lowered the stop right above the high of that fair value gap because if it's now going to trade back to it, it's going to go higher.

rules.rule: Trail behind an inversion FVG once candle bodies have spent time inside it.
rules.quote: Bring the stop up again. Now the stop here is below the inversion fair value, guy, because we've spent a lot of time with the bodies in there

rules.rule: Raise the stop only to a level that sits behind verified PD arrays (wick CE, session gap low, imbalance low) so a retrace has to break all of them first.
rules.quote: So I can actually bring my stop up and lock in a little bit more juice out of this lemon because if it's going to retrace, it shouldn't find its way below this wick's consequent encouragement.

rules.rule: Stop sits just below the swing-low wick; when that low is cleared, roll the stop to just below the next low.
rules.quote: defense is this swing low, which is why I have my stop loss just below this wick. Okay? Once it does that, then I'm going to roll the stop just below that low right there.

rules.rule: Tiered stops: attach a stop to part of the position so it acts as a defensive partial on a retracement while the rest keeps its own stop or target.
rules.quote: I had seven contracts net long. I put two contracts on a stop right here. So, if it goes below there, it's going to sell two of the seven I had as a partial

rules.rule: Elevated macro volatility: bring the stop up aggressively once price clears the opening-range gap high.
rules.quote: delivers above the opening range Gap high and then I bring the stop loss up here because if it stops me out that's fine

rules.rule: Near the final target, after the last intermediate swing high breaks, move the stop into profit so a winner cannot turn into a loss.
rules.quote: move my stop loss and remove the risk because it's too close to my Target and I don't want to see a trade get close to my Target and then come back and put me into a losing trade

rules.rule: Do not jam the stop to break-even early; let price displace away from the entry array first.
rules.quote: I'm not in a rush to jam my stop

rules.rule: Never retract a trailed stop once committed (2026); a stop only moves toward profit.
rules.quote: As soon as you commit to a stop loss that's adjusted that way, stick with that.

rules.rule: Never pull the stop back after locking in profit.
rules.quote: never never never want to pull the stop back. I've secured a payday

rules.rule: Position trading: scale out at weekly objectives and trail the runner behind daily swing lows.
rules.quote: Scale out 30% at the first weekly objective, 30% at the second, and hold the remaining 40% with a trailing stop behind daily swing lows until the macro target is reached.

rules.rule: If the mean threshold of the framing candle breaks, the trade is probably wrong, which is why a very tight stop is acceptable: it gives immediate feedback.
rules.quote: chances are it's probably not a good trade. So that means you can have a really ultra tight stop loss on your long entry or you can have immediate feedback that you're on the wrong side.

rules.rule: A candle body closing beyond the reference level invalidates the position; the stop is rolled to just beyond the candle extreme once the short-term high is taken.
rules.quote: I don't want to see a close or a body laid down below this level here

rules.rule: When the stop behind the three PD arrays is hit, accept it as the operator's error and exit; do not argue, widen or re-hope.
rules.quote: It doesn't mean my system or methodology is flawed, it means I made the error. There's nothing to argue about, it's time to get out.

rules.rule: Position trades on the daily chart: trail behind intermediate daily swing lows (Month 05).
rules.quote: Trailing stops: as price continues to expand, you lock in profit by trailing stops behind intermediate swing lows on the daily chart.

rules.rule: Charter Model 12 FX scalping: about 20-pip stop for students, 15 pips at his lowest.
rules.quote: personally my lowest is about 15 Pips but as a mentor I'm trying to keep you around that 20 pip threshold for stop

rules.rule: NQ morning trail anchor (2025): raise the stop to the consequent encroachment of the first presented FVG formed 9:31-10:00 New York time.
rules.quote: raise the stop up so now I have the stop at the middle or consequent encroachment of the first presentive fair value Gap that occurs between 9:31 and 10:00 always eastern time.

rules.rule: Pre-market: a few minutes before the 9:30 bell, move the stop above entry as loss covering.
rules.quote: We have 4 and 1/2 more minutes before the opening bell, so I'm going to take the stop above entry. Just as a loss covering.

rules.rule: Do not tighten the stop within about a minute of the 9:30 open (bell volatility).
