rules.quote: because it's 1 minute away from the opening bell, I don't want to roll the stop up below that low here.

rules.rule: After 15-20 minutes into the opening range the stop may be rolled up normally.
rules.quote: But, if we had been trading for like 15 minutes or 20 minutes in the opening range, then I would have rolled the stop up below here

rules.rule: Ahead of scheduled news (10:00 Fed chair speech), raise the stop and accept being stopped; do not hold wide risk into the release.
rules.quote: dropping cuz I know the Fed chair speech is getting ready to be posted at 10:00

risk_money.summary: Fixed-fractional risk: size every trade at a small percent of current equity (1% typical, 2% hard ceiling), only take setups framed at 3:1 or better, cut risk 50% after a full loss (ladder 2>1>0.5 or 1>0.5>0.25) and step back up only after recovering 50% of the loss, take partials and move the stop to breakeven, aim for a small weekly pip objective (about 20-25 pips = about 6%/month) and re-enter at half size after a stop-out.
risk_money.needs_clock: No. Everything is computed from equity, stop distance, R multiples, win and loss sequence and equity recovery, so it can run on 24/7 synthetic indices using only price delivery. The one time-based element is the weekly pip objective. 2017 phrases it as 'don't trade again this week' with a Tuesday/Wednesday remark; on synthetics substitute a rolling N-trade, N-bar or fixed-length window. Clock rules such as 7-10am for FX and 8:30-11am for index futures belong to the entry models (for example Charter Model 13), not to this one.
risk_money.how_to_code:
Settings: base_risk (default 1.0%, hard cap 2.0%), ladder, recovery_fraction 0.5, min_rr 3, weekly_goal_R.
State: equity, tier, dd_ref, wins_in_row, window_R.

1. Setup gate. Reject any signal whose planned reward / planned risk is below min_rr (3, prefer 5).
2. Size. risk$ = equity x current_risk_pct. units = floor_to_lot(risk$ / (stop_distance x value_per_point)). Always round down. The stop is mandatory. If several tranches are open, the sum of their risk must not exceed the cap.
3. Management. Take a partial at the first target and move the stop to breakeven. Variants: +1R, or 50% off at 3R when risking 2%, or the 25-50-75 stop trail with breakeven only at 75% of the objective.
4. On a full -1R stop-out. Set tier = min(tier+1, floor), so risk_pct is halved. Record dd_ref = (equity before the loss, equity after it).
   - Ladder: 2 > 1 > 0.5 (2017) or 1 > 0.5 > 0.25 (2022). The Charter wording has only one halving.
   - If tier is at the floor, stay there.
5. On a win. wins_in_row += 1. Step the tier back up one level only when equity has recovered at least 50% of the dip recorded in dd_ref.
   - Optional 2024 rule: wins_in_row == 5 halves risk.
   - Optional 2017 flatline variant: after a loss go to base units and ramp only on wins, capped at 5.
6. Re-entry. If stopped out and the same setup or narrative re-qualifies (fresh MSS/FVG or equivalent), size = 0.5 x original size.
7. Weekly or window cap. Track window_R. When it reaches the goal (about 20-25 pips, about 1-1.5R, about 1.5% per week for 6% a month), stop trading until the window resets.

Subjective or undefined in his teaching:
- The base percent (0.25% to 2%).
- What counts as 'recovered by 50%' (equity dip versus the R-multiple of the loss).
- What 'a turn in equity' means.
- Whether partial-win trades count as wins.
- What counts as the 'same setup' for a half-size re-entry.
- Whether the five-win rule cuts or caps the ramp.
- Whether the weekly goal is in pips or in R.
- Stop distances are never fixed (10-20 pips in FX, structural otherwise).
risk_money.changes_over_time:
Base risk and ceiling:
- Dec 2017 (RtMRykCZtC4 03:04): 2% is the maximum, his own appetite is 0.5-1%, and he admits past risks of 3.5-7%.
- Nov 2017 (UuMaC9n8Uy4 14:03): start at 1% and only creep toward 2%, never above 2% without years of profitability.
- Feb-Apr 2022 (G8-z91acgG4, IEa1N0rTtbc, Q6GFu8-Z4rY): below 1%, 'half a percent aim for one percent', 1% as the maximum with 0.5% or 0.25% preferred.
- Jun 2022 (2XhDi5GoNUI): standard is 1%.
- Aug-Sep 2022 Core Content: 1.5% (Month 2 small accounts, Month 6 swing), 1-2% (No Fear Of Losing), 2% (10% Per Month), at most 1% for position trades (Month 5).
- Jan 2023 funded (tnxvmHq8xEg): 1-1.2%.
- Jan-Feb 2024 Charter: 0.75% (oVSGM3BK97s), 1% (Models 4, 10, 11, 12), a $20k/1.5% example (Models 7 and 8, per the dossier overview), 2% or less (Model 13), and 2% split over four 0.5% orders (Model 6).
- Aug 2024 (iLe_4m84_yw 86:10): a line about a quarter of 1%.

Loss response:
- Dec 2017 offers two systems. One is the tier ladder 2>1>0.5 with step-up after recovering 50% of the equity dip (tlKC9nvLRK0). The other is the 'flatline' (RtMRykCZtC4 34:47/37:02): drop to the lowest unit after any loss, then ramp on wins.
- Jun 2022 uses 1>0.5>0.25 (2XhDi5GoNUI).
- The Dec 2023-Feb 2024 Charter wording has a single halving until 50% is recovered (Models 1, 2, 5, 7). The second tier is not restated.
- Several dossiers carry drawdown-percent circuit breakers with no verbatim quote: JOy9KzkLlag (-3%, -6%, -8%, a 2% daily limit), aGdx-YmxawQ (-5% halves risk, two losses a day shuts down) and qXPZB_H6tVo (-6% goes to 0.25%). They are dossier-written 'algorithmic rules', not his words, so do not rely on them.

Five wins:
- 2017 uses five wins as a cap on the ramp-up ('we stopped at five winning trades').
- Feb 2024 Models 7 and 8 (G4lhid5dh0I 10:17, F-8hPvSyIB4 09:11) cut risk 50% after five wins in a row. It is absent from Models 1, 2 and 5.

Reward-to-risk:
- 3:1 minimum with 5:1 or 10:1 preferred runs through 2017, Aug-Sep 2022 and the 2022 swing videos.
- E9F_aT9f038 41:46 (May 2020) says 'forget risk to reward... don't think it has to be three to one it has to be five to one if it's one to one it's still good'. That is accuracy first, and a different stance.
- Charter Model 12 scalping banks 80% at about 20 pips against a roughly 15-20 pip stop (3xgtrXok-xs, xi0N9BG1Qvs), so that is not 3:1.

Weekly objective and monthly goal:
- Nov 2017: 23-25 pips a week at 2% for 6% a month (UuMaC9n8Uy4, 1Wmh8829mZs), but also 50-75 pips a week (1Wmh8829mZs 09:50, and Charter Model 10).
- Aug 2022: 20 pips at 1.5%.
- Feb 2024: 25 pips (Model 8).
- The monthly goal moves between 6%, 6-10% and 10%+ (via a 2% risk, half off at +3R).

Stop management:
- Early breakeven at +1R (vWDElb65YHg, mjVHmE1gVMg) versus 'you're not rushing to get Break Even', the 25-50-75 trail with breakeven only at 75% (2XhDi5GoNUI 46:59, NB7Bku099tU 11:53, KQdsa7S1LoQ).

Re-entry:
- Half size after a stop-out appears only in Dec 2023 (H1-Ni_J-tOw 17:23, _ZOFkSXfvsg, which is visual-only and tagged IMPLIED).
- Model 5 says 're-enter if stopped out on a solid entry' with no size given (NB7Bku099tU 09:32).

Source reliability:
- The Aug-Sep 2022 Core Content dossiers (mjVHmE1gVMg, pFdW8wdR9sQ, vWDElb65YHg, pctqB3UD6dk, crPpMwgwa7k) hold polished quotation blocks with time ranges that read as paraphrase-adjacent. Treat their exact numbers (1.5%, 20 pips) with less confidence than the 2017 and 2022 Episode 41 transcript cells.
- The Model 8 dossier's own example (15-pip stop, 1%, +60 pips described as '+6%') does not reconcile: 4R at 1% is about 4%.
- crPpMwgwa7k has no drawdown percentages, only drawdown-control and 3:1+ statements.
risk_money.markets: Market-agnostic. He says it applies to all leveraged markets, and the 2017 ledgers use FX majors in pips on $5,000 and $10,000 accounts. The trade-table rows tied to it total 10 across 6 videos, 4 of them simulated ledgers: tlKC9nvLRK0 (2), RtMRykCZtC4 (2). I counted the 6 chart trades. They are NQ futures in _ZOFkSXfvsg (-15 handles, then a 50%-size re-entry for +63), NQ in QjjnCS_qTXo (two morning losses of about $2,000, then a recovery), GBPUSD in fHp3JkxFFjU (20-pip stop, +25 pips) and GBPUSD in F-8hPvSyIB4 (15-pip stop, +60 pips). pFdW8wdR9sQ adds four simulated 10-trade P&L scenarios. Other markets named: ES (2022 Episode 41, funded-account videos), EURUSD swing and position trades, and AUDUSD/USDCHF in the Charter scalping models. Index futures are converted from pips (Model 8 says 5-15 handles a week).

rules.rule: Applies to every trade on every account. A long losing streak is treated as certain, not unlikely (he uses 8 in a row; 10% risk after 8 losses is his ruin example), so size so that a streak cannot break the account.
rules.quote: eight string loss that is absolutely realistic guys I don't care how good a trader you are you're going to get this upside your head one day and you need to be prepared for it

rules.rule: Drawdown control matters more than hit rate. A low-accuracy system can still be profitable, and accounts die from losses compounding.
rules.quote: it's the losses that erode by the means of drawdown every losing trader every busted account starts with a single loss and it compounds

rules.rule: The edge is the payoff ratio. At 3:1 reward-to-risk, 3 wins and 7 losses (30% accuracy) at 1% risk still nets about +2% on 10 trades; at 5:1 it nets about +8%.
rules.quote: Losing is inevitable. If you have an accuracy rate of 30 percent, that means you're losing 70 percent of the time. But with a reward-to-risk ratio of three to one, for every one dollar that we risk, we make three

rules.rule: Setup filter: only take setups whose framed objective is at least 3 times the stop distance (5x preferred). Otherwise pass.
rules.quote: Limiting setups to 3 to 1 reward to risk permits as low as 34% accuracy to be net profitable

rules.rule: Risk budget = current account equity x risk percent. One percent is the maximum he names here, preferably half or a quarter of one percent.
rules.quote: percentage risk on equity so that means you're simply going to look at how much money you have in the account take that times that by one percent okay one percent is the maximum preferably you should be doing a half a one percent or maybe a quarter of one percent

rules.rule: Never size by a fixed dollar amount per trade. Always use fixed percentage risk on equity.
rules.quote: if you're risking you know a thousand dollars per trade okay you're thinking about money-wise don't do that you think about it in terms of fixed percentage risk on equity

rules.rule: Position size formula: (equity x risk%) / (stop distance in pips x value per pip).
rules.quote: position size equals account Equity times risk percent divided by stop loss in Pips

rules.rule: Worked example: $10,000 x 1% = $100; a 20-pip stop costs $2.00 per micro lot, so 50 micro lots. Round the lot size down so loss never exceeds the risk ceiling.
rules.quote: $100 divided by $2.00 = 50 micro lots per trade or 1% of the Account Equity. Always round down.

rules.rule: A hard stop must be placed on every trade; it is what defines the 1R used in the sizing formula.
rules.quote: if you don't put a hard stop in you're not really respecting the risk

rules.rule: Keep the stop tight (his FX examples use 10-20 pips) and let the reward be large. Small risk is what produces the high R multiples.
rules.quote: we don't need to take huge risks. We let the market offer us big potential on the upside, but we put our stop loss a little bit closer.

rules.rule: With a 2% position, the first objective is 3R. Take half off there (+3% on the account) and the original risk is gone.
rules.quote: If we take our two percent position and we look for a first profit objective of three to one reward to risk

rules.rule: The 3:1 template: 20-pip stop, 60-pip objective.
rules.quote: 20 pips risked and we're aiming for 60 pips

rules.rule: 2017 weekly pip objective: about 23-25 pips a week at 2% risk compounds to 6% a month.
rules.quote: you only need 23 pips a week at two percent risk and you can double your account every single calendar year by compounding six percent return six percent a month is not a lot it's very easy to get to

rules.rule: 2022 weekly pip objective: 20 pips a week at 1.5% risk equals 6% a month.
rules.quote: All it takes is 20 pips per week. With one and a half percent risk on a trade that pays out 20 pips, that's six percent per month.

rules.rule: 2024 Charter Model 8: the plan is 25 pips a week, targeting 6% a month.
rules.quote: the ICT price action model number eight the 6% trading model building the career on 25 Pips per week

rules.rule: 6% a month is presented as a sufficient goal; no need to chase more.
rules.quote: profitable Trader if you can only just make 6% a month don't let anybody tell you that's not enough

rules.rule: At the first profit objective take partials and move the stop to breakeven. Then the trade cannot damage the account.
rules.quote: When you reach your first profit objective at 20 pips, take partials, move your stop to breakeven, and let the rest work. You've protected your capital and locked in guaranteed positive growth.

rules.rule: Weekly objective cap (2017): once the weekly pip objective is made, stop trading for that week.
rules.quote: I know the likelihood is I want to be trading on Tuesdays and Wednesdays if I can get my entire weekly objective which is 50 to 75 pips per week if I can get that done in one day then I won't do any more trading after that regardless of what day of the week it is

rules.rule: When pyramiding or adding, the combined risk of all tranches must stay within the cap (1%), so the first entry must risk less than the cap.
rules.quote: you don't want to exceed 1% that means if you have intentions of potentially adding to the position then you have to use less than 1% on your first entry

rules.rule: The event that changes size is a full-R loss. After it, cut the risk percent by 50% until half of that loss is recovered (Charter Model 1; the same wording appears in Models 2 and 5).
rules.quote: what we do if we go into a drawdown on a trade is you drop the percent of Risk by 50% again until that loss is recovered by 50%

rules.rule: 2017 tier ladder: 2% -> 1% after a loss -> 0.5% after another loss.
rules.quote: if you take a loss of 2% the next trade you will only assume 1% risk now should this trade result in a loss the next trade will only assume 1/2 of 1%

rules.rule: The floor is 0.5%. Stay there until equity turns up.
rules.quote: the moral of the story is if you have a loss cut your risk if you have a loss again you cut your risk and you drop down to 1/2 of 1% and you stay there until we have a turn in equity

rules.rule: Step-up rule (2022): to go back up one tier, first recover 50% of the loss.
rules.quote: to step back up to one percent you must recover 50 percent of what you lost
if that half a percent trade loses, drop down to a quarter of a percent (0.25%)

rules.rule: 2024 Models 7 and 8 add a winning-streak rule: after 5 wins in a row, halve risk.
rules.quote: if you take a series of five winning trades in a row drop your risk percent by 50% and the reason why is you want to protect your capital

rules.rule: 2017 'flatline' variant: after a loss drop to the lowest unit, raise size only after wins, and cap the ramp at five winning trades.
rules.quote: when we start making money then we can start increasing the leverage and we take a loss we keep leverage low again until we take a win and we can start ramping it up again but we stopped at five winning trades

rules.rule: Re-entry after a stop-out is taken at half the original position size (Dec 2023). _ZOFkSXfvsg shows it on NQ but is tagged IMPLIED with no spoken quote.
rules.quote: if I get stopped out I'm going to go right back in with half the position

rules.rule: Never raise size or risk after a loss to win it back. The first response to a loss is to cut risk.
rules.quote: when we experience a loss the first thing you want to do is number one reduce risk that's the absolute first thing you think in your mind not let me get that kinda try to get my money back no you cut risk

rules.rule: Hard ceiling of 2% of equity per setup (Charter Model 13 slide, 2024).
rules.quote: The Risk: We use 2% or less Risk per setup of the total equity of the trading account.

rules.rule: 2% is the standard maximum. He admits he has gone much higher himself (3.5% to 7%, 'cowboy') and does not endorse it.
rules.quote: standard 2% as a maximum and truth be told there's been times when I was I've risked as much as three and a half percent and sometimes when I was really being a cowboy I was risking as much as five and seven percent

rules.rule: Position-trade ceiling is 1% (big in time held, not in allocation).
rules.quote: How much money should you be risking? No more than 1%

rules.rule: Pass on any swing setup framed below 3:1 reward-to-risk.
rules.quote: Use nothing less than 3 to 1 reward to risk ratios

rules.rule: Used on a basket of USD majors. Three to four setups a week appear across pairs, so a small weekly pip objective is reachable without trading every day.
rules.quote: if you look at every major that's paired against the dollar you can get about three to four solid setups per week now that means that you're probably not going to get us up every single trading day chances are one pair among all the ones that are available will provide you a set up

rules.rule: Swing timeframe (weekly and monthly levels, 4h entry): about six trades a year at 1.5% risk, 3:1 payoff and a roughly 50-pip stop is said to more than double equity per year.
rules.quote: Six trades, that's it. Six trades risking 1.5%, using 3 to 1 leverage, and about a 50 pip stop, you're more than doubling your equity every single year.

rules.rule: On futures funded or evaluation accounts (ES), keep per-trade risk at or below 1%.
rules.quote: if you were funded with a $100,000 trading account, trade one run risking no more than one percent.

pm_session.summary: ICT's afternoon framework for index futures: skip the choppy morning and the noon-1 PM lunch hour, then take the one clean post-lunch setup (sweep of the lunch lows or highs, then a Market Structure Shift and FVG entry aimed at the morning or lunch liquidity); on consolidation days fade the 3-4 PM false breakout back to the 50% of the daily range, and use the AM/PM daily-range profile (AM rally into a higher-timeframe premium array then PM decline, and the reverse) to decide continuation versus reversal.
pm_session.needs_clock: Yes, as taught. Every rule is tied to New York time: AM session to about 11:00-12:00, noon to 1 PM lunch (no-trade), PM watch from 1:30 PM (or 1:00 PM in Oct 2022), the 3:00 PM bond close, the 3-4 PM false-breakout window (later the 3:45/3:50-4:00 PM market-on-close macro), and in 2024 the 1:50-2:10 and 2:50-3:10 macros. He gives the reasons as flow-based: lunch liquidity build-up, the bond close, and market-on-close orders. The dossiers contain no statement that it works without the clock. The price-only core can run on 24/7 synthetic indices: a trend or expansion leg, then a consolidation, then a sweep of the consolidation low (or high), then displacement with a Market Structure Shift and FVG, then entry on the retrace with the stop beyond the sweep and the target at the prior extreme or the 50% of the range. The AM/PM profile can be approximated by splitting each synthetic 'day' into a first leg, a middle consolidation and a last leg, and the daily-range-profile logic (did the first-leg extreme tag a higher-timeframe array?) can use higher-timeframe bars. What cannot be reproduced is the clock-specific edge: the lunch dead zone, the bond close, MOC orders and the macros. Expect the synthetic version to be a different, unproven model, and test it separately.
pm_session.how_to_code:
Detection logic (NY-time version):
1. Build the session clock: AM = 09:30-12:00 (record the AM high and low, and which came first), lunch = 12:00-13:00, PM = 13:30-16:00, bond close = 15:00, final window = 15:00-16:00.
2. Context (subjective parts marked): on the daily/4H/60m, find the draw on liquidity (relative equal highs or lows, old high or low, unfilled imbalance; SUBJECTIVE bias). Flag whether the AM high or low traded into a 4H/daily/weekly premium or discount array (FVG or OB, detectable by code); if so the AM extreme is 'defended' and the PM is more likely a reversal or a lunch-extreme run only. Classify the day: trend day, or consolidation day (rule of thumb: prior outside day fell about 1 handle short of an old daily low, or neutral daily order flow, or AM already tagged a key level; mostly SUBJECTIVE).
3. Lunch-low sweep long (bullish bias, AM rally then lunch range): after 13:00 (best from 13:30), detect price trading below the lunch-range low (or the low of the last 3-bar swing low inside the lunch range). Then require displacement: a close above the most recent short-term swing high (MSS) that leaves a three-candle FVG (candle 3 low above candle 1 high). Enter a limit order inside the FVG (or at an existing bullish OB or FVG the sweep ran into; prefer a 15m FVG below the 50% of the dealing range). Stop below the sweep low or the FVG low. Targets: lunch high, AM high, relative equal highs, then the higher-timeframe draw; take partials at each pool. Exit the remainder if price closes through the OB that was meant to hold. Mirror for shorts (lunch-high sweep, bearish breaker or FVG).
4. PM session reversal (2023 form): same as above, but the 'original consolidation' (the prior range containing the lunch) must be cleared. Require a purge of the consolidation extreme, an MSS (smart money reversal), then buy the internal FVG on the retrace, target the opposite side of the consolidation.
5. 3-4 PM false-breakout fade (consolidation day only): from 15:00 to 16:00, detect a sweep of the day's relative equal highs (or lows) outside the daily range; then a 1m swing-low break with an FVG; short the retrace into that FVG; stop above the swept high; target the 50% of the day's range. Skip if price is mid-range and no sweep has occurred.
6. AM rally / PM decline profile: if the AM high (the 09:30-12:00 extreme) is inside a higher-timeframe premium array, a lunch range forms, and after 13:00 price sweeps the lunch high but fails to exceed the AM high, then look for a short on MSS plus FVG, targeting the lunch low, the 50% of the day's range, or the 15:00 low.
7. Filters: no entries 12:00-13:00; one trade per day or per session (his rule changed over time); skip the PM if the morning goal was hit; optional SMT check (ES vs NQ vs YM, noon to 3 PM).
Subjective and hard to code: 'bias' and 'draw on liquidity' selection, whether a displacement is 'energetic', whether a setup is 'clean and obvious', whether a day is a consolidation day, HTF array quality, SMT obviousness ('when it's not obvious, assume it's not there'). For synthetics, replace steps 1 and 2 with 'bars since leg start' and 'consolidation = N-bar range with contracting volatility after an impulse', and drop the bond-close and MOC steps.
pm_session.changes_over_time:
1) Clock definitions drift. 2022 mentorship: noon-1 PM is no-trade and the PM killzone is 1:30-4:00 (Ep 41; Ends series 1:30-3:30). Oct 2022 Month 10 (2017 footage): the PM trend starts about 1:00 PM and the lunch window is 11:00-1:00, though that same dossier's markets table says 11:30-1:00; the bond lecture splits AM to noon and PM noon to 3:00. 2023: PM expansion 1:30-3:00 and the 2:00-3:00 PM Silver Bullet (a separate model), plus 'wait through lunch' (vuBRMFhFZAY). 2024: the PM is chopped into macros at 1:50-2:10, 2:50-3:10, 3:15-3:45 and 3:50-4:00 MOC. 2024-26: the 11:30-1:30 Lunch Macro becomes its own setup. 2026: the 1:30-2:00 PM opening range frames the session.
2) Day end. Month 10 treats the 3:00 PM bond close as the end of the IPDA day and the usual high or low pivot. Earlier 2022 episodes (Eps 32 and 33) and later work still trade 3:00-4:00 PM, calling it an engineered market-on-close liquidity run. The 3-4 PM false breakout is only given for consolidation days (hzoMJQlEv5M), and in the 2026 consolidation-day video (0olLwAiLa3o) he says consolidation 'is going to occur in the afternoon' once a key level is hit.
3) Reversal versus continuation. The Month 10 profile lectures (P5pyzmgZA1s, yWBxZsbmK1U) tie a PM reversal to the AM extreme tagging a higher-timeframe array, and use the 50% of the range as the target on consolidation days. The 2022 episodes treat the lunch sweep as a long in the direction of a bullish bias (even calling Ep 27 'counter-trend PM'). QKvjPltjsqU calls it a 'PM session reversal model' (smart money reversal / market maker buy model clearing the original consolidation). The P5pyz dossier says 'eight' projected-range profiles but lists six. Its 'if and only if the AM high trades into a 4-hour, daily, or weekly premium array' rule is an unquoted summary; the quoted version is softer ('it may just want to run the lunchtime hour highs').
4) Management changes. June 2022: a mechanical ladder (50% of target trims the stop to 25%, 75% moves it to break even, and risk steps down 1% to 0.5% to 0.25% after losses). Later in 2022: partials in premium above the 50% of the retracement. 2023: 'my partials are based on liquidity'; the dossier text says do not trail to break even too early and keep the stop sheltered below the iFVG low (unquoted), and MqOVbd1oqZk trails the stop under new 1m swing lows. 2024: stop to break even once price breaks the NDOG low, then pyramid inside the macro (Fv3gNx9ta0I, shown, not quoted). 2025: re-enter the PM with morning profits at 1-to-1 risk (Q0Xa-Vqy5vo) and contract caps of 30 AM / 20 PM (mQsT-xux5Xk).
5) Trade count. Ep 16: no more than four trades, two AM and two PM. Ep 39: do not trade the PM after hitting the morning goal. Sept 2022 Ends series: one setup per day, AM or PM, not both. 2025: PM re-entries allowed. The title 'One Trading Setup For Life' (2023) refers to the single clean post-lunch setup, not the one-per-day cap.
6) News. June 2022 (Ep 41): do not trade while the Fed Chair speaks. 2023 (vuBRMFhFZAY): if Powell is speaking, wait through lunch and trade the afternoon. Ep 30: the 2:00 PM Fed or news move is often a false first move and is not traded without MSS plus FVG.
7) Entry timeframe and naming. 2022 uses 1m/2m/5m FVG, OB or breaker (Ep 39) and a 15m discount FVG (Ep 38). 2023 uses a 15-second inversion FVG (vuBRMFhFZAY). 2024 uses 15s/1m on NQ. The name moves from 'PM Session Model' (2022) to 'PM Session Reversal Model / MMBM' (2023) to 'PM Session Turtle Soup' and 'PM Silver Bullet' (2024).
8) Source reliability. These are model-written dossiers, not transcripts. Many 2022 'quotes' read like normalized full-sentence rules, and the Month 10 and 2023 lecture tables mix true quotes with paraphrases. I used only text inside quote marks, as is. The iFVG details, the 4,416/4,422 levels in vuBRMFhFZAY, and the 'if and only if' reversal rule appear only in unquoted summary text. Trade counts are table rows and may include summarizer errors.
pm_session.markets: Equity index futures only. About 20 trades sit in the dossier trade tables: 13 on E-mini S&P (ES), 7 on E-mini Nasdaq (NQ). The breakdown is 11 in the 2022 mentorship episodes (Eps 5, 9, 16, 27, 30, 32, 33, 34, 38, 39, 41), 4 in the Oct 2022 Month 10 index lectures (June 2017 footage), 3 in 2023 (QKvjPltjsqU, vuBRMFhFZAY live 15-second ES, MqOVbd1oqZk) and 2 in 2024 (NQ PM Turtle Soup of 30 Aug 2024, shown in HM2M9a4OEFQ, odS7IIktqOY and krdRxohMI3g, and the 3 Sep 2024 NQ short Fv3gNx9ta0I). About 5 more PM review walkthroughs have no trade table (fq62gXyRRWQ, wOzyoZD7b7M, mkAuOOPTEKw, _ra-GlgdMZU, -o4zXIhggFs). I did not count the 2:00-3:00 PM Silver Bullet trades or the 11:30-1:30 Lunch Macro trades, which are separate models. Dow (YM) is used only as an SMT comparison. The 30-year bond (ZB) has its own split-session rules (AM to noon, PM noon to 3 PM) and is not part of this model. Entry timeframes run from 15-second to 5-minute (1m and 2m most common); the 15m chart is the bellwether, and 60m/4H/daily set the bias and the arrays.

rules.rule: Morning is sideways chop (typically a Fed or news day): do not trade it, sit out through lunch and take the single obvious afternoon setup (the 2023 'One Trading Setup For Life' lesson).
rules.quote: The market's going sideways, just churning up accounts, beating up everybody. You have to wait until we get through lunch!

rules.rule: Index futures only: if overnight made a big run, skip the New York morning and wait for the other side of lunch (1:00 PM) for the afternoon setup.
rules.quote: if there a big run overnight avoid the New York session don't even mess with the New York session wait until the other side of lunch at 1:00 in the afternoon

rules.rule: If the morning does not form clean delivery (no clear displacement and MSS), downgrade it and wait for the clearer afternoon session.
rules.quote: when price action in the morning does not cleanly form standard delivery mechanics, treat it as lower probability and wait for the clearer afternoon session

rules.rule: Consolidation-day classification: an outside day that stops about 1 handle short of an old daily low means the next day is expected to be a consolidation day, the precondition for the 3-4 PM false-breakout fade.
rules.quote: when it falls short of taking out an old daily low by about 1 handle, expect the current day to be a consolidation day

rules.rule: Daily bias comes from the daily chart: what price is reaching for (an imbalance or an old high/low), checked over a 20-40 day lookback.
rules.quote: look at the daily chart, see what price is reaching for: an imbalance or an old high/low.

rules.rule: Intraday PM targets come from daily and 60-minute relative equal highs or swing highs, the primary draw on liquidity.
rules.quote: daily and 60-minute relative equal highs or swing highs provide the primary draw on liquidity for intraday session targeting

rules.rule: If the day is expected to expand higher, the PM session first retraces into discount (below the dealing-range 50%) before the run.
rules.quote: in the afternoon session starting at 1:30 PM, the algorithm seeks liquidity; if the day is expected to expand higher, it will seek discount pricing first via a retracement

rules.rule: AM rally / PM decline profile discriminator: if the AM high reached a higher-timeframe premium array it is defended and not re-attacked; the PM may only run the lunch-hour highs and then decline.
rules.quote: If there's a higher time frame premium array that AM session hit, then it's likely that it won't go back up there because they've already defended that level and it may just want to run the lunchtime hour highs

rules.rule: If the AM low bounced off a nested higher-timeframe level that is also a 15m/60m discount array, the intraday low is protected: do not expect the PM to sweep the AM low.
rules.quote: If the AM session bounces into the lunch off of a higher time frame nested level that's also seen on a 15 or a 60 minute discount array, then we don't expect the intraday low to be taken out in the afternoon session

rules.rule: Opposite case: an AM low formed above a higher-timeframe discount array is unprotected and the PM is expected to run it (the PM low sweep that starts a PM reversal up).
rules.quote: but if that AM session low is forming above a higher time frame discount array, then we would anticipate a lower run on the intraday low in the PM session.

rules.rule: Oct 2022 Month 10 definition: the PM trend session begins about 1:00 PM New York and runs to the 4:00 PM close.
rules.quote: It begins around 1:00 PM New York time and extends all the way to 4:00 PM at the close.

rules.rule: June 2022 mentorship working window: the PM index killzone is 1:30 PM to 4:00 PM New York time.
rules.quote: 1:30 PM to 4:00 PM New York Local Time

rules.rule: The afternoon watch starts at 1:30 PM.
rules.quote: at 1:30 that's when we start watching the afternoon PM session

rules.rule: Noon to 1 PM New York is a hard no-trade window; it is where lunch liquidity is built, not traded.
rules.quote: noon to 1:00 in the afternoon New York time that is a no trade time period

rules.rule: At the 3:00 PM bond close the day's high or low (relative to what the AM session made) is usually set, and the algorithm spools price toward the draw.
rules.quote: As soon as the bond market closes at 3:00 PM New York time, that's usually when the market makes its high or low in respective terms to what was seen in the AM session.

rules.rule: On consolidation days the late 3:00-4:00 PM window is where the false breakout outside the daily range is engineered before price returns to the midpoint.
rules.quote: on consolidation days, wait until the 3:00 PM to 4:00 PM window for the algorithm to engineer a false breakout outside the daily range to seek liquidity before returning to the midpoint

rules.rule: 2024 variant: the PM is subdivided into clock macros; the 1:50-2:10 PM macro is where PM expansion or the PM reversal often starts.
rules.quote: 1:50 and 2:10 macro, look at that beautiful delivery right there, boom, right at the low.

rules.rule: 2024 variant: second PM macro 2:50-3:10 PM, a window where price spools and runs for liquidity.
rules.quote: 2:50 to 3:10 macro, and it's just a time when the market will spool and run for liquidity.

rules.rule: 2026 variant: the first 30 minutes of the PM (1:30-2:00 PM) is the PM session opening range that frames PM trading.
rules.quote: and then the next 30 minutes [1:30 PM] is your PM session opening range, which sets the stage for PM session trading.

rules.rule: Lunch-low sweep: sell stops under the lunch-hour lows are the PM liquidity pool; lows made between noon and 1 PM get swept.
rules.quote: here's noon to one and I taught you in the mentorship that many times you'll see that the lows at lunch time will get swept

rules.rule: Bullish version of the lunch sweep: if bullish and the market consolidates at lunch, mark the lunch lows as the level to be swept.
rules.quote: if you're bullish and it consolidates in lunch find the lunch lows to be swept

rules.rule: AM rally then lunch consolidation: look for a drop below the lunch low that takes the sell stops before the PM rally.
rules.quote: if the morning session rallies and then consolidates during the lunch hour, look for a drop below the lunch low to sweep sell stops before the afternoon rally

rules.rule: Why a tight stop under the lunch consolidation fails: that is exactly where the sweep goes.
rules.quote: stop losses resting just below the lunch hour consolidation are primed to be targeted and swept

rules.rule: Mirror (bearish) case: lunch-hour highs get swept to engineer an afternoon reversal down (shown as a 1:35 PM bearish breaker short).
rules.quote: the algorithm often seeks out liquidity to engineer a reversal for the afternoon

rules.rule: PM session reversal model structure (Jan 2023): liquidity purge, smart money reversal, low-risk market maker buy that clears out the original consolidation.
rules.quote: and I told you I would teach you a model: smart money reversal, low risk buy, market maker buy model that clears out the original consolidation.

rules.rule: 3-4 PM false breakout: the late breakout above equal highs is a liquidity run to fill market-on-close orders, not continuation; fade it back into the range.
rules.quote: retail traders view the late breakout as continuation, but algorithmically it is an engineered liquidity run to fill market-on-close orders before a mean-reverting retracement

rules.rule: Do not act on the sweep alone: wait for the algorithm to show displacement plus a Market Structure Shift.
rules.quote: wait for the algorithm to communicate a shift through displacement and Market Structure Shift

rules.rule: A sweep followed by an aggressive move is not a trade unless it prints MSS with an imbalance (FVG).
rules.quote: if price sells off or rallies aggressively following a sweep but does not print the required mentorship model criteria (market structure shift with an imbalance / Fair Value Gap), do not trade the move

rules.rule: Optional confirmation filter: between noon and 3 PM compare the index triad highs and lows; one index failing to confirm the extreme (SMT) qualifies the PM direction.
rules.quote: We're looking for the highs and the lows between noon and 3:00 PM New York time

rules.rule: Setup quality filter: the afternoon setup must be unambiguous, it should jump off the chart.
rules.quote: Just wait through lunch! If you do that, you will get the cleanest setup of the day. What does that mean? Where everything simply jumps off the chart and makes itself very obvious.

rules.rule: Lunch-low sweep long: buy when price trades below the lunch lows into an existing bullish imbalance or bullish Order Block.
rules.quote: long entries on afternoon continuation setups can be executed when price trades below the lunch hour lows into an existing bullish imbalance or bullish Order Block

rules.rule: Long entry location: a 15-minute FVG sitting in discount (below 50%) of the current dealing range.
rules.quote: enter long when price retraces into a 15-minute Fair Value Gap that is located within a Discount (below 50% equilibrium) of the current Dealing Range

rules.rule: 2022 entry mechanics: swing high broken with energy, FVG left behind, buy the retrace into the FVG.
rules.quote: we have a swing high right here it breaks it does it trade above that yes was it energetic yes does it have a fair value Gap yes so now the market trades down into it here

rules.rule: 3-4 PM false-breakout fade: after the buy-stop sweep above relative equal highs, wait for a 1-minute swing-low break with an FVG, then short the retrace into that FVG.
rules.quote: when price sweeps buy stops above relative equal highs between 3:00 PM and 4:00 PM on a consolidation day, wait for a 1-minute swing low breakdown with a Fair Value Gap, then enter short when price trades back up into that FVG

rules.rule: 2023 variant (One Trading Setup For Life): after the lunch sweep he adds on the 15-second chart inside an inversion FVG that overlaps a bullish order block, treated as dynamic support.
rules.quote: That entire range is the order block, and I'm adding into it here inside the fair value gap that is already identified as an inversion fair value gap. So this is going to be dynamic support here

rules.rule: Long stop: just below the FVG low or the swing low that was the sweep.
rules.quote: your stop would be right below that fair value Gap low or below that swing low

rules.rule: Short stop (3-4 PM fade): above the newly formed swing high that swept the liquidity (about 4.25 ES points in the shown trade).
rules.quote: stop loss placed above the newly formed swing high that swept the liquidity

rules.rule: A hard stop is placed at entry, always.
rules.quote: if you don't put a hard stop in you're not really respecting the risk

rules.rule: Consolidation-day fade target: the 50% midpoint of the daily range.
rules.quote: in the middle there's your midpoint and it's going to want to gravitate back to the 50 percent midpoint of the daily range

rules.rule: Trend-style PM target (Oct 2022 Month 10): hold for the 3:00 PM bond close if at all possible.
rules.quote: At least try to aim for holding until three o'clock Bond close New York time if at all possible.

rules.rule: Targets are liquidity pools; price does not have to reach the ultimate higher-timeframe draw for the trade to pay.
rules.quote: price does not need to reach the ultimate draw on liquidity for an intraday trade setup to be valid and profitable

rules.rule: Scale out at liquidity pools rather than holding for the top tick.
rules.quote: Everything that I've outlined here is shown to you on a time-based chart. My partials are based on liquidity.

rules.rule: Take partials when price reaches premium above the 50% of the retracement swing.
rules.quote: take partial profits when price moves into premium above the 50% halfway point of the retracement swing

rules.rule: June 2022 mechanical stop ladder: at 75% of the expected target move the stop goes to break even (at 50% it is trimmed to 25%).
rules.quote: now when price moves to 75 percent of the expected targeted range and it means from your entry to here if it moves 75 of that then the stop goes to break even

rules.rule: Exit the remainder if the order block that was supposed to hold is traded through.
rules.quote: kill the remaining portion of a long trade if price trades through a bullish order block that was supposed to act as support

rules.rule: Trade count (Sept 2022 income plan): one qualifying setup a day, AM or PM, not both.
rules.quote: You only need to find one setup and then be done for the day. So if you find it in the AM session, you're not doing in the PM session, vice versa.

rules.rule: Inside the middle of an established consolidation range it is 50/50, so no continuation setups there.
rules.quote: when price is trading near the middle of an established consolidation range, the directional probability drops to 50/50; traders should not seek continuation setups in this zone

rules.rule: Do not chase an already-extended displacement; wait for the retracement into discount.
rules.quote: do not chase after displacement has occurred; wait for the retracement into discount

rules.rule: Skip the PM if the morning goal was already hit.
rules.quote: do not trade live in the afternoon session if you have already hit your goal for the day in the morning; observe or demo to avoid greed

rules.rule: Never force a trade in the noon-to-one lunch window.
rules.quote: Do not try to force trades during the noon to one o'clock hour.

rules.rule: The 15-minute chart is the bellwether chart for the dealing range and arrays; entries refine down to 5m/1m (later 15-second).
rules.quote: relative to the 15 minute time frame remember that's our bellwether chart

rules.rule: When the index triad cracks, execute in the S&P only, not the Dow or Nasdaq.
rules.quote: If I see that crack among all three, my trade's going to be taken in the S&P

rules.rule: E-mini S&P 500 is the preferred index market.
rules.quote: E-mini S&P 500 is the preferred index market because it is professional, highly liquid, and systematically delivers price without spread issues

rules.rule: Review ES and NQ side by side in the PM; the relative-strength leader (NQ that day) is the vehicle for the long.
rules.quote: Here is the hourly chart on the left-hand side on S&P, and on the right is Nasdaq. Look at how Nasdaq is the relative strength leader to the upside.
